Let a cleric and layman do penance for five years, two of them on bread and water, and be deprived of communion and sacred order.

If anyone fornicates with a blood relative, sister, or mother, let a bishop do penance for fifteen years; a presbyter, twelve years; a deacon and monk, ten; a cleric and layman, seven. Let all these do penance on bread and water, and be deprived of communion and sacred order.

If anyone fornicates with the wife whom her master has left, let a bishop do penance for twelve years, three on bread and water, and be deprived of communion. A presbyter, twelve years, three of them on bread and water. A deacon and monk, seven years, three of them on bread and water. A cleric and layman, five years, two of them on bread and water; let them be deprived of priestly honor.

If anyone fornicates with a four-footed animal, let a bishop do penance for twelve years, three of them on bread and water, and be deposed. A presbyter, ten years, three of them on bread and water, and be deposed. A deacon and monk, seven years, three of them on bread and water, and be deposed. A cleric and layman, three years, one of them on bread and water; let them not approach the priestly rank.

If anyone desires to fornicate but cannot, or the woman does not consent, let a bishop do penance for seven years; a presbyter, five; a deacon and monk, three, one of them on bread and water. Let a cleric and layman do penance for two years.

If anyone fornicates by himself, by any method whatsoever, let a bishop do penance for three years, one of them on bread and water. A deacon and monk, one year; a presbyter, two, half of them on bread and water. A cleric and layman, half a year. If it happens to them repeatedly, let them be deprived of communion for one year.

Whoever lies with animals shall do penance for ten years. A monk who commits fornication shall do penance for seven years. If it occurs on the thighs, three [years?] for those who do it. If a child suffers such things by being overpowered, let him do penance for forty days. Let him be chastised either with psalms or continence.

If anyone finds his wife in adultery and does not wish to dismiss her but to keep her in marriage, let him do penance for two years, and let him free a male or female slave for his own sake. For the other two years, let him give alms. After seven years, let him receive communion by the judgment of the priest. Or, as long as she does penance, let him abstain from marital relations.

### Concerning Perjury

If anyone commits perjury, let a bishop do penance for twelve years, three of them on bread and water. A presbyter, ten years, three of them on bread and water; let him be deposed until he completes his penance, and then reconciled. A cleric, five years, two of them on bread and water. A layman, three years, one of them on bread and water.

If anyone commits perjury under compulsion of some necessity or unknowingly, let him do penance for three years, one of them on bread and water. If a layman commits perjury out of greed, let him sell all his possessions and give them to the poor, and, having entered a monastery, serve God until death.

If, through greed, he incurs danger to his soul or danger of death, let him do penance for four years as an unarmed exile, on bread and water, and abstain from meat and wine. If anyone abducts a virgin, let him do penance for three years, one of them on bread and water.

If, in the manner of sinners, persons related by blood have entered into marriage before their twentieth year, let them do penance for ten years; after the appointed prayers have been completed, let them begin to be admitted to communion. After the twentieth year, let them be received into communion with an offering. Their conduct during the time of penance must also be examined. Thus let this be treated with humanity.

But if some have committed this crime after a longer period, while having wives and being beyond twenty years of age, let them do penance for fifteen years and one [additional year?]. [Col. 0429A] After completing penance, let them be admitted to the communion of prayers. After another five years, let them be received into full communion with an offering.

But if some, while having wives, have fallen into this after their fiftieth year, let them merit communion only at the end of life. If a woman marries two brothers, she ought to be rejected until the day of death; but, because of humanity, she may be reconciled to communion at the end of life. If she should recover her health, however, let her be admitted to penance after the marriage has been dissolved.

If a woman bound in such a union has died, the penance of the survivor shall be different. Both woman and man must observe this judgment.

If a gentile man dismisses a gentile wife, it shall be in his power after baptism to have her or not to have her. Likewise, if one has been baptized and the other is a gentile. If someone’s wife is an unbeliever or gentile, and he cannot convert her, let him dismiss her.

A woman must abstain from her husband for three months when she has conceived and before she gives birth. After childbirth, whoever has intercourse shall do penance for forty days; whoever has intercourse on Sunday shall do penance for four days.

If a man’s wife has departed from him and then returned, let him receive her at night. Let her herself do penance for one year. Likewise let the husband do penance if he has taken another woman.

If a man or woman is sterile, both he and she shall practice continence. If a woman fornicates with a woman, let one penance of three years be imposed. Widows and girls should perform a greater penance if they commit this sin.

A woman who has had a husband, if she fornicates, and the one who has emitted semen in her, shall do penance for seven years. This is a very serious evil. Elsewhere it has been judged differently: that both should do penance until the end of their lives. Or twelve years, or seven, for one who has fornicated repeatedly. The first canon judged ten years, the second seven; but because of human weakness, or by decision of a council, they said that he or she should do penance either three or seven years.

If anyone fornicates with a natural brother through sexual intercourse, let him do penance for fifteen years and abstain from all meat. If a mother engages in fornication with her young son, let her do penance for three years, abstaining from meat, and let her fast one day each week until evening.

Let anyone who is deceived into fornication by a thought do penance until the thought is overcome. Whoever loves a woman should ask God mentally for forgiveness. If he speaks of love and affection, but she has not accepted it, let him do penance for seven days. Let him do penance for a full year and six months if he wished to fornicate in this way but was unable to.

If a layman secretly takes a nun from a monastery, let him either enter the monastery to serve God or undergo secular punishment. Money belonging to the Church that has been stolen or carried off shall be repaid fourfold; money taken from secular persons, twofold.

Whoever repeatedly commits theft shall do penance for seven years, or according to the priest’s judgment. Let him likewise make compensation to those he harmed. The thief, led to penance, must always be reconciled with the one he offended and restore according to the harm he caused; this will greatly shorten his penance. But if he is unwilling or unable to perform the prescribed period of penance in full, the thief is to be admonished. Let him also give to the poor.

“Juratus consecratam” [the printed reading and its sense are uncertain]: let him do penance for three years without fat, and then receive communion. If anyone has been ordained by heretics, he ought to be ordained again if he is irreproachable; otherwise he must be deposed.

If anyone passes from the Catholic Church to heresy and later returns, he cannot be ordained except after a long penance and in a case of great necessity. Pope Innocent asserts, on the authority of the canons, that this person may not become a cleric even after penance.

Whoever celebrates Easter with the Jews on the fourteenth day of the moon shall be expelled from the whole Church unless he performs penance before death. If he prays with such a person as with a Catholic cleric, let him do penance for one week. If he has neglected the matter, let him do penance for forty days.

If, at the first occasion, anyone wishes to encourage their heresy and does not perform penance, he too shall be expelled, the Lord saying: “Whoever is not with me is against me.”

If anyone is baptized by a heretic who does not rightly believe in the Trinity, let him be baptized again. If anyone gives or receives communion from the hand of a heretic, not knowing that the Catholic Church rejects this, and later understands it, let him do penance for one full year. If he knows and has neglected the matter, and later performs penance, let him do penance for ten years. Others judge seven years, and more humanely, five.

If anyone permits a heretic to celebrate his mass in a Catholic church, without knowing it, let him do penance for forty days. But if he did so out of reverence for the heretic, let him do penance for one year. If he did so to the detriment of the Catholic Church, let him be expelled from the Church as a heretic unless he repents.

If anyone withdraws from the Catholic Church into a gathering of heretics, or persuades others to do so, let him do penance for twelve years: four years outside the Church, seven among the hearers, and two outside communion. Concerning such persons it is said in the Synod [alternative: “canon”]: in the tenth year let them receive communion or the offering [alternative: “communion without the offering”].

If a bishop or abbot orders his monk to sing a mass for heretics who have died, it is not expedient for him to obey. If this happens to a presbyter, and he celebrates the mass there and names the dead, naming heretics together with Catholics, once he understands what he has done after the mass, let him fast for a week. If he does this frequently, let him do penance for the entire year.

If anyone has arranged a mass for the death of a heretic and, out of religious devotion, made relics from him because he had fasted greatly, and later understood the matter and performed penance, he ought to burn the relics in fire and do penance for one year. If he knows and neglects the matter, let him, moved to penance, do penance for forty years.

If anyone abandons the faith of God without any necessity and thereafter accepts penance with his whole heart, let him do penance for three years outside the Church, seven years in the Church among the penitents, and two further years outside communion, one among the hearers, according to the Council of Nicaea.

Whoever commits perjury in the Church shall do penance for eleven years; but whoever is compelled by necessity to do some such thing, one year. Whoever swears by the hand of a human being has done nothing. But if he swears by the hand of a bishop, presbyter, or deacon, or upon an altar or consecrated cross, let him do penance for one year; perjurers, seven.

Concerning those who have committed many evils—that is, homicide, adultery with a woman, and sin . . . . and theft—let them go to a monastery and do penance [Col. 0431A] until death.

Whatever has been seized in another province conquered by an enemy—that is, after another king has been defeated—a third part of it shall be given to the Church or to the poor. Let penance be performed for forty days, because it was the king’s command.

Whoever drinks blood or semen shall do penance for three years. Forgiveness for evil thoughts is granted if they are not carried out in deed and if the person has not consented to them. Twelve periods of three days are to be reckoned as one year. Theodore approved this.

A faint-hearted person who eats unclean meat, or tears apart carrion mangled by beasts, shall do penance for forty days. If necessity compels it, there is no offense. Whoever, out of necessity, eats an animal that appears unclean, whether bird or beast, is not at fault.

If a flea falls into a liquid, let it be removed, and let the liquid be sprinkled with holy water if the flea is alive. But if it is dead, [Col. 0431B] the entire liquid shall be thrown outside. It must not be given to anyone, and the vessel shall be cleansed.

Likewise, if a liquid food in which a mouse or weasel has drowned is involved, let it be purified and sprinkled with holy water, and let it be consumed if necessity requires. If birds defecate into any liquid, let the dung be removed from it and let it be sanctified with water; the food will then be clean.

To swallow blood unknowingly with saliva is not a sin. Whoever bleeds is polluted in whatever manner. Nothing is unclean if he knows it; let penance be imposed according to the degree of pollution.

### Concerning Priests Who Have Lustful Desire
If a priest is defiled by touching and kissing a woman, let him do penance for forty days. If he has kissed a woman out of desire, let him do penance for twenty days. If he has emitted semen through [Col. 0431C] thought, let him fast for a week; if his hand has stimulated him, eleven days, or a year. If polluted, let him fast for three weeks. If a presbyter has rejected penance by his conduct, he will be guilty of his own soul, because the Lord says: “At whatever hour the sinner turns back, he shall live and shall not die.” For true confession can be made even at the last moment, since our Lord is an examiner not only of time but also of the heart. Thus the thief, at the final hour, by confession in a single moment merited being in paradise. If a monk fornicates with a nun, let him do penance for seven years. Whoever emits semen through the violence of thought, let him do penance for three days. If it happens to him a second time, let him do penance for forty days or a year. If more instances are added, let him fast either for [Col. 0431D] one year or for three Lents. Whoever pollutes himself, let him do penance for 140 days. If he is a boy, let him be beaten for twenty days. If he is in orders, let him do penance for three Lents or one year, if he has done it frequently.

If someone renounces the world and afterward returns to the world in dress as well, if he is a monk and subsequently does penance, let him do penance for ten years. If he has been proved throughout his penance, in tears and prayers, a merciful bishop may restore him. If he was not a monk when he withdrew from the Church, let him do penance for seven years. If a bishop, presbyter, or deacon commits fornication, they must be degraded and do penance. If anyone, after making a vow, has taken secular dress, he must absolutely never advance to any ecclesiastical rank. If one of the presbyters or deacons has taken a foreign [Col. 0432A] wife, let him be deposed in the presence of the people. If he has committed adultery with her and this has become known publicly, let him be cast out of the Church and do penance among the laity for as long as he lives. If anyone has concubines, he must not be ordained.

For any presbyter, whether in his own province or another, wherever he may be found, who refuses to baptize a sick person entrusted to him, or [if that person] dies while travelling without baptism, let him be deposed. Likewise, let the one who kills a man, or commits fornication, be deposed. If anyone has taken a widow, he cannot be ordained, like those who have had two wives. If anyone baptizes presumptuously without having been ordained, he must be expelled from the Church and must never be ordained. Those whose baptizers are unknown do not require penance for this, except that, according to the canons, they cannot [Col. 0432B] be ordained unless great necessity compels it.

Those who have been baptized a second time—as though they were crucifying Christ again—let them do penance for seven years, on the fourth and sixth days [Wednesday and Friday], during three Lents. If it occurred because of some defect, and if he thought this permissible for the sake of purification, let him do penance for three years. Whoever works on Sunday, let him do penance for seven days or be beaten. If anyone fasts on Sunday through negligence, let him fast the entire week. If it happens a second time, let him do penance for twenty days. If it happens on a fifth Sunday, let him do penance for forty days. If anyone fasts on Sunday out of condemnation [of the day], let him be abominated by the whole Catholic Church like a Jew. If he has despised the matter and, when the Church had proclaimed a fast, has observed a Lent contrary to the decrees of the elders, let him do penance for forty days. If it occurs during Lent, let him do penance for one year. If he does it frequently and makes it habitual, let him [Col. 0432C] be exterminated from the Church, the Lord saying: “Whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble,” etc.

## Concerning Communion of the Eucharist, as a sacrifice

According to the canons, penitents ought not to receive communion before completing their penance. Out of mercy, we grant them permission after one year or six months. The period must be adjusted according to the degree of the offense, sooner or later.

Whoever receives the sacrifice after eating, let him do penance for seven days. Every sacrifice spoiled by foul age must be burned in the fire. If wild animals or birds devour it accidentally, let him fast for three weeks. If through negligence, three Lents. If a married man, or a woman bound by a vow of virginity, enters into marriage, let him not put her away, but let him or her do penance for three years. A woman [Col. 0432D] may not make a vow without her husband’s consent; but if she wishes, she may be dismissed by the judgment of the priest. A woman who has joined herself adulterously in the manner of fornication, let her do penance either seven or three years, like a fornicator. Likewise the woman who mixes her own semen into food so that he may receive greater love. A wife who has tasted her husband’s blood as a remedy, let her do penance for eighteen days.

Women during menstruation must not enter the Church or receive communion, whether laywomen or nuns; and if they have received it, let them fast for three weeks. Likewise, a woman who enters the Church before the blood following childbirth has been cleansed shall do penance for forty days. Whoever marries during these periods, let him do penance for thirty days. Whoever marries on Sunday, let him do penance for three days. If a man has intercourse with his [Col. 0433A] wife from behind, let him do penance for forty days. If he has intercourse with her anally, he must do penance like one who has intercourse with animals. If anyone commits capital theft—that is, steals four-footed animals—or [Col. 0434A] breaks into a house, let him do penance for five years, three of which … [lacuna].

[Col. 0433]

# [MARTYROLOGY (G)]

## Notice concerning the following Martyrology

Among the spurious writings of Jerome we have included this work, which is certainly worthy of being read and, compared with the others, a little work of good substance. We have taken it from the edition of D. Luc d’Achery, whose notice we have thought it better to reproduce here than to offer our own warning in these words. We have added only two letters on this subject, inscribed under the false names of Heliodorus and Jerome, which he had omitted, so that nothing relevant to our purpose, or belonging to the complete collection of writings attributed—though improperly—to Jerome, might be lacking. Concerning these matters one may consult what Baronius observed with sufficient learning in chapters 5, 6, and 7 of his preface to the Roman Martyrology. D’Achery’s preface runs as follows:

“I did indeed find a very ancient Martyrology attributed to Saint Jerome in a manuscript of the monastery of Corbie, written about six hundred years ago, which Hugo Menard had prepared for printing. Yet I would not dare assert that it is a genuine and complete offspring of that Doctor, since it is clear that many saints more recent than he were added at different times, both by clerics and by monks, at their pleasure—especially patrons and others whose yearly observances are celebrated in the churches of various places. The martyrologies of Bede, Usuard, and Ado suffered similar additions; consequently learned men would repeatedly have been forced to deny the authority of these martyrologies if they did not separate the additions from the original material.

“Moved by the same consideration, I arranged for many—not all—of the saints later than Jerome’s time to be marked in a different type, as they came to mind; and before me our Menard had done the same in many places. A little later he says:

“‘Although there are writers—and serious men of excellent reputation among them—who affirm that Jerome composed a Martyrology, or was the translator of Eusebius, the Venerable Bede says in his *Retractation on the Acts of the Apostles*, chapter 1: “The book of the Martyrology, which is entitled with Jerome’s name and preface, also supports this view; although Jerome was not the author of that book but its translator, while Eusebius is said to have been the author.” Bede likewise praises the same Martyrology in chapter 6 of his commentary on the Gospel of Mark; Walafrid Strabo, in chapter 28 of *On Ecclesiastical Matters*, says: “Jerome, following Eusebius of Caesarea, composed a Martyrology throughout the year,” and so forth.’

“Yet indeed I am pleased to excerpt and insert into my preface the principal testimonies from the dissertation of the most distinguished Henry Valesius on the Roman Martyrology edited by Rosweyde—both because of his singular learning and diligence, and because of the benefit of our friendship, but especially because he clearly demonstrates with strong arguments that no Martyrology older than ours has so far been publicly published.

“First, then, he proves that the Roman Church once possessed nowhere a proper and particular Martyrology for the use of the whole Church, before the one published at the command of Pope Sixtus V; rather, the more distinguished churches always had their own registers, in which the names of bishops and the birthdays of martyrs who had suffered among them were recorded. He then proves at greater length that the Martyrology we are making public must be considered, chiefly on the authority of Gregory the Great, the oldest of all, and as it were the source of the others.

“Valesius says that Gregory’s passage, from his letter to Eulogius, bishop of Alexandria, reads as follows:

“‘We possess in one codex the collected names of almost all the martyrs, with their passions distinguished according to the individual days; and on each day we celebrate the solemn rites of Mass in their honor. Yet in the same volume it is not stated how each one suffered, but only the place of his passion is given. Hence it comes about that many, from different lands and provinces, are recognized on the individual days—as I have said—as having been crowned by martyrdom. But we believe that you, most blessed men, possess these things.’

“There is here no mention of a Roman Martyrology, and so forth. Therefore the Martyrology mentioned there by Gregory was not proper to the Roman Church, but common to the other Western churches. At that time this was none other than the Martyrology of Blessed Jerome. Gregory’s passage must therefore be understood of it.

“That this Martyrology of Blessed Jerome was commonly received in Italy and the regions of the West is certainly shown by Cassiodorus in chapter 32 of *On Divine Readings*. From this it follows that the Martyrology, although it falsely bears Jerome’s name, is nevertheless extremely ancient and was published shortly after Jerome’s death by someone unknown.

“We recently read it from a copy lent to us by the most learned and religious D. L. D. from the library of Saint-Germain; and at the same time we saw that the words of Gregory the Great agree admirably with this Martyrology. For what Gregory says—that only the place and day of the passion were set down in that volume—is plainly found in this Martyrology of Blessed Jerome. Moreover, what Gregory adds, that the names of many martyrs were recorded ‘on each day,’ can also be seen in the Martyrology I have mentioned, in which no day is without a company of martyrs, unlike Rosweyde’s Martyrology.

“Therefore Gregory the Great’s passage cannot in any way be understood of that Martyrology which Rosweyde published as ancient, since in Rosweyde’s Martyrology the name of almost a single martyr is assigned to each day. Thus far Valesius. I omit the rest, which has no bearing at all on our purpose, lest I become too lengthy and thereby weary the reader.

“From all this it is abundantly clear, as I understand it, that those are seriously mistaken who maintain that martyrologies are older in proportion as they are shorter—namely, those in which the name of one saint or another is assigned to each day. That would perhaps be unquestionable if we now possessed martyrologies from the first or second Christian centuries. But since everyone agrees that before the time of Eusebius no registers, calendars, or martyrologies at all are found anywhere in the world, we must acknowledge and hold firmly what Valesius affirms on the basis of Gregory: namely, that the martyrology must be considered older in which the names of many martyrs are recorded together for each day of the year, with the place of their passion added.

“Finally, in order to purge the Martyrology I am publishing of certain errors, some assistance was supplied by engraved copper plates—although they are sprinkled with far more blemishes than our manuscript—which the industrious and distinguished Balthazar Moretus sent me from Antwerp with exceptional generosity. They contain most of the Martyrology of Jerome, from the beginning through the twelfth day before the Kalends of July. They reproduce the Saxon characters as they appear in the manuscript from which they were taken. Moretus told me that his father had undertaken the engraving for the public benefit, when he visited our Saint-Germain library in Paris during the past year.

“I had brought my preface to an end and had withdrawn my hand from the tablet when the Reverend Father Jean Bolland, S.J., a priest highly skilled in ancient matters and a diligent investigator, arranged with the greatest possible care to have conveyed to me, from a parchment manuscript, the months of the Martyrology that are missing from the aforementioned plates—from the twelfth day before the Kalends of July to the end—when I had appealed to him by letter. But because almost the entire Martyrology had already been printed when I received those months, I was able to fill only a very few lacunae.”

## Letter of Bishops Chromatius and Heliodorus to Blessed Jerome concerning the collection of the Martyrology

[Col. 0435A]

To the holy Lord Father Jerome, Chromatius and Heliodorus, bishops: greetings in the Lord.

When the most religious Augustus Theodosius had entered the city of Milan and had invited all the bishops of Italy to him, and was conducting an inquiry concerning certain bishops who had polluted their souls with the dregs of Arianism, it happened that our littleness too was present at that same council. When everything that had to be said had been [Col. 0436A] said and everything that had to be defined had been defined, the most Christian prince began to commend Saint Gregory, bishop of the Church of Córdoba, for this reason: every day, whether he was not fasting and celebrating the morning Masses, or whether he was fasting and celebrating the evening Masses, he recalled the names of very many martyrs whose feast-days were being observed. It was therefore decided by all of us to write to your charity, asking you to investigate the most famous daily registers from the archive of Saint Eusebius, bishop of Caesarea in Palestine, and send us the feasts of the martyrs, so that through your holy diligence we might offer this service to the martyrs more suitably and perfectly, to the honor of God.

[Col. 0435]

Thus far they. What follows is a letter bearing the title of an epistle in Jerome’s name.

## Blessed Jerome’s response to them on the same matter (C, G, S)

[Col. 0435B]

To Chromatius and Heliodorus, holy bishops: Jerome, presbyter.

It is established that our Lord Jesus Christ receives every day the triumphs of his martyrs, whose passions we find written by Saint Eusebius, bishop of Caesarea. For when the Emperor Constantine had entered Caesarea and had told that bishop to request some benefits useful to the Church of Caesarea, Eusebius is said to have replied as follows: the Church, enriched by its own resources, was compelled by no necessity to request benefits; nevertheless, he had one fixed desire—that, by careful investigation and examination of public [Col. 0435C] records, they should search out whatever had been done throughout the Roman world against the saints of God by judge after judge; and that, on imperial order, they should send Eusebius from those archives the records of which martyrs had won the palm of their passion, under what judge, in what province or city, on what day, and with what steadfastness.

Thus it came about that, being a competent narrator, he both rewove ecclesiastical history and, as a diligent historian, made known the triumphs of almost all the martyrs of all the Roman provinces, so that every day, [Col. 0436B] when offering sacrifice to God, we might remember their names; and so that we might honor those who on the very day when the sacrifice was offered had proved victorious over the devil, and, prevailing and rejoicing in the triumph of their martyrdom, had reached their own king, Christ.

For this reason we have written down the feasts of each month and of each day, as you had ordered, trusting that the memory of our littleness would endure when, throughout so many years and days, the holy names of the saints had been solemnly celebrated. And because on each day the names of more than eight hundred and nine hundred martyrs from different provinces and different cities have been recorded—so that there is no day that cannot be found entered among the number of five hundred, except the day of the Kalends of January—I have [Col. 0436C] considered that the reader’s mind might grow weary amid innumerable crowds within a single month. To prevent this, I have briefly and concisely mentioned above all the others only those who are celebrated in their own places with the greatest solemnity, so that, once tedium had been cut away, a single little book entered for all might suffice.

In the first part of the little book we have written down the feasts of all the blessed apostles, so that the different days might not appear to divide those whom the one dignity of apostleship made exalted in heavenly glory.

## The Most Ancient Martyrology, Distinguished by the Name of Saint Jerome the Presbyter

[Col. 0435]

## Feasts of the Apostles: In place of a preface

[Col. 0435D]

**The third day before the Kalends of July.** At Rome, the feast-day of the apostles Peter and Paul.

**The second day before the Kalends of December.** The feast-day of Andrew the apostle in the city of Patras, province of Achaia.

**The Kalends of May.** In the city of Hierapolis, province of Asia, the burial of Philip the apostle.

[Note: *Philip the apostle.* Eusebius gives a different account: he says that Philip died at Hierapolis not as an apostle but as one of the seven deacons.]

**The twelfth day before the Kalends of January.** The feast-day of Thomas the apostle, who suffered in India.

[Col. 0436D]

**The sixth day before the Kalends of January.** The establishment of the episcopate of Saint James the apostle, the brother of the Lord, who was the first of the Jews to be appointed bishop at Jerusalem by the apostles. And the Assumption of Saint John the Evangelist at Ephesus, the city from whose tomb manna flows.

**The seventh day before the Kalends of August.** The feast-day of Saint James the apostle, brother of John the Evangelist.

**The ninth day before the Kalends of September.** The feast-day of Saint Bartholomew the apostle, who was beheaded in Further India for Christ, by order of King Astriages.

**The eleventh day before the Kalends of October.** The feast-day of Matthew the apostle and evangelist, who suffered for Christ’s name in Ethiopia, in the city of Thartium.

[Col. 0437A]

**The fifth day before the Kalends of November.** The feast-day of the apostles Simon the Canaanite and Judas the Zealot, who were killed by the chief priests of the temples in Susa, a great city in Persia.

# The Martyrology Begins

**The eighth day before the Kalends of January.** At Bethlehem, the nativity according to the flesh of our Savior Jesus Christ. At Rome, Juvinus, Pastor, Basil, Victurina, Achileus, Eutychus, Symphronianus, Saturninus, Timedus, Ignatius, Cyriacus, Gaius, Januaria, and Dativus. In the cemetery of Apronianus, on the Latin Way at Rome, the passion of Saint Eugenia, virgin, Syrmia, and Anastasia. At Milan, Felicitas. At Pergamum, Saint Saturninus. At Constantinople, Saint Anastasius.

[Col. 0437B]

**The seventh day before the Kalends of January.** In the city of Jerusalem, at the village of Caphargamala, the passion of Saint Stephen, deacon, martyr, and apostle, who was stoned by the Jews. At Rome, the burial of Saints Dionysius, Helias, and Dorostolus. At Antioch, Julian, Martian, Neander, and Januaria.

**The sixth day before the Kalends of January.** The Assumption of Saint John the Evangelist at Ephesus. And the establishment of the episcopate of Saint James, the brother of the Lord, who was the first of the Jews to be appointed bishop at Jerusalem by the apostles and was crowned with martyrdom at Easter.

**The fifth day before the Kalends of January.** At Bethlehem, the feast-day of the holy Infants and nursing children who suffered for Christ under Herod. At Ancyra in Galatia, Eutychius the presbyter and Domitian the deacon. In Africa, Castor, Octavius, Victor, Gata, Rogatus, Eusebius, Probatus, Januarius, Saturius, Cato, Restituta, and Saturninus. In Thrace, Gaianus and Domitia. At Edessa, the translation of the body of Saint Thomas the apostle.

[Col. 0437C]

**The fourth day before the Kalends of January.** In Africa, Domitius, Victor, Crescentius, Primianus, Libosus the bishop, Secundus, Saturninus, Honoratus, Victuria, Saturus, and Felix. At Rome, Felix and Boniface the bishop, concerning the ordination.

**The third day before the Kalends of January.** At Alexandria, Mansuetus, Securus, Donatus, Honoratus, Polyclitus, Appianus, Serenus, Paul, Stephen, Papianus, Cletus, and Clement. At Tours, the city, Perpetuus the bishop and confessor. On the island of Oia, Saint Florentius.

[Col. 0437D]

**The second day before the Kalends of January.** At Carthage, Donatus, Caelestinus, and Saturninus. At Bologna, Gaius and Serenus. At Rome, Donatus, Paul, Rogata, Dominanda, and Hilarina. And the burial of Saint Sylvester, bishop and confessor. In Raetia, Hermes the exorcist. In the province of Sicily, in the city of Catania, Stephen, Potitian, Attalus, Fabian, Cornelius, Sextus, Floridus, Cotta, Quintianus, Minervinus, Saint Sequentus, Amon, Calendion, Evelpistus, Exuperantius, Saturninus, Agnes, Paulina, Donata, Nominanda, and Rogatus. At Sens, the city, the passion of Saint Columba, virgin.

## The Month of January

It has thirty days. The letter of the indiction.

**The Kalends of January.** The Circumcision of our Lord Jesus Christ [Col. 0438A] according to the flesh. In the East, Stephen. At Nicomedia, Euphrosinus the bishop, Primianus, and nine others. In Raetia, Eventius and Hermes. At Bologna, Gaius and Heraclius. In Africa, Victor, Felix, Narcissus, Argyrus, and four others, Papatus, Primianus, and Saturninus. Likewise Saturninus, Victor, Honoratus, Leusius, and Hermes. At Rome, on the Appian Way, thirty military martyrs crowned. At Ravenna, the burial of Saint Severus the confessor. At Autun, the burial of Blessed Agrippinus the bishop. In the city of Ruspe, the burial of Blessed Fulgentius, bishop and confessor.

**The fourth day before the Nones of January.** At Antioch, Siridon, bishop of that place; Stratonica, Macarius the abbot, Saturus, Possessor, Firmus, Maximian, Acutio, Timothy, and Heresius. At Arthaxa, Vitalis, Acuta, and Tobias. In Ethiopia, [Col. 0438B] Rutula, Claudia, Auriga, and Vitalis. At Jerusalem, Stephen.

**The third day before the Nones of January.** In the Hellespont, in the city of Parethia, Cyricus, Primus, and Theogenes.

[Note: *The city of Parothia.* That is, on the island of Peparethus.]

In the city of Tomis, Claudion, Eugenius, Rhodus, and the three brothers Argeus, Narcissus, and Marcellinus the boy; Christianifilius the bishop, Eugentius, and Rhodon. In Africa, Lucidus, Martialis, Statulianus, Constans, Possessor, Hilarinus, Pennica, Firmus, Candidus, Rogatianus, Eugenia, and Acuta. Likewise Candidus. At Paris, Saint Genevieve, virgin. At Vienne, Blessed Florentius, bishop and confessor.

**The second day before the Nones of January.** In Africa, Aquilinus, Germinus, Eugentius, Martianus, Quintus, Theodotus, and Tryphon; in the East. At Bologna, Hermes, Aggeus, Gaius, Peter, Mark, Serenus, Sennis, and Anastasia.

[Col. 0438C]

**The Nones of January.** In Africa, Felix, Secundus, Honorius, Lucian, Candidus, Januarius, Caelesforus, Jocundus, Acutus, Peter, Mark, Serenus, Sennis, and Anastasia. At Jerusalem, Simeon the prophet, when Mary and Joseph presented Jesus to him; and the burial of that prophet. At Antioch, the burial of Saint Simeon the monk and confessor, who stood on a column.

**The eighth day before the Ides of January.** The Epiphany of our Lord Jesus Christ. In Africa, Forus, Jocundus, Peter, Mark, Acutus, Januaria, Julius, Honorius, and Antoninus. Likewise Forus. At Sirmium, Anastasia. At Antioch, the passion of Saints Julian and Basilissa. In India, Celsus the boy, Julian, and Antoninus. And the passion of Saint Fausta. In the city of Redon, the nativity, episcopal ordination, and passing of Saint Melanius, bishop and confessor, which are celebrated there.

[Col. 0438D]

**The seventh day before the Ides of January.** At Nicomedia, Lucian the presbyter, who was divided into four parts. In the city of Militene, the feast-day of Saint Polyeuctus and Candida. In the city of Heraclea, Felix and Januaria. In Greece, in the city of Policostinus, Palladius and Candida. Elsewhere, Poliartus, Philoronus, Candidianus, and Eutychius.

**The sixth day before the Ides of January.** In Greece, Rusticus, Phiseus, Timothy, Jocundus, Ratites, Lucius, Peter, Florus, and Anastasia. Elsewhere, Satheus and Mark. In Gaul, in the city of Beauvais, the passion of Saints Lucian, Marianus, and Julian, martyrs. At Autun, the burial of Blessed Aegemonius, bishop.

[Col. 0439A]

**The fifth day before the Ides of January.** In Africa, Epictetus, Jocundus, Quintus, Secundus, Saturninus, and Vitalis. Likewise Quintus, Felix, Artaxis, Fortunatus, Rusticus, Sillus, Quietus, and seven others; Martialis and Saturus. At Smyrna, Revocatus, Firmus, Sillus, Possessor, Januarius, Saturninus, and Saturus.

**The fourth day before the Ides of January.** In Africa, Revocatus, Firmus, Nirthus, Possessor, and two others. At Rome, in the cemetery of Callistus on the Appian Way, the burial of Melchiades the bishop. In Africa, Saturus, Vitalianus, Felicitas, and Quintus, whose acts are preserved by Artatius.

**The third day before the Ides of January.** At Alexandria, Peter, Severus, Saint Lucius the confessor, Assolamus, and Quintus. In Africa, Philoromus, Ingenuus, Quintus, Januarius, Saturninus, and Vincentius. In Spain, Augentius, Donatus, Augustine, Salvius, and Felix. Likewise Felix, Donatus the presbyter, Florus, Zeminus, Pausalmius, Eugentius, Victor, Stephen, and twelve others. And the burial of Hortensius the bishop.

[Col. 0439B]

**The day before the Ides of January.** In Achaia, Cyriacus, Moscentius, and Saturus. In Africa, Zoticus, Castulus, Quintus, Rogatus, Modestus, Ebicianus, Caroticus, and Castolinus. In Egypt, Philoromus, Zoticus, Castulus, Peter, and Aventinus.

**The Ides of January.** In Africa, Ingenuus, Vincentius, Sattius, Felicitas, and Modestus. In Campania, at Naples, Cyriacus, Ciminus, Zoticus, Erisius, Clerus, Felix, and Januarius. At Rome, Secunda and Rogata. On the Lavican Way, forty military martyrs crowned. Elsewhere, Eos, Quomo, and Eononis. At Poitiers, the burial of Saint Hilary, bishop and confessor. At Amiens, the finding of Saint Firminus, bishop and confessor.

[Col. 0439C]

**The nineteenth day before the Kalends of February.** At Antioch, Clerius the deacon, who suffered many ancient tortures and was thrown into the sea. In Africa, Paul, Successus, Victorinus, Saturus, Messor, Gerontius, Lucritia, Januarius, Florida, and Theocosa. At Nola in Campania, Saint Felix. Elsewhere, the burial of Euphrasius the bishop.

**The eighteenth day before the Kalends of February.** In Egypt, Chrisconius, Thyrsus, Leucius, Gaianus, Genonus, and Menelampius. In the East, Cornelius, Caelestus, and the others. At Antioch, Leucerius the deacon. Elsewhere, the burial of Habakkuk the prophet. At Rheims, the burial of Saint Remigius, bishop and confessor. At Poitiers, the dedication of the basilica of Saint Amantius.

**The seventeenth day before the Kalends of February.** At Rome, on the Salarian Way, in the cemetery of Priscilla, the burial of Saint Marcellus, bishop and confessor. On the Appian Way, in the cemetery of Callistus, the passion of Saints Martha and Audeina, martyrs. On the Cornelian Way, in the cemetery, nine soldiers and thirteen others, whose names are written in the book of life. In Africa, Saturninus, Faustinus, Flavinianus, and six others. At Arles, the burial of Saint Honoratus, bishop and confessor.

**The sixteenth day before the Kalends of February.** In Africa, Micah, Victor, Mistrianus, Salvius, Misilianus, Victor, Theocosa, Fortunata, Veneria, Sata, Saturninus, Hostesianus, Leucius, Missurianus, Vincentius, Alba, Moses, Ingenuula, and Victuria. In the East, Natalis, Rubentia, and Marterius. In Egypt, in the Thebaid, the burial of Antony the monk. At Langres, the passion of the holy martyr siblings Speusippus, Elasippus, Melasippus, Leonella, Meonus, and Junella. And the burial of Saint Marcellus the bishop. In Gaul, in the city of Bourges, the burial of Saint Sulpitius, bishop and confessor.

[Col. 0440A]

**The fifteenth day before the Kalends of February.** The dedication of the chair of Saint Peter the apostle, on which he first sat at Rome. In Pontus, a city of Asia, Moses, Amon, Micah, Asterius, Fortunatus, Zeno, Zosimus, Menelampius, Daedalus, and Valens. And the passion of Saint Thyrsus with his companions, Leucius and Gallinicus. In Africa, Seonisius, Successus, Valens, Felerianus, Paul, Majulus, Lucius, Victorinus, Honoratus, Saturninus, Florida, Luricus, and fourteen others. And the passion of Saint Prisca.

**The fourteenth day before the Kalends of February.** In Africa, Quintus, Paul, Gerontius, Januarius, Saturninus, Successus, Germana, Tertulla, and many others. At Tibiritani, Majulus, Victorianus, Honoratus, Fortunatus, Julius, Lucius, Marcus, Publius, Felix, Gaius, Vitalis, Cassianus, Victor, Secundus, Primus, Hispanus, and Cacinarius. Likewise Lucius, Saturnina, Florida, Caelestica, and Molendio. At Jerusalem, Martha and Mary, the sisters of Lazarus. At Carthage, Pigaria, Pia, and thirty-eight others. Zosimus, Menelampius, Tiberianus, and Fortunatus. At Lyons, the establishment of the episcopate of Saint Nicetius.

[Col. 0440B]

**The thirteenth day before the Kalends of February.** At Rome, in the cemetery, Fabianus the bishop; and the passion of Saint Sebastian the martyr. In the cemetery, Marius and Martha his wife, Audifax, and Habakkuk. At Nicomedia, Leontius, Bitius, Cyriacus, Ursus, Cendeus, Felix, Coelidonia, Martia, Nicetius, Nivedunius, Thyrsus, Quiriacus, and Gellinicus. At Lyons in Gaul, Clement the presbyter.

**The twelfth day before the Kalends of February.** At Rome, the passion of Saint Agnes, virgin. And the feast-day of Felix, Fructuosus, Celsion, Felogica, Caeciliana, Augurius, and Martialis. Likewise Felix, Vitus, Candeus, Flora, Leontius, Cyriacus, and Faustacus. At Nicomedia, Deustasius the confessor. In Africa, Solutor and Hermes. In Spain, in the city of Tarragona, the passion of Saints Fructuosus the bishop, Augurius and Eulogius the deacons, Saturninus, Quintus, Marinus, Dacius, Satyrus, Gaddianus, Caelenianus, Zabulius, Mammas, Vincentius, Rogatus, Victor, Reposita, Primus, Lucius, Majulinus, Honoratus, Marcus, Secundus, Castinus, Gaius, Caelestinus, Ermis the bishop, and Publius. Likewise Leontius. At Troyes, the passion of Saint Patroclus the martyr. At Clermont, the burial of Blessed Avitus the bishop.

[Col. 0440C]

**The eleventh day before the Kalends of February.** In Spain, in the city of Valencia, the passion of Saint Valerius the bishop, Vincentius the deacon and martyr, and eighteen martyrs with their companions: Quintilianus, Cassianus, Matutinus, Publius, Urbanus, Martialis, Faustus, Paul, Successus, Peter, Felix, Januarius, Primitivus, Ebotius, Optatus, Caecilianus, Fronto, Julius, Januarius, Lupercus, Apodimus, Orion, Mennon, Hermes, and Januaria. In Africa, Quiri with his companions Gemellus, Saturus, Januarius, Felix, Ticius, Florus, and Orion. At Gemellae, Clement, Saturninus, and Municipius.

**The tenth day before the Kalends of February.** In Mauretania, in the city of Neocaesarea, the passion of Saint Severianus and Aquila his wife, Bellus, Municius, Castulus, Florus, Saturninus, Basilla, and Anastasius the martyr. Elsewhere, Cornelius the exorcist. At Ancyra [Col. 0441A] in Galatia, Donatus, Castulus, Popica, Dematus, and all their companions. Elsewhere, the passion of the holy martyrs Eugenius, Emerentiana, Macarius, and Pulvius.

**The ninth day before the Kalends of February.** At Antioch, the passion of Saint Babylas the bishop with three children. In the city of Neocaesarea, Mardonius and Eugenius. In Africa, Epictetus and Rufus. At Carthage, Gelia. At Rome, Felicissimus with his companions.

**The eighth day before the Kalends of February.** At Nicomedia, Bitius. At Rome, the translation of Saint Paul the apostle. At Carthage, Donatus, Secundus, and Papia. In Africa, Epictetus, Publianus, and Saturus. And Praiectus the martyr.

**The seventh day before the Kalends of February.** At Nicaea in Smyrna, the passion of Saint Polycarp the bishop. In Campania, at Puteoli, Arthemas and Armata, Donata.

[Note: *In Campania, at Picteolis.* Acherius thought that a certain saint named Picteolus was being commemorated; but one should read *Puteolis*, which is a city of Campania.]

At Laodicea, Artemius, Fabianus, Sabinus, Sidon, and Macarius. At Ravenna, Antemasius, Sabinus, Leodocius, Theogenes, and thirty-six martyrs. At Bethlehem, the falling asleep of Saint Paula.

[Col. 0441B]

**The sixth day before the Kalends of February.** In Africa, Donatus, Dativus, Misurianus, Publius, Victor, Quintillus, Publianus, Festus, Felix, Vosonius, Processus, Veneria, Marina, Fortunatus, Theosa, Egoditis, Secunda, Epictilis, Vincentius, Rogatus, Primus, Aurelius, Hilary, Perpetua, Juliana, and forty-four others. At Nicomedia, Leacius. At Apollonia, Gallinicus, Lucius, Honoratus, Marusus, Secundus, Castus, Gaius, and Caelestinus. Sulpitius the bishop and confessor. And the dedication of the basilica of Saint Victor.

**The fifth day before the Kalends of February.** At Rome, Saint Agnes, Julian, Tellianus, Reotus, Telipta, Vincentia, Victorinus, Secundus, Papecantius, Victor, Aemilianus, and thirty-five other martyrs.

[Col. 0441C]

**The fourth day before the Kalends of February.** In the city of Galba, Saint Paul. In Africa, at Perusia, Victor and Honoratus. In Tursia, Constantius and Hippolytus the bishop, from ancient times. At Trier, the burial of Blessed Valerius, bishop and confessor.

**The third day before the Kalends of February.** At Antioch, the passion of Saint Hippolytus the martyr. In Africa, Pellianus, Clerius, Felippianus, and 124 others. At the monastery of Chelles, the burial of Queen Balthild. At the monastery of Corbie, the dedication of the basilica of Saint John the Evangelist.

**The day before the Kalends of February.** At Alexandria, Tarsicius, Zoticus, Ammonius, Comminus, Cyriacus, Geminus, Gelasius, Hippolytus, Ursinus, and Thyrsus. And the passion of the holy martyrs Gallinicus and fifteen other priests. In Africa, Victor, Publius, Saturninus, and Polycarp, Gaius.

## The Month of February

It has twenty-eight days.

[Col. 0441D]

**The Kalends of February.** In Greece, the holy Polycarp the bishop, Poenis, and Dionysius. Likewise Dionysius; likewise Poenis and fifteen other martyrs. In Africa, Publius, Saturninus, Maurinianus, Libosus, Vincentia, and twenty-four others. At Ravenna, Severus the bishop, Victor, Lucian, Apollinaris, Hilary, Amon, Zoticus, and Cyriacus. Likewise Severus the confessor. And the burial of Pietus the presbyter; and the passion of the holy Vindemialis and Eugenius. In Scotland, Saint Brigid, virgin.

[Col. 0442A]

**The fourth day before the Nones of February.** The Purification of Blessed Mary, when Jesus was presented in the temple. In Africa, the feast-day of Victor, Marinus, Honoratus, Urbanus, Hilary, Perpetua, Juliana, Brivatula, and seventy-four other martyrs. At Rome, at the Forum of Symphronius, on the Flaminian Way, 174 miles from the city, Laurentius and Hippolytus. And the feast-day of Fortunatus, Felicianus, Firmus, Candidus, Castula, Secunda, Cappa, Rogatiana, Gaius, Gregory, Felicitas, and Placidus. Likewise Victor, Martialis, Cornelianus, Salustius, Maricus, Urbicus, Pubius, Secundianus, Ingenuus, Mustula, Victuria, Honoria, Forosus, and Prunus. Likewise Victor, Natalis, Primus, Hilary, Rogata, and Saturninus. At Orléans, the burial of Saint Fusculus the bishop, and the burial of Sicaria, consecrated to God, who died there.

[Col. 0442B]

**The third day before the Nones of February.** In Africa, Felix, Celerina, and Felicitas. At Vappincum, the burial of Eporteredius and Remedius. At Lyons, the burial of Blessed Lupicinus the bishop.

**The day before the Nones of February.** At the Forum of Symphronius, the feast-day of Geminus, Gelarius, Magnus, Donata, Aquilinus, and Geminus. Likewise Donata and Theophilus the bishop with his daughter.

## Nones of February

In Sicily, in the city of Catania, the martyrdom of Saint Agatha the virgin, Saturus, Revocatus, Gelasius, Felix, and Saturninus. In the East, in the city of Patras, the ordination to the episcopate of Saint Andrew, bishop and martyr. At Vienne, the deposition of Avitus, bishop and confessor.

## 6 February

At Rome, on the Appian Way, in the cemetery of the same name, the martyrdom of Soter, virgin and martyr. In Achaea, Saturninus, Revocata, and Victoria. At Caesarea in Cappadocia, the martyrdom of Saints Dorothea and Theophilus [Col. 0442C] Scholasticus. At Syracuse, the martyrdom of Saint Lucy the virgin, Antolianus, and Saturninus. At the monastery of Elnone, the deposition of Saint Amandus, bishop and confessor. At Arras, the deposition of Saint Vedastus, bishop and confessor.

## 7 February

In Britain, in the city of Augusta, the commemoration of Augulus, bishop, Anatolius, Andrew, Ammon, Statianus, Nepotianus, Saturninus, Lucius, and Saturnina.

## 8 February

In Lesser Armenia, the commemoration of Dionysius, Aemilianus, and Sebastianus. At Rome, the deposition of Saint Paul, bishop. And elsewhere, Lucius.

## 9 February

At Suevo in Cyprus, the commemoration of Alexander, Ammon, Alexandria, Paul, and Dionysius. And at Membras [Note: “At Membras.” Acherius says that perhaps “at Mandras” should be read. I recognize a place of this name not far from Constantinople; but whether those now mentioned suffered there, others may determine.], Ammon, Aemilianus, Lassa, Poemus, and Didymus. Likewise Ammon and thirty-four others. And the deposition of Thomas. In Egypt, Julianus, Pleseus, [Col. 0442D] Thyrsus, Ronus, Germanus, Orphasius, Miligutus, Oridion, Agatho, Recumbus, Bastamus, Armata, Prothiorion, Colotus, Aratus, Theona, Yppullus, Saturnilla, Epitimus, Serapion, Liastinonus, Papias, Pampirus, Dioscorus, Erudius, Potanion, Petecon, Decominus, Dioscodius, Zotimus, Cyriacus, and Papias. At Parrona, the commemoration of Furseus the confessor.

## 10 February

At Alexandria, the martyrdom of Apollonius, Protheus, Orion, Plavius, and twenty others. At Rome, Sotheris, Zoticus, Hyacinthus, Irenaeus, and Dionysius. In Campania, [Col. 0443A] the commemoration of Silvanus, bishop and confessor. At Bethlehem, under Herod, the martyrdom of Saints Andrew and Aporus. At the city of Sanctonas, the deposition of Urbanus, bishop and confessor. And of Baldegundis, abbess.

## 11 February

At Apamea, Poenus, Euphraxius, and Armata. In Campania, Basilianus, Amantius, and Talicus. In Africa, Victor, Felix, Januarius, Vitalis, Zoticus, Cyriacus, Ammon, Pelionicus, Basilius, and Germanus. At Rome, Sorotedius.

## 12 February

In Africa, the martyrdom of Saint Domianus and Victoria. At Carthage, Posinnus, Modestus, and Revocatus. At Alexandria, Julianus, Victor, Felix, Secundus, Severianus, Carporus, Germius, Cyriacus, Ammon, Pamphilus, Dorothea, and Theophilus. Likewise Julianus. In Italy, Donatus, Heraclius, Vincentius, Susanna, Orbana, [Col. 0443B] Donata, and Eulalia. And the deposition of Saint Simplicius, bishop.

## 13 February

At Nicomedia, the martyrdom of Saint Julianus. At Alexandria, Tullianus and Ammon. And elsewhere, the commemoration of Dicentius and Simplicius. At Lyon, the deposition of Blessed Stephanus, bishop.

## 14 February

In Tuscany, in the city of Spoleto, the commemoration of Vitalis and Cyrion. And of Martianus and Vitalis. At Terni, on the Flaminian Way, sixty-four miles from the city of Rome, the commemoration of Saint Vincentius and Talicus. In Lycia, the commemoration of the holy martyrs Germanus and Julianus. At Alexandria, the commemoration of Basianus, Tonion, Moses, Basion, Dionysius, and Hermon, Arphasius. Likewise Dionysius, bishop, Paulus, Leviorius, Orphasius, and Plebius. Likewise Dionysius, bishop, and Amandus. In the city of Militana, [Col. 0443C] the commemoration of Saint Polictus. At Heraclea, the commemoration of Saints Felix and Januarius. In Greece, Palladius, Candidianus, Poliarctus, and Philerobis; Passamonas, Jonas, and Ammonius; Toppius, Proditus, Praeco, Moses, Lector, and Januarius. In the city of Spolisium, Vitalis and ninety-nine soldiers. In Africa, the commemoration of Valentinus. At Terni, fifty-four soldiers. On the Flaminian Way, Athenius, Martianus, Thionius, Celerinus, and Magnus. In Sicily, Egias and Julianus; the martyrdom of Saint Serenus. At Alexandria, Saturninus, Praecognius, and Maximus.

## 15 February

At Antioch, the commemoration of Josephus, the deacon, Zeno, Apollonius, Phoebus, Romanus, Zosimus, Baradus, Rufinus, and Zosus the presbyter. At Terni, the commemoration of Saint Agatha the virgin, Saturninus, Castula, Magnus, Lucius, Rogatus, John, and twelve other martyrs. [Col. 0443D] At Barcelona in Spain, the martyrdom of Saint Loquumfa. In Syria, Aventus, Sixtus, Pompinius, Gemellus, Victor, and Generosus. Likewise Victor, Gemellianus, Coturnus, Castulus, Januarius; and the deposition of Saint Silvinus.

## 16 February

In Britain, the commemoration of Saints Faustinus and Juventia. And elsewhere, Blaesius, Donatus, Dionysius, Hierappus, Martialis, Nundinarius, Prosianus, Paulus, Gallonus, Honorius, Jucundus, Memmius, Vincentius, [Col. 0444A] Fructuosus, Primus, Cicilius, Fabianus, Paulus, Maximus, and Urbanus. In Spain, at Barcelona, the martyrdom of Saint Cucufas. In Africa, Maximus. Likewise Vincentius, Paulus, Honorius, and Martialis. Likewise Maximus. Likewise Paulus, Martialis, Terapius, Marcus, and Marpius. At Nicomedia, the martyrdom of Saint Juliana, virgin and martyr. Likewise Marcus, Martialis, Marcellus, Donatus, Secundus, Marcopius, and Lucella. Likewise Secundus, Maxima, Saul, Stupuris, Mustacus, Praesens, Secunda, Junella, and 154 with them. At Fisinari, Pamphilus, Valens the deacon, Seleucus, Profidus, Theophilus, and Julianus, with five thousand Egyptians. And elsewhere, the deposition of Setradius, bishop.

## 17 February

In Africa, in the city of Concordia, the martyrdom of Saints Donatus, Secundianus, and Pamphilus. At [Col. 0444B] Aquileia, Chrysanthus, Eutychus, Concordia, Justa, Romulus, Salonus, Silvanus, and eighty-four others, whose names God knows. And elsewhere, Januarius and Felicianus. Likewise Januarius, Donatus, and Castus. Likewise Donatus, Victor, Agatha, Donatiana, Guddinus, Dativus, Fortunio, Marcella, Quintianus, and Julia. Likewise Januarius, Crescentius, Caelestinus, Saturnus, Gipton, Felicitas, Donatianus, Victoria, Emilia, Bassula, Saturus, Ebasus, Secundus, Felix, Octavianus, Faustinus, Albina, Rogatiana, Victuris, Martius, and Cetula. At Rutula, Silvanus and Guovili.

## 18 February

In Africa, the commemoration of Saints Ritulus, Silvanus, Classicus, Secundinus, Fructulus, Damasus, and Orion. At Interrapis, Paulus, Maximus, Marcellus, Marcopius, Martialis, Gemellus, Romulus, Silvina, Casticus, and Fructulus, [Col. 0444C] Januarius.

## 19 February

In Africa, the commemoration of Saints Publius, Julianus, and Marubius. Likewise Julianus, Barecheus, Marcellus, Tullius, Lampasius, Majulus, Julius, and Saturninus.

## 20 February

At Cyprus, the commemoration of Potamina, Missus, Didymus, Jucundus, and Florus. At Rome, on the Appian Way, in the cemetery of Callistus, the deposition of Gaius, bishop. And elsewhere, Victor, Corona, and ten others.

## 21 February

In Africa, the commemoration of Saints Virulus, Secundinus, Servulus, Syricus, Felix, Jucundus, Saturninus, Fortunatus, and seventeen others. And elsewhere, Victurinus, Mappalicus, Pusitinus, Thedra, Crispinus, Petrus, Secundola, Dinaris, Rusticus, Titus, Tumulus, Massedus, Justus, Securus. Likewise Massedus, Gloriosus, and Alciator. Likewise Justus, Amator, Secunda, [Col. 0444D] Syricus, and Jucundus.

## 22 February

The commemoration of the Chair of Saint Peter the apostle, at which he sat at Antioch. At Nicomedia, the commemoration of Thecla, virgin and disciple of Saint Paul the apostle. In Africa, the commemoration of Saints Victurinus, Nucerius, Palatinus, Donatus, Fortuna, and twenty-nine others. At Rome, on the Tiburtine Way, at Saint Laurence, the commemoration of Saint Concordia, Felix, and Syrmia; the commemoration of Saint Senerus and seventy-two others. Likewise at Nicomedia [Note: [Col. 0443D] “Likewise at Nicomedia.” Here the copyist committed a double error, which led Acherius into two errors. For he recognized “Nicomedi” where “Nicomedia” should be read—the city in which those now listed suffered—and among them counted one person named [Col. 0444D] “Palatinus,” whereas the writer of the Martyrology intended by that word to inform us that there was one Euterius, ἐκ τῶν ἐν βασιλικαῖς οἰκετίαις, “from those in the imperial household,” to speak with Eusebius, Ecclesiastical History, book VIII, chapter 1. The same error occurs in various places: on the sixth day before the Kalends of March, [Col. 0445D] mention is made of Peter Palatinus, and on the sixth day before the Ides, of Gurgonius likewise Palatinus. Since Eusebius, in the cited book, chapter 6, counts these among Diocletian’s chamberlains, we may reasonably conjecture that wherever the name Palatinus is [Col. 0446D] read in this Martyrology, one of those who served the emperors in the palace is indicated—whether his name has been preserved, as in the cases of Euterius, Gaius, Maris, and others, or whether oblivion has obscured it.], Euterius, [Col. 0445A] Palatinus, Victorina, Paula, Emerita, Antonina, Dativa, Rogatianus, Antiga, Urbana, Maxima, Marina, Matrona, Peregrina’s daughter, Secundola, Justa, Castula, Florentius, Victoria, Marcellinus, Casta, Donatula, Libosa, and Flavianus the martyr. Likewise Donata, Fortunatus, Lucianus, Amia, Regina, Cyriacus, Valerius, Gurgonius, and Felix.

## 23 February

In Pannonia, Senerotus, Antigonus, Rutulus, Libius, and Rogatianus. In Asia, Polycarp, bishop, with twelve other martyrs. At Smyrna, Saints Eros, Carporus, and Gerontius. In Africa, Grisgonius, Zeno, Minander, Carinianus, Arion, Hippolytus, Diodorus, Menelantus, Athrora, Petrus, Lambesis, Luciana, Felix, and thirty-six others. In Asia, Cosconius, Synorus, Herulus, Zononus, Menalippus, [Col. 0445B] Sinertius, and Syricus with their companions.

## 24 February

The commemoration of Matthias the apostle. At Caesarea in Cappadocia, the commemoration of Saints Herulus and Sergius. At Rome, Absolon at the harbor, and Primitiva. At Nicomedia, Editius, Palphetrus, Lucianus, Felix, Urbanus, Martha, Crescentia, Florentina, Rotagula, and Donatula. Likewise Donatula, Marcellina, Rommodus, Feliciana, Nina, Castus, Jaffer, Tullianus, Julianus, Julia, Innula, Gaius, Exuppius, Dacianus, Flavianus, Januarius, Securus, Diddus, Sellaris, Subitana, Gemelliana, Fortunata, Peregrina, Victuricus, Maxentius, Gegolius, and Julia. Likewise Lucianus, Honorius, Flavianus, Felix, Saturus, Felicissimus, Victor, Maria, Januaria, Rufinianus, Fortunatus, Aurelius, Rutilus, and Faustinus. At Nicomedia, the commemoration of the holy martyrs Oceanus the presbyter, Peter [Col. 0445C] Palatinus, and Aevitius. In Egypt, the commemoration of Saints Victorinus, Victor, Ninivita, Nicophorus, Claudianus, and Dioscorus, Sarapion.

## 25 February

In Africa, the commemoration of Saints Donatus, Justus, Rutilus, Hereneus, Pision, Aurelius, Primosus, Ingenua, and forty-five others. And elsewhere, Ingona, Fortunata, Pussinna, and Hereneus. Likewise Justus, Crescentius, Rogatus, Anianus, Januaria, and Luciosa. Likewise Fortunatus and Victorinus. In Pamphylia, the commemoration of Saints Nestor and Casta, Claudianus.

## 26 February

The commemoration of Saints Alexander, Nestor, Theon, Epion, Justus, Donatus, Ampliatus, Ingenuus, Epion, Antius, Fortunatus, and twenty-seven others. At Alexandria, Felix with his companions.

## 27 February

At Thessalonica, the commemoration of Saints [Col. 0445D] Alexander, Antigonus, Abundantius, Titianus, Magarus, Severianus, Gaianus, Fortunio, Januarius, Luciosa, and Rutulus. In Africa, Dionysius and thirty-four others. In the city of Smyrna in Asia, the commemoration of Saints Servilianus, Datianus, Leander, and Menelampus.

## 28 February

The commemoration of Saints Celer, Pupillus, Gaius, Serapion, Justus Opotus, Claudianus, Theophilus, Victurinus, Saturninus, Eutychia, Astuta, Mustila, Alexander, Victorinus, Secundilla, Nicophorus, Diodorus, Papias, Macaria, Felix, Eunuculus, Januarius, [Col. 0446A] Quintianus, Mansuetus, Hermes, Gittaeus, Donatus, Servilia, Veneria, and Basilla. Likewise Servilia. Likewise Veneria, Januaria, Stercula, Silvanus, Manirra, Rufina, and Leander.

# March

The month has 31 days.

## 1 March

The commemoration of Saints Leo, Donatus, Abundantius, Adrastus, Carisius, Nicophorus, Donatella, and nine other martyrs. In Africa, Adrianus, Victorinus, Secundilla, Massilia, Hermes, Gittaeus, Felix, Eunuculus, and Januarius with thirty-four others. In the city of Angers, the deposition of Saint Albinus, bishop and confessor.

## 2 March

Jorgius, Hercules, Absolom, Areneus, Lucius, Primitivus, Secundula, Januaria, and Luciosa.

## 3 March

Felix, Luciola, Julius, Fortunatus, Martianus, Martia, Hierotes, Antigonus, Januarius, Tutella, Gabianus, Quirinus, Julius, and Marinus. Likewise Felix, Florianus, Donatus, Fortunatus, Helbianus, Gagius, Paula, Gajosa, Gallosa, Galla, and Lupicinus. In Africa, Gajola, Felix; the deposition of the remaining ones. Eremita, Cellidonius. Likewise Felix, Savinianus, and Galegorius. Likewise Emeritus. Likewise Felix. Likewise Ecaeledonius. Likewise Julius, Felix, Marinus, Donata, Nicephorus, Charissimus, Claudianus, Papias, Luciola, Sabiniana, Junola, Asterius, Phocius, Georgius, Isicius, Sisinnius, Castus, Basilisolus, Artilas, Antonius, Cyricus, Eutychius, Gorgonius, Asclepius, Frunimius, and Zosimus.

## 4 March

The commemoration of nine hundred martyrs. At Rome, the deposition of Julius, bishop. Rotius and thirty-nine others; Archelaus and Gaius. Palatinus, drowned at sea; Asterius, Uranius, Sisinnius, Paulus, and Philippus. Herifelius, Basilius, Tepicerius, Gregorius, Euricus, Victorinus, Marius, Honorius, Asclepianus, Sisinnius, Felix, Lucius, Gajosa, and Fortunatus. Likewise Lucius, Pelvianus, Rusticus, Flurianus, Donatus, and Helarianus. Likewise Fortunatus. Likewise Gaius, Pylicus, Autonius, Fronimus, Asclepiades, Fortunio, Castus, Fortius, and nineteen others. At Nicomedia, the martyrdom of Saints Adrianus with thirty-three others.

## 5 March

In Africa, Adrianus, Ebolus, Eusebius, Julianus, and Octavius. At Antioch, the martyrdom of Saint Phoca, Rusticus, Herebus, Maris Palatinus, and nine other martyrs. At Antioch, Victor, Adrianus of Pamphylia, Palatus, and Martius. At Antioch, Saturninus, Justus, Lucosa, Siria, [Col. 0446D] Saturninus, Martinus, Petrus, and Cariathon. Likewise Saturninus, Martius, and twelve other martyrs, and Barbalabia.

## 6 March

At Nicomedia, Victor, Victorinus, and Neocepolius, Papias, Alexander, Diodorus, Claudianus, and Carisius. Likewise Claudianus, Mercurius, Perpetua, Felicitas, Jucundus, and Saturus. At Nicomedia, Saturninus, Cassius, and Victor with two other martyrs, Papias, and Nicophorus. In Italy, Filagonia, Victorinus, Hianulus, Silvanus, and Fermia. Likewise Saturus, Saturninus, Revocatus, [Col. 0447A] Planfagonius. In Italy, Petronius, Diodorus, Niger, Caristus, Donatus, and Vibianus.

## 7 March

In Africa, Saturus, Revocatus, Jucundus, Victorinus, Saturninus, Servanus, Rogatus, and Crocus. At Antioch, Leucius, Saturus, Taxis, Nestor, Equinus, Saturninus, Revocatus, Secundilus, Italicus, and Jucundus. In Mauretania, in the city of the Turbitani, the martyrdom of Saints Perpetua and Felicitas. In Thrace, Danda; Leununcula, Secundus, Nestor, Artaxas, and Quintus. Likewise Secundus, Serri, and Occatus. Likewise Danda. In Africa, Saurus, Silvanus, Rogatus, and Manilius.

## 8 March

At Nicomedia, Quintilius, bishop, and Capitulinus. In Africa, Rogatianus and Felix. Likewise Rogatus, Beroma, Erema, Felicitas, Urbanus, Cyril, bishop, Silvanus, and Manilius, Datius.

## 9 March

In Armenia, Sebastianus and forty soldiers, Julianus, Isicius, and Cyril. In Africa, Felix, Philippus, Cede, Cedis, Cendeus, Marianus, Rogatus, Concessus, and Juvencula.

## 10 March

At Nicaea, Gorgonius Palatinus and Firmus. At Antioch, Agatha, virgin and martyr, Marianus of Smyrna, and Phion. In Persia, forty-seven martyrs. At Nicomedia, Palatinus, Rusticus, and Pion. At Alexandria, Heraclius, Zosimus, Alexander, and Gaio.

## 11 March

At Carthage, Heraclius, Zosimus, Alexander, Philomus, bishop, Candidus, Valerius, Quirillus, Petronius, Gaius, Martianus, Isicius, Piperion, and fifteen others, Rogatus and Cendeus. At Nicomedia, Eunuculus, Euchius, Gorgonius, Firmus, Paulus, and Fortunatus.

## 12 March

At Nicomedia, Egdo, presbyter, and seven other men suffocated. At Alexandria, Zeno, bishop, Alexander the deacon, Dunus, Neon the deacon, and Julius. In Africa, John and forty-four others. And at Albua, Salvianus, Andus, and Minandus. At Rome, the deposition of Saint Innocentius, Rasius, bishop, and Julianus. At Nicomedia, Migdonus and Eutychius. Likewise Migdonus, Maximus, Domna the virgin, Ruginus, Marius, Petrus, and Smaragdus. And Vingelosinus, Hilarius, Maria, Ner. [lacuna] Auginus, Dorotheus, Gorgonius, Matulus. At Alexandria, Orion the deacon and Gaius. In Asia, Carpus, Petronius, bishop, Firmus, Paulus, Agatho, Macedonius, Pacritia, Modestus the presbyter, Domitianus the presbyter, Zosimus the presbyter, Eustasius the presbyter, Basilissa his wife, Felicio, [Col. 0447D] Juvinianus, Hilarius, and Concessus. At Smyrna, Pion and Metrodus. At Rome, the deposition of Saint Gregory, pope of blessed memory.

## 13 March

At Nicomedia, Macedonius the presbyter, Matricia his wife, and Modestia, daughter of Cion the presbyter; Saturninus, Januarius, Salvius, Petronius, Modestinus, Zosimus, Eustasius the presbyter, and Basilissa his wife; Epipodius the deacon with two others. Geratilacus, Carpistus, Galata, Domitianus, Hieromeus, Lucetella, Zeddo the presbyter, and Patricia his wife; Patyfrigia. Likewise Basilissa, Claonus, and Minervinus. In the city of Nicaea, Teusete and Horis, her sons, Theodorus, Nympodora, Marcus, and Araba: all these were burned by fire. Julius, bishop, Alexander, Pion, Maria with two others, Dionysius, Trabia, Quarta, Misetheus, Nymphadoba, Ariaba, Poenus, Parta, Victoria, and Victorinus. In the city of Thessalonica, Alexander and Dionysius. At Nicomedia, Euphrasia, Domitianus, Macedonius, Patricia, Lucius, and Duonius. Likewise Domitianus, Scalerva, Pacta, Pion, Fronimus, and Callidus. Likewise Dionysius, Severinus, Petronius the boy, Salvianus, Julianus, and Felix; Hilarius, Concessus, and Martialis.

## 14 March

Euphrosius, Frunimius, and Fortunio. At Nicomedia, Felicissimus, Dativa, Frontinus, and Jucundus. In Africa, Dione, Alexander, Peter, Mammerus, and Naborus, martyrs; Fronto and Maria. At Thessalonica, Euphrasius, Alexander, Frunimius, and Basilius. At Antioch of Nicomedia, Pion.

## 15 March

In Cappadocia, Saint Longinus the martyr. [Col. 0448B] In Cappadocia, Lucius, bishop and martyr. Fausta, Silvius, Ingenua, Januarius; at Carthage, Paulus and Solutor; and Saint James the apostle, brother of the Lord; Alexander, Theophilus, Theodulus, Petronius, and Manilius. At Jerusalem, James the apostle and Luke the evangelist. Ratoldus, abbot of blessed memory, died.

## 16 March

At Aquileia, Hilarius, Tasianus, Datianus, and Julianus the martyr. At Nicomedia, Castorius, Dionysius, Nonnus, Serenus, Cyriacus, Milisa, Eugenia, Julianus, Asclepiodotus, and Pion. In Greece, Cyriaca, Panpinus, and Cassianus. The feast of Saint Gertrude.

## 17 March

At Nicomedia, Dionysius, Januarius, Nonna, Cyriaca, Victorina, Maria, Basil. [lacuna] At Aquileia, Largus, Hilarius, Titianus, Cato, Dativus, and Jucundus. At Rome, Alexander, bishop, and Theodulus, deacon. [Col. 0448C] The deposition of Patricius, bishop and confessor.

## 18 March

At Alexandria, Collegius the deacon, Collotus the deacon, Pampotus, Mineptus, Rogatianus, Quartus, Saturus, Quintasius, Marinus, Jemsolus, Martius, Rogatus, Samphronius, Aurelius, Capelledus, Dionysius, Januarius, Victor, Vogonuptus, and Samphorus with nine other martyrs; Maria with her companions. At Nicomedia, Aprilis and Servulus. In Campania, Quintus, Rogatus, Ingenua, Quartilla, Rogata, Lucianus, Aurelius, Saturninus, Victor, and Maurus. In Mauretania, Currentius, Timotheus, and Salda, Felicianus, and Jucundus.

## 19 March

At Caesarea in Cappadocia, Theodulus the presbyter. In Africa, Lucellus, Bassus, Fiscianus, Pomenus, Josephus, Apollonius, Ammonius, Saturninus, Basilia, and nine others; Theodorus, bishop, Gaius, Gadulinus, [Col. 0448D] and the deposition of Saint Leontius, bishop; Sorentius, Quintus, Quintillus, Quartilla, and Marcus with nine others; Florentius and Vonoctus.

## 20 March

At Antioch, Saint Josephus and Luke. In Syria, Paulus, Cyril, Eugenius, Serapion, Tigrinus, Claudius, Exuperius, Victorinus, Victuricus, and Domnus.

## 21 March

At Alexandria, Serapion the monk, Josephus, Volotianus, Philocalus, Cotianus, Honus, Nonnus, Lucius, Ammonius, Philocarpus, and Amator. And the deposition of Blessed Benedict, abbot.

## 22 March

In the city of Narbonne, the feast of Saint Paul the confessor. In Africa, Saturninus and nine others. At Sebaste, Deeronius, Orion, and Ammonius.

## 23 March

In Africa, the feast of Saint Fidelis. At Antioch, [Col. 0449A] Theodorus the presbyter. In Provence, Carmilla, Paulus, Caesaria, Julianus, and Julius. In the city of Caesarea, Agathius and Alexander. Likewise Fidelis, Tyomolus, and Dionysius. Likewise Dionysius and Rusticus.

## 24 March

In Syria, Seleucus. In Africa, Agapitus, Molaius, Romulus, Phison, Alexander, and Diophus. In Africa, Rogatus, Catula, Uta, Victorinus, and Saturninus. Likewise Saturninus, Salutaris, Aprilis, and Josephus.

## 25 March

At Jerusalem, our Lord Jesus Christ was crucified. And the Annunciation of Saint Mary by the angel. And the martyrdom of Saint James the apostle, who is also the Lord’s brother, as it is contained in the Acts of the Apostles. At Nicomedia, the feast of Dula, Victorinus, Alexander, Euphrasius, Castula, Nicostratus, Lucella, and four hundred martyrs; of Saint Theodula; and the deposition of [Col. 0449B] Juvinus the Burgundian.

## 26 March

At Rome, in the cemetery on the Lavican Way, the feast of Saint Castula and Syrmia. At Sirmium, Munatius the presbyter, Maxima his wife, and Jucundus. In the city of Sebaste, Peter, bishop, and Paulinus. In Thrace, Sarmatinius. At Heraclea, Martianus, bishop. At Celer [lacuna], the feast of Saint Cassianus, bishop. At Antioch, Timotheus, Diogenes, Madiaria, Maxima, Theodorus the bishop, Hyrinus the deacon, Serapion, Ammon the lector, and Julianus. In Africa, Pictor, Saturninus, Salutaris, and fourteen others.

## 27 March

At Jerusalem, the Resurrection of our Lord Jesus Christ. In Africa, Romulus, Acutus, Marobius, Pinnarius, Successus, Misia, Matutina, Donatus, and Saturninus.

## 28 March

At Caesarea, Rogatus, Alexander, Dorotheus, Audacta, and Modestus. At Tarsus in Cilicia, Castorius and Menelampus. At Chalon, the deposition of King Gundibrammus.

## 29 March

At Nicomedia, Pastor, Victorinus, Saturninus, and Juliana, with four other martyrs. At Antioch, Theodorus the presbyter, Poentalis, Julianus, and Achacius.

## 30 March

In the city of Thessalonica, Domninus; at Philippopolis, Acacius Palatinus; and elsewhere, Victor, Marcellinus, Satullus, Crusus, Agathonia, Aquila the virgin, Saturninus, and Eulalia the virgin. At Philippopolis, Dativus and Pastor. In Africa, Anesius, Felix, Protida, Cornelia, and Valeria [lacuna].

# April

The month has 30 days. A litany is to be proclaimed.

## 1 April

In Armenia, the feast of Saints Fortunatus, Quintianus, Victor, and Secundus. In the city of Heraclea, likewise Victor, Chionia, Agape, Hereneus, and Castus. At Thessalonica, the feast of Saints Ingenua, Saturninus, Patrinus, Dionysius, Panterus, and Alexander. In Egypt, the martyrdom of Saints Victor and Stephanus [lacuna]. At the monastery of Iganau, the deposition of Blessed Walaricus the confessor.

## 2 April

In Africa, Saints Amphianus, Victor, and four other martyrs. And elsewhere, Marcellus, Satullus, Marcellinus, Saturninus, Cyriacus, Regina, Proculus, and fourteen others. At Thessalonica in Macedonia, Theodulus, Agathopus, Martius, Publius, and Valerius with three others; Urbanus, Julianus, Proculus, Gaius, [Col. 0450A] Agapitus, Dionysius, and others; Gordionius, Magnus, Julius, and Donatus. At Lyon in Gaul, the deposition of Saint Nicetius; and at the monastery of Luxeuil, the deposition of Eustasius, abbot.

## 3 April

In Sicily, the commemoration of Saints Thomas, Evagrius, Benigna, Christus, Aristus, Sinnidia, Rufus, Patricius, and Zosimus. At Tauromenium in Sicily, the commemoration of Saint Prancatus. In Moesia, Agathaemeritus of the ancient ones. At Caesarea in Palestine, the commemoration of Theodosia the virgin. At Nicomedia, Donatus and the martyrdom of Amphianus. In the city of Eumis, Evagrius and Benignus.

## 4 April

At Thessalonica, the commemoration of Saints Agatho the deacon and Theodulus. And elsewhere, Paulus and Matutinus. At Milan, Urbanus, Saturninus, Quintilianus, Publius, Ingenius, Victor, Successus, Julianus, and two others; Palatinus and Julius. At Milan, the deposition of Blessed Ambrose, [Col. 0450B] bishop and confessor.

## 5 April

At Nicomedia, the commemoration of Saint Claudianus. In Egypt, the commemoration of Saints Martiana, Nicanor, and Apollonius. At Alexandria, the commemoration of Didymus the presbyter. And elsewhere, Quintus, Pancratius, and Successus. In Sicily, the commemoration of Saint Honorius the Great. At Thessalonica, the commemoration of the holy virgins Chionia, Irene, and Agape. At Caesarea, Licia, and the commemoration of Saint Amphianus. In Cilicia, the commemoration of Saints Tarachus, Andronicus, and Probus. And elsewhere, Arulfus, bishop and confessor.

## 6 April

At Nicomedia, Firmus, Heneus the bishop, Himnarius, Salutaris, Cyriacus, Moses, Romanus, Donatus, Sixtus, Victor, Gagius, and Saturus. And at Sirmium, Rufina, Moderata, Romana, Secundus with seven others. [Col. 0450C] Florentinus, Geminianus, and Saturus. In Africa, the commemoration of Saints Epiphanius, bishop, Donatus, Sixtus, Rufinus, Modesta, and eleven others. In Macedonia, Timotheus and Diogenes. At Alexandria, the commemoration of Clausius the presbyter. At Pentapolis, Timotheus, Macaria, Martia, and Maxima. In Upper Libya, the commemoration of Superia, Theodorus the bishop, Hereneus the deacon, Serapion, Ammon the lector, Summista, Apricius, and Victor. And elsewhere, the commemoration of Saint Marina, and of Tegulianus and Urbanus.

## 7 April

At Antioch in Syria, the commemoration of Saints Timotheus, Diogenes, Macharia, and Maxima. And elsewhere, Leusius the presbyter. In Upper Libya, Coprica and Victor and Donatus. At Alexandria, the commemoration of Pelusius the presbyter.

## 8 April

In Africa, the commemoration of Saints Timorus, Moecharus, Conexus, and Maximus. And elsewhere, Concessus, Salutaris, Pinnarius, Ammonius, Successus, and Donata.

## 9 April

At Sirmium, the commemoration of four virgins, whose names God knows. And elsewhere, Demetrius the deacon, Hilarius, Concessus, and Marius. At Sirmium, Fortunatus, Donatus, and six others. And the commemoration of seven canonical virgins. At Ravenna, the dedication of the oratory of Saint Polictus.

## 10 April

At Alexandria, Apollonius the presbyter, Gaianus, Hilarius, Donatus, Concessus, Saturninus, and Saturus. In Thrace, the commemoration of Gaianus. In Africa, seventeen martyrs, whose names God knows. And elsewhere, Pinnatus, Successus, and Marcellus. At Antioch, the commemoration of Saint Theodorus the presbyter.

## 11 April

In Mauretania, the commemoration of Salonius, [Col. 0451A] Maximus, Hilarius, and Concessus with the other saints, and of Domninus, bishop. At Salona in Dalmatia, Domnio, bishop, nine soldiers, and Dalmata. In Africa, Fortunatus, Donatus, and 240 others. At Nicomedia, the commemoration of Saints Eustasius the presbyter, Nestor, Philo, and Caeremonia. At Lyon in Gaul, the deposition of Siagrius and Patricius.

## 12 April

In Asia, at Pergamum, the commemoration of Saints Carpus, bishop, Paulus, Isaac, and Agatho. At Rome, in the cemetery of Calepodius, Lupicinus. On the Aurelia Way, at the third milestone, the deposition of Julius, bishop. And elsewhere, Agapitus, Bassus, Julianus, Felix, Paulus, Maurus, Hercula, Verecunda, and forty-two others; Quartus, Saturninus, Secundus, Decimus, and Darius. Likewise Secundus. Likewise Saturninus, Quintus, Dexter, Victor, [Col. 0451B] Donatus, Varicus, Butto, Venustus, and Titianus. Likewise Victor, Sytilla, Lucius, Justus, and Orbana. Likewise Orbana, Martius, Januarius, Cittinus, Paternus, Pacinus, Puttus, Muricus, and Optatus.
