In the city of Tomis: the anniversary of Saints Stratorius, Valerius, Merobus, Gordianus, and Nicomedes, martyr. At [Col. 0475D] Nicomedia: the anniversary of Saints Areius and Archeus. At Nuceria in Campania: the anniversary of Saint Constantius. At Ancyra: the burial of Paul, bishop. In the territory of Chalon, at the fortress of Ternocius: the anniversary of Saint Valerian, martyr. At Lyon in Gaul: the burial of Albinus, bishop. The anniversary of Saint Aicadrus, abbot.

### 16th day before the Kalends of October

At Chalcedon: the anniversary of Saint Euphemia, virgin. At Rome: the anniversary of Saints Victor, Felix, Alexander, Papias, and Magnus. On the Nomentan Way, at Cap. [Col. 0476A] in the cemetery of Martha: the anniversary of Saint Emerentiana. Also the anniversary of Saints Paphies, Felix, Victor, Speratus, Navinus, Chorintus, Secunda, Donatus, and Generosa. Likewise Secunda and Lupatus. At Nuceria: Priscianus and Maximus. At Rome: the passion of Saint Cecilia, virgin, and of Salutius and Thyrsus.

### 15th day before the Kalends of October

At Nevedunum: the anniversary of Saints Valerian, Magrinus, and Gordianus. At Nuceria: the anniversary of Saints Constantius and Sanctinus. At Chalcedon in Bithynia: the anniversary of Saints Euphemia and Saleusius. At Suiportus: the burial of Paul, bishop, and of Macrobius, Gaudianus, and Isicius, martyrs. In Gaul, in a village called Leodius: the passion of Saint Landebertus, bishop and martyr.

### 14th day before the Kalends of October

At Alexandria: the anniversary of Saint Trophimus. At Nicomedia: the anniversary of Saints Oceanus, Sixtus, and Medacus. At Milan: the burial of Saint Eustorgius, [Col. 0476B] bishop, and Satyrus.

### 13th day before the Kalends of October

At Alexandria: the anniversary of Saints Demetrius, Paleus, Nilipacius, Madelius, Castor, Saturninus, Caetus, bishop, Castus, and Julius. At Naples: the anniversary of Saints Januarius and Anicetus. At Synnada in Phrygia: the anniversary of Saint Trophius. In the city of Vienne: the anniversary of Saint Ferreolus, the dedication of his basilica, and the translation of many bodies, with the head of Saint Julian, martyr of Brioude, placed beneath the altar. In the city of Trier: the burial of Militius, bishop. Elsewhere: the anniversary of Saints Trogus, bishop, and Pius, deacon, and of Capileus, Nilus, Paternus, and Muscus, with one hundred and fifty others. In the territory of Bourges, in the village of Vellaunum: the anniversary of Saint Marianus. At Nuceria: Hermeus, Blessed, bishop, Felix, Constantia, Privatus, Euphemia, and Sygona. In the territory of Langres, in the monastery of Segestro: Saint Sigo, [Note: [Col. 0475D] Saint Sigo. Acherius observes that it ought to be read “Saint Sequanus,” but this does not please me. For since it could have arisen from the vernacular “Saint Seine,” it seems to me that ignorant writers—of whom the Middle Ages produced very many—may have imagined that some saint was venerated in that monastery who [Col. 0476D] had given his name to the river Sequana. In my view, the name Sigo must altogether be retained. And all the more because it is written no differently in the Martyrologies of Gellone and Saint Gall.] priest and confessor.

### 12th day before the Kalends of October

At Synnada in Phrygia: the anniversary of Saints Dormido, Dorotheus, Privatus, Felix, and Constantia. Likewise Felix. At Nuceria: the anniversary of Saints Felix and Constantia, who suffered under Nero.

### 11th day before the Kalends of October

In Persia, in the city of Tarrium: the anniversary of Saint Matthew, evangelist. In the city of Piralis: the anniversary of Saint Luke, evangelist. At Milan: the anniversary of Saint Victor. In the monastery of Corbie: the dedication of the basilica of Saints Albinus and Marcellinus, bishops.

### 10th day before the Kalends of October

At Rome, on the old Salarian Way, in its cemetery: the anniversary of Saint Basilla. In the city of Sidon, at a place called Agaunum: the anniversary of Saints Mauritius, Exuperius, Candidus, Victor, Innocent, [Col. 0476D] and Vitalis, with six thousand five hundred and eighty-five companions, [lacuna]. At Auxerre: the arrival and reception from Italy of the body of Saint Germanus, bishop and confessor.

### 9th day before the Kalends of October

At Seleucia: the anniversary of Saint Thecla, martyr. At Alexandria: the anniversary of Saint Mark, evangelist. At Rome: the burial of Saint Liberius, bishop.

### 8th day before the Kalends of October

At the fortress of Machironta: the Conception of Saint John the Baptist. Elsewhere: the anniversary of Saints Julius, [Col. 0477A] Christopher, Laurence, Martial, Victor, Gargilius, Mark, Nobilis, Victoria, Secundola, Faustina, Valeria, Celerina, and Donatula. In the city of Autun, at the village of Sedelocus: the anniversary of Saints Andochius, Thyrsus, Aprilis, and Felix, martyrs, and Lucrosa. At Lyon: the burial of Saint Lupus, bishop and confessor. At Clermont: the burial of Saint Rusticus, bishop.

### 7th day before the Kalends of October

In Asia: the anniversary of Saints Eucarpus and Bardas, with twenty others. In Gaul, in the city of Amiens: the passion of Saint Firminus, bishop and martyr. Elsewhere: the burial of Saint Mark.

### 6th day before the Kalends of October

At Rome, on the Appian Way, in the cemetery of Callistus: the burial of Saint Eusebius, bishop and confessor. At Albano: the anniversary of Saint Senator. Elsewhere: the anniversary of Saint Migignus, Nabor, and Faustinus. In Sardinia: the anniversary of Saint Luxurius, martyr. At Clermont: the burial of Apollinaris, bishop and confessor.

### 5th day before the Kalends of October

At Caesarea in Cappadocia: the anniversary of Saint Eleutherius. At Tarsus in Cilicia: the anniversary of Saints Taracus, Probus, and Andronicus, and Justinus. In the city of Aducia: the anniversary of Saints Cosmas and Damian, martyrs. At Ephesus: the anniversary of Saint Timothy, disciple of the Apostle Paul. In the territory of the city of Autun: Saints Florentinus, Silvanus, and Firmus.

### 4th day before the Kalends of October

In Africa: the anniversary of Saints Laurence and Faustinus, and of Victoria, Candida, Valeria, Donata, Leva, Fuciosa, Gagilus, Placidus, and many others, and of Longinus, Victoria, and Priscinianus. At Rome: the anniversary of Saint Stacteus. In the city of Genoa: the burial of Salonius, bishop and confessor. At Auxerre: the burial of Saint [Col. 0477C] Alodius, bishop and confessor.

### 3rd day before the Kalends of October

In Thrace: Euricus, Plautus, Plancitus, Ambutus, Araclia, Thracia, and Donata; at Rome, sixty-eight soldiers. The dedication of the basilica of the Archangel Michael on the mountain called Garganus. Elsewhere: Januarius, Sosius, Ampunus, Celedonius, and Justinus. At Auxerre: the burial of Fraternus, bishop and confessor.

### The day before the Kalends of October

In the city of Piacenza: the anniversary of Saint Antoninus, martyr. At Milan: the translation of the body of Saint Victor, martyr. In the city of Bethlehem: the burial of Saint Jerome, priest.

## The Month of October

It has thirty-one days.

### Kalends of October

A litany is to be proclaimed. Priscus and Faustinus, martyrs; [Col. 0477D] Alexander, Eopropus, Saturninus, Spes, Primus, and Donatus. Likewise Digna, Paphicus, and Prepus. At Tomis: Julius. At Auxerre: the burial of Germanus, bishop. At Reims: Saint Remigius. At Trier: Saint Nicetius.

### 6th day before the Nones of October

At Nicomedia: Eleutherius. At Antioch: Primus, Quirillus, and Pitinus. At Rome: the anniversary of Saint Eusebius; elsewhere, of Leo, Gaianus, and Secundus. Likewise Secundus and Plato. Longinus. In Gaul: the passion of Saint Leodegarius, bishop and martyr.

### 5th day before the Nones of October

At Antioch: Theogenes. In Africa: Victor, Urbanus, and Sapargus. Elsewhere: Felix, Amponus, and Castus.

### [Col. 0478A] 4th day before the Nones of October

In Egypt: Mark and Martianus, martyrs. In Africa: Marcisius, Restitutus, and Julius. Elsewhere: Saint Dasius; and elsewhere, Marcellus, bishop. At Auxerre: the burial of Saint Marsus, priest and confessor.

### 3rd day before the Nones of October

In Sicily: Placidus, Eutychus, and thirty others. Elsewhere: Baricus, Victorinus, Faustus, and Pelagius. In the city of Valencia: the burial of Apollinaris, bishop and confessor. At Auxerre: the burial of the holy siblings Firmatus, deacon, and Flaviana, virgin consecrated to God.

### The day before the Nones of October

At Capua: the anniversary of Saints Marcellus, Castus, Emilius, Saturninus, and Donatellus. At Rome: Balbina, and the burial of Saint Mark, bishop, and Julianus. In Africa: Rogatus, Saturninus, Januarius, Faustinus, and Martialis. In Apulia: Castus, Emilius, Saturninus, and Ammonius, [Col. 0478B] priest. In the city of Agen: the anniversary of Saint Faith, virgin and martyr. In the city of Auxerre: the burial of Saint Romanus, bishop.

### 9th day before the Ides of October

At Rome, on the Appian Way: the burial of the holy martyrs Apuleius and Marcellus, bishop, and of Mark, bishop and confessor. At Capua in Campania: Quartus and Marcellinus. Elsewhere: Saint Julia, Syrgius, and Bacchus, and the anniversary of Saint Matthew, evangelist. In the city of Bourges: Saint Augustine, priest and confessor.

### 8th day before the Ides of October

At Antioch: Dionysius, bishop, Januarius, Faustinus, martyrs, Martial, Privatus, Heraclius, Julianus, and Pelagia.

### 7th day before the Ides of October

In the city of Laodicea in Phrygia: the anniversary of Saint Theodulus. Elsewhere: Atticus, Luddulus, Septimus, and Julius. [Col. 0478C] In the city of Cologne: the anniversary of three hundred and seventeen holy martyrs. In the province of Crete, in the city of Augusta: the anniversary of Saint Afra, martyr. In the city of Vienne: the anniversary of many martyrs. At Paris: the anniversary of Saints Dionysius, bishop, Rusticus, priest, and Eleutherius, deacon. In the monastery of Centula: the translation of the body of Richarius, confessor. At Rome: Marcellus, Genuinus, Novius, and Justus. At the Two Laurels: Saint Primiva, Custus, and Julius. In Cilicia: Taracus, Probus, and Andronicus. In the monastery of Centula: the burial of the body of Blessed Richarius, confessor. In the monastery of Corbie: the burial of Theofridus, abbot.

### 6th day before the Ides of October

In Africa: Heraclius, Dionysius, Septima, Secunda, and Salsa. Elsewhere: Caius, Quintasius, Septimus, Venustus, Beatus, Secundus, Donatus, Serenus, Crescentius, [Col. 0478D] Taracus, Probus, Andronicus, and Nicetius. The anniversary of Firminus, Heraclius, Cassius, Eusebius, Florentius, and Victor. At Cologne: Mallustus, with three hundred and thirty martyrs. On the same day, the anniversary of Saint Cerbonius, confessor, at Populonia.

### 5th day before the Ides of October

At Acerno [Note: [Col. 0477D] At Acerno. It had been printed as *in acervo*.] in Sicily: Saint Athanasius, priest, Ampodius, Placidus, Faustus, Januarius, Martial, Marcellus, and Juvinianus. At Antioch: Saint Heraclius. On the same day: Saint Nicasius and other martyrs.

### 4th day before the Ides of October

In the province of Syria: Saints Evagrius and Prosiria. In Egypt: Eustasius, priest. In Campania: the anniversary of Saints Eucaristus and Fortunatus. [Col. 0479A] At Ravenna, on the Laurentine Way: the anniversary of Saint Edictus. At Rome: Callistus and Saturus. At Bourges: Saint Opio.

### 3rd day before the Ides of October

In Spain, in the city of Córdoba: Faustus and Martia. At Chalcedon: the anniversary of Saint Adrian. Likewise Faustus, Januarius, and Marcellus. At Alexandria: Athanasius, bishop and confessor.

### 2nd day before the Ides of October

At Rome, on the Aurelian Way, in the cemetery of Calepodius: Callistus, bishop, and Saturus. In Cappadocia: Luprampodius, Modestus, Lucianus, Saturninus, Simplicius, Saturus, and Placidus. In the city of Córdoba: Lupus, Aurelia, and Maximus. At Lyon in Gaul: the translation of the body of Saint Justus, bishop and confessor.

### Ides of October

In the city of Cologne: the anniversary of the holy Mauri from among the soldiers. At Capua: Luplilius. On the Aurelian Way, in its cemetery: Saint Fortunata.

### [Col. 0479B] 17th day before the Kalends of November

At Baiae: Saint Suffus, martyr. In Africa: Cecra and two hundred and seventy others who suffered together—Merius, Aufidius, Saturninus, and Nereus.

### 16th day before the Kalends of November

At Nicomedia: Alexander. In Mauretania: Ninus, Victoria, Nobilitanus, Mauritanus, Lucius, Citinus, Crescentianus, Rufianus, Donatus, Defensor, Rusticianus, Servilianus, Sacratus, Veneria, Januarius, Mustula, Quintasius, Memma, Prima, Donata, Severia, Victoria, Basilla, and Magnilius.

### 15th day before the Kalends of November

In the East: the translation of the body of Saint Luke, evangelist. At Nicomedia: Luke, Victurina, and Justinus. At Axiopolis: Hermes and Taxis, and Julius. Near the Roman port: the passion of Saint Agnes, virgin. In the city of Puteoli in Campania: Januarius and Felix, and the burial of Justus, a boy. In Africa: Lucius, Victor, Dasius, [Col. 0479C] Leucius, Victoricus, Beresius, bishop, Victrix, Faustinus, and Martial. In the city of Évreux: the anniversary of Saint Aquilinus, bishop and confessor.

### 14th day before the Kalends of November

At Ostia: Austerius, priest. At Naples: Sussius, Januarius, Festus, and Desiderius. In the cemetery at Puteoli: Proculus, Prosdocus, and Nica, his mother. Domna, virgin, Astius, and Buitus. At Antioch in Syria: the anniversary of Saints Pelagius, Beronicus, Pelagia, and forty-eight other martyrs.

### 13th day before the Kalends of November

In the city of Puteoli: Dasius, Anosinimus, Januarius, Dorotheus, Susimius, and Januaria. At Nicomedia: Eusticus, Promachus, Lucius, Marcellinus, and Berniacus. Likewise Susimius, Januarius, and Julius. In the city of Agen: Saint Caprasius, martyr.

### 12th day before the Kalends of November

At Nicomedia: Dasius, Zoticus, and Gaius, [Col. 0479D] with twelve thousand martyrs. In Africa: Modestus, Eutychus, Materus, and Disseus. At Nicaea in Bithynia: Afrigis, Macharius, Diceus, and Proculus. At Naples: Modestus and eighty-four others. At Puteoli in Campania: Proculus, Eutychus, Macharius, and Donatella. At Lyon in Gaul: Viator, a boy and disciple of Saint Justus, bishop.

### 11th day before the Kalends of November

At Adrianople in Thrace: Philip, bishop. Eusebius, Hermes, and Severus. At the Port: Saint Valerius, martyr. In Thrace: likewise Severus. Elsewhere: the passion of Saint Leugatus.

### 10th day before the Kalends of November

At Adrianople: Severus and Dorotheus. At Caesarea in Cappadocia: Seuresius, Magnus, and Justus. In Gaul: the burial of Saint Gratianus, martyr.

### 9th day before the Kalends of November

At Nicomedia: Severus, Vitalis, Felix, [Col. 0480A] Rogatus, Paperius, Victoria, Flavianus, and Victor. At Hierapolis in Phrygia: Claudianus, Eutherius, Flavinus, Justus, and Victor.

### 8th day before the Kalends of November

At Rome: Maximus and one hundred and twenty other soldiers, whose names God knows. At Javols: the burial of Blessed Hilary, bishop and confessor. In Africa: Saturninus, Claudianus, Primivus, Flavianus, and Zoticus. In Sardinia: Sabinus, Saturus, Asterius, and Chari. In the city of Soissons: the anniversary of Saints Crispinus and Crispinianus, martyrs; Claudianus, Rogatus, Paparius, Felix, and Vitalis. At Saintes: the translation of the body of Saint Vivianus, confessor and bishop.

### 7th day before the Kalends of November

At Nicomedia: Saints Lucianus, Mardianus, Florius, Heraclius, and Tutus.

### 6th day before the Kalends of November

In Africa: Saints Saturninus and Flavius. In Phrygia: Tarsus, Polycarp, Caius, Euminus, Nocomus, Longinus, Diodorus, Metrobius, Eumina, and Tutus. At Rome: Marianus, Lucius, and Vivetus. In Sardinia: Potus, Januarius, Tarreus, Comuina, and Saint Florentius.

### 5th day before the Kalends of November

At Antioch in Syria: Marandus, Mariana, and Arcelludus. At Carthage: Saint Sophronisa. Elsewhere: Saints Simon the Cananaean and Jude the Zealot, apostles. Amarantus, Quintus, Justus, and Lucius.

### 4th day before the Kalends of November

In Lucania: Sacinctus [lacuna], Quintus, Feliciana, and Luciana, martyrs.

### 3rd day before the Kalends of November

At Nicomedia: Januarius, Calendion, Martial, Germanus, Mark, Theophilus, and Eusebius. In Africa: the passion of one hundred and twenty holy martyrs. Likewise Felix, Quintus, Luke, Lucianus, Victor, Vitalis, Donatus, Peter, Marius, Januarius, Firia, [Col. 0480C] Hermes, Urbanus, and Attitus. Also the passion of Saint Felicianus with his companions. At Antioch: Januarius, Martianus, Nazarius, Gervasius, Protasius, and Celsus, a boy. At Toulouse: the translation of the body of Saint Saturninus, bishop and martyr.

### The day before the Kalends of November

In Africa: Clacovius, Julianus, Fortunatus, Silvanus, Calendion, Bonifacia, Casta, [lacuna], Gallica, Agape, Victoria, Felix, Simon, Donatus, Rusticianus, Fortunatus, Romanus, Silvanus, Mimus, Angelaphus, Nuncinus, Felicissimus, and twenty-nine others, Valerius, and Vincentius. In Spain: Januarius. In Macedonia: Vitalis, Peter, Crescentius, Alterinus, and Victorinus. Likewise Peter, Mar[...], Mammarius, Saturninus, Vigilantius, and Nuncinus. Magnilius. At Nicomedia: Philip and Calendion. At Augusta Viromanduorum in Gaul: [Col. 0480D] Saint Quintinus.

## The Month of November

It has thirty days.

### Kalends of November

A litany is to be proclaimed. The feast of All Saints. Peter, Mammertus, Saturninus, and Magnus. Also the passion of Eustachius, martyr, with his wife and children. In Macedonia: Basilus, James, and Saint John, evangelist. At Terracina: the anniversary of Saints Meldegasius, Julianus, Victor, Felix, Satius, Perseverans, Octavia, Cessia, Eristeus, Saturninus, Simplicius, Primus, Caesarius, Magnus, and Justus. At Caesarea: the anniversary of Saint Macedonius. Elsewhere: the anniversary of Saints Januarius, Peter, Crescentius, Victorinus, and other martyrs. At the fortress of Dijon: the passion of Saint Benignus, priest and martyr, [Col. 0481A] and Saint Melantius. At Autun: the burial of Saint Primus, bishop. In the city of Bayeux: Saint Vigorius, bishop and confessor. At the monastery of Sithiu: the burial of Saint Audomarus, bishop and confessor. In the city of Poitiers: the dedication of the basilica of Saint Hilary, bishop and confessor.

### 3rd day before the Nones of November

The dedication of the basilica of Saint Andrew the Apostle. At Caesarea in Cappadocia: the anniversary of Saints Germanus, Theophilus, Caesarius, Egrilus, and Vitalis. Elsewhere: the passion of Saint Agricola, virgin and martyr. Likewise Felix and Crescentius.

### The day before the Nones of November

In Africa: the anniversary of Saints Primus, Caesarius, Gregorius, Porphyrius, Saturus, Amantius, Publius, Secunda, Victorina, Perpetua, Victor, and Quartus. At Nicaea: the anniversary of Saint Domninus. At Autun: the burial of Proculus, bishop. In the city of Rodez: the burial of [Col. 0481B] Saint Amantius, bishop and confessor. At Bourges: the burial of Saint Lusor, a boy and confessor.

### Nones of November

At Caesarea in Cappadocia: the anniversary of Saints Domninus, Caesarius, Epiphanius, Gregorius, Appinus, Saturninus, Amantius, Publius, and Martyr. In Campania: the anniversary of Saints Marcia and Secunda. In the city of Capua: the anniversary of Saints Evrasias, Quartus, Jocus, and Ludus.

### 8th day before the Ides of November

At Nicomedia: the anniversary of Saints Adrian, Julia, and Eusebia. In Africa: the anniversary of Saints Donatus, Paul, Balsamus, Domninus, Prima, Dulia, Fortunata, Januaria, and Quarta. In Toniza, Africa: the anniversary of Saint Felix. In Phrygia: the anniversary of Saints Januarius, Atticus, Baricus, Mammarius, Venericinus, and Veneria. At Regidona: the anniversary of Saint Melanius, [Col. 0481C] bishop and confessor.

### 7th day before the Ides of November

At Nicomedia: the anniversary of Saints Eusebius, Pobisius, Eustasius, Marius, Primus, Julia, Januaria, Rogatiana, Optatus, and Adrian. In Africa: the anniversary of Saints Rogatus, Donatus, Prima, and Julia.

### 6th day before the Ides of November

At Rome: the anniversary of Saints Simplicius, Sympronius, Claudius, Custor, and Nicostratus, and of the Four Crowned Saints: Severus, Severianus, Carpophorus, and Victorinus. In Africa: the anniversary of Saints Primus, Macharius, Justus, Amarantus, and ninety-four others. At Nicomedia: the anniversary of Saints Damian, Eusebius, Callistus, Eustasius, Marius, and Magnus.

### 5th day before the Ides of November

At Nicomedia: the anniversary of Saints Damian, Donatus, Restitutus, Victorinus, Salutaris, Crescentius, Demetrius, Nemesius, Exuorgius, and Eusebius. At Rome: the anniversary of Saints Clement and Symphronius. In Spain: the anniversary of Saints Faustus, Januarius, and Martial, martyrs.

### 4th day before the Ides of November

At Antioch: the anniversary of Saints Primus, Macharius, deacon, Eustasius and his companions, Januarius, and Candidianus. In Africa: the anniversary of Saints Saturninus, Donatus, Annibonia, and seventeen others. At Rome: the burial of Saint Leo, bishop. In the city of Orléans: the burial of Blessed Monotor, bishop and confessor.

### 3rd day before the Ides of November

At Ravenna: the anniversary of Saints Valentinus, Felicianus, Octavius, Felix, Januarius, Eurundinus, Victorinus, Felix, Nisaeus, Julianus, Vincentius, Januarius, Giddinus, Bonifacia, martyr, Minacus, Domnus, Firma, [Col. 0482A] Maria, Felicitas, Felicia, Innocentia, Fortunatus, Principia, Domnicella, Clementinus, Januaria, Victoria, and Julianus. At Alexandria the metropolis: the anniversary of Saint Menas, martyr. In the city of Tours: the burial of Saint Martin, bishop and confessor. At Lyon in Gaul: the burial of Veranus, bishop.

### The day before the Ides of November

In Africa: the anniversary of Saints Aurulus, Publius, and Vincentius. At Caesarea in Cappadocia: the anniversary of Saints Germanus, Theophilus, Caesarius, and Saint Eusebius.

### Ides of November

In Thrace: the anniversary of Saints Aedictus, Eutychius, Felix, Hermogenes, and Agiestus, martyrs. At Caesarea in Cappadocia: the anniversary of Saints Antonius, Gebenna, Germanus, Mannica, and Adrian, with their companions. In the city of Ravenna: the anniversary of Saints Valentinus, [Col. 0482B] Solutor, and Victor. Elsewhere: the burial of Saint James, Apostle. In the city of Rodez: the burial of Saint Amantius, bishop and confessor. In the city of Tours: the burial of Saint Brictius, bishop and confessor.

### 18th day before the Kalends of December

In the city of Heraclea in Thrace: the anniversary of Saints Clement, Clementinus, Theodota, Philomenus, and many others. On the same day: the anniversary of Saint Heraclius.

### 17th day before the Kalends of December

In Africa: Saints Secundus, Fidentianus, Varicus, and Martial. In the city of Africa: the anniversary of Saints Seddinus, Saturninus, Servus, Calendion, Galanus, and Primus. At Genua: Secunda, Theodotus, Demetrius, Parens, Satura, and Firmus. At Antioch: the anniversary of Saints Donatus, Restitutus, Valerian, and Fructuosus, with twelve others. The burial of Saint Machutus, bishop.

### [Col. 0482C] 16th day before the Kalends of December

In Africa: the anniversary of Saints Rufianus, Mark, Valerius, Victor, Paul, Honoratus, Donatus, Baricus, Vitalis, Januarius, and Justus. Elsewhere: the anniversary of Saints Fidentianus, Martial, Donatus, Valerian, and Poetianus. Also the anniversary of Saints Nereus, Paul, Adrian, Secundianus, Martial, Victor, Victorius, Antecon, Aurilianus, Marcellus, Mariana, Secundus, Fronto, Majulinus. At Antioch: Augustinus, Justa, Aurica, Pontia, Fructuosa, Matrona, Fructa, Vincentia, Mark, Aruspex, Maria, Fista, Fortuna, Felicitas, and Silvanus. At Capua: the anniversary of Saints Vitalis, Januarius, Justus, Augustianus, and Justa. At Lyon in Gaul: the burial of Saint Eucherius, bishop and confessor.

### 15th day before the Kalends of December

In the city of Capua: the anniversary of Saints Augustine, Eusurius, and Felicitas. At Nicomedia: the anniversary of Saint Ammon. In Asia: the anniversary of Saints Phileas, Matrona, and Thecla, virgin. In the city of Hierapolis: the anniversary of Saints Victor, Alpheus, and Romula. At Rome, across the Tiber: the anniversary of Saint Caecilius. At Nicomedia: the anniversary of Saint Ammonius. In Asia: Saints Diobides and Didas. In the city of Heraclea: the anniversary of Saints Gregoria, Victor, and Gemmus. At Caesarea: the anniversary of Saints Theodota, Alphaeus, Zacchaeus, and Romanus. At Carthage in Africa: Dubitatus, Tuscus, Valentius, Saint Calendion, and Montanus. In the city of Orléans: the burial of Anianus, bishop and confessor.

In the city of Antioch: the anniversary of Romanus, monk, Baralus, and Hesychius, martyrs. In Spain, in the city of Córdoba: the anniversary of Ascicla, martyr. At Caesarea: Bonulus, Victor, Proximus, Lucianus, Cartherius, and Martianus. At Heraclea: likewise Cartherius and forty others.

At Caesarea: Maximus, Mutianus, Neoserius, Tobias, Januarius, Vitalis, Carterius, Martianus, Dicentius, and Zephorus. At Heraclea: the holy Woman with her forty-six companions. At Autun: Simplicius, bishop.

Lucianus, Martianus, Claudianus, Cyprianus, Martial, Peter, Felix, Vitalis, Julianus, Victor, Januarius, Donatus, and Quiriacus.

At Rome: Saints Siricius, bishop, and Saturninus. At Aquileia: Valerian, bishop and confessor, Ammonius, Serenus, and Romana. At Alexandria: Peter. In Africa: Mona, Melisa, Berina, Victorina, and Marcellinus. At Autun: the burial of Saint Amator, bishop.

### 5th day before the Kalends of December

At Nicomedia: Marcellus, Peter, Numerius, Serenus, Melisa, and Victorinus. In Gaul, in the city of Bologna: Agricola and Vitalis, Magnus, and Julius. At Milan: Luke, Andrew, John, Severus, and Euphemia. In the city of Riez: the burial of Saint Maximus, bishop.

### 4th day before the Kalends of December

In Syria: Trophimus, Theodulus, Expecasius, Eucherius, Eusebius, and Julius.

### 3rd day before the Kalends of December

At Rome: Aroson, Saturninus, Chrysanthus, Daria, Maurus, and seventy-two others. In Gaul, in the city of Toulouse: the anniversary of Saturninus, bishop and martyr.

In the province of Achaea, in the city of Patras: the anniversary of Saint Andrew, apostle and martyr. At Nicomedia: Saints Carion and Tyro. At Antioch: Domnus and Merola. At Milan: Saint Ambrose, bishop, concerning the reception of baptism. At Rome: Saints Castulus, Euprepes, Saturninus, Chrysanthus, Maurus, Centulus, Theodulus, and Januarius.

## The Month of December

It has thirty-one days.

[Col. 0484B]

### Kalends of December

A litany is to be proclaimed. At Rome: Saint Candida, Ambon, Philatus, Lucius, Matrona, and Justinus. In Africa: Victor, Rogatus, Mammarius, Alequata, and Quintasia, and the anniversary of Saint Cassianus, Klenpiminus, Donatus, Saturninus, Fortunatus, Lucianus, and Optatus. In Gaul, in the city of Noyon: Saint Eligius, bishop and confessor.

At Rome: the anniversary of Saints Primitus, Pontianus, Piminus, and Juvenianus. In Mauretania: Severus, Securus, Januarius, Victorinus, Fortunatus, Megginus, Debbuchus, Victurinus, Clemens, Pontianus, Candida, Mammaria, Agnes, Donata, Prima, Victoria, Secunda, Septimia, Maxima, Donata, Saturnina.

In the East: Merobius, Claudicus, and Felix. At Nicomedia: Umbucus. Likewise Felix, Victoricus, and Julius. In Africa: Crispinus, Magna, John, Stephen, Victor, Martin, and Savinianus. At Bologna: Saint Agricola, and Intingus, Cassianus, and Crispinus.

At Heraclea: Christianus, Pudens, Miginus, and Victurus. In the metropolis of Laodicea: Felix, Merobius, Faladus, and Umbunus.

The anniversary of Saint Crispinus. In Africa: Humilis, Felix, Julius, and Patomia. Eusebius, bishop; Usannus, priest; Successus, bishop.

In Africa: Peter, Successus, Basinus, Victor, Toninus, Porphyrius, Urbanus, Januaria, Malanus, and Pascentius. Likewise Urbanus, Januaria, Malanus, and Pascentius. Likewise Urbanus, Bonifatius, and twenty-three others. At Antioch: Gerontius, Polintia, Silvanus, Valentia, Valentina, Maria, Donata, Victoria, [Col. 0485A] Agnilla, Juventia, Rogata, Hermogenes, Felix, Luticianus, and Flavianus.

### 4th day before the Ides of December

Victor, Consentius, Adrian, Heraclius, Erumentius, Pudens, Miginus, Victurianus, Paul, Urbanus, Mark, Cyrenicus, Caecilia, Orbanella, Crispina, Polentia, Privata, Vibianella, Cyriacus, and Julius. At Rome: the burial of Damasus, pope; Germanus, Eludius, Evangelus, Thrason, and Maurus. In the city of Clermont: Agricola and Vitalis, martyrs. In Spain, in the city of Mérida: the passion of Saint Eulalia, virgin.

### 3rd day before the Ides of December

At Rome: Saint Eulalia, Thrason, Pontianus, Capitulinus, and many others without number. At Alexandria: Sammon. At Mérida: Urbanus. In Spain: Eutychianus. At Antioch: Secundianus, Secundus, Zosimus, Paul, Cyriacus, and Justus. In the city of Amiens: the anniversary of Victoricus, Fuscianus, and Gentianus, martyrs. Elsewhere: the anniversary of Saint Mary and many others.

### The day before the Ides of December

Hermogenes, Donata, and twenty-two others.

### Ides of December

In the city of Ravenna: Ursio, Leocadius, confessor, and Valentinus, martyr. In the city of Syracuse in Sicily: the anniversary of Saint Lucy, virgin, and of Saint Sicensis, Saturninus, Castus, Paul, Felix, Quintilianus, Modestus, Victorinus, Januarius, Getdinus, Felicianus, Stercorius, Felicia, Donata, Valeria, Colonia, Saturninus, Urbana, Maritimus, Victoria, Simplicia, Securus, and Dativus.

### 19th day before the Kalends of January

At Antioch: Drusus and his companions, three in number; Zosimus; and Saint Lucy, virgin. At Lyon in Gaul: Saint Victor, bishop and confessor. At Vienne: Lupicinus, bishop. At Reims: the anniversary of Saint Nicasius, bishop, and of Sacrepius, Aspedia, and Theodulus.

### 18th day before the Kalends of January

In Africa: Faustinus, Lucius, Candida, Materus, Mark, Januarius, Victor, Caecilianus, Maximus, Marcia, Machaonia, Victoria, Secunda, Prima, Saturnina, Machrosa, Nina, Restituta, and eleven others. At Ascalon: Helias and Candidus. In the city of Orléans: Maximus, priest and confessor.

### 17th day before the Kalends of January

At Ravenna: Valentinus, Navalis, Agricola, Concordius, and Justinus. At Arles: the dedication of the basilica and altar of Saint Genesius, martyr.

In Africa: Victor, Victorianus, Adiutor, [Col. 0486A] Quartus, Honoratus, Simplicius, Ampamovus, Felix, Vincentius, and thirty-nine others together. Also Octor, Quintus, Donatus, Victoria, Dioscorus, and Justinianus.

### 15th day before the Kalends of January

In the city of Laodicea: Theotinus and Basilianus. In Africa: Quintus, Simplicius, Pompinius, Artifa, Chrestus, Dignus, Datulus, Urbanus, Martyrius, Honoratus, Evasus, Victurinus, Salvator, Terturinus, Victoria, Caecilianus, Septimus, Rusticus, Bessa, Vicinianus, Honoratus, Lucania, Reductula, Victoria, Privata, Caecilia, Saturninus, Phamon, Felix, Vincentius, Arestus, Muscus, Seddinus, and Adiutor. At Rome: Lucia, martyr, and Auceia, queen, together with Antoninus, Ireneus, Papeusa, Apollonia, Apamia, Phoenicia, Cussevarion, Papisseus, Saturius, and Satarius. The passion of Saint Afra, virgin, [Col. 0486B] and of Victurus, Basilianus, Honoratus, with twenty-two other martyrs.

### 14th day before the Kalends of January

In the city of Nicaea in Bithynia: Zosimus, Paul, Secundus, and Cyriacus. Elsewhere: Saints Anastasius and Seddinus, bishops, and Chrysanthus and Daria, martyrs. At Auxerre: Blessed Gregory, pope.

### 13th day before the Kalends of January

In Thrace, in the city of Gildoba: Julius. The anniversary of Thecla and Saint Libertinus, and Zosimus.

### 12th day before the Kalends of January

In Mesopotamia: the anniversary and translation of Saint Thomas, apostle, who was translated from India; his passion is celebrated there. At Heraclea: Saint Passinus. At Rome: the burial of Saint Innocent, and the passion of Saints Phocas, Florius, and Honoratus, bishop and confessor.

### 11th day before the Kalends of January

At Antioch: Saints Basil and Serapion. [Col. 0486C] At Rome, on the Lavican Way, between the Two Laurels: the anniversary of thirty martyrs crowned on one day. At Ostia: the anniversary of Saints Demetrius and Honoratus. Elsewhere: the anniversary of Saints Felix and John. At Rome, on the Salarian Way: the burial of Saint Felix, and the passion of Saint Theodosia, virgin, and Didymus, monk.

### 10th day before the Kalends of January

The burial of Saint Victoria at Rome under Decius. Since she was betrothed to a pagan man, and rel[...].

The rest could not be read in the manuscript because it had been eaten away by moths—namely, from this day to the 8th day before the Kalends of January, from which this Martyrology begins.

[Col. 0485]

## THE BOOK OF THE COMES (C, G)

### NOTICE CONCERNING THE FOLLOWING BOOK
As for the many old scholarly works that claim Jerome as their author under one pretext or another, scarcely any of them demands for itself a place in this little book, entitled the *Comes*, with a more ancient title and a certain right of its own. The most ancient document of all, the Charter of the Donation of the Cornutian Church, mentions it by name: “Likewise,” it says, “four Gospel books, the Apostle, the Psalter, and the *Comes*.” Since this document was written in the year 471, it is clear evidence that the author of the book—whoever he may have been—lived in Jerome’s time.

That it was Jerome himself is expressly asserted by a great many writers of a later age, whose numerous testimonies Pamel­lius cites in the prolegomena to the *Liturgica*. Indeed, that was the commonly accepted opinion, and a belief that no one would call into question: for, on the basis of a preconceived notion, it was generally believed that whatever books in the Church were especially useful and especially suited to the needs of priests had proceeded from the pen of our holy Doctor, or at least had been revised and prepared for us by his care.

A factor by no means slight in commending the work’s authority was the dedicatory letter of Jerome to Constantius, called—so it is described in the ancient Chifflet manuscript—the “Preface of the book entitled *Comes*.” For the holy Father himself wished such prologues to distinguish his writings from those of others, so that works possessing a prologue might be regarded as genuinely his.

We do not, however, value these arguments so highly, nor do we repeat them with the intention of appearing to defend the work’s genuine descent from Jerome. We wish only to establish this much: that such a book has hitherto been unjustly neglected, and that we have done something worthwhile by enrolling it as a servant in the remaining household of the holy Father.

We therefore obtained the letter to Constantius, which all the editions of the *Comes* themselves lacked, from volume XIII of the *Spicilegium* of the blessed Luca Bacherio, who had received it from Chifflet, as we indicated earlier. As for the book itself, to conceal nothing, we long remained uncertain from which copy we should transcribe it. For the form that prevailed in Jerome’s time was subsequently enlarged by successive interpolations and, I think, grew into something almost different in bulk and form.

Long ago it was corrected, at the command of Charlemagne, by Paul the Deacon of Aquileia; then by Alcuin, at the order of the same emperor; and finally by the priest Theotinchus, whose codex is preserved in the library of the Church of Beauvais under this title:

“In Christ’s name, the book of the cycle of the year, the *Comes*, begins, enlarged by Theotinchus, an unworthy priest, at the request of the venerable man Hechiard, count of Amiens; yet in such a way that the holy sayings of the Evangelists, as well as those of the apostles and prophets, might be preserved unchanged and inviolate.”

Thus, even in the printed books, there are three editions of the same work that differ considerably from one another. The first is Pamel­lius’s, in the second volume of the *Liturgies*; the second is Baluze’s, at the end of the capitularies of the Frankish kings; the third is in the ancient books of the Mass belonging to the venerable Cardinal Tommasi. Since an old and genuine archetype is no longer available to us, Baluze’s edition—which was transcribed from the Beauvais codex and from Theotinchus’s recension—seemed preferable to the others because it is fuller.

## In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, the Letter of Saint Jerome to Constantius Begins: Preface to the Following Book, Which Is Called the *Comes*

[Col. 0487]

Although the gathering of heavenly readings may be undertaken with some freedom, and although the work itself is commonly called by ecclesiastical men the *Comes*—a name which, I think, may have arisen in either of two ways, either from the custom of each individual Church (for this very kind of compilation is recognized to be diverse), or certainly from the wish of an eager reader who, if it could be done, desires to possess in a small volume everything that shines wonderfully in the divine Scriptures and everything that is rich in moral instruction, gathered together because of the constraint of poverty—I nevertheless, with Christ’s help, using such ability as I possessed, and especially because the opportunity was offered when you wished me to undertake it, Constantius, my venerable brother, assumed this work, although insufficiently equipped, so that such an understanding of the excerpts might appear to have a reasonable foundation and purpose.

For since, as the Apostle says, all Scripture inspired by God is useful for teaching, for instruction, and for righteousness, so that the man of God may be perfect, equipped for every good work; and since everything that has been written up to now was written for our instruction, so that through the patience and consolation of the Scriptures we might have hope—what could I judge to be shorter or more useful than to select from such a great abundance of divine books, for each festival, whatever was suitable or appropriate, and arrange it in a thoroughly ordered manner?

[Col. 0488A]

Beginning, therefore, with the Nativity of Christ, which falls on the eighth day before the Kalends of January, I supplied simple readings from both Testaments, in order, at Vigils and at None, according to the arrangement that I had continually learned in the Church.

Furthermore, since it is established that the edition translated into Latin from the Hebrew volumes was made in this manner—namely, by determining which reading from each prophecy accords with the festival in question, what the apostles teach, or what authority from the Gospel announces under the same heading—I judged it appropriate, now that the year had already turned, to arrange everything for reading on all the feast days of the Church according to the proper season.

But many other passages were gathered there for the sake of edification and inserted under their appropriate headings: namely, at the beginning of Lent, concerning abstinence from food and sobriety; likewise during Lent, concerning repentance, chastity, the forgiveness of enemies, and many other matters. I took care to write all these things in obedience to your requests, for the benefit of many, my venerable and most beloved brother.

## The Book of the *Comes*, or Lectionary for the Cycle of the Year, Begins

[Col. 0487]

[Col. 0487C]

In Christ’s name. The book of the cycle of the year, the *Comes*, begins, enlarged by Theotinchus, an unworthy priest, at the request of the venerable man Hechiard, count of Amiens; yet in such a way that the holy sayings of the Evangelists, as well as those of the apostles and prophets, should be preserved unchanged and inviolate, and that on the days when proper holy readings were lacking, readings should be supplied as they had been gathered together by the holy Fathers.

If, however, anything seems to anyone to be lacking either on weekdays or on the festivals of the saints, let him turn to whichever week he wishes, and he will always find one, two, or more weekdays beyond the eight, from which he may read, so that nothing will be lacking to him.

(Because of the frequent interruption of the sequence of time, it was necessary in certain letters to add this ω, which signifies the end, and again α, because of the beginning of another letter [Note: [Col. 0487] These words were added in the margin by a more recent but ancient hand].)

[Col. 0489A]

On the Vigil of the Lord’s Nativity, the eighth day before the Kalends of January, at Saint Mary’s, from None, according to the holy Fathers:

Reading from the Letter of the blessed Paul the Apostle to the Romans. “Brothers, Paul, a servant of Christ Jesus,” up to “and you are called to belong to Jesus Christ our Lord.”

Likewise, at the same place. Reading from the prophet Isaiah. “Thus says the Lord: For Zion’s sake I will not be silent,” up to “God has taken pleasure in you.”

The Gospel according to Matthew. “At that time, when the mother of Jesus, Mary, had been betrothed,” up to “he will save his people from their sins.”

Likewise, at Saint Mary’s, during the night:

Reading from the Letter of the blessed Paul the Apostle to Titus. “Beloved, the grace of our Savior God has appeared,” up to “in Christ Jesus our Lord.”

[Col. 0489B]

Likewise, at the same place:

Reading from the prophet Isaiah. “Thus says the Lord: The people of the nations,” up to “forever.”

The Gospel according to Luke, chapter III. “A decree went out from Caesar,” up to “peace to people of good will.”

Likewise, at Saint Anastasia’s, in the morning:

Reading from the Letter of the blessed Paul the Apostle to Titus. “Beloved, the kindness and humanity of God our Savior appeared,” up to “in Christ Jesus our Lord.”

Likewise, at the same place:

Reading from the prophet Isaiah. “Thus says the Lord: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me,” up to “redeemed by the Lord God.”

The Gospel according to Luke, chapter III. “The shepherds were speaking,” up to “it was told to them.”

Likewise, at Saint Peter’s, during the day:

Reading from the Letter of the blessed Paul the Apostle to the Hebrews. “Brothers, in many and various ways,” up to “your years shall not fail.”

Likewise, at the same place:

Reading from the prophet Isaiah. “Thus says the Lord: Therefore my people shall know,” up to “and all the ends of the earth shall see the salvation of our God.”

The beginning of the holy Gospel according to John. “In the beginning was the Word,” up to “and of truth.”

On the Nativity of Saint Stephen, that is, the seventh day before the Kalends of January:

Reading from the Acts of the Apostles. “In those days Stephen, full of grace,” up to “he fell asleep in the Lord.”

The Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CCXL. “Jesus was saying to the crowds of Jews,” up to “blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord.”

On the Nativity of Saint John the Evangelist, that is, the sixth day before the Kalends of January:

Reading from the Book of Wisdom. “Whoever fears God will do good,” up to “our Lord God will make him heir in the eternal name.”

The Gospel according to John, chapter CCXXXI. “Jesus said to Peter, ‘Follow me,’” up to “because his testimony is true.”

On the Nativity of the Holy Innocents, that is, the fifth day before the Kalends of January:

Reading from the Book of the Apocalypse of the Apostle John. “In those days I saw upon Mount Zion a Lamb standing,” up to “before the throne of God.”

The Gospel according to Matthew, chapter VI. “Behold, an angel of the Lord appeared in a dream to Joseph,” up to “he shall be called a Nazarene.”

On the Kalends of January, if they fall on a Sunday, these readings from the book of the *Comes* are to be read:

The Letter of the Apostle Paul to the Galatians. “Brothers, as long as the heir is a child,” up to “an heir through God.”

The Gospel according to Luke, chapter II. “Joseph and Mary, the mother of Jesus, were there,” up to “the grace of God was upon him.”

If it falls on another day, these are to be read:

Reading from the Book of Genesis. “In those days, therefore, the Lord formed man from the dust,” up to “the fourth river is the Euphrates itself.”

The Gospel according to Matthew, chapter XIII. “Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan,” up to “in whom I have been well pleased.”

On the third day before the Kalends of January:

Reading from the Book of Genesis. “In those days the Lord God took the man,” up to “that is his name.”

The Gospel according to Matthew, chapter XVIII. “When Jesus heard that John had been handed over,” up to “for the kingdom of heaven is near.”

On the day before the Kalends of January:

The Nativity of Saint Sylvester.

Reading from the Letter of the blessed Paul the Apostle to the Hebrews. “Brothers, many have become priests according to the law,” up to “our Lord Jesus Christ, by offering himself.”

The Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CCLXIII. “Jesus said to his disciples, ‘Keep watch, because you do not know,’” up to “he will appoint him over all his possessions.”

On the Kalends of January:

The Octave of the Lord. The same reading that is appointed for the Vigil of the Lord during the night is to be read.

The Gospel according to Luke, chapter III. “When the eight days had been completed,” up to “glory to your people Israel.”

On the fourth day before the Nones of January:

Reading from the Book of Genesis. “In those days Adam found no helper like himself,” up to “the eyes of both of them were opened.”

The Gospel according to Matthew, chapter XXIII. “Jesus went about all Galilee,” up to “from beyond the Jordan.”

On the third day before the Nones of January:

The Nativity of Saint Genovefa, virgin.

Reading from the Book of Wisdom. “Beautiful is the chaste generation,” up to “he shall be in refreshment.”

The Gospel according to Matthew, chapter XXXVII. “You have heard that it was said to the ancients, ‘You shall not commit adultery,’” up to “from one who wishes to borrow from you, do not turn away.”

On the day before the Nones of January:

Reading from the prophet Daniel. “In those days Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem and besieged it,” up to “those who ate the king’s food.”

The Gospel according to Matthew, chapter LXVII. “When Jesus had come into the house of Simon Peter,” up to “bury their own dead.”

On the Nones of January:

Reading from the Book of Genesis. “In those days, when they had recognized that they were naked—Adam, that is, and his wife,” up to “you shall return to dust.”

The Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CXXXIII. “Jesus spoke to the crowd and his disciples, saying, ‘Seeing, they do not see, and hearing, they do not hear,’” up to “and your ears, which hear.”

Also on the same day, during the Vigil of the Theophany:

Reading from the Letter of the blessed Paul the Apostle to Titus. “Beloved, the kindness and humanity appeared,” up to “in Christ Jesus our Lord.”

The Gospel according to Matthew, chapter VI. “When Herod had died, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared in a dream to Joseph,” up to “he shall be called a Nazarene.”

On the eighth day before the Ides of January, at the Theophany:

Reading from the prophet Isaiah. “Arise, shine, Jerusalem,” up to “proclaiming praise to the Lord.”

The Gospel according to Matthew, chapter IV. “When Jesus had been born in Bethlehem of Judea,” up to “they returned to their own country by another road.”

On the seventh day before the Ides of January:

Reading from the prophet Isaiah. “In those days the prophet Isaiah spoke, saying: In the year when King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord seated upon a high throne,” up to “your sin shall be cleansed.”

The Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CXXXIX. “When Jesus had finished these sayings,” up to “let him who can accept it accept it.”

On the sixth day before the Ides of January:

At Beauvais, the Nativity of Saint Lucian, martyr.

Reading from the Book of Wisdom. “Hear, O kings, and understand,” up to “they will find what they should answer.”

The Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CCLVI. “Jesus said to his disciples, ‘As lightning comes out from the east,’” up to “their boundaries.”

[Col. 0491B]

On the fifth day before the Ides of January:

Reading from the prophet Isaiah. “In those days the Lord said to Isaiah, ‘Go out to meet Ahaz,’” up to “if you do not believe, you shall not remain.”

The Gospel according to Mark. “Jesus said to his disciples, ‘The kingdom of God is like this: as when a man casts seed upon the earth,’” up to “he did not speak to them without a parable.”

On the fourth day before the Ides of January:

Reading from the prophet Isaiah. “In those days the Lord spoke to the prophet Isaiah, saying: Because this people has rejected the waters of Shiloah,” up to “because God is with us.”

The Gospel according to Mark, chapter LXII. “Jesus said to his disciples, ‘Come away by yourselves; let us go to a deserted place,’” up to “they ran there together.”

On the third day before the Ides of January:

Reading from the prophet Isaiah. “In those days Isaiah said: For thus the Lord said to me, as he instructed me with a strong hand,” up to “by the Lord of hosts who dwells on Mount Zion.”

The Gospel according to Mark, chapter XC. “Jesus came to his disciples and saw a great crowd,” up to “what are you arguing about among yourselves?”

On the day before the Ides of January:

Reading from the prophet Isaiah. “In those days the prophet Isaiah spoke, saying: If your people, Israel, should be like the sand of the sea, a remnant shall return,” up to “upon the mountain of the daughter of Zion.”

The Gospel according to Mark, chapter XCVII. “John answered Jesus, saying, ‘Teacher, we saw someone,’” up to “whoever is not against you is for you.”

On the Ides of January:

The Octave of the Theophany.

Reading from the prophet Isaiah. “My Lord God, I will honor you,” up to “announce these things throughout the whole earth.”

The Gospel according to John. “John saw Jesus coming toward him,” up to “because this is the Son of God.”

On the first Sunday after the Theophany:

Reading from the Letter of the blessed Paul the Apostle to the Romans. “Brothers, I appeal to you by the mercy of God,” up to “in Christ Jesus our Lord.”

The Gospel according to Luke, chapter III. “When Jesus was twelve years old,” up to “with God and with human beings.”

**Monday.** Reading from the prophet Ezekiel: “Thus says the Lord God: Behold, I myself will seek out my sheep,” up to “in judgment and justice, says the almighty Lord.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter 272: “When the Son of Man comes in his majesty,” up to “but the righteous into eternal life.”

Another reading from the book of Deuteronomy: “In those days Moses said to the children of Israel,” up to “as the Lord your God spoke to you.”

**Tuesday.** Reading from the book of Exodus: “In those days the Lord our God spoke to his people.” Gospel according to John, chapter 75: “When the feast was already half over, Jesus went up into the temple and taught,” up to “many from the crowd believed in him.” [Col. 0501B]

**Wednesday.** Reading from the prophet Ezekiel: “Thus says the Lord God: I will sanctify my great name,” up to “and I shall be your God, says the almighty Lord.” Gospel according to John, chapter 89: “As Jesus passed by, he saw a man blind from birth,” up to “and falling down, he worshiped him.”

**Thursday.** Reading from the book of Kings: “In those days the Shunammite woman came to Elisha on the mountain,” up to “he returned to Gilgal.” Gospel according to John, chapter 40: Jesus said to the crowds of the Jews, “My Father is working until now, and I am working,” up to “the resurrection of judgment.” [Col. 0501C]

**Friday.** Reading from the book of Kings: “In those days the son of the woman, the mistress of the house, fell ill,” up to “and the word of the Lord in your mouth is true.” Gospel according to John, chapter 94: “There was a certain man who was ill, Lazarus,” up to “they believed in him.”

**Saturday.** Reading from the prophet Isaiah: “Thus says the Lord: At an acceptable time I answered you,” up to “I will not forget it, says the almighty Lord.”

Another reading from the prophet Isaiah: “Thus says the Lord God: All who thirst, come to the waters,” up to “that shall go forth from my mouth, says the almighty Lord.” Gospel according to John, chapter 86: Jesus said to the crowds of the Jews, “I am the light of the world,” up to “for his hour had not yet come.”

[Col. 0501D] **Fifth Sunday in Lent.** Reading from the Letter of the blessed apostle Paul to the Hebrews: “Brothers, Christ, standing as High Priest,” up to “of the eternal inheritance in Christ Jesus our Lord.” Gospel according to John, chapter 89: Jesus was saying to the crowds of the Jews and to the chief priests, “Which of you will convict me of sin?” up to “and he went out of the temple.”

**Monday.** Reading from the prophet Jonah: “In those days the word of the Lord came to Jonah,” up to “and the Lord our God had mercy on his people.” Gospel according to John, chapter 79: “The chief priests and Pharisees sent officers,” up to “believing in him.”

**Tuesday.** Reading from the prophet Daniel: “In those days the Babylonians gathered before the king,” up to “from the lions’ den.” [Col. 0502A] Gospel according to John, chapter 75: “Jesus was walking in Galilee,” up to “because of fear of the Jews.”

**Wednesday.** Reading from the book of Leviticus: “In those days the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, ‘I am the Lord your God. You shall not steal,’” up to “for I am the Lord your God.” Gospel according to John, chapter 92: “The Feast of Dedication took place in Jerusalem,” up to “and I am in the Father.”

**Thursday.** Reading from the prophet Daniel: “In those days Daniel prayed, saying,” up to “over the whole earth,” up to “each to his own house.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter 74: “At that time someone was asking Jesus,” up to “he loved much.”

**Friday.** Reading from the prophet Jeremiah: “In those days Jeremiah said, ‘Lord, all who forsake you shall be put to shame,’” up to “crush them, O Lord our God.” Gospel according to John, chapter 94: “The chief priests and Pharisees convened a council,” up to “with his disciples.”

[Col. 0502B] **Saturday. Alms are given.** Reading from the prophet Jeremiah: “In those days the wicked Jews said to one another,” up to “in the time of your wrath, O Lord my God.” Gospel according to John, chapter 66: Jesus said to his disciples, “Amen, amen, I say to you: Unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man,” up to “who was going to betray him, being one of the Twelve.”

**Palm Sunday.** (Reading from the Letter of the blessed apostle Paul to the Philippians.) “Brothers, let this mind be in you which was also in Christ Jesus,” up to “because the Lord Jesus Christ is in the glory of God the Father.” Passion of our Lord Jesus Christ according to Matthew, chapter 274: Jesus said to his disciples, “You know that after two days the Passover will take place, and the Son of Man,” up to “sealing the stone with guards.”

[Col. 0502C] **Monday.** Reading from the prophet Isaiah: “In those days Isaiah said, ‘The Lord God opened my ear,’” up to “and they imitate [him] in the Lord their God.” Gospel according to John, chapter 98: “Six days before the Passover Jesus came to Bethany, where Lazarus had been dead,” up to “that the Son of Man may be glorified.”

**Tuesday.** Reading from the prophet Jeremiah: “In those days Jeremiah said, ‘Lord, you showed me, and I knew,’” up to “for to you I reveal my cause, O Lord my God.”

Another reading. Reading from the book of Wisdom: [Col. 0502D] “In those days the wicked Jews said among themselves,” up to “of their souls, says the almighty Lord.” Gospel according to John, chapter 104: Jesus said to his disciples, “Amen, amen, I say to you: Unless a grain of wheat falling into the earth,” up to “for they loved the glory of men more than the glory of God.”

**Wednesday.** Reading from the prophet Isaiah: “Thus says the Lord God: Say to the daughter of Zion, ‘Behold, your Savior comes,’” up to “over all that the Lord our God has given back to us.”

Another reading from the prophet Isaiah: “In those days Isaiah said, ‘Lord, who has believed our report?’” up to “so that they might not perish, says the almighty Lord.” Passion of our Lord Jesus Christ according to Luke, chapter 260: “The feast of Unleavened Bread, which is called Passover, was approaching,” up to “no one had yet been laid there.”

[Col. 0503A] **Thursday, the Lord’s Supper.** Reading from the Letter of the blessed apostle Paul to the Corinthians: “Brothers, when you come together,” up to “so that you may not be condemned with this world.” Gospel according to John, chapter 112: “At that time, before the feast of Passover,” up to “he will immediately glorify him.”

**Friday. At Jerusalem.** Reading from the prophet Hosea: “Thus says the Lord God in his tribulation,” up to “more than a burnt offering.”

As above. Reading from the book of Exodus: “In those days the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt,” up to “for it is the Passover, that is, the Lord’s passage.” Passion according to John, chapter 156: “At that time Jesus went out across the brook Cedron,” [Col. 0503B] up to “because the tomb where they placed Jesus was nearby.”

The readings for the vigil of Easter begin.

**I.** Reading from the book of Genesis: “In the beginning God created heaven and earth,” up to “and he rested on the seventh day from all the work that he had done.”

**II. As above.** Reading from the book of Genesis: “Now Noah, when he was five hundred years old,” up to “the Lord smelled the fragrance of sweetness.”

**III. As above.** Reading from the book of Genesis: “In those days God tested Abraham and said to him,” up to “and they went away together to Beersheba, and he dwelt there.”

**IV.** Reading from the book of Exodus: “In those days, during the morning watch,” up to “this song to the Lord.” Canticle: “Let us sing to the Lord.”

[Col. 0503C] **V.** Reading from the prophet Isaiah: “This is of the servants of the Lord,” up to “that shall go forth from my mouth, says the almighty Lord.”

**VI.** Reading from the prophet Jeremiah: “Hear, Israel, the commandments of life,” up to “and he dwelt among human beings.”

**VII.** Reading from the prophet Ezekiel: “The hand of the Lord came upon me,” up to “and I will give you rest, says the almighty Lord.”

**VIII.** Reading from the prophet Isaiah: “In those days seven women shall seize,” up to “from the whirlwind and from the rain.” Canticle: “A vineyard has been made.”

**IX.** Reading from the book of Exodus: “In those days the Lord also said to Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt, ‘This month,’” up to “that is, the Lord’s passage.”

**X.** Reading from the prophet Jonah: “In those days the word of the Lord came to Jonah the prophet a second time, saying,” [Col. 0503D] up to “and the Lord our God had mercy on his people.”

**XI.** Reading from the book of Deuteronomy: “In those days Moses wrote a song,” up to “and completed it all the way to the end.” Canticle: “Give ear, O heaven.”

**XII.** Reading from the prophet Daniel: “In those days King Nebuchadnezzar made a golden statue,” up to “praising and blessing the Lord.” Canticle: “As the deer.”

**Holy Saturday.** Reading from the Letter of the blessed apostle Paul to the Colossians: “Brothers, if you have risen with Christ,” up to “with him in glory.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter 352: “When evening came on the Sabbath,” up to “there you will see him; behold, I have told you.”

[Col. 0504A] **Holy Sunday. At Saint Mary’s.** Reading from the Letter of the blessed apostle Paul to the Corinthians: “Brothers, purge out the old leaven,” up to “and of truth.” Gospel according to Mark, chapter 30: “Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James, and Salome,” up to “there you will see him, as he told you.”

**Monday.** Reading from the Acts of the Apostles: “In those days Peter, standing in the midst of the people, said, ‘Men, brothers, you know what happened,’” up to “who believe in him.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter 339: “Two of Jesus’ disciples were going that same day to a village,” up to “they recognized him in the breaking of the bread.”

**Tuesday.** Reading from the Acts of the Apostles: “In those days Paul rose and, signaling silence with his hand, said,” up to “raising Jesus Christ.” Gospel according to [Col. 0504B] Luke, chapter 340: “Jesus stood in the midst of his disciples and said to them, ‘Peace to you,’” up to “and repentance for the forgiveness of sins among all nations.”

**Wednesday.** (Reading from the Acts of the Apostles.) “In those days Peter opened his mouth and said, ‘Men of Israel and you who fear God, hear,’” up to “that your sins may be blotted out.” Gospel according to John, chapter 219: “Jesus revealed himself by the Sea of Tiberias,” up to “when he had risen from the dead.”

**Thursday.** Reading from the Acts of the Apostles: “In those days the angel of the Lord spoke to Philip, saying, ‘Rise, go toward the south,’” up to “he evangelized all the cities with the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.” Gospel according to John, chapter 211: “Mary was standing outside by the tomb, weeping,” up to [Col. 0504C] “because I have seen the Lord, and he said these things to me.”

**Friday.** Reading from the Letter of the blessed apostle Peter: “Beloved, Christ died once for sins, the righteous for the unrighteous,” up to “through the resurrection of Jesus Christ, who is at the right hand of God.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter 355: “The eleven disciples went to Galilee,” up to “to the consummation of the age.”

**Saturday.** Reading from the Letter of the blessed apostle Peter: “Brothers, putting aside all malice and all deceit,” up to “but now you have obtained mercy.” Gospel according to John, chapter 212: “When it was evening on that day, the first day of the week, and the doors were closed where the disciples were gathered because of fear of the Jews,” up to “and whose sins you retain are retained.” [Col. 0504D]

**The eighth day before the Kalends of April. On the Conception of Saint Mary.** Reading from the prophet Isaiah: “In those days the Lord spoke to Ahaz, saying, ‘Ask for yourself a sign from the Lord your God,’” up to “so that he may know how to reject evil and choose good.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter 3 [sic]: “The angel Gabriel was sent from God,” up to “let it be done to me according to your word.”

**Sunday, the octave of Easter.** Reading from the Letter of the blessed apostle John: “Beloved, everything that is born conquers the world,” up to “the one who has believed in the Son of God has God’s testimony in himself.” Gospel according to John, chapter 216 [sic]: “Thomas, one of the Twelve,” up to “that you may have life in his name.”

[Col. 0505A] **Monday after the octave of Easter.** Reading from the Acts of the Apostles: “In those days Philip, going down to the city of Samaria, preached Christ to them,” up to “they received the Holy Spirit.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter 108: “Jesus began to reproach the cities in which very many mighty works had been done,” up to “I tell you, it will be more tolerable for the land of Sodom in the day of judgment than for you.”

**Tuesday after the octave of Easter.** Reading from the Acts of the Apostles: “In those days, when many days had passed, the Jews formed a plot to kill Paul,” up to “the vessel was immediately taken up into heaven.” Gospel according to John, chapter 111: Jesus said to his disciples, “The one who believes in me does not believe in me but in him who sent me,” up to “as the Father told me, so I speak.”

[Col. 0505B] **Wednesday after the octave of Easter.** Reading from the Letter of the blessed apostle Paul to the Hebrews: “Brothers, obey your leaders,” up to “through Jesus Christ, to whom be glory forever and ever.” Gospel according to John, chapter 153 [sic]: “Jesus looked upon his disciples and said, ‘Holy Father, keep them,’” up to “but that you may preserve them from evil.”

**Thursday after the octave of Easter.** Reading from the Acts of the Apostles: “In those days, while Peter was inwardly perplexed as to what the vision might mean,” up to “who fears him and practices righteousness is acceptable to him.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter 196: Jesus said this parable to his disciples: “There was a certain rich man, and he was clothed in purple and fine linen,” up to “nor will they believe if someone rises from the dead.”

[Col. 0505C] **The third day before the Ides of April. On the feast of Saint Leo the pope.** Reading from the book of Wisdom: “Behold the great priest,” up to “as an aroma of sweetness.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter 269: Jesus said this parable to his disciples: “A certain man going abroad,” up to “enter into the joy of your lord.”

**The eighteenth day before the Kalends of May. On the feast of Saints Tiburtius, Valerian, and Maximus.** Reading from the book of Wisdom: “The tongue of the wise adorns knowledge,” up to “the one who follows righteousness is loved by the Lord.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter 24: up to “your reward is abundant in heaven.”

**Friday after the octave of Easter.** Reading from the Acts of the Apostles: “In those days the apostles and the brothers who were in Judea heard,” up to “God has granted repentance and life to the Gentiles.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter 354: “The women went out quickly from the tomb,” up to “to this very day.”

**Saturday after the octave of Easter.** Reading from the Acts of the Apostles: “In those days, those who had been scattered by the persecution,” up to “through the hands of Barnabas and Paul.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter 135: “As Jesus was speaking, a certain Pharisee asked him to dine with him,” up to “but you build their tombs.”

**First Sunday after the octave of Easter.** Reading from the Letter of the blessed apostle Peter: “Beloved, Christ suffered for us,” up to “of your souls.” Gospel according to John, chapter 89: Jesus said to [Col. 0506A] his disciples, “I am the good shepherd,” up to “there will be one flock and one shepherd.”

**The eighth day before the Kalends of May. On the feast of Saint George the martyr.** Reading from the book of Wisdom: “Honor and glory belong to the sensible in speech,” up to “his action shall be according to him.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter 95: Jesus said to his disciples, “Nothing is hidden that shall not be revealed,” up to “before my Father who is in heaven.”

**Monday of the week after Easter.** Reading from the Acts of the Apostles: “In those days Peter recounted how the Lord had brought him out of prison,” up to “marveling at the teaching of the Lord.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter 242: “The chief priests and scribes were seeking to lay hands on Jesus,” up to “they marveled at his answers.”

[Col. 0506B] **The fifth day before the Kalends of May. On the feast of Saint Richarius the confessor at Centula.** Reading from the book of Wisdom: “My son, receive instruction from your youth,” up to “and you shall place upon yourself a crown of rejoicing.” Gospel according to John, chapter 52: “The next day the crowd that was standing across the sea,” up to “that you may believe in the one whom he sent.”

**Tuesday of the first week after the octave of Easter.** Reading from the Acts of the Apostles: “In those days there was a certain distinguished man, lame in his feet,” up to “but they remained for no little time with his disciples.” Gospel according to John, chapter 132: Jesus said to his disciples, “I am the true vine,” up to “that your joy may be made complete.”

**Wednesday of the foregoing week.** Reading from the Letter of the blessed apostle Peter: “Beloved, knowing that you were not redeemed with perishable things, silver or gold,” [Col. 0506C] up to “but the word of the Lord remains forever.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter 336: “On the first day of the week, very early,” up to “and he went away, marveling within himself at what had happened.”

**Thursday of the foregoing week.** Reading from the Acts of the Apostles: “In those days certain men came down from Judea,” up to “in the synagogues where it is read every Sabbath.” See the Gospel that was read on Sunday.

**Friday of the foregoing week.** Reading from the Acts of the Apostles: “In those days it seemed good to the apostles and elders,” up to “to speak the word of God in Asia.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter 73: “John’s disciples came to Jesus,” up to “and both are preserved.”

**Saturday of the foregoing week.**

[Col. 0506D] **The third day before the Kalends of May. The feast of Saint Theodora the virgin and Saint Vitalis.** Reading from the book of Wisdom: “Honor God with all your soul,” up to “for they could love only what pleased themselves.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter 140: Jesus said to his disciples, “The kingdom of heaven is like a treasure hidden,” up to “new things and old.”

**Second Sunday after the octave of Easter.** Reading from the Letter of the blessed apostle Peter: “Beloved, I beseech you as sojourners and pilgrims,” up to “for this is grace in Christ Jesus our Lord.” Gospel according to John, chapter 148: Jesus said to his disciples, “A little while, and you will not see me,” up to “no one shall take your joy from you.”

[Col. 0507A] **On the anniversary of Easter.** Gospel according to John, chapter 24: “There was a man of the Pharisees named,” up to “but may have eternal life.”

**The Kalends of May. Feast of Saints Philip and James; at Amiens, of Accius and Acciolus.** Reading from the book of Wisdom: “The righteous shall stand with great steadfastness,” up to “their lot is among the saints.” Gospel according to John, chapter 127: Jesus said to his disciples, “Let not your heart be troubled; you believe in God,” up to “I will do these things in my name.”

Reading from the book of Wisdom: “Let righteous men be your guests,” up to “of the honored and the poor.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter 148: Jesus said to his disciples, “When you hear of wars,” up to “by your patience you shall possess your souls.”

[Col. 0507B] **Monday of the foregoing week.** Reading from the Acts of the Apostles: “In those days, when the apostles had come into Mysia,” up to “you will be saved, you and your household.” The Gospel that was read on the preceding Sunday.

**The fifth day before the Nones of May. Finding of the Holy Cross.** Reading from the Letter of the blessed apostle Paul to the Galatians: “Brothers, I am confident concerning you in the Lord that you will think nothing otherwise,” up to “the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world.” The Gospel that is read on the anniversary of Easter.

**Wednesday of the foregoing week.** Reading from the Acts of the Apostles: “In those days the apostles spoke the word of the Lord to the keeper of the prison and to all who were in his house,” up to “not a few noble women.” The Gospel that is read on Sunday.

**Thursday of the foregoing week.** Reading from the Acts of the [Col. 0507C] Apostles: “In those days the Jews, being zealous against the apostles and taking men from the common people,” up to “either to say or to hear anything new.” Gospel according to John, chapter 125: Jesus said to his disciples, “Little children, I am with you yet a little while,” up to “but afterward you will follow.”

**Friday of the foregoing week.** Reading from the Acts of the Apostles: “But Paul, standing in the midst of the Areopagus, said,” up to “teaching them the word of God.” The Gospel that is read on Sunday.

**Saturday of the foregoing week.** Reading from the Acts of the Apostles: “In those days the Jews rose up with one accord against Paul,” up to “an evil spirit was going out.” The Gospel that is read on Sunday.

**Third Sunday after the octave of Easter.** Reading from the Letter of [Col. 0507D] the blessed apostle James: “Beloved, every good gift,” up to “which can save your souls.” Gospel according to John, chapter 147: Jesus said to his disciples, “I am going to him who sent me,” up to “he will announce it to you.”

**The second day before the Nones of May. Feast of Saint Matthew the apostle.** Reading from the book of Wisdom: “God’s blessing hastens as the reward of the righteous,” up to “you will be a companion to one richer than yourself.” Gospel according to John, chapter 135: Jesus said to his disciples, “This is my commandment: that you love one another,” up to “he may give it to you in my name.”

**The Nones of May. Feast of Saints Alexander, Eventius, and Theodolus.** Reading from the book of Wisdom: “Blessed is the man who has not fallen by his word,” up to “he shall be honored in it.” [Col. 0508A] Gospel according to Matthew, chapter 86: Jesus said to his disciples, “Behold, I am sending you,” up to “he shall be saved here.”

**Wednesday of the foregoing week.** Reading from the Letter of the blessed apostle Paul to the Thessalonians: “Brothers, you are all sons of light and sons of day,” up to “and build one another up in Christ Jesus our Lord.” Gospel according to Mark, chapter 233: “Jesus, rising early on the first day of the week,” up to “they announced it to the others.”

**Thursday of the foregoing week.** Reading from the Acts of the Apostles: “In those days there arose no small disturbance concerning the Way,” up to “when he had said these things, he dismissed the assembly.” The Gospel that is read on Sunday.

**At Rome, the feast of Saint Gordianus.** Reading from the book of Wisdom: “God hates every sacrament of error,” up to “in truth I proclaim his knowledge in judgment.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter 95: Jesus said to his disciples, “Do not suppose that I have come to bring peace,” up to “he shall not lose his reward.”

**Saturday of the foregoing week.** Reading from the Acts of the Apostles: “In those days, after the tumult had ceased,” up to “they escorted him to the ship.” Gospel according to John, chapter 46: “Jesus went across the Sea of Galilee,” up to “he was sitting there with his disciples.”

**Fourth Sunday after the octave of Easter.** Reading from the Letter of the blessed apostle James: “Beloved, be doers of the word,” up to “to keep oneself unspotted from this age.” Gospel according to John, chapter 150: Jesus said to his disciples, “Amen, amen, I say to you: If you ask the Father for anything,” up to “in this we believe, that you came forth from God.”

**The Greater Litany.** Reading from the Letter of the blessed apostle James: “Confess your sins to one another,” up to “and covers a multitude of sins.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter 124: Jesus said to his disciples, “Which of you has a friend,” up to “to those who ask him.”

**On the vigil of the Lord’s Ascension.** Reading from the Acts of the Apostles: “In those days, of the multitude of believers,” up to “as each had need.” Gospel according to John, chapter 154: “Jesus lifted up his eyes to heaven,” up to “and I am going to you.”

**On the Ascension of the Lord.** Reading from the Acts of the Apostles: “I composed the first account,” up to “going up into heaven.” [Col. 0508D] Gospel according to Mark, chapter 233: “While the eleven disciples were reclining,” up to “by the signs that followed.”

**Sunday after the Lord’s Ascension.** Reading from the Letter of the blessed apostle Peter: “Beloved, be prudent,” up to “let God be honored through Jesus Christ the Lord.” Gospel according to John, chapter 145: Jesus said to his disciples, “When the Paraclete comes,” up to “remember that I told you.”

**The fourth day before the Ides of May. At Rome, the feast of Saints Nereus and Achilleus, Saint Pancratius the martyr, and Saint Soteris the virgin, with 603 others.** Reading from the book of Wisdom: “The soul of a human being is vital,” up to “but the mercy of God is over all flesh.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter [Col. 0509A] 189: “The Pharisees came to Jesus,” up to “but to those to whom it has been given.”

**The third day before the Ides of May. At Maastricht, the deposition of Saint Servatius, bishop and confessor.** Reading from the book of Wisdom: “Whoever has mercy teaches and instructs,” up to “and in it to fear God.” Gospel according to John, chapter 138: Jesus said to his disciples, “These things I command you,” up to “who hated me without cause.”

**The second day before the Ides of May. Feast of Saint Cyriacus the martyr and the 304 who suffered with him at Milan.** Reading from the book of Wisdom: “In all wisdom there is the ordering of the law,” up to “the prudent man shall be appeased by a magnate.” Gospel according to John, chapter 138: Jesus said to his disciples, “These things I command you,” up to “they hated me without cause.”

**Thursday of the foregoing week.** Reading from the Acts of the Apostles: “In those days, when we had remained there several days,” up to “he addressed them in the Hebrew language.” Gospel according to John, chapter 25: “Jesus went away with his disciples,” up to “my joy may be complete.”

**Friday of the foregoing week.** Reading from the Acts of the Apostles: “In those days the apostle Paul spoke, saying, ‘Men, brothers and fathers, hear,’” up to “he appointed Paul among them.” Gospel according to John, chapter 134: Jesus said to his disciples, “If you remain in me,” up to “your joy may be complete.”

**Saturday of the foregoing week.** Reading from the Acts of the Apostles: “In those days, when Paul had fixed his attention on the council,” up to “so that they may say it to you.” Gospel according to John, chapter 46: “Jesus went across the Sea of [Col. 0509C] Galilee,” up to “and there he sat with his disciples.”

**On the vigil of Pentecost.** Reading from the book of Genesis: “In those days God tested Abraham.”

Second reading from the book of Deuteronomy: “In those days Moses wrote.”

Third reading from the prophet Isaiah: “In those days seven women shall seize.”

Fourth reading from Jeremiah: “Hear, Israel, the commandments of life.”

**At Mass on that same Saturday.** Reading from the Acts of the Apostles: “In those days, when Apollos was at Corinth,” up to “persuading them concerning the kingdom of God.” Gospel according to John, chapter 128: Jesus said to his disciples, “If you love me,” up to “I will reveal myself to him.”

**Pentecost Sunday.** Reading from the Acts of the Apostles: “In those days, when the day of Pentecost was being fulfilled,” [Col. 0509D] up to “the mighty works of God.” Gospel according to John, chapter 130: Jesus said to his disciples, “If anyone loves me,” up to “as the Father commanded me, so I do.”

## Monday

At the Chains, in the week mentioned above. Reading from the Acts of the Apostles: “In those days, Peter opened his mouth and said … in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.” Gospel according to John, chapter XXIV: “Jesus said to his disciples, ‘For God so loved the world … the works that are done in God.’”

## Tuesday

At Saint Anastasia. Reading from the Acts of the Apostles: “In those days, when the apostles who were in Jerusalem had heard … they received the Holy Spirit.” Gospel according to John, chapter LXXXIX [Col. 0510A]: “Jesus said to his disciples, ‘Amen, amen, I say to you: Whoever does not enter through the door … may have it more abundantly.’”

## Wednesday
