At Saint Mary. Reading from the Acts of the Apostles: “In those days, Peter, standing with the eleven … whoever calls upon the name of the Lord shall be saved.” Gospel according to John, chapter LX: “Jesus said to his disciples, ‘No one can come to me … for the life of the world.’”

## Thursday

At the Apostles. Reading from the Acts of the Apostles: “In those days, Philip, going down to a city of Samaria … joy in that city.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter LXXXVI: “Jesus called his twelve disciples together … healing everywhere.”

## Friday

[Col. 0510B] Reading from the Acts of the Apostles: “In those days, Peter opened his mouth and said, ‘Men of Israel, hear these words … you will fill me with joy in your presence.’” Gospel according to Luke, chapter XXXVI: “It happened on one of the days … because today we have seen marvelous things.”

## Saturday

At Saint Stephen. Reading from the Acts of the Apostles: “In those days, the whole city assembled … they were filled with joy and the Holy Spirit.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter XXVI: “Jesus rose from the synagogue … I must preach the kingdom of God.”

## Sunday within the Octave of Pentecost

Reading from the Book of the Apocalypse of John the Apostle: “In those days, I saw a door opened in heaven … they will worship the one who lives forever and ever. Amen.” Gospel according to John [Col. 0510C], chapter XXIV: “There was a man from the Pharisees, Nicodemus … but may have eternal life.”

## Fourteenth day before the Kalends of June

The feast of Saint Pudentiana. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “I will confess to you, Lord King … deliver them from the hand of those who hate them, Lord our God.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CXL: “Jesus told his disciples this parable: ‘The kingdom of heaven is like a treasure hidden … new things and old.’”

## Thirteenth day before the Kalends of June

At Rome, the feast of Saints Gervasius and Protasius. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “The expectation of the righteous is joy … the city will be exalted.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CLXXXIX: “The Pharisees approached Jesus … not all understand this saying, but only those to whom it has been given.”

## Wednesday of the first week after Pentecost

[Col. 0510D] Reading from the Epistle of the blessed Apostle Paul to the Corinthians: “Brothers, if Christ is preached as having risen from the dead … each in his own order, through Jesus Christ our Lord.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter CCXLIII: “Some of the Sadducees approached Jesus … they did not dare ask him anything further.”

## Eleventh day before the Kalends of June

In Corsica, the passion of Saint Juliana, virgin. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “Lord, my God, you have exalted my dwelling above the earth … and I will bless your name, Lord our God.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CCLXVIII: “Jesus said to his disciples: ‘The kingdom of heaven is like ten [Col. 0511A] virgins … therefore keep watch, because you do not know the day or the hour.’”

## Friday of the week mentioned above

Reading from the Acts of the Apostles: “In those days, the soldiers, according to the command given them … you will go to Caesar.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter CXLVIII: “Jesus said to his disciples: ‘When they bring you into synagogues … so is the one who lays up treasure for himself and is not rich toward God.’”

## Saturday of the week mentioned above

Reading from the Acts of the Apostles: “In those days, after several days had passed … to announce the light to the people and to the nations.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter XCIII: “The disciples approached John (Jesus) … and they were filled.”

## Second week after Pentecost

[Col. 0511B] Reading from the Epistle of the blessed Apostle John: “Beloved, God is love … should love his brother.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter CXCIII: “There was a certain rich man, and he was clothed …”

## Eighth day before the Kalends of June

The feast of Saint Urban, bishop and confessor. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “The Lord gave confession to his holy one … he will be blessed among the blessed.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CCLXIII: “Jesus said to his disciples: ‘Keep watch, therefore … he will appoint him over all his possessions.’”

## Tuesday of the week mentioned above

Reading from the Acts of the Apostles: “In those days, while the Apostle Paul was speaking and offering prayer … and they suffered to have it cut down.” Gospel according to John, chapter CLIII: “Jesus looked [Col. 0511C] upon his disciples and said … but that you may preserve them from evil.”

## Wednesday of the week mentioned above

Reading from the Epistle of the blessed Apostle Paul to the Colossians: “Brothers, put to death your members that are upon the earth … and in all things Christ.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter XXIII: “Jesus said to his disciples: ‘Do not think that I came to abolish the law … he will be called great in the kingdom of heaven.’”

## Fifth day before the Kalends of June

At Paris, the deposition of Saint Germanus, bishop and confessor, and the translation of the body of Saint Gentianus, martyr of Amiens. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “Whoever guards justice will possess understanding … he remains always in the commandments of God.” Gospel according to John, chapter CXXXIX: “Jesus said to his disciples: ‘This is my commandment … whatever you ask the Father in my name, he may give [Col. 0511D] you.’”

## Fourth day before the Kalends of June

At Trier, the deposition of Saint Maximinus, bishop. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “Lord, Father and ruler of my life … looking upon hidden places.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CCLXIII: “Jesus said to his disciples: ‘Keep watch, therefore … he will appoint him over all his possessions.’”

## Third day before the Kalends of June

The feast of Saint Petronilla. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “All things were known to the Lord God before they were created … and among my chosen ones send down roots.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CXL: “Jesus said to his disciples: ‘The kingdom of heaven is like a treasure hidden … new things and old.’”

## Third week after Pentecost

Reading from the Epistle of the blessed Apostle John: “Beloved, do not be surprised if the world hates you … but in deed and in truth.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter XXXV: “Jesus said to his disciples: ‘Unless your righteousness surpasses … then, when you come, you will offer your gift.’”

## Monday of the week mentioned above

Reading from the Acts of the Apostles: “In those days, when dawn began to break … they supplied what was necessary.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter XCVI: “Jesus said to his disciples: ‘There was a certain rich man, and he was clothed in purple … nor will they believe even if someone rises from the dead.’”

## Tuesday of the week mentioned above

Reading from the Acts of the Apostles: “In those days, after several months we sailed in an Alexandrian ship … this is [Col. 0512B] Jesus Christ, the Son of God, through whom the whole world will begin to be judged.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter CXCVII: “Jesus said to his disciples: ‘It is impossible that scandals should not come … we have done what we ought to do.’”

## Fourth day before the Nones of June

At Rome, the feast of Saints Marcellinus and Peter, exorcists, with forty-two others. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “The souls of the righteous are in the hand of God … the Lord of them will reign forever.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter CCXLVIII: “Jesus said to his disciples: ‘When you hear of wars … by your patience you will possess your souls.’”

## Third day before the Nones of June

At Orléans, the deposition of Saint Liphardus, presbyter. Reading from the Epistle of the blessed Apostle Paul to the Hebrews: “Brothers, many became priests … [Col. 0512C] our Lord Jesus Christ offered himself once.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CCLXIX: “Jesus told his disciples this parable: ‘A certain man went abroad … enter into the joy of your lord.’”

## Friday of the week mentioned above

Reading from the Book of the Apocalypse of John the Apostle: “In those days, the Apostle John spoke, saying: ‘Blessed is the one who reads and those who hear the words of this prophecy … the deeds of the Nicolaitans, which I also hate. Whoever has an ear … in the paradise of my God.’” Gospel according to Luke, chapter CLXXXI: “Jesus told this parable: ‘A certain man made a great supper … they shall taste my supper.’”

## Saturday of the week mentioned above

[Col. 0512D] Reading from the Book of the Apocalypse of John the Apostle: “In those days, the Lord said: ‘Write to the angel of the Church of Smyrna … before my Father and before his angels … whoever has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the Churches.’” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CCV: “As Jesus was leaving Jericho … they followed him.”

## Fourth week after Pentecost

Reading from the Epistle of the blessed Apostle Paul: “Beloved, humble yourselves beneath the powerful hand of God … to him be glory and dominion forever and ever.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter CLXXXVI: “Tax collectors were approaching Jesus … while doing penance.”

## Monday of the week mentioned above

[Col. 0513A] Reading from the Book of the Apocalypse of John the Apostle: “In those days, the Lord said: ‘Write to the angel of the Church of Philadelphia … I sat with my Father on his throne,’ and the rest.” Gospel as on the Sunday of that same week.

## Tuesday of the week mentioned above

Reading from the Book of the Apocalypse of John the Apostle: “In those days, the four living creatures, casting their crowns before the throne, said: ‘You are worthy, Lord … who will be able to stand?’” Gospel as on the Sunday of that same week.

# The readings of the fourth month begin

## Wednesday

At Saint Mary. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “Love justice, you who judge … this one who contains all things possesses knowledge of speech.” Another reading: from the Prophet Isaiah: “Thus says the Lord: ‘Hear, Jacob, my servant, concerning your offspring … says the almighty Lord.’” Gospel according to Luke [Col. 0513B], chapter XCIII: “The disciples approached Jesus … and were filled.”

## Thursday of the week mentioned above

Reading from the Book of the Apocalypse of John the Apostle: “In those days, I saw four angels standing at the four corners of the earth … God will wipe away every tear from their eyes.” Gospel as on the Sunday of that same week.

## Friday

Reading from the Prophet Joel: “Thus says the Lord God: ‘Rejoice, sons of Zion … my people forever,’ says the almighty Lord.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter CLXXXVI: [lacuna].

## Saturday, with twelve readings

At Saint Peter. Reading from the Prophet Joel: “Thus says the Lord God: ‘I will pour out my Spirit upon all flesh … [Col. 0513C] everyone who calls upon the name of the Lord shall be saved.’”

Likewise in the place mentioned above. Reading from the Book of Leviticus: “In those days, the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: ‘Speak to the children of Israel, and say to them: When you have entered the land … in all your dwellings and throughout your generations,’ says the almighty Lord.”

Likewise in the place mentioned above. Reading from the Book of Deuteronomy: “In those days, Moses said: ‘Hear, Israel, what I command you today … the Lord your God will have given you.’”

Likewise in the place mentioned above. Reading from the Book of Leviticus: “In those days, the Lord said to Moses: ‘If you walk in my commandments … you shall be my people,’ says the almighty Lord.”

Likewise in the place mentioned above. Here the Prophet Daniel is read. Reading from the Epistle of the blessed Apostle Paul to the Romans: “Brothers, [Col. 0513D] justified by faith, let us have peace with God … through the Holy Spirit who has been given to us.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CCV: “As Jesus was leaving Jericho … they followed him.”

## Fifth week after Pentecost

Reading from the Epistle of the blessed Apostle Paul to the Romans: “Brothers, I consider that the sufferings are not worthy … awaiting the redemption of our body in Christ Jesus our Lord.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter LVI: “Jesus said to his disciples: ‘Be merciful, therefore … the splinter from your brother’s eye.’”

## Fifth day before the Ides of June

The feast of Saints Primus and Felicianus. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “Come over to me, all you who desire me … but the beginning of faith is joined [Col. 0514A] to it.” Gospel according to John, chapter CXXXIV: “This is my commandment … he may give you whatever you ask in my name.”

## Ninth day before the Kalends of July

The vigil of Saint John the Baptist. Reading from the Prophet Jeremiah: “In those days, the word of the Lord came to me, saying … ‘you shall build and plant,’ says the almighty Lord.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter I: “There was in the days of Herod, king of Judea … a perfect people.”

Likewise on the eighth day before the Kalends of July. Reading from the Prophet Isaiah: “Thus says the Lord: ‘Listen, islands … and the Holy One of Israel, who chose you.’” Gospel according to Luke, chapter III: “At that time, when Elizabeth’s time for giving birth was fulfilled … the redemption of your people.”

## Tuesday of the week mentioned above

[Col. 0514B] Reading from the Book of the Apocalypse of John the Apostle: “In those days, when he had opened the seventh seal … nor from their thefts.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter XXXVI: “Jesus said to his disciples: ‘Be reconciled with your adversary … lest your whole body be cast into Gehenna.’”

## Seventh day before the Kalends of July

The vigil of John and Paul. Likewise on that day: seek the Epistle and Gospel that are found among the other saints.

## Wednesday of the week mentioned above

Reading from the Book of the Apocalypse of John the Apostle: “In those days, I saw another mighty angel descending from heaven … they gave glory to the God of heaven.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter CLXXXVI: “Tax collectors and sinners were approaching Jesus … while doing penance.”

## Second day before the Ides of July

[Col. 0514C] On the feast of Saints Basilides, Nabor, and Nazarius. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “The fear of the Lord is the beginning of love … a beautiful ornament for his house.” Gospel according to John, chapter XXIV: “There was a man from the Pharisees … may have eternal life.”

## Friday of the week mentioned above

Reading from the Epistle of the blessed Apostle to the Colossians: “Brothers, whatever you do in word or deed … the reward of the inheritance through Jesus Christ our Lord.” Gospel according to Mark, chapter CXX: “When Jesus had entered Jerusalem and the Temple … whatever he says will be done for him.”

## Saturday of the week mentioned above, eighteenth day before the Kalends of July

The feast of Saint Felicula. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “A shining lamp upon a holy lampstand … whoever [Col. 0514D] sets a snare for another will perish in it.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CXL: “Jesus told his disciples this parable: ‘The kingdom of heaven is like a treasure hidden … new things and old.’”

## Sixth week after Pentecost

Reading from the Epistle of the blessed Apostle Peter: “Beloved, be all of one mind in prayer … but sanctify the Lord Christ in your hearts.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter XXIX: “When the crowds were looking at Jesus … leaving everything, they followed him.”

## Fourteenth day before the Kalends of July

The feast of Saints Mark and Marcellianus and Saint Marina, virgin. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “The tongue of the wise adorns [Col. 0515A] knowledge … whoever follows justice is loved by the Lord.” Gospel according to John, chapter CXXXIV: “Jesus said to his disciples: ‘This is my commandment … whatever you ask the Father in my name, he may give you.’”

## Thirteenth day before the Kalends of July

The feast of Saints Gervasius and Protasius, Nazarius and Celsus, the boy. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “Those who fear the Lord will not be unbelieving … until the visitation of him, the Lord our God.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter CLIV: “Jesus said to his disciples: ‘Let your loins be girded … he will appoint him over all that he possesses.’”

## Fourth day before the Kalends of July

The vigil of the Apostles Peter and Paul. Reading from the Acts of the Apostles: “In those days, Peter and John were going up to the Temple … concerning what had happened to him.” Gospel according to John, chapter CCXXVII: “At that time Jesus said to Peter: ‘Simon [Col. 0515B], son of John, do you love me? … you will glorify God.’”

Likewise on the third day before the Kalends of July. Reading from the Acts of the Apostles: “In those days, King Herod stretched out his hands … of the Jewish people.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CLXVI: “Jesus came into the region of Caesarea Philippi … will be loosed in heaven.”

On that same day, the vigil of Saint Paul. Reading from the Epistle of the blessed Apostle Paul to the Galatians: “Brothers, I make the Gospel known to you.” The Gospel that is read at the vigil of Saint Peter.

Likewise on that day. Reading from the Acts of the Apostles: “In those days, Saul, still breathing threats … affirming that this is the Christ.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CXCV: “Simon Peter said to Jesus: ‘Behold, we have left everything and followed you … he will possess eternal [Col. 0515C] life.’”

## Wednesday of the week mentioned above

Reading from the Epistle of the blessed Apostle Paul to the Colossians: “Brothers, clothe yourselves as God’s chosen … giving thanks to God the Father through Jesus Christ our Lord.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter XCIII: “The disciples approached Jesus and said to him … and were filled.”

For the twelve readings, consult [the proper place].

## Thursday of the week mentioned above

Reading from the Book of the Apocalypse of John the Apostle: “In those days, the seventh angel sounded his trumpet … this is the patience and the end of the saints.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter CLXXXVI: “Tax collectors were approaching Jesus … while doing penance.”

## Friday of the week mentioned above

[Col. 0515D] Reading from the Book of the Apocalypse of John the Apostle: “In those days, I saw a beast rising from the earth … for their deeds will follow them.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter CLXXXV: “A man named Jairus came to Jesus … your faith has saved you; go in peace.”

Consult the twelve readings for the Saturday of the month of June.

## Saturday of the week mentioned above

Reading from the Book of the Apocalypse of John the Apostle: “In those days, I saw a white cloud, and upon the cloud … your judgments are true and just.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CXCIII: “Someone approaching Jesus said to him … come, follow me.”

## Sunday after the feast of the Apostles

Gospel [Col. 0516A] according to Matthew, chapter LVI: “Beware of false prophets … will enter the kingdom of heaven.”

## Ides of July

The feast of Saint Cyriacus. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “The watchfulness of honor will waste away the flesh … the assembly of the saints will declare it.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter CCLXX: “There arose a dispute among the disciples … of the tribes of Israel.”

## Fifteenth day before the Kalends of August

At Metz, the deposition of Saint Arnulfus, confessor. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “Hear me, my son, and do not despise me … do not oppress him and provoke him again.” Gospel according to Mark, chapter CXXXVII: “As Jesus was leaving the Temple … he will be saved to the end.”

## Wednesday of the week mentioned above

Reading from the Apocalypse of John: “In those days, the fourth angel [Col. 0516B] poured out his bowl upon the sun … he carried me away into the desert in spirit.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter LXXXIII: “When Jesus had come out of the boat … how great things God had done for him.”

## Twelfth day before the Kalends of August

The feast of Saint Praxedis. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “They appointed you ruler; do not exalt yourself … he will be reproached with persecutions.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CXL: “Jesus told his disciples this parable: ‘The kingdom of heaven is like a treasure hidden in a field … new things and old.’”

## Friday of the week mentioned above

Reading from the Apocalypse of John the Apostle: “In those days, I saw a woman sitting upon a scarlet beast … which has dominion over the kings of the earth.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter CXCVI: “Jesus told his disciples [Col. 0516C] this parable: ‘There was a certain rich man … nor will they believe if someone rises from the dead.’”

## Tenth day before the Kalends of August

The feast of Saint Apollinaris. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “My son, do nothing without counsel … and from the earth from which Adam was created.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter CCLXX: “There was a dispute among the disciples … of the tribes of Israel.”

## Fourth Sunday after the feast of the Apostles

Reading from the Epistle of the blessed Apostle Paul to the Romans: “Brothers, there is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus … life and peace in Christ Jesus our Lord.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter CXC: “Jesus told his disciples this parable: ‘There was a certain rich man who had a steward … inner tabernacles.’”

## Eighth day before the Kalends of August

[Col. 0516D] The feast of Saint James the Apostle and Saint Christopher, martyr; and at Amiens, the translation of Saint Firminus. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “Mockery and insult are upon the proud … those who perished through their tongue.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter CLIV: “Jesus said to his disciples: ‘Let your loins be girded … the Son of Man comes.’”

## Fourth day before the Kalends of August

The feast of Saints Felix, Simplicius, Faustinus, and Beatrice. At Troyes, the deposition of Saint Lupus, bishop and confessor. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “Blessed is the one who is protected from an evil tongue … and it will benefit you more than gold.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter CCXLIX: “When you hear of wars … you will possess your souls.”

## Wednesday of the week mentioned above

[Col. 0517A] Reading from the Book of the Apocalypse of John the Apostle: “In those days, I saw another angel descending from heaven, having great authority … God has judged your judgment.” Gospel as on the Sunday of that week.

## Third day before the Kalends of August

The feast of Saints Abdon and Sennen. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “Whoever loves his son applies the scourges to him … a man's treasure of life will not fail in holiness.” Gospel according to John, chapter CXXXIV: “This is my commandment … they hated me without cause.”

## Friday of the week mentioned above

Reading from the Book of the Apocalypse of John the Apostle: “In those days, a mighty angel lifted up a stone … for the testimony [Col. 0517B] of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter CLXVI: “The ruler of the synagogue, answering with indignation … which were gloriously done by him.”

## Saturday of the week mentioned above

Reading from the Book of the Apocalypse of John the Apostle: “In those days, I saw heaven opened, and behold, a white horse … they were sated with their flesh.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CXLVII: “When evening came, Jesus’ disciples approached him … about five thousand men.”

## Fifth Sunday after the feast of the Apostles

Reading from the Epistle of the blessed Apostle Paul to the Romans: “Brothers, we are debtors, not to the flesh … but co-heirs with Christ.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter CXXI: “A certain lawyer stood up … and you do likewise.”

## Kalends of August

[Col. 0517C] The passion of the seven Maccabean brothers and of Saint Felicitas under Antiochus. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “In the abundance of the Lord’s discipline … distribute your inheritance.” Another reading from the Book of Wisdom: “Who can find a strong woman? … let her works praise her in the gates.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CXLVIII: “Jesus ordered his disciples to get into the boat … truly you are the Son of God.”

## Fourth day before the Nones of August

At Rome, the feast of Saint Stephen, pontiff. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “The spirit of those who fear the Lord is sought … atonement for sins is to depart from injustice.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter CCXXVIII: “Jesus told his disciples this [Col. 0517D] parable: ‘A certain nobleman went to a distant region … to everyone who has, it will be given, and he will have abundance.’”

## Thursday of the week mentioned above

Reading from the Book of the Apocalypse of John the Apostle: “In those days, I saw an angel descending from heaven, holding a key … day and night forever and ever.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter XCIX: “As Jesus descended from the mountain with his disciples … he restored him to his mother.”

## Friday of the week mentioned above

Reading from the Book of the Apocalypse of John the Apostle: “In those days, one of the seven angels who had the bowls came … and they will reign forever and ever.” Gospel as on the Sunday of that week.

## Eighth day before the Ides of August

At Rome, the feast of Saints Sixtus, Felicissimus, and [Col. 0518A] Agapitus. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “He repays a favor who offers fine flour … his mercy will delight the righteous.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter LXXXVI: “Jesus said to his disciples: ‘Behold, I send you … he will be saved to the end.’”

## Sunday

[Lacuna: Reading from the Epistle of the blessed Apostle Paul to the Corinthians.] “Brothers, not all flesh is the same flesh … afterward, the spiritual.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter CCXIV: “Jesus said this to certain people who trusted in themselves … whoever humbles himself will be exalted.”

## Sixth day before the Ides of August

At Rome, the feast of Saint Cyriacus. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “The mercy of God is beautiful in the time of tribulation … and you will inherit them as from the beginning.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CXCII: “Jesus said to his disciples: ‘Nothing is hidden that will not [Col. 0518B] be revealed … before my Father who is in heaven.’”

## Fifth day before the Ides of August

The vigil of Saint Lawrence. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “I will confess to you, Lord King … from the hands of distress.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CLX: “Jesus said to his disciples: ‘If anyone wishes to come after me … in his kingdom.’”

Likewise on that day, the fourth day before the Ides of August. Reading from the Epistle of the blessed Apostle Paul to the Corinthians: “Brothers, whoever sows sparingly … the harvest of your righteousness.” Gospel according to John, chapter CIV: “Jesus said to his disciples: ‘Unless a grain of wheat … my Father who is in heaven.’”

## Third day before the Ides of August

At Rome, the feast of Saints Tiburtius, Valerian, Caecilia, Susanna, and Cassian; and at Cambrai, the deposition of Saint Gaugericus. Reading from the Book of the Apocalypse [Col. 0518C] of John the Apostle: “In those days, I saw a door opened in heaven … strength to our God forever and ever. Amen.”

Another reading from the Book of Wisdom: “The righteous will stand with great steadfastness … their portion is among the saints.”

Another reading from the Book of Wisdom: “God will repay the reward … they praised together, Lord our God.”

Gospel according to John, chapter CXXXIV: “Jesus said to his disciples: ‘This is my commandment … whatever you ask the Father in my name, he may give you.’”

Another Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CXL: “Jesus told his disciples this parable: ‘The kingdom of heaven is like a treasure hidden … new things and old.’”

## Second day before the Ides of August

The feast of Saint Eupolus. [Col. 0518D] “In those days.” Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “Have mercy on your people, over whom your name has been invoked … a helper who is according to him, and a pillar for rest.” Gospel according to John, chapter CXLIX: “Jesus said to his disciples: ‘Amen, amen, I say to you, you will weep … and no one will take your joy from you.’”

## Second Sunday after Saint Lawrence

Reading from the Epistle of the blessed Apostle Paul to the Corinthians: “Brothers, we know that if the earthly … that we may be made manifest through Jesus Christ our Lord.” Gospel according to Mark, chapter LXXIV: “When Jesus went out from the borders of Tyre … and the mute to speak.”

## Ides of August

[Col. 0519A] The feast of Saint Hippolytus. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “Every friend will say, ‘I have formed a friendship’ … it is sweet to his soul.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter CXLIV: “Jesus said to his disciples: ‘Beware of the leaven … before the angels of God.’”

## Nineteenth day before the Kalends of September

The feast of Saint Eusebius. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “Whoever speaks sophistically … for the peace of God is upon the face of the earth.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CCLXIII: “Jesus said to his disciples: ‘Keep watch, because you do not know … he will appoint him.’”

## Eighteenth day before the Kalends of September

The Assumption of Saint Mary, Mother of the Lord. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “My son, in your weakness … and comfort him at the departure of his spirit.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter CXXIV: “Jesus entered a certain village … it will not be taken away from her.”

## Seventeenth day before the Kalends of September

[Col. 0519B] The feast of Saint Leudegarius. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “Write wisdom at the proper time … seeking in the law of the Most High.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter CLIV: “Jesus said to his disciples: ‘Let your loins be girded … the Son of Man comes.’”

## Friday

Reading from the Book of the Apocalypse of John the Apostle: “In those days, the angel said to me: ‘These words are most faithful and true … whoever wishes, let him take the water of life freely.’” Gospel according to Luke, chapter LXXIV: “A certain Pharisee invited Jesus … because she loved much.”

## Saturday

Reading from the Book of Kings: “In those days, David consulted the Lord … of the wilderness at Gibeon.” Gospel as on the Sunday of that same week.

## Third Sunday after Saint Lawrence

[lacuna] [Col. 0519C] Gospel according to Luke, chapter CXX: “Jesus said to his disciples: ‘Blessed are the eyes that see … you do likewise.’”

## Fifteenth day before the Kalends of September

The feast of Saint Agapitus. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “The wisdom of all the ancients … bless the Lord in his works.” Gospel as among the saints.

## Fourteenth day before the Kalends of September

The apparition of the Holy Cross, and the feast of Saint Andrew, master of the soldiers. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “Give greatness to the name of the Lord … praise and bless the name of the Lord.” Gospel according to John, chapter XXIV: “There was a man from the Pharisees … eternal life.”

## Thirteenth day before the Kalends of September

[Col. 0519D] At Jumièges, the feast of Saint Philibert. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “A great occupation has been created … they covered him with all glory.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter CLXXXII: “Jesus said to his disciples: ‘If anyone comes to me … whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.’”

## Thursday of the week mentioned above

Reading from the Epistle of the blessed Apostle Paul to the Hebrews: “Brothers, we ought to observe more carefully … to help those who are being tempted.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter XXVI: “Jesus rose from the synagogue … to preach the kingdom of God.”

## Eleventh day before the Kalends of September

The feast of Saint Timothy. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “My son, during your lifetime do not lack … but a good name will remain forever.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter LXXXII: “Jesus said to his disciples: ‘If anyone comes to me … whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.’”

## Saturday of the week mentioned above

[Col. 0520A] Reading from the Epistle of the blessed Apostle Paul to the Hebrews: “Brothers, participants in a heavenly calling … if they shall enter into my rest.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CXVII: “The Pharisees went away and took counsel … they will hope in his name.”

## Fourth Sunday after Saint Lawrence

Reading from the Epistle of the blessed Apostle Paul to the Galatians: “Brothers …” [lacuna] Gospel according to Luke, chapter CCI: “As Jesus was going to Jerusalem … your faith has saved you.”

## Ninth day before the Kalends of September

In India, the feast of Saint Bartholomew the Apostle; at Rheims, of Saint Aurea, virgin; [Col. 0520B] and the deposition of Saint Audoenus, bishop and confessor. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “Preserve discipline in peace … in the sight of all men.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter CLXVI [or CXVI]: “Whoever hears you … are written in heaven.”

## Eighth day before the Kalends of September

At Arles, the feast of Saint Genesius, martyr. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “A daughter is hidden from her father … seeing his glory.” Gospel according to Mark, chapter CXXXVIII: “Jesus said to his disciples: ‘See that no one deceives you … he will be saved to the end.’”

## Wednesday of the week mentioned above

Reading from the Epistle of the blessed Apostle Paul to the Hebrews: “Brothers, with the works completed from the foundation of the world … you have become weak in hearing.” Gospel according to Luke [Col. 0520C], chapter CLXIX: “As Jesus went through the cities and villages … will recline in the kingdom of God.”

## Thursday of the week mentioned above

Reading from the Epistle of the blessed Apostle Paul to the Hebrews: “Brothers, although by this time you ought to be teachers … within the veil.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter CXLIX: “Someone from the crowd said to Jesus … and God feeds them.”

## Fifth day before the Kalends of February

At Rome, the feast of Saint Hermes. In Africa, the deposition of Saint Augustine. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “The firmament on high is its beauty … to send forth judgment.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter XLV: “Jesus descended from the mountain and stood in a place … abundant in heaven.”

## Fourth day before the Kalends of September

[Col. 0520D] In Campania, the feast of Saint Sabina, virgin, and the passion of Saint John the Baptist. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “The treasures were opened … he gave wisdom to those who act piously.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CXL: “Jesus told his disciples this parable: ‘The kingdom of heaven is like a treasure hidden … new things and old.’”

## Third day before the Kalends

Likewise, on Saint John’s day. Reading from the Epistle of the blessed Apostle Paul to the Hebrews: “The saints experienced mockery and scourging … they were found tested in Christ Jesus our Lord.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter LIX: “Herod sent … and they placed it in a tomb.”

## Fifth Sunday after Saint Lawrence

Reading from the Epistle of the blessed Apostle Paul to the Galatians: “Brothers, walk by the Spirit … [Col. 0521A] in desires.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter XLVIII: “Jesus said to his disciples: ‘No one can serve two masters … and these things will be added to you.’”

## Monday of the week mentioned above

Reading from the Epistle of the blessed Apostle Paul to the Hebrews: “Brothers, Jesus, the forerunner, entered for us within the veil, according to the order of Melchizedek … concerning which no one has served at the altar.” Gospel as on that Sunday.

## Tuesday of the week mentioned above

[Col. 0521B] Reading from the Epistle of the blessed Apostle Paul to the Hebrews: “Brothers, it is clear that our Lord arose from Judah … which the Lord established, and not man.” Gospel as on that Sunday.

## Kalends of September

At Amiens, the deposition of Saint Firminus, bishop and confessor. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “Let us praise glorious men … all flesh in the flood.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CCLXXIII: “Jesus said to his disciples: ‘Keep watch, therefore … he will appoint him.’”

Thursday of the week above. Reading from the Epistle of the blessed apostle Paul to the Hebrews: “Brothers, every high priest is appointed to offer gifts,” up to “the worldly sanctuary.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter XVIII: “A leper came to Jesus,” up to “they came together to him from every direction.”

Friday of the week above. Reading from the Epistle of the blessed apostle Paul to the Hebrews: “Brothers, the first tabernacle was made,” up to “eternal redemption having been obtained” [Col. 0521C]. Gospel according to Luke, chapter CCXXVIII: “Jesus told his disciples this parable: A certain nobleman,” up to “going up to Jerusalem.”

Saturday of the week above. Reading from the Epistle of the blessed apostle Paul to the Hebrews: “Brothers, if the blood of goats,” up to “with better sacrifices than these.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CCXXXII: “Jesus said to the crowds of the Jews and to the chief priests: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees,” up to “not to omit that.”

Sunday of the sixth month. Reading from the Epistle of the blessed apostle Paul: “Brothers, if we live by the Spirit,” up to “members of the household of faith.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter LXVII: “Jesus was going into a city,” up to “his people.”

[Col. 0521D] September 5. At Besançon, the commemoration of the holy Feriolus and Ferrutio, with their companions. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “Abraham, great father of a multitude,” up to “he chose him from all flesh.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter XLV: “Jesus, coming down from the mountain,” up to “great is your reward in heaven.”

Tuesday of the week above. Reading from the Epistle of the blessed apostle Paul to the Hebrews: “Brothers, not into handmade sanctuaries,” up to “he sits at the right hand of God.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter XXXIX: “Jesus said to his disciples: You have heard that it was said, You shall love your neighbor,” up to “he will repay you in secret.”

Wednesday of the week above. Reading from the Epistle of the blessed apostle Paul to the Hebrews: “Brothers, from now on the Lord Jesus awaits until his enemies are placed,” up to “it is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.” Gospel as on Sunday.

September 8. The Nativity of holy Mary, Mother of God, and the commemoration of Saint Adrian the martyr. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “Moses heard the Lord and his voice,” up to “I anointed him with holy oil.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter III: “Mary arose and went into the hill country,” up to “in God my Savior.”

Also, a reading from the Book of Wisdom: “He was made for the holy one into an eternal covenant,” up to “he made them an eternal nation.” Gospel according to John, chapter CXXXII: “Jesus said to his disciples: I am the true vine,” up to “may he fulfill your joy.”

September 9. The deposition of Saint Audomar, bishop and confessor. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “Strong in battle, Jesus son of Nave,” up to “their name remains forever.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter CLIV: “Jesus said to his disciples: Let your loins be girded,” up to “the Son of Man comes.”

September 10. The deposition of Saint Hilary, bishop. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “Samuel, beloved by his God,” up to “the rejoicing of Goliath.” Gospel according to Mark, chapter CXXXVIII: “Jesus said to his disciples: See that no one leads you astray,” up to “he will be saved here.”

September 11. The commemoration of Saints Protus and Hyacinth. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “David called upon the almighty Lord,” up to “the power of his enemies.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter LXXXIX [Col. 0522C]: “Jesus said to his disciples: When they persecute you in this city,” up to “before my Father who is in heaven.”

Sunday of the eighth month. Reading from the Epistle of the blessed apostle Paul to the Ephesians: “Brothers, I beseech you, a prisoner in the Lord,” up to “in all of us.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter CLXVI: “When Jesus entered the house of a certain man,” up to “will be exalted.”

Monday of the week above. Reading from the Epistle of the blessed apostle Paul to the Hebrews: “Brothers, remember the former days,” up to “though dead, he still speaks.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter CCXL: “As Jesus was teaching the people in the Temple,” up to “by what authority I do these things.”

September 13. At Duro... [place-name uncertain], the deposition of Saint Lidorus, bishop; and at Angers, the deposition of Aurelian [read: Maurilius], bishop. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “Solomon obtained this in days of peace,” up to “he delivered them.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter LXXXIX: “Jesus said to his disciples: When they persecute you in this city,” up to “before my Father who is in heaven.”

September 14. The commemoration of Saint Cornelius, pontiff, and Saint Cyprian, together with the Exaltation of the holy Cross. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “Elijah the prophet arose like fire,” up to “and they came to pass.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter CXL: “Jesus was saying to the crowds of Pharisees and to the rulers,” up to “so that they might accuse him.”

Also, concerning the Cross. Reading from the Epistle of the blessed apostle Paul [Col. 0523A] to the Philippians: “Brothers, have this mind among yourselves,” up to “in the glory of God the Father.” Gospel according to John, chapter XXIV: “There was a man from the Pharisees,” up to “eternal life.”

September 15. The commemoration of Saint Nicomedes. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “In the composition of fragrance,” up to “in the origin of Adam.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter XCVI: “Jesus said to his disciples: If anyone wishes to come after me,” up to “they may see the kingdom of God.”

September 16. The commemoration of the holy virgins Lucy and Euphemia. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “I flourished like a vine,” up to “they will have eternal life.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CXL: “Jesus said to his disciples: The kingdom of heaven is like a treasure hidden,” up to “new things and old.”

[Col. 0523B] September 17. At Liège, the deposition of Saint Lambert, bishop. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “Simon, son of Onias, the great priest,” up to “the perfection of virtue.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter XCVI: “Jesus said to his disciples: If anyone wishes to come after me,” up to “they may see the kingdom of God.”

Sunday of the seventh month. Reading from the Epistle of the blessed apostle Paul to the Corinthians: “Brothers, I give thanks to my God,” up to “the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CCXXIII: “The Sadducees approached Jesus,” up to “they were amazed at his teaching.”

Monday of the week above. Reading from the Epistle of the blessed apostle Paul to the Hebrews: “Brothers, by faith Enoch was taken away,” up to “strangers upon the earth.” Gospel [Col. 0523C] according to Luke, chapter XXXVIII: “Jesus saw a tax collector named Levi,” up to “sinners to repentance.”

Tuesday of the week above. Reading from the Epistle of the blessed apostle Paul to the Hebrews: “Brothers, those who lead strangers and sojourners astray upon the earth signify themselves,” up to “in the course of seven days.” Gospel as on that Sunday.

Wednesday, a fast day, of the week above. Reading from the prophet Amos: “Thus says the Lord: Behold, days are coming, and the plowman will overtake,” up to “from their land which I gave them, says the almighty Lord.” Gospel according to Mark, chapter XCI: “One of the crowd answered and said,” up to “in prayer and fasting.”

Thursday of the week above. Reading from the Epistle of the blessed apostle Paul [Col. 0523D] to the Hebrews: “Brothers, by faith Rahab the prostitute,” up to “he sits at the right hand of the throne of God.” Gospel as on that Sunday.

Friday of the week above. Reading from the prophet Hosea: “Thus says the Lord: Return to the Lord your God,” up to “the righteous will walk in them.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter XXXVI: “Jesus was sitting and teaching,” up to “we have seen wonderful things today.”

Saturday with twelve readings. Reading from the Book of Leviticus: “In those days the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: On the tenth day of the seventh month,” up to “your Sabbaths, says the almighty Lord.”

Another reading from the Book of Leviticus: “In those days the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: On the fifteenth day of the seventh month” [Col. 0524A], up to “I am the Lord your God.”

Also, a reading from the prophet Micah: “Lord our God, feed your people,” up to “from ancient days, Lord our God.”

Also, a reading from the prophet Zechariah: “In those days the word of the Lord came to me, saying,” up to “love peace, says the almighty Lord of hosts.”

Also, a reading from the Book of Exodus: “In those days Moses prayed to the Lord his God, saying: Why, Lord, is your wrath kindled,” up to “against your holy people, Lord our God.”

Reading from the Epistle of the blessed apostle Paul to the Hebrews: “Brothers, the first tabernacle was made,” up to [Col. 0524B] “eternal redemption having been obtained.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter CLXIV: “Jesus was teaching in the synagogues,” up to “gloriously performed by him.”

Sunday of the seventh month. Reading from the Epistle of the blessed apostle Paul to the Ephesians: “Brothers, be renewed in the spirit of your mind,” up to “those who are in need.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter LXX: “Jesus went up into a boat,” up to “such authority to human beings.”

September 20. The commemoration of Saints Dorondonius, Dorotheus, Privatus, Felix, and Constantia, who suffered under Nero. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “At the ascent of the holy altar,” up to “according to his mercy.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CCLXIII: “Jesus said to his disciples: Watch, because you do not know the day,” [Col. 0524C] up to “he will appoint him.”

September 21. In Persia, the commemoration of Saint Matthew, apostle and evangelist, and of Saint Luke the evangelist. Reading from the Book of the Apocalypse of the apostle John: “In those days I saw a door opened in heaven,” up to “they will worship him who lives forever and ever.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter XXXVIII: “Jesus saw a tax collector named Levi,” up to “sinners to repentance.”

September 22. At Agaunum, the commemoration of Saints Maurice, Exsuperius, and Candidus, together with six thousand six hundred and eighty-five others. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “May God grant us gladness of heart,” up to “because the light of God is his footprint.” Gospel according to John, chapter CXXXVIII: “I command you this: that you love one another,” up to “they hated me without cause” [Col. 0524D].

September 23. The commemoration of Saint Thecla, virgin, and Saint Mark the evangelist. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “I will confess to you, Lord King,” up to “I will bless your name, Lord my God.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CCXLVIII: “Jesus said to his disciples: See that no one leads you astray,” up to “he will be saved here.”

September 24. The commemoration of Saint John the Baptist and Saints Julian and Christopher. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “The Lord gave me a tongue as my reward,” up to “yours in its proper time.” Gospel according to Mark, chapter CXXXIX: “See that no one leads you astray,” up to “he will be saved here.”

September 25. In Gaul, at Amiens, the commemoration of Saint Firminus [Col. 0525A], martyr. Reading from the Epistle of the blessed apostle Paul to the Hebrews: “Brothers, consider the Lord who endured such things,” up to “through it he will render them practiced in righteousness.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CCLXIII: “Jesus said to his disciples: Watch,” up to “he will appoint him.”

Third Sunday after Saint Cyprian. Reading from the blessed apostle Paul to the Ephesians: “Brothers, see carefully how you walk,” up to “with one another in the fear of Christ.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CCLXXXVIII: “Jesus told his disciples this parable: The kingdom of heaven is like a king who wished to settle accounts,” up to “from your hearts.”

Monday of the week above. Reading from the Epistle of the blessed apostle Paul to the Hebrews: “Brothers, strengthen your drooping hands” [Col. 0525B] “and your weakened knees,” up to “speaking better than Abel.” Gospel according to Mark, chapter CXXI: “One of the scribes questioned Jesus,” up to “he is not far from the kingdom of God.”

Much is missing here.

Gospel according to Mark, chapter CXVII: “When Jesus had gone out on the road,” up to “Come, follow me.”

Friday. Reading from the Epistle of the blessed apostle Paul to the Ephesians: “Brothers, to each one of us grace has been given,” up to “as truth is in Christ Jesus our Lord.” Gospel according to Mark, chapter LXXVII: “The Pharisees went out and began,” up to “he dismissed him to his house.”

November 8. The commemoration of the four holy Crowned Martyrs [Col. 0525C] and Saint Ragnulfus the martyr. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “The expectation of the righteous is joy,” up to “the city will be exalted.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter XLV: “Jesus, coming down from the mountain,” up to “great is your reward in heaven.”

Second week. Reading from the Epistle of the blessed apostle Paul to the Corinthians: “Brothers, let a person regard us in this way,” up to “then each one will receive praise from God.” Gospel according to John, chapter IX: “The Jews sent from Jerusalem,” up to “where John was baptizing.”

November 9. The Passion of Saint Theodore the martyr. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “Blessed is the man who finds wisdom,” up to “the clouds become dense with dew.” Gospel according to John, chapter CXXXIV: “This is my commandment: that you love one another,” up to “they hated me without cause.”

November 10. At Rome, the commemoration of Saint Leo, bishop, [Col. 0525D] and Saint Menna. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “The tongue of the wise,” up to “will be loved by the Lord.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter CCLXX: “There was contention among the disciples,” up to “the twelve tribes of Israel.”

November 11. At Tours, the commemoration of Saint Martin, bishop and confessor. At the vigil. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “The Lord led the righteous,” up to “the Lord our God, into eternal glory.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter CLIV: “Jesus said to his disciples: Let your loins be girded,” up to “the Son of Man comes.”

Also, on the day itself. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “Behold the great priest,” up to “of sweetness.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CCLXIX: “Jesus told his disciples this parable” [Col. 0526A]: “A certain man went abroad,” up to “into the joy of your lord.”

Monday. Reading from the Epistle of the blessed apostle Paul to the Ephesians: “Brothers, let no evil speech,” up to “as an odor of sweetness.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter CCXL: “As Jesus was teaching in the Temple,” up to “by what authority I do these things.”

November 13. The commemoration of Saint Brictius. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “The blessing of the Lord is upon the head of the righteous,” up to “a crown of glory.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter CCXXVIII: “Jesus told his disciples this parable: A certain nobleman went away,” up to “will abound.”

Tuesday. Reading from the Epistle of the blessed apostle Paul to the Ephesians: “Brothers, do not participate in the unfruitful works,” up to “what the will of the Lord is.” Gospel [Col. 0526B] according to Luke, chapter LXXIV: “A certain Pharisee asked Jesus,” up to “he loved much.”

Also, Wednesday. Reading from the prophet Isaiah: “In those days the prophet Isaiah said: It shall come to pass in the last days,” up to “in the light of the Lord our God.”

Also, as above. Reading from the prophet Isaiah: “In those days the Lord spoke to Ahaz, saying,” up to “to choose the good.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter III: “The angel Gabriel was sent from God,” up to “let it be done to me according to your word.”

Friday. Reading from the prophet Isaiah: “Thus says the Lord God: A shoot will come forth,” up to “faithfulness is the belt around his loins.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter III: “Mary arose,” up to “in God my Savior.”

[Col. 0526C] Saturday with twelve readings. Reading from the prophet Isaiah: “In those days they will cry out to the Lord because of the oppressor,” up to “the Lord our God will heal them.”

Also, as above. Reading from the prophet Isaiah: “Thus says the Lord God: The wilderness will rejoice,” up to “the Lord our God, the fountains of waters.”

Also, as above. Reading from the prophet Isaiah: “Thus says the Lord God: Go up upon a high mountain,” up to “in his bosom the Lord our God will carry them.”

Also, a reading from the prophet Isaiah: “Thus says the Lord God to my anointed one, Cyrus,” up to “I am the Lord; I created him.”

Also, a reading from the prophet Daniel: “In those days an angel descended” [Col. 0526D], up to “exalted above all forever.”

Also, at Mass. Reading from the Epistle of the blessed apostle Paul to the Colossians: “Brothers, we beseech you by the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ,” up to “and will destroy it by the manifestation of his coming, to his God.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter III: “In the fifteenth year,” up to “and all flesh will see the salvation of God.”

First week before Christmas. Reading from the Epistle of the blessed apostle Paul to the Philippians: “Brothers, rejoice in the Lord always,” up to “your understanding in Christ Jesus our Lord.” Gospel according to John, chapter IX: “They sent from Jerusalem,” up to “where John was baptizing.”

Also, as above. Reading from the Epistle of the blessed apostle Paul [Col. 0527A] to the Hebrews: “Brothers, do not abandon your confidence,” up to “for the gaining of the soul.”

Also, a reading as above. Reading from the prophet Jeremiah: “Behold, days are coming, says the Lord,” up to “into their own land, says the almighty Lord.”

At the vigil of Christmas. At the ninth hour. Reading from the prophet Isaiah: “Thus says the Lord: For Zion’s sake I will not be silent,” up to “because the Lord was pleased with you.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter III: “When the mother of Jesus had been betrothed,” up to “from their sins.”

November 16. In Gaul, the deposition of Saint Eucherius, bishop. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “Blessed is the man who finds wisdom,” up to “the clouds become dense with dew.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CCLXIII: “Watch” [Col. 0527B], up to “he will appoint him.”

November 17. The deposition at Orléans of Saint Anianus, bishop and confessor. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “The Lord led the righteous,” up to “the Lord our God into eternal glory.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CCXLIII: “As Jesus sat upon the Mount of Olives,” up to “he will be saved.”

November 22. The feast of Saint Cecilia, virgin, and the martyrs Valerian, Tiburtius, and Maximus. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “Lord my God, you have exalted above the earth,” up to “your name, Lord our God.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CCLXVIII: “Jesus told his disciples this parable: The kingdom of heaven is like ten virgins,” up to “neither the hour.”

November 23. The feast of Saint Clement, Saint Felicitas, [Col. 0527C] and Saint Columban. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “Blessed is the man who abides in wisdom,” up to “the Lord our God will inherit him.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CCLXIX: “Jesus told his disciples this parable: A certain man going abroad,” up to “into the joy of your lord.”

Also, a reading from the Book of Wisdom: “A strong woman,” up to “her works at the gates.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CXXX: “As Jesus was speaking to the crowds,” up to “is sister and mother.”

November 24. The feast of Saint Chrysogonus. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “The righteous man devoted his heart to watchfulness,” up to “it might be sought from generation to generation.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter CCXLIX: “Jesus said to his disciples: When you hear of wars,” [Col. 0527D] up to “your souls.”

November 29. The feast of Saint Saturninus. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “Blessed is the man who is found without blemish,” up to “the whole assembly of the saints.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CXXXIX: “Jesus said to his disciples: See that no one leads you astray,” up to “he will be saved here.”

November 30. The feast of Saint Andrew. At the vigil. Reading from the Epistle of the blessed apostle Paul to the Ephesians: “Brothers, blessed is the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who blessed us,” up to “he abounded toward us.” Gospel according to John, chapter XVI: “John was standing, and two of his disciples,” up to “upon the Son of Man.”

[Col. 0528A] On the day itself. Reading from the Epistle of the blessed apostle Paul to the Romans: “For with the heart one believes unto righteousness,” up to “their words.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter XX: “As Jesus was walking beside the Sea of Galilee,” up to “they followed him.”

And on that same day, Saint Ambrose.

December 1. The deposition of Saint Eligius. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “Blessed is the man who finds wisdom,” up to “the clouds become dense with dew.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter CLIV: “Jesus said to his disciples: Let your loins be girded,” up to “the Son of Man comes.”

December 10. At Rome, the deposition of Saint Damasus, pope. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “Blessed is the man who is found without blemish,” up to “the whole assembly of the saints.” Gospel according to John, chapter CXXXVIII: “Jesus [Col. 0528B] said to his disciples: I command you this, that you love one another,” up to “who hated me without cause.”

December 11. The Nativity of Saint Eulalia, virgin, and of the holy martyrs Victor, Fuscianus, and Gentianus. Reading from the Epistle of the blessed apostle Paul to the Corinthians: “Brothers, let the one who boasts boast in the Lord,” up to “to present him to Christ.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CCLXVIII: “Jesus told his disciples this parable: The kingdom of heaven is like ten virgins,” up to “nor the hour.”

Also, a reading from the Epistle of the blessed apostle Paul to the Romans: “Brothers, we know that for those who love God all things work together for good,” up to “he handed him over.” Gospel according to John, chapter CXXXVIII: “Jesus said to his disciples: I command you this, that you love one another,” [Col. 0528C] up to “who hated me without cause.”

December 12. The deposition of Saint Walericus the confessor. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “The Lord led the righteous,” up to “the Lord our God into eternal glory.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CCLXIX: “Jesus said to his disciples: A certain man went abroad,” up to “into the joy of your lord.”

December 13. The deposition at Cambrai of Saint Autbert, bishop, and the feast of Saint Lucy, virgin. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “Wisdom conquers wickedness,” up to “the discipline of God.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter CCLI: “Jesus said to his disciples: Put this into your hearts,” up to “your souls.”

December 18. The feast of Saint Afra, virgin. Reading from the prophet Malachi: “Thus says the Lord God” [Col. 0528D]: “Behold, I will send my angel,” up to “of ancient years, says the almighty Lord.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CXL: “Jesus told his disciples this parable: The kingdom of heaven is like a treasure hidden,” up to “new things and old.”

December 21. At Rome, the deposition of Saint Innocent, bishop. Reading from the Epistle of the blessed apostle Paul to the Romans: “Brothers, who will separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord?” Gospel according to Luke, chapter XLV: “Jesus, coming down from the mountain,” up to “great is your reward in heaven.”

December 22. At Rome, between the two laurels, the feast of thirty holy martyrs. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “The righteous will live forever,” up to “the Lord our God will lead him there” [Col. 0529A]. Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CCLXIII: “Jesus said to his disciples: Watch,” up to “he will appoint him.”

December 23. At Nicomedia, the feast of eight hundred and sixty holy martyrs. Reading from the Book of Wisdom: “The souls of the righteous,” up to “peace to God’s chosen.” Gospel according to Mark, chapter CXXXVIII: “Jesus said to his disciples: See that no one leads you astray,” up to “he will be saved here.”

December 22. In Cappadocia, the feast of forty virgins. Reading from the Epistle of the blessed apostle Paul to the Corinthians: “Brothers, let the one who boasts boast in the Lord,” up to “to present him to Christ.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter XL: “Jesus told his disciples this parable: The kingdom of heaven is like a treasure [Col. 0529B] hidden in a field,” up to “new things and old.”

For an abundance of rain, or moderation of the weather. Reading from the prophet Joel: “Thus says the Lord: Do not fear, earth,” up to “what he has done with you in wonderful ways.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter LXXXIII: “It happened on one of the days,” up to “they obey him.”

For a lack of rain. Reading from the prophet Jeremiah: “Thus says the Lord God: Have you utterly rejected Judah by casting her away?” up to “all these things, Lord our God.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CLX: “Jesus said to his disciples: I have compassion on the crowd,” up to “his disciples with him.”

On a day of war. Reading from the prophet Isaiah: “In those days Hezekiah fell sick,” up to “I will protect him, says the almighty Lord.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter CL [Col. 0529C]: “Jesus said to his disciples: Do not be anxious,” up to “they will be added to you.”

For the commemoration of a pope. Reading from the Epistle of the blessed apostle Paul to the Hebrews: “Brothers, every high priest,” up to “the order of Melchizedek.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter CCLXX: “There was contention among the disciples,” up to “the twelve tribes of Israel.”

At the ordination of deacons. Reading from the Epistle of the blessed apostle Paul to Timothy: “Dearest, appoint deacons who are modest,” up to “in the faith which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.” Gospel according to John, chapter CIV: “Jesus said to his disciples: Amen, amen, I say to you, unless a grain of wheat,” up to “who is in heaven.”

At the ordination of a priest. Reading from the Epistle of the blessed [Col. 0529D] apostle Paul to Titus: “Dearest, Paul, a servant of Christ and an apostle,” up to “sound doctrine through Jesus Christ our Lord.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CCLXIII: “Jesus said to his disciples: Watch therefore,” up to “he will appoint him.”

At the ordination of a bishop. Reading from the Epistle of the blessed apostle Paul to Timothy: “Dearest, the saying is trustworthy: if anyone desires the office of bishop,” up to “of our God in all things.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CLXV: “Jesus said to his disciples: Who, do you think, is the faithful servant?” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CLXVI: “Jesus came into the region of Caesarea Philippi,” up to “loosed in heaven.”

At the dedication of a basilica or oratory. Reading from the Apocalypse [Col. 0530A] of the apostle John: “In those days I saw the holy city Jerusalem,” up to “I make all things new.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter LX: “Jesus said to his disciples: There is no good tree that produces bad fruit,” up to “it had been founded upon a rock.” Also, Gospel according to Luke, chapter CCXXV: “Jesus went out,” up to “salvation has come to this house.”

For blessing brides. Reading from the Epistle of the blessed apostle Paul to the Corinthians: “Brothers, do you not know that your bodies,” up to “glorify God in your body.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CCXXI: “Jesus was speaking with his disciples,” up to “but few are chosen.”

Also, Gospel according to Matthew, chapter CLXXXIX: “Jesus came into the region of Judea,” up to “what God has joined together, let no human being separate” [Col. 0530B].

At the arrival of judges. Reading from the Epistle of the blessed apostle Paul to Timothy: “Brothers, I beseech you first of all,” up to “in faith and truth.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter CCXXVIII: “Jesus told his disciples this parable: A certain nobleman was there; he had [a corrupt/incomplete reading],” up to “to the one who has, it will be given, and he will abound.”

In tribulation or civil disturbance. Reading from the prophet Jeremiah: “Thus says the Lord God: Does one fall,” up to “but the word of the Lord remains forever and unto ages of ages.”

Also, from the same prophet: “Thus says the Lord God: Practice judgment and righteousness,” up to “his servants and his people, says the Lord God.”

Also, from the same prophet: “If our iniquities have prevailed,” [Col. 0530C] up to “do not forsake us, Lord our God.” Gospel according to Luke, chapter CCXXV: “Jesus went out and traveled through Jericho,” up to “to save what had perished.”

At the commemoration of priests. Reading from the prophet Malachi: “Thus says the Lord: You will know that unless the commandment is sent to you,” up to “because he is the angel of the Lord of hosts.” Gospel according to Mark, chapter LII: “Jesus went around throughout the region,” up to “the sick, and they will be healed.”

A Mass which the priest sings for himself. Reading from the Epistle of the blessed apostle Paul to the Romans: “Brothers, we know that the law is spiritual,” up to “this grace of God through Jesus Christ our Lord.” Gospel according to Matthew, chapter LXXVI: “Jesus went around all the cities,” up to “every illness.”

[Col. 0530D] Votive Mass. Reading from the prophet Isaiah: “Thus says the Lord: On that day the gift to the Lord is deferred,” up to “my inheritance, Israel, says the almighty Lord.”

For the sick. Reading from the Epistle of the blessed apostle Paul [read: James]. “Brothers, is anyone among you sad?” up to “pray for one another, that you may be saved.”

For travelers. Reading from the Book of Genesis: “In those days Abraham said: The Lord of heaven, who brought me from the house,” up to “he himself will send his angel before you.”

For the office of the dead. Reading from the Book of Maccabees: “In those days Judas, a very brave man,” up to “that they might be freed from sins.”

Also, a reading from the Epistle of the blessed apostle Paul to the Thessalonians [Col. 0531A]: “Brothers, we do not want you to be ignorant concerning those who sleep,” up to “therefore comfort one another with these words in Christ Jesus our Lord.”

Also, a reading from the prophet Isaiah: “Thus says the Lord God: Your light will rise in the darkness,” up to “because the mouth of the Lord has spoken.” Gospel according to John, chapter XCIV: “Martha said to Jesus,” up to “who came into this world.”

Also, Gospel according to John, chapter XXXIX: “Jesus said to his disciples and to the crowds of the Jews: For just as the Father raises the dead,” up to “from death into life.”

Also, according to John, chapter LVI: “Jesus said to the crowds of the Jews: Everything that the Father gives me,” up to “on the last day.”

Also, according to John, chapter LXV: “Jesus said [Col. 0531B] to his disciples and to the crowds of the Jews: I am the living bread,” up to “on the last day.”

## Readings for the Dead

[Col. 0532A]

1. “Spare me, Lord, for my days are nothing,” up to “I shall not remain.”

2. “My soul is weary of my life,” up to “I can escape.”

3. “Your hands,” up to “guarded my spirit.”

4. “Answer me: how many iniquities do I have?” up to “a garment that is consumed by the moth.”

5. “A human being born of a woman, living for a short time,” up to “until the desired thing comes.”

6. “Who will grant me this, that you may protect me in hell?” up to “but spare my sins.”

7. “My spirit will be weakened, my days will be shortened,” up to “you are my patience, Lord my God.”

8. “Though my skin is consumed with flesh,” up to “may they be carved in flint” [Col. 0532B].

9. “For I know that my Redeemer lives,” up to “this is my hope in my bosom.”

# PART THREE: COMMENTARIES ON THE NEW TESTAMENT

[Col. 0531]

## Exposition of the Gospels [C, G, S]

## Prefatory Notice to the Following Exposition

The Benedictine editor was the first to add this work to the commentaries falsely attributed to Jerome on the New Testament. He had found it in manuscript codices bearing the name of the holy Doctor, and copied it from a single manuscript which seemed to him the more ancient Gemeticensis. Its title was—and we retain it—*Exposition of the Four Gospels, issued from the Brief Proverb, by Jerome the Priest*. From these words alone, however, it remains uncertain, as far as I know, whether the work was composed by Jerome himself or extracted by others from his writings.

Martianaeus thought its true author was Walafrid Strabo of Fulda. Yet he wished to attribute all the monstrous faults throughout the verbal texture to an utterly incompetent copyist. But if we know Walafrid well, he deserves to be valued far more highly than to be compared with the compiler of this work; nor is it credible that so much dignity could have been lost by a good writer merely through scribal errors.

Moreover, we do not see on what testimony of the ancients he based that conjecture. For none of those who discuss Walafrid’s writings—Sigebert, the Anonymous of Melk, Trithemius, Miraeus, and others—attribute anything of this kind to him. But whoever the author may have been, Martianaeus would certainly have served literary scholarship less badly if he had entirely refrained from publishing it. For he published it swollen and disfigured by every kind of error, many of which could have been removed with little difficulty, so that every third line or so had its meaning interrupted and mutilated; to say nothing more, he shamefully wasted the pages through culpable negligence.

Since it was no longer possible for us to omit the book altogether, we corrected innumerable passages as far as could be done without the support of manuscript codices, or indicated in the notes which passages required correction.

## Exposition of the Four Gospels, Issued from the Brief Proverb

[Col. 0531]

## Prologue

[Col. 0531B] First, the time, place, and person of every book must be sought; and why no more than four Gospels are accepted out of twelve: because the whole world consists of four elements, namely heaven, earth, fire, and water. John is represented by heaven, because just as heaven surpasses everything, so does John, who said: “In the beginning was the Word.”

Matthew represents earth, for he said: “The book of the generation of Jesus Christ.”

Luke represents fire, for he said: “Was not our heart already burning within us?”

Mark represents water, for he said: “The voice of one crying in the wilderness” [Note: [Col. 0533D] A passage seems to have fallen out here, alluded to from Genesis, chapter I: “And a river went out from the place of delight to water Paradise, and from there it is divided into four heads.” Accordingly, the passage should also be restored in what follows, approximately as follows: “The four evangelists signify: The river signifies the fountain, that is, Christ.” Compare Druthmar’s *Exposition on Matthew*.]

That is, the four rivers from one spring signify the four evangelists, that is, Christ. Pishon, “breathing forth,” signifies John; Gihon, “swiftness,” signifies Matthew; the Tigris, “happiness,” signifies Mark; the Euphrates, “fruitfulness,” signifies Luke.

They water the world, that is, the Church, and signify the four virtues: prudence, temperance, fortitude, and justice. Just as four rivers water Paradise, so these four virtues water our heart [Col. 0533B].

The human being also consists of four elements: air, fire, water, and earth. From air comes breath; from fire, blood; from water, flame; from earth, the body. The head is heaven, where the two luminaries are; the breast is air; the belly is water; the feet are earth.

Moreover, Adam received his name from four stars, which is [Note: [Col. 0533D] Read *arctos, dysis, anatole, mesembria*, Greek ἄρκτος, δύσις, ἀνατολή, μεσημβρία. These are not the names of stars, as the author calls them, but the names of the four regions of the world. The fact that the name Adam is signified by their initial letters is also transmitted in Saint Augustine, *Tractate X on John*, and in the treatise *On the Mountains of Sinai and Zion* at the end of Saint Cyprian, as well as in Amalarius Fortunatus, book I, chapter 7, *On Ecclesiastical Offices*, and elsewhere. The *Sibylline Oracles*, book II, also call Adam…]
. . . having fulfilled the name

“East and west, south and north” [Greek: Ἀντολίην τε δύσιν τε μεσημβρίαν τε καὶ ἄρκτον]. “Artis, dosis, anatholis, mesimbrio,” or they signify the four evangelists. And just as every human being is born from Adam, so through the four evangelists all come to the faith.

Likewise, Noah’s ark is read as having been made square from wood: its length was 300 cubits, its breadth 50, its height 30, and it was completed with one cubit. It signifies the Church: through the four evangelists, length signifies the hope of eternal life, breadth charity, height faith in the Trinity, and the one cubit worship of the one Lord. The bitumen within and without signifies love of God and of neighbor. Likewise, the ark of the covenant, in which were the two tablets and Aaron’s rod, was carried by four golden rings; and the poles covered with gold signify the four evangelists. The ark signifies the Church, the poles the teachers. Just as those poles were enclosed by rings, so priests are instructed in the Old and New Testaments. The four evangelists carry the Church by defending it against heresy. By the rod the cross is shown: and just as a square piece of wood stands firm whichever way it is turned, so a person instructed by the four evangelists becomes firm against heresy and tribulation.

Likewise, Matthew means “given”; Mark, “a lofty gift”; Luke, “rising”; John, “the grace of the Lord.” Likewise, wheel within wheel means spirit within the wheel: the preaching of the Gospel revolving throughout the world. Spirit within the wheel means the Holy Spirit in the Gospel. Likewise, the linen vessel, and the four lines upon it, signify the four evangelists: these are the clean and the unclean, Jews and Gentiles. Likewise, the four living creatures have eyes before and behind and cry out, “Holy”: they are the four evangelists.

Likewise, Jacob supplanted his brother three times: first by the blessing, second by the lentils, third by the blessing. Esau signifies the devil, Jacob Christ, who conquered and supplanted him three times. Thus we too must supplant our brother the devil three times—in thought, in word, and in deed. He is therefore our brother because God created him as he created us; we have one Father, God. He created him good, but through his own vice, by becoming proud, he deprived himself of that goodness.

The four evangelists signify: Matthew, the face of a human being; Luke, a calf; Mark, a lion; John, an eagle. The Lord Jesus Christ fulfilled all of these: a human being by being born, a calf by being sacrificed, a lion by rising, and an eagle by ascending. Wheel within wheel means law within law, the old within the new.

Why are the four evangelists not written by four apostles, but by two disciples and two apostles? Because the sons of Jacob were born from two free women and two maidservants. Matthew is honey; Mark, milk; Luke, oil; John, wine.

## THE GOSPEL ACCORDING TO MATTHEW

### The book of the generation of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham

He names two fathers for this reason: of David it is said, “From the fruit of your womb I shall place upon my throne”; of Abraham it is said, “In your seed all the nations shall be blessed.” David is written before Abraham because he is nearer to Christ, who was to be born from that lineage.

“Jacob begot Joseph”: he said this according to creation. Luke spoke according to the law, so that he might be the son of Heli. Women are included in Christ’s genealogy because they too come to eternal life as men do. Sinners are therefore named in Christ’s genealogy because he said, “I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners.”

Luke, speaking of Christ from Adam, shows that through Christ’s lineage Adam is released from sin, or that those who come forth from Christ return to the Father. The figure of the forty-two men in Christ’s genealogy corresponds to the forty-two stations of the children of Israel from Egypt to the promised land—that is, from the world to heaven. This signifies coming to Christ through three sets of things: faith, hope, and charity.

What does the number fourteen signify, except the ten words of the Law and the four virtues? The first is prudence: to serve God, not idols. The second is temperance: not to covet. The third is justice: not to commit adultery. The fourth is fortitude: to forgive, not to kill.

The world was ruined through four things—through a man, a woman, a tree, and a serpent—and it is restored through four things: through Christ, Mary, the cross, and the man Joseph.

The serpent that was in Israel signified Christ. It was made of bronze, with four round wheels. Those who looked at it were healed. And he raised it upon the top of the staff, so that all might see it, and the animals of the desert might flee from fear of the wheels. Thus each person is healed if he looks upon Christ on the top of the staff—that is, upon the cross. The four wheels signify the four evangelists. Thus the devil flees the Gospel when it sounds in heaven.

### Now the generation of Christ was as follows

That is, they spoke according to the flesh. He is called “Christ” so that Christians might be named from him by a derivative term. Again, by etymology, Christ means “anointed,” because through him, after baptism, we received the anointing of chrism.

Thus it was according to eternity. “Mary” sounds like “star of the sea,” because a star is sweet while the sea is bitter. Thus Mary was in the sea of the world, among sinners, like a star of the sea: just as, when there is death, a star brings people to the harbor if they follow it, so Mary was in the world in which Christ was born, and Christ leads all to life if they follow him.

### His mother had been betrothed

That is, for four reasons: so that she would not be stoned as an adulteress; so that she might have comfort in flight; so that Christ’s genealogy might be traced through Joseph; and so that the birth might be concealed from the devil.

### Before they came together

That is, before they had been in the same dwelling, she was found by Joseph to be with child—not in the womb in the ordinary manner of a woman, but as a virgin, having conceived from the Holy Spirit. That is, he was made from the Spirit as Spirit, just as God makes an apple upon a tree and Eve from Adam’s rib.

### Joseph, her husband

For this reason he is called her husband, and for this reason he is called righteous: so that no one might suppose that there had been a human union.

### He did not wish to expose her

That is, in court, lest he violate the law, because he knew that she was a virgin, so that the devil might remain unaware of her childbearing.

While he was considering this—that is, whether to dismiss her or keep her—this prophecy was fulfilled: “A helper in times of need, in tribulation.”

### An angel of the Lord said in a dream
