If someone devours you, if someone takes from you. Banquets or gifts. If someone takes money.

If someone exalts himself. Jewish pride, whether concerning knowledge or the quality of one’s lineage.

If someone strikes you in the face. If someone also rebukes you openly.

I speak according to dishonor. For it is the greatest dishonor if a son of God boasts about earthly nobility.

As though we had been weak in this respect. As though we possessed something less than they do.

In whatever anyone dares—in foolishness I speak. Here he compares himself with the Apostles in consideration of his labors. It should also be noted that he calls daring something apparently rash.

I too dare. I can dare if I wish.

[Col. 0801C]

Are they Hebrews? So am I. Are they Israelites? So am I. Are they Abraham’s seed? So am I. If they boast in this, I too belong to this people.

Are they ministers of Christ? I am more so. I speak as one less wise. In far greater labors, in more abundant imprisonments, in blows beyond measure, in frequent deaths. Five times I received from the Jews the forty lashes less one. Three times I was beaten with rods; once I was stoned. Five times he received thirty-nine blows, as a transgressor of the law. Not all these things are found in the Acts of the Apostles, because the Epistles likewise do not contain everything written there.

[Col. 0801D]

Three times I was shipwrecked; I spent a night and a day in the depths of the sea. This was in the final danger, when we thought that the ship, driven into the depths by a violent storm, was being covered by the waves hour by hour.

Often on journeys: dangers from rivers, dangers from robbers, dangers from my own people, dangers from Gentiles, dangers in the city, dangers in the wilderness, dangers at sea, dangers among false brothers. They entered secretly to investigate our freedom.

In labor and hardship, in many sleepless nights, in hunger and thirst, and in many fasts; in cold and nakedness. Hunger is imposed by necessity; fasting is undertaken willingly.

Besides the other things that are external, there is my daily pressure: the care of all the churches. This is in addition to those matters that seem lighter because they are borne with gentleness.

Who is weak, and I am not weak? Who is scandalized, and I am not inflamed? He did not say, “I am scandalized,” because the other person is scandalized in faith. I am weak with those who are weak; with those who perish, I consider myself to perish. For I am so burned by sorrow that I feel myself burning inwardly.

If it is necessary to boast. If boasting is necessary, I will boast not in things belonging to joy but in things belonging to grief.

I will boast of the things that concern my weakness. The Apostle plainly indicates by his weaknesses the temptations and persecutions that he endured. He also defined all the foregoing necessities by the single name “weakness,” because these things prevail over human frailty.

[Col. 0802B]

The God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who is blessed forever, knows that I am not lying. Since he was about to speak of something apparently difficult—that the Jews had even stirred up the rulers of the nations against him—he first appeals to God’s testimony, lest it be attributed to true boasting that kingdoms had risen against him and had been unable to prevail. He enumerates these matters in order to show the difference between true and false apostles.

At Damascus, the governor under King Aretas guarded the city of the Damascenes in order to seize me. But I was let down through a window in a basket over the wall, and so I escaped his hands. He was the governor of that people over whom King Aretas ruled.

## CHAPTER XII

[Col. 0802C]

If it is necessary to boast, it is not expedient. It is not expedient for me, who am compelled by necessity.

But I will come to visions and revelations of the Lord. He attributes weaknesses to himself and visions to the Lord.

I know a man in Christ. Either, out of humility, he speaks about himself in the person of another, or he speaks about someone else; either possibility can be true.

Fourteen years ago—whether in the body or outside the body, I do not know; God knows—such a one was caught up to the third heaven. Because he repeats the point, he shows that this was another vision. See how great the necessity was that he was forced to reveal what he had concealed for fourteen years.

And I know such a man—whether in the body or outside the body, I do not know; God knows—that he was caught up into paradise. By repeating the reference to such a man, the Apostle shows that he was caught up a second time: once to the third heaven, where he saw visions, and once into paradise, where ineffable words were revealed to him.

And he heard secret words that it is not lawful for a human being to speak. Either words that no one is permitted to utter, or words that human nature is unable to recount. This is directed against the Arians.

On behalf of such a one I will boast; but on my own behalf, nothing. Whether concerning the vision or the man, I will not boast on my own account, because it is not my revelation but God’s.

Except in my weaknesses. For even if I wished to boast, I would not be foolish, since I would speak the truth. Here he seems to show that, although he speaks about another, even if he does speak, he does not wish to claim a reason for boasting.

[Col. 0803A]

But I refrain, lest anyone regard me as being above what he sees in me or hears from me. What is manifest is sufficient, even if hidden things are concealed.

And lest the greatness of the revelations exalt me, there was given me a thorn in my flesh, an angel of Satan. How great do you suppose those things must be which I conceal, so that, deservedly, a thorn was necessary for me—one that would always demonstrate to me that I am a human being? By “a thorn in the flesh” and “an angel of Satan,” the Apostle signifies that he endured the temptations of persecutions.

Who should buffet me. Either by stirring up tribulations or by inflicting pains. For some say that he frequently suffered from headaches.

For this reason I besought the Lord three times that it might depart from me. And he said to me: My grace is sufficient for you, for [Col. 0803B] power is made perfect in weakness. Here we understand that even saints sometimes, unknowingly, have asked for things that could not be obtained; at the same time we learn that an insistent request may merit an answer even when it does not merit fulfillment.

Therefore I will gladly boast in my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may dwell in me. After I learned that what I had thought harmful was beneficial.

For this reason I am pleased with my weaknesses, with insults. Not with honors.

With necessities. Not in leisure, not in riches.

In persecutions, in hardships for Christ. Not for a crime. Thus the Savior taught that we should suffer only for the cause of righteousness, and Peter likewise attested this.

For when I am weak, then I am powerful. The greatest power [Col. 0803C] is to become weak for Christ, and great riches are to be in need.

I have become foolish. He says that a person is foolish when he boasts of his labors or virtues.

You compelled me. For I ought to have been commended by you. I did nothing less than those who are apostles beyond measure. But you compelled this, since, although you ought to have satisfied others concerning me—that I was in no respect inferior to the great Apostles—you again require us to commend ourselves to you anew.

Although I am nothing, yet the signs of my apostleship have been performed among you with all patience, with signs, wonders, and powers. As a human being I am indeed nothing; but my apostleship has displayed its signs among you—that is, patience in conduct and wonders in signs.

[Col. 0803D] What is there, then, in which you were inferior to the other churches, except that I myself did not burden you? Forgive me this wrong. To whom other Apostles preached. He is speaking of the Apostle’s integrity and of the severity of the authority received from the Lord against those who refused repentance.

Behold, this is the third time I am ready to come to you, and I will not burden you. For I do not seek what is yours, but you. I desire your salvation, not gifts.

For children ought not to store up for their parents, but parents for their children. If I possessed anything, I ought rather to give it to you.

But I will most gladly spend and be spent, even for your souls, more abundantly myself, although, loving you more, I may be loved less. [Col. 0804A] What I have, I spend through immense labor, and I will spend more than I can. For perfect love not only freely spends everything it has, but also gladly spends itself beyond that, if necessary.

But let it be so. I did not burden you, but, being crafty, I caught you by deceit. Did I take advantage of you through any of those whom I sent to you? In every respect he clears himself, continually calling upon their own conscience as witness; at the same time he shows them how they can guard against such people.

I urged Titus and sent a brother with him. Did Titus take advantage of you? Did he take anything from you to bring to me?

Did we not walk in the same spirit? Did we not follow the same [Col. 0804B] footsteps? Did we not conduct everything in one spirit?

Do you think that we have long been excusing ourselves before you? We do not please ourselves, as I said above; rather, we say this lest, when we come, we be compelled to exact punishment more severely.

Before God, in Christ, we speak. And all things, beloved, are for your edification. He whom it is impossible to deceive.

For I fear that perhaps, when I come, I may not find you as I wish, and that I may be found by you as you do not wish. I fear that, if I do not find you righteous, I may be found severe toward you. He joins threats to his expressions of affection.

Lest perhaps there be among you quarrels, jealousies, hostilities, dissensions, slanders, whisperings, conceits, and disturbances. Lest, when I come again, God should humble me before you. Because of such things he said that he would exact the severest punishment. What would he do if he encountered such things in our times, when, in comparison with other crimes, these are not even considered sins?

And I should mourn over many of those who sinned previously and did not repent. This is directed against the Novatians, who denied repentance: for if he mourns those who do not repent, then clearly he rejoices over those who do repent.

Over the impurity, fornication, and shamelessness that they committed. Shamelessness is more serious than fornication, as a monstrous disgrace—like the man who took his father’s wife.

## CHAPTER XIII

Behold, this is the third time I am coming to you: “In the mouth of two or three witnesses every word shall stand.” According to the Law, against the Manichaeans.

[Col. 0804D] I told you before, and I tell you beforehand, as though I were present with you, and now, while absent, I say it to those who sinned previously and to all the others: that if I come, I will not spare again. I will not spare those who sin after the examples of their predecessors, because the downfall of those who came before ought to make those who follow more cautious.

Do you seek proof of the one who speaks in me—Christ? Or are you testing Christ in me, to see whether he has power to exact punishment among you?

Who is not weak among you. You yourselves are not ignorant that he is not weak but powerful.

But he is powerful among you. How much more among you who criticize him!

For even if he was crucified through weakness, he lives through the [Col. 0805A] power of God. His being crucified belongs to our weakness; his living belongs to his power.

For we too are weak in him, but we shall live with him through the power of God among you. Either: you who challenge us as though we were weak will find that we live with Christ in the power of God when we begin to exact punishment from you. Or: we are presently made weak, but in the future we shall live with him, not through our own power but through God’s.

Test yourselves, whether you are in the faith; examine yourselves. If you are in the faith, recognize yourselves in us also. Pass judgment in the case of the sinner, and see whether punishment does not immediately proceed at your word.

Do you not recognize yourselves, that Jesus Christ is in you? Unless perhaps you are rejected. The power of God, that is, if he has not rejected you entirely.

But I hope that you will recognize that we are not rejected. I hope that you will perceive how we conduct ourselves.

We pray to God that you do nothing evil—not so that we may appear approved, but so that you may do what is good, while we ourselves may appear rejected. For if you did something evil, we would appear approved by exacting punishment; but we preferred to appear rejected, provided only that you do what is good.

For we can do nothing against the truth, but only for the truth. The judgment of our innocence cannot harm anyone except one who has certainly sinned.

[Col. 0806A] For we rejoice that we are weak, while you are powerful. We rejoice if there is no need for our power to appear, as Peter’s appeared in Sapphira and Ananias.

We also pray for your perfection. That you may be perfect and powerful.

For this reason I write these things while absent, so that, when present, I may not act more harshly, according to the authority that the Lord gave me. If you do not correct yourselves, I shall act more harshly still than I now announce in writing.

For edification. So that you may correct yourselves thereafter, and others may fear to sin.

And not for destruction. The pseudo-apostles usurp such authority for themselves.

Finally, brothers, rejoice; be perfected; exhort one another. It should be noted that, writing to the whole Church, he says that all of them ought to be perfect, and that he commands the laity [Col. 0806B] to exhort one another.

Be of the same mind. Have peace, and the God of peace and love will be with you. Otherwise, the author of dissension and hatred will be opposed to you, and you will remain with him forever, if he remains here always with you.

Greet one another with a holy kiss. All the saints greet you. Not the honored or the rich.

The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit. Against the Arians, who contend that the Father is greater because he is usually named first in the order.

Be with all of you. Amen. Not with only some; or, he wishes all to be perfected in these gifts.

# ON THE EPISTLE TO THE GALATIANS

[Col. 0805]

## CHAPTER I

[Col. 0805C]

Paul, an apostle, not from men nor through a man. As the authority of the sacred Scriptures testifies that no one comes to the Father except through the Son and the Holy Spirit, and likewise that no one comes to the Son except the one whom the Father and the Holy Spirit call, so here too it is clearly shown that Paul the apostle was called to preach the Gospel through Jesus Christ and God the Father by the Holy Spirit. As the book of the Acts of the Apostles teaches, saying: “While they were ministering to the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said: Set apart for me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have appointed them.” And again, below in the same passage: “And they, being sent by the Holy Spirit, departed for Seleucia.” But by placing Jesus Christ first here, and then the Father, while elsewhere he indiscriminately places God the Father first and also frequently the Holy Spirit, he shows that in the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit there is neither order nor greater or lesser status, but one glory and the same substance. In saying “not through a man, but through Jesus Christ,” he indicates the person of the deity. But when he says, “who raised him from the dead,” he signifies the incarnation of the assumed human being. Alternatively: not through human presumption, as they say, nor through other Apostles, as Aaron came through Moses, but through the Lord himself, as Moses and all the Apostles or Prophets did. Most, however, are appointed by men, when, unworthily, through the favor of the people, they despise the Lord’s patience and are appointed to the divine priesthood contrary to their merit.

But through Jesus Christ. Who chose Peter and the other Apostles for the ministry of apostleship.

And God the Father. He shows that the Father and the Son have one operation.

Who raised him from the dead. Insofar as he was able to die, namely according to the flesh.

And all the brothers who are with me, to the churches of Galatia. So that he would not seem alone to resent the trampling down of his teaching, the Apostle, intending to rebuke the Galatians for their conduct, writes to them not merely in his own name but in the name of all the brothers who were in fellowship with him. He calls them apostles in the Epistle to the Corinthians, saying: “Whether they are our brothers, apostles of the Church of the glory of Christ.”

Grace to you. Because you have been saved by faith alone.

And peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. By whom, with all their sins forgiven, they had been reconciled to God.

Who gave himself for our sins. He displays the benefits of Christ, for which they were ungrateful, wishing to live under the Law [Col. 0807A] that was given to sinners, although all their sins had been forgiven.

That he might deliver us from the present evil age. Not because the age itself is evil, but because the things done in the age are evil. Thus the Lord also says in the Gospel: “Sufficient for the day is its evil.” Not because the day itself is evil, but because of the things—whether good or evil—that are done in its time it is called so. Likewise, the works of the age are called evil when they are committed in it.

According to the will of God and our Father. Not according to our merits.

To whom be glory forever and ever. Amen. Infinite benefits are owed infinite glory.

I am astonished that you are so quickly transferring from him who called you into the grace of Christ to another Gospel, which is not another. Having displayed the benefits, he says that he is amazed that they could have separated themselves from him.

Except that there are some who trouble you. For there cannot be another true Gospel except Christ’s.

And wish to overturn the Gospel of Christ. Whereas the Law ought to have advanced toward the Gospel, they, by reversing the order, attempt to force the Gospel back toward the Law.

But even if we or an angel from heaven should preach to you contrary to what we preached to you. Briefly, he wished to forestall every person, since he permitted neither an Apostle to preach against what he had first proclaimed nor even the voice of an angel speaking from heaven to be heard. This sentence applies against all heretics who attempt to alter the apostolic traditions.

Let him be anathema. That is, let him be abominable to you.

[Col. 0807C] As we said before, and now I say again: If anyone preaches to you contrary to what you received, let him be anathema. What is repeated is commended more forcefully.

For am I now persuading human beings, or God? Am I seeking to persuade you for the sake of men, as I formerly did for the sake of Jewish traditions? He wishes to show that he does not fear human hatred but freely defends the truth.

Or am I seeking to please human beings? Wherever human beings are mentioned in Scripture without any qualification, it is understood negatively. As in the saying: “Every human being is a liar”; and: “Who do people say that he is?”; and: “Are you not human beings?”; and: “Are you not walking according to man?” Therefore whoever wishes to please such people must do their will. The saints, however, please God alone and those who love God—those who have deserved to be more than merely human beings.

If I were still pleasing human beings, I would not be Christ’s servant. For that is why they hate me: because I am Christ’s servant.

For I make known to you, brothers, the Gospel that was preached by me. He wishes to clear away the disgrace of usurpation and human tradition.

For it is not according to man. For I neither received it from a human being nor learned it, but through a revelation of Jesus Christ. I did not invent it myself, nor receive it from another human being, nor learn from anyone that the Gentiles would be saved by faith alone.

For you heard of my former conduct in Judaism. Nor, I believe, are you unaware of what I say. He wishes to show how firmly he held to Judaism and how faithfully he attacked the Church for the traditions of his ancestors, so that we may understand that he could not have separated from it by human counsel but only by divine revelation.

For I persecuted the Church of God beyond measure and tried to destroy it, and I advanced in Judaism beyond many of my contemporaries among my own people, being more abundantly zealous for the traditions of my ancestors. Not beyond everyone, lest he should appear boastful.

But when it pleased him who set me apart from my mother’s womb. Here he shows God’s foreknowledge and his love for the Apostle before he was born. Likewise, the one who set me apart from the womb in his foreknowledge, when he wished, brought about what he knew would happen.

And called me through his grace. Not through my merits.

To reveal his Son in me, so that I might preach him among the Gentiles. So that he might reveal his Son to the Gentiles through me.

Immediately I did not consult flesh and blood. He says that, according to the mystery of the revelation, he carried out the preaching of the Gospel entrusted to him; nor did he then heed the voice of flesh and blood, but of God.

Nor did I go up to Jerusalem to those who were apostles before me, but I went away to Arabia; and again I returned to Damascus. Not because it was necessary for me to be taught anything by them, but because I went immediately from Damascus to Arabia to teach what had been revealed to me by God.

Then after three years. He shows that he did not need instruction, since he had already preached for three years to others.

I went up to Jerusalem. When he was attempting to join himself to the disciples.

[Col. 0808C] To see Peter. He shows that he was received by him in love, and that in so short a time he could have learned nothing.

And I remained with him fifteen days. In order to see him, not to learn.

But I saw none of the other Apostles. So that he would not seem to have learned from them either.

Except James, the brother of the Lord. Now concerning what I am writing to you, behold, before God, I do not lie. Who would doubt that brothers are called brothers in four ways? First, by nature; second, by kinship; third, by nation; fourth, by affection. Thus James is called the Lord’s brother according to kinship, because he is shown to have been born of Mary of Clopas, the sister of the Lord’s mother.

Then I came into the regions of Syria and Cilicia. But I was personally unknown to the churches of Judea. It should be noted that for three years he was unknown to the churches of Judea.

Which were in Christ. They had only heard that the one who once persecuted us was now preaching the faith that he once tried to destroy. Those who were from the Jews were regarded as churches separately and were not mixed with those who were from the Gentiles.

And they glorified God because of me. From a very difficult matter arises the greatest astonishment, and God was praised, since he alone could accomplish this. He is speaking of the false brothers and of Peter appointed among the circumcision, while Paul was appointed among the Gentiles.

## CHAPTER II

Then after fourteen years. When the question concerning the burdens of the Law was being raised.

[Col. 0809A] I again went up to Jerusalem with Barnabas, taking Titus also. Not by my own wish, but by the necessity of divine command.

I went up according to revelation. The Apostle says this: “When I came to Jerusalem according to God’s revelation, I gave an account of my preaching to the assembly of the brothers for my edification, privately and to the Apostles—not so that I might be instructed by them, since I had received complete grace, but so that I might make known to them, in proper order, that I was preaching Christ’s Gospel.”

And I laid before them the Gospel that I preach among the Gentiles. I did not learn the Gospel by which the Gentiles are saved by faith alone; I laid it before them.

But privately before those who seemed to be something. So that the disciples would not think to doubt the Gospel.

Lest perhaps I should be running, or had run, in vain. This does not express doubt but rather confirmation.

But not even Titus, who was with me, although he was a Gentile, was compelled to be circumcised. He ran in vain.

But because of the secretly introduced false brothers. He gives the reasons why he circumcised Titus: not because circumcision would benefit him, but so that the impending scandal might be avoided.

Who slipped in to spy out our freedom, which we have in Christ Jesus, in order to reduce us to slavery. From which we have been freed from the yoke of the Law.

To them we did not yield in submission even for an hour, so that the truth of the Gospel might remain with you. So that we might avoid the danger, and so that there might be among us those who would confirm the truth of the Gospel.

But from those who seemed to be something. Here he refers to those who had compelled the Galatians to Judaize—those who had once been distinguished among the disciples of the Apostles and who at that time were turning people from the Christian faith to Jewish observance.

Whatever they once were makes no difference to me. For God does not accept a person’s status. I do not care that they once walked with the Lord, since neither time prejudices the faith nor status the labor.

But those who seemed to be something contributed nothing to me; rather, when they saw that the Gospel of the uncircumcision had been entrusted to me. So that I should preach among the Gentiles, just as the Gospel had been entrusted to them among the Jews.

And to Peter of the circumcision. For the one who worked in Peter for the apostleship of the circumcision also worked in me among the Gentiles. And when they recognized the grace that had been given to me. I am in no respect inferior to him, because we were appointed to the ministry by one God.

James, Cephas, and John, who seemed to be pillars. Upon whom the Church had been established.

They gave the right hand of fellowship. Thus they taught that we ought to teach.

To me and Barnabas, partnership: that we should go to the Gentiles, and they to the circumcision. For both had been sent together to preach to the Gentiles.

Only that we should remember the poor. Those who distributed all their possessions and laid the proceeds at the Apostles’ feet. Or those whose goods had been seized by the Jews, as we read in the Epistle to the Hebrews.

[Col. 0810A] Which I was also eager to do. That is, this is what he writes in almost every Epistle.

But when Cephas came to Antioch, I opposed him to his face, because he was blameworthy. The weakness of the Galatians compels him to relate that he did not spare even Peter, the chief of the Apostles, when he was not openly defending the truth of the Gospel. He also reveals, for the benefit of the Corinthians, the vision that he had concealed for fourteen years. He says all this to show that he had never been an advocate of circumcision, as the false Apostles falsely alleged about him. Hence elsewhere he says: “But if I, brothers, still preach circumcision, why am I still persecuted?”

For before certain people came from James, he ate with the Gentiles. Knowing that it had been shown to him that he should call no person of any kind unclean.

But when they came, he withdrew and separated himself, fearing those who were of the circumcision; and the other Jews joined him in his hypocrisy. He was not blameworthy because he ate with them, but because afterward, for the sake of human beings, he withdrew himself.

So that even Barnabas was led by them into that hypocrisy. He had been sent with me to the Gentiles and had taught that there was no distinction among them.

But when I saw that they were not walking rightly according to the truth of the Gospel. Although he did this because of the Jews’ scandal, I confronted him publicly, so that arrogance among the Jews and despair among the Gentiles might be removed.

I said to Cephas before everyone. A public scandal could not be corrected privately.

[Col. 0810C] If you, though you are a Jew. If you do not observe what you were born into, how do you compel them to observe what they were not born into? He gives a reason; he does not insult him.

Live like a Gentile, and not like a Jew. You know that you have found life in Christ not through the works of the Law but through faith alone, like the Gentiles.

How do you compel the Gentiles to Judaize? Why do you withdraw from them as though they were sinners?

We are Jews by nature and not sinners from the Gentiles. Yet we were sinners, because Scripture confined everything under sin.

But knowing that a person is not justified by works of the Law except through faith in Jesus Christ, we too have believed in Christ Jesus, so that we might be justified by faith in Christ and not by works of the Law. For this reason, by works of the Law no flesh will be justified. The works of the Law are circumcision, the Sabbath, feast days, and other things that were commanded not for righteousness but to tame the people’s hardness.

But if, while seeking to be justified in Christ, we ourselves were found to be sinners, is Christ therefore a minister of sin? Certainly not. For if faith alone does not save the Gentiles, neither does it save us, since no one is justified by works. Therefore we remain sinners, and Christ is a minister of sinners, as though he were unable to forgive sins.

For if I rebuild the things that I destroyed, I constitute myself a transgressor. If I destroyed the Jews and now, as they say, rebuild them, I am found to be a transgressor against my own judgment.

[Col. 0811A] For through the Law I died to the Law. This is what he says: through the Law of Christ I died to the Law of Moses. Or certainly, through that very Law of Moses, I was freed from observance of its regulations, since it is written in that same Law: “Abraham was justified by faith, and not by works of the Law.” Likewise, through the Law of Christ I died to the letter of the Law and to the old Law of Moses, because that Law itself foretold that it would cease.

So that I might live for God. Because he renewed his Law.

I have been crucified with Christ to the cross. I have died to all the sins for which the Law was given; therefore the Law is by no means necessary.

But I live—no longer I. The old human being.

But Christ lives in me. Christ lives in the one in whom Christ gives life to conduct and life itself.

[Col. 0811B] But the life I now live in the flesh, I live in faith in the Son of God. In faith alone, because I owe nothing to the ancient Law.

Who loved me and gave himself for me. Not money or any other price, but himself.

I do not reject the grace of God. I must not be ungrateful to him who loved me so greatly that he even died for me. For grace is rejected if it is not sufficient for me by itself.

For if righteousness comes through the Law, then Christ died for nothing. If the Law could justify, Christ died needlessly.

## CHAPTER III

O foolish Galatians. This is not contrary to the Savior’s command, by which he forbade calling a brother foolish; for here the term is not used without cause.

[Col. 0811C] Who bewitched you? Using a popular expression, he signifies envy, as Solomon says: “The bewitching of vanity obscures good things.”

That you should not obey the truth? Before whose eyes Jesus Christ was publicly displayed. Through my preaching his Passion was so made manifest to you that you might think you saw him hanging before you. He was publicly displayed because he received the sentence of condemnation.

And crucified among you. As though everything had taken place among you. Or: you now regard him as truly condemned and even dead, and despise him, while you think that he is not sufficient for your salvation.

This alone I wish to learn from you. This one thing I ask you.

Did you receive the Spirit from works of the Law, or from hearing [Col. 0811D] with faith? If you received the Spirit through the merit of faith, what more can the Law give us?

Are you so foolish that, having begun with the Spirit, you are now being brought to completion by the flesh? Since even the Jews receive the Spirit in no other way than through faith in Christ, you, by contrast, think that the Spirit is not sufficient for you without the Law.

Have you suffered so many things in vain—if indeed in vain? He shows that, while established in Galatia, they suffered persecution for the faith of Christ. Likewise, you endured so much for Christ in vain if you do not correct yourselves again for Christ. Or, the expression “if indeed in vain” here is not speech expressing doubt but rather confirmation, according to the saying: “If indeed it is just before God to repay those who trouble us with tribulation.”

[Col. 0812A] Therefore, does he who supplies the Spirit to you and works powers among you do so from works of the Law, or from hearing with faith, as it is written? You received the Holy Spirit through faith alone; he is received only by the righteous, and it is clear that you are righteous without the burdens of the Law.

Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness. Thus faith alone is sufficient for you also for righteousness.

Know therefore that those who are of faith are sons of Abraham. Whether Jews or Greeks, they are not circumcised according to the flesh.

And Scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the Gentiles by faith, announced beforehand to Abraham: “In you all the Gentiles shall be blessed.” Not one Jewish nation alone, but all who are from the works of the Law.

Therefore those who are of faith shall be blessed with faithful [Col. 0812B] Abraham. For the Gentiles were not circumcised so that they could be blessed through works.

For all who are of the works of the Law are under a curse. For it is written: the habit of sinning prevailed so greatly that no one now fulfills the Law.

Cursed is everyone who does not persevere in all the things written in the book of the Law, to do them. That is, whoever does not keep all the commandments of the Law, even unto faith. It is rightly asked here whether faith alone is sufficient for a Christian and whether the one who despises the Gospel commandments is not accursed. But faith is effective for this purpose: at the beginning of belief, when people approach God, it justifies them if thereafter they remain in justification. Otherwise, without the works of faith—not the works of the Law—faith is dead. For the Savior also taught that those who do not believe the commandments, and those who despise the precepts of the Gospel, are accursed, saying: “Depart from me, you accursed, into eternal fire.” And the Apostle James demonstrated that the transgressor of one commandment is guilty of all.

But that no one is justified before God by the Law is clear. Because no one keeps it, it was said that believers would be justified by faith alone. He also wishes to show that a person cannot be justified by the works of the Law of Moses unless he also has faith, which grants forgiveness to the one who believes in God. For those who believe in Christ cannot live without the Law.

Because the righteous person lives by faith. Perfect faith is not merely to believe in Christ, but also to believe Christ.

But the Law is not from faith. Faith alone does not justify.

But the one who does these things shall live by them. Let him acquire righteousness through his own labor, and he will live forever.

Christ redeemed us from the curse of the Law, having become a curse for us. He was not under a curse, because he fulfilled the Law in every respect. Therefore, by his undeserved curse our debt was discharged, so that he might free those who pass over to faith.

For it is written: “Cursed is everyone who hangs on a tree.” It is written thus: “If anyone receives the sentence of death, you shall hang him on a tree.” He is not accursed because he hangs; rather, he hangs because he is accursed. Christ, therefore, for whom there was no sentence of death, no cause requiring crucifixion, and no guilt of a curse, accepted a curse for us [Col. 0813A] because we were all accursed, liable to the tree, and therefore accursed because we did not persevere in all the things written in the Law.

So that the blessing of Abraham might come upon the Gentiles in Christ Jesus. So that the Gentiles might be blessed in Christ through faith alone, as had been promised to Abraham.

So that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith. This was promised through the prophet Joel to all flesh, that is, to the entire human race.

Brothers, I speak in human terms: even a human covenant, once confirmed. I use a human example. Human things may be compared with divine things for the sake of clearer understanding; they cannot be made equal to them.

No one rejects it or adds anything to it. The promises were spoken to Abraham and to his seed. He does not say “and to seeds,” as though referring to many, but as though referring to one: “and to your seed,” who is Christ. For the Law was given after so much time.

Now I say this: a covenant confirmed by God. In Christ Jesus.

The Law, which came four hundred and thirty years later, does not annul it so as to nullify the promise. Lest anyone think there is a contradiction, because in the book of Genesis God says to Abraham: “Know beforehand that your seed will be a stranger in a land not its own; they will subject them to slavery and afflict them for four hundred years,” while here the Apostle adds thirty years. What he says is this: in the seventy-fifth year of his age Abraham received the promise from God; from that time until the beginning of the Mosaic Law, four hundred and thirty [Col. 0813C] years are completed in the following manner. From the time of the promise until Abraham’s hundredth year, when Isaac his son was born to him, twenty-five years are counted. Thereafter, in the fifth year of his age, the little Isaac began to be afflicted by Ishmael, as the same Apostle writes in this very Epistle. It is therefore clearly shown that, according to God’s word to Abraham, his seed began to suffer persecution one hundred and thirty years after the promise.

For if the inheritance is from the Law, it is no longer from the promise. But God granted it to Abraham through the promise, not through the Law, which did not yet exist.

Why then the Law? Why, therefore, was the Law given?

It was established because of transgressions, until the seed should come to whom he had made the promise. It was given for this reason: either to compel us or to teach us not to transgress until Christ should come.

Ordained through angels. In this passage he indicates that Moses, the mediator of God and the Hebrews, received the Law through an angel of the Lord, as Stephen says in the book of the Acts of the Apostles: “This is Moses who was in the assembly in the wilderness with the angel who spoke to him on Mount Sinai.” We also frequently read that angels were present with the people through the Law.

In the hand of a mediator. Either Moses, as some think, or Christ. For they say that Moses too was a mediator between God and the people.

But a mediator is not of one alone. That is, of one party.

[Col. 0814A] But God is one. He adds this so that no one would think that Christ was entirely divided from the unity of the divine nature because he had assumed the office of mediator.

Is the Law therefore contrary to the promises of God? Certainly not. For if a Law had been given that could give life, righteousness would truly be from the Law. As he says to the Romans: “What was impossible for the Law, in which it was weakened”—namely, because no one kept it.

But Scripture confined everything under sin, so that the promise might be given to believers through faith in Jesus Christ. With the coming of Christ, those who were under the Law of Moses were confined under sin if they wished to continue beyond that point in observance of the Law. For those who served the shadow of the Law are accursed when the reality is present. He also shows that no one could be found to whom the promise might be given for believers, so that it was necessary for believers to be saved by faith alone.

But before faith came. Before the one came in whom we were to believe.

We were guarded under the Law, confined for that faith which was to be revealed. We were preserved by the Law for this faith, which was to be revealed in its own time.

Therefore the Law was our pedagogue in Christ, so that we might be justified by faith. It held us more tightly under discipline, while reserving perfect instruction for the teacher.

But when faith came, we are no longer under a pedagogue. Disciples of mature age do not need a pedagogue.

For you are all sons of God through faith, which is in Christ Jesus. Jews and Gentiles alike, through faith in Christ Jesus, by which you believed Christ, are sons of God.

[Col. 0814C] For all of you who were baptized into Christ Jesus have put on Christ. Having put on the Son of God and having become entirely his members, you must be sons of God. Why, then, do you need the Law, which was given to slaves and sinners, whose sins have been forgiven through baptism?

There is neither Jew nor Greek; there is neither slave nor free; there is neither male nor female. For you are all one in Christ Jesus. Previously there was great diversity not only between Jew and Greek but also between tribe and tribe.

But if you belong to Christ, then you are Abraham’s seed and heirs according to the promise. If you are all one body of Christ, you are Abraham’s seed and true heirs—not generated from carnal seed but from the divine promise.

## CHAPTER IV

[Col. 0814D]

I say, then: As long as the heir is a child, he differs in nothing from a slave, although he is lord of all; but he is under guardians and administrators until the time appointed by his father. For formerly priests and princes exercised dominion; these he calls guardians and administrators. Now, however, they are commanded not to exercise dominion but to provide an example, because we are a priestly people and have everything in common, although through them we receive the sacraments.

So also we, when we were children, were enslaved under the elements of the world—that is, under days and seasons, which were necessary for their weakness, according to the character of the time.

[Col. 0815A] But when the fullness of time came, God sent his Son. The time had already been fulfilled when, because of evil custom, no one could keep the law.

Made from a woman. By saying “made from a woman,” he signifies sex, not corruption. Moreover, to show clearly that he was born from a virgin, he says “from a woman,” not “through a woman.” In saying “from a woman,” he shows that Christ assumed human incarnation not in the customary manner, from the union of man and woman, but through the Holy Spirit, from the mother alone. For the same Apostle, writing to the Corinthians, says: “As the woman is from the man, so also the man is through the woman.” Therefore, just as at the beginning of generation the woman was taken from the man, so Christ according to the flesh is from the mother alone. But all the remaining human generation [Col. 0815B] is not “from a woman,” according to the Apostle’s statement, but “through a woman,” so that it may be clear that human generation is created from the man through the woman.

Made under the law, in order to redeem those who were under the law. Christ was made under the law so that, conquering sin in the flesh, he might free those who believed in him from the bonds of the law. He remained under the law until, after being baptized, he began to preach the Gospel of the New Testament. Likewise, if he had not been made under the law, he could not have saved the Jews; but, placed under the law, he could redeem the Gentiles.

So that we might receive adoption as sons. For we would not all have received adoption if he had not been made under the law.

But because you are sons of God, God sent the Spirit [Col. 0815C] of his Son into your hearts, crying, “Abba, Father.” From this he proves that we are sons of God: because we have received the Spirit of Christ.

Therefore he is no longer a slave but a son; and if a son, also an heir through God. Why do you wish to be a slave again, when you are already a son and heir? Here too he plainly shows that the whole people is called one son.

But at that time, when you did not know God, you served those who by nature are not gods. He turns to those who had believed from among the Gentiles, and reproves them because they wanted to observe the feast days and seasons of the Jews, just as previously they had done so for idols. For these days were granted to the Jews for this very reason: lest, through their love of festivals, they should offer them to idols.

But now, since you have come to know God—or rather, have been known by God. Previously you were unknown to him, because he does not know [Col. 0815D] the wicked; and you did not seek him, but he sought you when you were lost.

How can you turn back again to the weak and beggarly elements, to which you wish to be enslaved anew? The Apostle clearly shows that the Galatians, after receiving faith in Christ, had returned again to the worship of idols.

You observe days, and months, and seasons, and years. We do not observe them in the same way: for we do not celebrate the Kalends, nor feast days in luxury and banquets, but we feast in sincerity on unleavened bread.

I fear that perhaps I have labored among you in vain. For it profits nothing that you have become Christians if you observe these things again.

Become as I am, because I also am as you are. That is, he says: Imitate me in living as a Gentile, because I too live as a Gentile, having laid aside Jewish observance, just as the Apostle says to the apostle Peter in this same Epistle: “If you, though a Jew, live as a Gentile, how can you compel the Gentiles to Judaize?”

Brothers, I beg you, you have done me no wrong. Thus you may rightly think that I am moved not for the sake of hostility but for the sake of your salvation.

You know that it was because of weakness of the flesh that I preached the Gospel to you formerly. Either because of suffering, or even because of natural weakness, since he carried the treasure of grace in earthen vessels.

And you did not despise or reject your trial in my flesh. The Apostle says this reprovingly, because when he preached the faith of Christ among the Galatians, he suffered persecution [Col. 0816B] from their unbelieving fellow citizens; nevertheless, they allowed the Apostle to remain subject to that trial and to various injuries. It is also a great trial if a holy man is either weakened or injured with impunity. But God permits him to suffer these things so that he may perfect virtue through weakness, and so that, recognizing this corruption, they may seek incorruptible life with greater zeal and love.

But you received me as an angel of God. When he rejoices at being compared with angels, he proves that angels are greater than human beings.

As Christ Jesus. Not merely as an angel.

Where, then, is your blessedness? Which you then received in such a manner.

For I bear you witness that, if it had been possible, [Col. 0816C] you would have torn out your eyes and given them to me. He shows with what great love they had loved him and how completely they had given themselves to his teaching. Indeed, they had desired to surrender to him the most beloved members of their body, judging this alone a worthy return for the Gospel light: that they should give him their own eyes.

So then, have I become your enemy by telling you the truth? Such is the condition of truth: that enmity always follows it, just as friendships are obtained through harmful flattery. For what pleases is willingly heard, while everything we do not want offends. So these too had begun to love the leisure of the Sabbath and the banquets of feast days, praising them against the Apostle, who by his own example showed them every form of self-restraint.

[Col. 0816D] They are zealous for you, but not rightly; rather, they want to exclude you, so that you may be zealous for them. “Zealous one” (*aemulus*) can be understood both as an imitator and as an enemy. Thus one is not rightly zealous when one is zealous to bring another down rather than to advance oneself. “But be zealous for the better gifts.”

But always be zealous for what is good, and not only when I am present with you. Do not imitate them; rather, always be zealous for what is good, and not merely in my presence.

My little children, for whom I am again in labor until Christ is formed in you. This clearly applies against heretics who do not grant repentance to those who sin after baptism. Likewise, Christ is truly formed in the one who understands the power of his faith and in whom his entire manner of life is expressed and portrayed.

But I would like to be with you now. For I cannot write as much as you deserve to hear.

And to change my voice. To change the voice of a kindly father into the severity of an old teacher.

Because I am perplexed about you. The confusion of disciples is the teacher’s confusion, just as their progress is the instructor’s glory. He is perplexed because, having already become sons, they wanted to be slaves again.

Tell me, you who wish to be under the law: have you not read the law? For it is written that Abraham had two sons, one by a slave woman and one by a free woman. But the one from the slave woman was born according to the flesh, while the one from the free woman was born through the promise. Ishmael was of the flesh; Isaac [Col. 0817B] was the son of faith. Abraham begot the former according to carnal usage; he received the latter contrary to nature, through the promise.

These things are spoken allegorically. These things indeed are spoken allegorically—that is, one thing is represented through another. Here the Apostle gives a rule for understanding allegorical interpretations: namely, that while the truth of the history remains, we should explain the figures of the Old Testament. For after saying that Abraham truly had two wives, he then demonstrated what they prefigured. He did the same where honorable deeds of the saints are related, not where sins are condemned. Otherwise, to interpret sins through mysteries is to accuse God either of impossibility or of ignorance. Whoever cannot otherwise display his mysteries—or who at least thinks that the sins of certain people were necessary—should first condemn them generally, and then, by reproving and punishing them, show that he did not wish them to be committed for the sake of his mysteries. Otherwise he will scarcely find the Apostle’s precepts, when explaining them in such a way that he seems to weaken their life.

For these are the two Testaments, the Old and the New, each bringing forth its own people.

One, indeed, at Mount Sinai, bringing forth into slavery. The Jews were compelled by fear of present things, like wild beasts; we, however, are invited by rewards as free people. They, as slaves, were burdened not only with moral precepts but also with various works; for us, as sons, the servile burdens are removed once the moral admonitions have been fulfilled. But they, serving their priests out of obligation, were also compelled to pay taxes [Col. 0817D]; we, owing nothing except love, honor our bishops voluntarily.

Which is Hagar. The synagogue possessed her type.

For Sinai is a mountain in Arabia, joined to the one that is now Jerusalem. By the qualities of the places he wishes the difference between the Testaments to be understood.

And she is in slavery with her children. Along with the children of Jerusalem, she serves the Gentiles.

But the Jerusalem above is free, and she is our mother. The Apostle rightly says that the heavenly Jerusalem is barren in the generation of sons, because she does not generate sons there; rather, here she receives those reborn in Christ through faith, and becomes the mother of those whom she has received. This also stands against the doctrine of those who say that souls are sent down from heaven to earth because of sin and infused into bodies at birth. When he says, “The children of the desolate woman are more numerous than those of her who has a husband,” he signifies by the children of the desolate woman the peoples of the Church gathered from the Gentiles. By the woman who has a husband he attests the synagogue of the Jews, as the prophet Hosea shows: “Judge your mother, judge her, for she is not my wife, and I am not her husband.” Likewise, the Church is the mother both of believing Gentiles and of Jews, whose children cannot be slaves. Therefore the mediator of the New Testament also came from heaven as High Priest, and the Gospel was preached not in one place but throughout the whole world.

[Col. 0818B] As it is written: “Rejoice, barren woman, who do not bear.” By prophetic testimony he proves that we have a better mother than the Jews.

Break forth and cry out, you who do not travail. Here “crying out” stands for prophecy.

Because the children of the desolate woman are more numerous. This was prefigured by Hannah, who said: “The barren woman has borne seven, and she who had many children has grown weak.”

Than those of her who has a husband. She who, thinking that she has a husband, boasts of her fertility—or because she had a husband before she was cast out with her son.

But we, brothers, are children of the promise according to Isaac. Just as the promise was made concerning Isaac, so it was made concerning us: namely, that all the nations would be blessed in him.

[Col. 0818C] But just as at that time the one who was born according to the flesh. Carnal people always persecute those who are spiritual. Therefore it is not surprising if carnal and worldly people now also harass and afflict the saints; indeed, they should be recognized as righteous precisely if they are oppressed by such people.

Persecuted the one who was according to the spirit. In Genesis this is indeed written, because Ishmael had mocked Isaac; but the Apostle shows that it was not a simple game, since he calls it persecution. Ishmael wanted to make Isaac a scoundrel and a frivolous person like himself, so that Isaac could not be preferred to him in the inheritance. Therefore Abraham, casting Ishmael out, orders him to obey Sarah’s voice.

So also now. So these people too strive to make their slaves like themselves.

[Col. 0818D] But what does Scripture say? “Cast out the slave woman and her son, for the son of the slave woman shall not be heir with the son of the free woman.” However much iniquity exalts itself, it is a slave woman and must be subjected to the saints, as must the Jews. Although they boast that they are children of Abraham, as long as they remain children of the slave woman they cannot share the inheritance with us.

Therefore, brothers, we are not children of the slave woman but of the free woman, with the freedom by which Christ set us free. We must not follow the slave woman after abandoning our mother, because although she was the wife of the same man, she was so only for a time, since Sarah’s time for giving birth had not yet come.

CHAPTER V.

Stand firm, and do not again be held by the yoke of slavery. Stand firm in the faith of the Gospel, for the time of the law has already passed [Col. 0819A]; do not drag along with the Jews a yoke that they themselves cannot bear.

Behold, I, Paul, say to you. I say this to you boldly, fearing no one.

That if you are circumcised, Christ will profit you nothing. For you do not think that he alone is sufficient for your salvation.

Again I testify to every person who circumcises himself that he is obliged to perform the whole law. Whoever has accepted the chief work of the law must necessarily bear its other members as well, lest he fall under the curse.

You have been emptied of Christ: you who are justified in the law have fallen from grace. If you place your hope in the law and believe that it can justify you, you judge Christ’s grace to be weak; and what you have already obtained freely, you wish to gain by your own labors, as though you did not possess it [Col. 0819B].

For through the Spirit, by faith, we await the hope of righteousness. By a spiritual way of life and perfected faith, we hope to receive the immortal reward of righteousness.

For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision counts for anything nor uncircumcision. In Christian times neither circumcision benefits nor uncircumcision harms.

But faith that works through love. Therefore faith too works through love, not through fear. For the one who believes God attends to his commandments; the one who believes in future things works more than the one who fears a present punishment.

You were running well. With the steps of faith and moral discipline.

[Col. 0819C] Who hindered you from obeying the truth? Who was the one who entangled you in the works of the law and impeded the course of your faith?

You shall agree with no one. This persuasion is not from the one who calls you. You ought to agree neither with them nor with me without the words of God, who calls you again to repentance.

A little leaven corrupts the whole lump. So that no one might say, “Why do you rebuke everyone, when not everyone has gone astray?” He shows that a little leaven of wickedness can corrupt the whole Church and its entire lump from the truth.

I am confident in you, in the Lord, that you will have no other mind. You will have no other mind than the truth of Christ.

But the one who troubles you will bear the judgment, whoever he may be [Col. 0819D]—judgment away from the truth of the Gospel.

But I, brothers, if I still preach circumcision, why am I still suffering persecution? The deceivers have lied to you about me, saying that I preach it to others. Why am I suffering persecution if I am not an enemy of circumcision itself, as is alleged?

Then the offense of the cross has been abolished? They suffer this offense because I say that salvation lies in faith in the cross alone.

Would that those who trouble you would cut themselves off. If they think this benefits them, let them not merely be circumcised but also cut themselves off; for if the removal of a member is beneficial, its complete abolition is even more so. Some say: “Would that, cut off from error, they might be grafted into the roots of truth.”

[Col. 0820A] For you were called to freedom, brothers; only do not give freedom an opportunity for the flesh. Only do not use the occasion of circumcision to return to the service of the law.

But through love of the Spirit serve one another. I am not introducing pride under the appearance of freedom; rather, I want service to be voluntary, not compelled.

For the whole law is fulfilled in one saying. Even the moral precepts of the law, whatever they are, can be summed up in one saying and fulfilled in this one commandment:

You shall love your neighbor. Love, or charity, consists in four forms: first, love of God; second, loving ourselves according to God; third, loving our neighbors; fourth, loving even our enemies. Therefore we must love God more than ourselves; our neighbor as ourselves; our enemy as our neighbor. The neighbor was loved under the law; and unless we first love God, we cannot love ourselves without sinning. We should love ourselves according to the pattern by which we love our neighbors; and if we do not love our neighbors, when will we be able to love our enemy? If, then, we wish to possess love, let us first love God more than our own souls. This is proved if, for God’s sake, we even disregard our own salvation and our very souls.

[Col. 0820B] As yourself. Whoever loves his neighbor as himself fulfills both kinds of commandments: he neither does evil to anyone but does good.

But if you bite and devour one another. Through quarrels, each judging himself better than the other.

[Col. 0820C] See that you are not consumed by one another. While one becomes an occasion of destruction for the other.

But I say in Christ: Walk by the Spirit. By the spiritual actions that he describes below.

And you will not fulfill the desires of the flesh. Not that the flesh covets without the soul; rather, when the soul itself thinks about carnal things, it is called “flesh,” but when it thinks about spiritual things, it becomes one spirit with God. Therefore, as long as there is a twofold desire or will in us, we do not accomplish whatever we wish, with one part building in us and another destroying.

For the flesh desires against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh. Carnal habit is opposed to spiritual desire.

For these oppose one another, so that you do not do whatever you wish [Col. 0820D]. Reason causes the effect not to follow the will.

But if you are led by the Spirit, you are not under the law. If you occupy yourselves entirely with spiritual actions, you do not need the law, which was given to the carnal.

Now the works of the flesh are manifest. It is not difficult to distinguish between the two kinds of works.

They are fornication, impurity, shamelessness, debauchery, idolatry, sorcery, enmities, quarrels, jealousies, anger, strife, dissensions, factions, envy, murders, drunkenness, revelries, and things like these. He calls enmities and the other things that follow carnal, although they belong to the soul rather than the flesh, lest the Manichaeans think that he was accusing the substance of the flesh. Rather, they define every evil as carnal and every good as spiritual, because heavenly [Col. 0821A].

I warn you, as I warned you before. From these I could have gathered the remaining examples, which I omitted for the sake of brevity.

That those who do such things will not obtain the kingdom of God. It should be noted and mourned that he completely excludes contentious and dissident people, and the angry, together with idolaters, sorcerers, and murderers, from the kingdom.

But the fruit of the Spirit is love. Love is the first of all virtues, which we have noted can be divided into four parts.

Joy. Spiritual joy.

Peace, patience. Even with those who hate peace.

Kindness, goodness. Always wishing to do good.

Forbearance. Patiently enduring injuries inflicted.

[Col. 0821B] Gentleness. Inflicting injury on no one.

Faith. Either you must believe, or fulfill your promises to everyone.

Moderation. Not becoming angry even when injured.

Self-control. In spiritual marriages.

Chastity. It is understood in virgins.

Against such things there is no law. For the law did not prohibit these things; and the one who fulfills the new law is not under the old Testament.

But those who belong to Christ have crucified their flesh with its vices and desires. If all vices have been crucified together, and the flesh, as if hanging on the wood, does not desire, why do we need the law, which was given to restrain vices? It should also be noted that he says those belong to Christ who have crucified the flesh with its vices. This [Col. 0821C] is directed against those who think that faith alone is sufficient.

CHAPTER VI.

If we live by the Spirit, let us also walk by the Spirit. If we have life through the Spirit, let us live spiritually and not serve the law carnally.

Let us not become desirous of empty glory. A person is desirous of empty glory when he tries to nullify another’s teaching, however true it may be, so that he may appear to have more disciples. Such people, however, are accustomed to provoke one another to anger, so long as they do not cease envying one another. Empty glory has another form: if we are all compelled to do things that are not commanded in the law beyond what we actually do, and when we ourselves cannot do them, we call these things superfluous.

[Col. 0821D] Provoking one another, envying one another. If you provoke those who have been deceived to anger by mocking them, and they envy you.

Brothers, even if a person is overtaken in some offense, you who are spiritual should restore such a one in a spirit of gentleness. He says this to those who had not been persuaded, so that they may correct those who have been overtaken, gently. Human frailty is overtaken in those things that are lighter and occur unexpectedly. Otherwise, there is no being overtaken where something is committed with deliberate counsel and long reflection.

Considering yourself, lest you also be tempted. Since you too, being human, can be overtaken in something and need help, just as the healthy support the sick and the living bury the dead, because they too believe that they can become sick and die.

Bear one another’s burdens, and so you will fulfill the law of Christ. The law of Christ is love, as he himself says: “I give you a new commandment, that you love one another, just as I have loved you.” It should be noted that grace is called law.

For if anyone thinks he is something when he is nothing, he deceives himself. This applies to one who thinks he cannot be tempted, or who believes the person praising him more than his own conscience.

But let each person test his own work. By the testimony of conscience.

And then he will have glory in himself alone, and not in another. In his own conscience, and not in another’s [Col. 0822B] flattery; or in his own righteousness, not in another’s sin. No one makes progress to another’s detriment, nor will he appear more righteous because of another’s offense.

For each person will bear his own burden. The praise of the one who follows a faction does not remove his burden.

Let the one who is instructed in the word share all good things with the one who instructs him. Either obedience to the word and imitation in actions, or the substance needed for his livelihood.

Do not be deceived: God is not mocked. A human being can be mocked by the serpent, which denies God’s vengeance, as Eve was. But God brings about what he promises. Indeed, to exclude all the serpent’s cunning, he gave back more to those who first sinned than he had promised, and he did for Lot’s wife even what he had not said he would do.

For whatever a person sows, that he will also reap; because the one who sows in his flesh will reap corruption from the flesh [Col. 0822C]. Whoever places his hope in carnal circumcision, or sows vices, will reap punishment.

But the one who sows in the Spirit will reap eternal life from the Spirit. This is because of spiritual conduct, or faith.

But in doing good, let us not grow weary. As Ecclesiasticus says: “Do not be hindered from praying always, and do not fear being justified unto death, for the Lord’s reward remains forever.” An unfailing reward follows unfailing righteousness, because the one who perseveres to the end will be saved.

For in its proper season we shall reap without failing. Now is the time for sowing, not for reaping.

Therefore, while we have time. This is the final time for sowing. Let us hurry, then, to sow all the fields; [Col. 0822D] but let us fill especially those that are most fertile, lest at harvest time we begin to hunger while others abound.

Let us do good to everyone, but especially to those who belong to the household of faith. Let us show mercy to needy Jews, pagans, and all Christians, good and bad alike; let us deny no one what the Lord has given in common. Yet especially let us show it to those who offer a particular service of faith.

See with what sort of letters I have written to you with my own hand. Understand that I do not fear those to whom I have recently written with my own hand.

For all who wish to please in the flesh compel you to be circumcised, only so that they may not suffer persecution for the cross of Christ [Col. 0823A]. Those who desire to please carnal Jews fear enduring persecution for the cross of Christ.

For even those who are circumcised do not keep the law. If circumcision caused one to keep the law, this persuasion would seem to have some rational basis.

But they wish you to be circumcised so that they may boast in your flesh. So that they may have praise among the Jews because of your flesh, or boast that they have drawn disciples to themselves.

But far be it from me to boast except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world. Not in my own righteousness or teaching, but in the conclusion represented by the cross, through which all my sins have been forgiven, so that I might die to the world and the world to me.

[Col. 0823B] For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision counts for anything nor uncircumcision, but a new creation. At this time only this is beneficial: that one who has been reborn in Christ should live by a new way of life, as the prophet says: “Renew for yourselves a new harvest, and do not sow among thorns.” [Col. 0824A] “Circumcise yourselves for your God, and circumcise the foreskin of your hearts.”

And upon all who follow this rule, peace and mercy. For hope is placed in faith alone for the souls.

And upon the Israel of God. Israel therefore belongs to God; for not all who are from Israel are Israelites.

From now on let no one trouble me. For I bear the marks of the Lord Jesus in my body. Let no one question me any longer as though doubting, because I have explained the whole truth. For I carry on my body signs and marks not of uncircumcision but of the cross and passion.

The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit, brothers. Amen. Such is the Apostle’s subscription. He wishes the grace of the Lord, not the works of the law, to accompany them. At the same time, observe that he says “with your spirit,” not “with your flesh,” in whose circumcision carnal people boast; but you should live spiritually, as those circumcised spiritually.

ON THE EPISTLE TO THE EPHESIANS.

[Col. 0823]

CHAPTER I.

[Col. 0823B]

Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ through the will of God. Not through my own merits.

To all the saints. All saints are faithful, but not all the faithful are saints. For catechumens too can be called faithful because they believe in Christ [Col. 0823C], yet they are not saints because they have not been sanctified through baptism. Or it should be understood in this way: he writes to those who faithfully preserve the grace of holiness.

Who are at Ephesus, and to the faithful in Christ Jesus. Not to all the Ephesians, but to those who believe in Christ.

Grace to you and peace. Grace will benefit you if you are not ungrateful toward it, attributing your salvation to your own merits. We shall preserve the peace of reconciliation if henceforth we do nothing contrary to his goodness or justice.

From God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. He demonstrates that the Father and the Son are one, working together equally.

Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ. He praises God because he has granted what follows.

[Col. 0823D] Who blessed us with every spiritual blessing. Not with only some, but with all the spiritual blessings of grace, so that just as nothing is lacking in us from him, so nothing may be lacking in us with respect to his will.

In the heavenly places. Not in carnal prosperity or earthly abundance.

In Christ. He blessed all the members in the head. Just as he chose us in him before the foundation of the world, so that we might be holy and blameless. For nothing is new to him with whom all things existed before they were made—not as certain heretics dream, that souls were previously separated in heaven.

In his sight. Not in the sight of human beings.

[Col. 0824B] In love. He did this because God loves the blameless.

Who predestined us for adoption as sons. He predestined this: that human beings who wished to believe should have the power to become sons of God, as it is written: “They spoke the word with confidence to everyone willing to believe” [Col. 0824C].

Through Jesus Christ into himself. So that we might be his members.

According to the purpose of his will. Not according to our merits.

For the praise of the glory of his grace. So that we may praise the glory of his grace.

By which he made us accepted in his beloved Son. In this grace he made us pleasing to himself in Christ.

In whom we have redemption through his blood, for the forgiveness of sins, according to the riches of his grace. He not only redeemed us but also forgave our sins; without our labor he makes us righteous, according to the riches of his glory.

Which he made abound toward us in all wisdom and prudence, making known to us the mystery of his will [Col. 0824D], according to his good pleasure, which he purposed in him. He made it abound beyond measure, so that he not only freely forgave the sins of those redeemed from death, but also gave us such great wisdom that we might know the hidden mysteries of his will.

In the dispensation of the fullness of times. In the last times, when every dispensation of the times of the law, of nature, and of the prophets had already passed.

To restore all things in Christ, those in heaven and those on earth, in him. Many have offered different interpretations of this matter. Some say that “heaven” means souls and “earth” bodies. Others say that “heaven” means the Jews, who had heavenly commandments, while “earth” means the Gentiles. Others assert that heaven does not signify angels but their knowledge, since from the time of Christ they progressed, having asked as though ignorant, “Who is this King of glory?” and being taught that he is the Lord of hosts. But since restoration is not spoken of except with regard to something fallen, it is better to say that their joy was restored in the salvation of human beings—the joy they had before human beings completely turned away from righteousness. No one is unaware that on earth the human race was restored through Christ.

In whom we too were called by lot. We who believe from among the Jews.

Predestined. Through faith, or foreknown.

According to his purpose. He purposed to restore all things [Col. 0825B], but first the lost sheep of the house of Israel.

Who works all things. The will of God is the cause of all these things; there is no doubt that it is reasonable.

According to the counsel of his will. Not according to our merits.

So that we might be for the praise of his glory. So that through our conduct and the signs we perform, glory may be given to God.

We who previously hoped in Christ. We apostles, or the Jews, who believed in Christ first, or who awaited him from the law.

In whom you too, when you heard the word of truth, the Gospel of your salvation. In whom salvation was also announced to you Gentiles.

[Col. 0825C] In whom, believing. In this Gospel, or in Christ.

You were sealed with the Holy Spirit of promise, who is the pledge of our inheritance. From this you are recognized as being one, because you have received the same Spirit, whose signs are the pledge of the inheritance to come. If raising the dead is a pledge, how great will that possession be! The pledge, however, produces faith in the promises through the Spirit of promise, who was not promised to the flesh.

For the redemption of the acquired possession, to the praise of his glory. Those whom he acquired by redeeming them with his blood, so that in this too we may praise his glory.

Therefore I too, having heard of your faith, which is in Christ Jesus. How firmly you maintain faith in Jesus.

And your love for all the saints. That is, you prove your faith by works and love all good people without exception of person or acquaintance. We are commanded, however, to beware of false prophets, not to believe every spirit, and not to judge before testing.

I do not cease giving thanks for you, making mention of you in my prayers. Not as some do amid the pleasure of a banquet; for me nothing is more pleasurable than prayer.

That the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of glory, may give you a spirit of wisdom and revelation. It should be noted that wisdom is preached by the Lord to those who possess faith and love, for he knew it to be the helper of the virtues.

For the knowledge of him. How does he wish them to know God, whom they already knew to such an extent that, believing in him, they loved all the saints for his sake? But he asks that they should perfectly recognize his greatness and power, by which he is able to fulfill the promised rewards or punishments in their full magnitude. Since he is everywhere, nothing at all can be hidden from him. Whoever knows this with certainty will be unable to sin in any place; for the one who blushes before human testimony can revere divine testimony much more. Hence the sons of Eli, although they were priests, are said not to have known God, because they did not fear his presence and power at all. The Apostle John also confirms that everyone who sins has not known God.

The eyes of your heart having been enlightened. Spiritual promises are perceived only by spiritual eyes.

So that you may know what is the hope of his calling and what are the riches [Col. 0826B] of the glory of his inheritance among the saints. If you knew to what great hope you have been called, you would easily despise every hope of the world; and if you saw the riches of God’s inheritance, every earthly inheritance would horrify you. For no one who hopes to be a steward of a kingdom together with its wealth is content to possess a modest estate.

And what is the surpassing greatness of his power toward us who believe, according to the working of the might of his power, which he worked in Christ Jesus, raising him from the dead. The whole greatness of God’s powers surpasses nature and the law, because he granted Christians this: that he did not spare his Son, but, having made him our head, placed him at his right hand in the heavenly places.

[Col. 0826C] And placing him at his right hand in the heavenly places. Here “right hand” signifies honor, lest God be thought corporeal. For the Father too is written to be at Christ’s right hand: “The Lord at your right hand has shattered kings in the day of his wrath.” Therefore both are at the right hand, because there is nothing left-handed in divinity.

Above every principality, authority, power, and dominion. Because the human being who was raised has now been taken up as one with God.

And every name that is named—not only in this age but also in the one to come. If there is any other one.

And he subjected all things under his feet. And he gave him as head over the whole Church, which is his body, and his fullness. The Church is the fullness of all its members.

[Col. 0826D] He who is filled in all things. When all shall believe, then his body will have been brought to completion in all its members. For he is wholly present in the members, not fulfilled in individuals, so that there may be no inequality of merits.

## CHAPTER II

And he made you alive together with him, when you were dead in your trespasses and sins.
