He begins to recount the benefits bestowed, so that, in accordance with the duty imposed by the commandments, they may be stirred more eagerly by contemplation of the mercy granted. For they were dead through sins that acted in them, just as Adam and Eve lived amid delights.

In which you once walked. It should be noted that he says they walked in sins, not that they walk in them.

[Col. 0827A] According to the age of this world. Following the pleasure of the devil, like the people of this age.

According to the prince of the power of this air, the spirit. According to the prince of that power who, with the satellites of this air, possessed great power for deceiving human beings through various sins.

Who now works in the children of distrust. He works by persuasion, not by force, in those who believe. But those who despair and distrust the promise of God are called children of disobedience, just as there are children of wrath, Gehenna, and death.

Among whom we all once lived. Not only you Gentiles, by refusing to believe, but also we Jews, by sinning.

In the desires of our flesh, doing the will of the flesh and of our thoughts. When our mind clung to earthly and fleshly things, we not only desired [Col. 0827B] whatever evil thought had suggested, but also did it.

And we were by nature children of wrath, as were the others. The custom of ancestral tradition had so possessed us that we seemed all to be born for condemnation.

But God, who is rich in mercy. Merciful toward human beings, because you love everything that you have made; for you established nothing while hating it.

Because of his very great love with which he loved us. Very great love is to love rebellious servants as though they were sons. From this one should consider how greatly he loves the saints and the perfect, since he deigned to love sinners so greatly.

[Col. 0827C] [Col. 0827D] And when we were dead in sins, he made us alive together with Christ. By making us, through baptism, without sin like Christ.

By whose grace you have been saved. On account of the work—or because he, by grace, died for you, with no merit of your righteousness intervening, although he himself was not guilty.

And he raised us up together and made us sit together in the heavenly places, in Christ Jesus. We cannot despair, since our nature already possesses this reality: where the head is, there also will be the body, just as he himself says, “I desire that where I am, these also may be with me.”

So that he might show in the ages to come. He predestined beforehand what he was going to complete in these times.

The abundant riches of his grace. Truly abundant is the grace that not only forgave sins, but also, raising us with Christ, placed us at the right hand of God in the heavenly places.

In goodness toward us in Christ Jesus. By example, or in the body of Christ.

For by grace you have been saved, through faith, and this is not from yourselves. Not by the merits of an earlier life, but by faith alone—yet not without faith.

For it is God’s gift, not from works, so that no one may boast. As though someone had received something in baptism by his own merits.

For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared so that we might walk in them. Because we have recently been reborn in Christ, so that we might practice what is taught in the Gospels. [The transmitted reading “io Evangeliis” is evidently corrupt.]

[Col. 0828A] Therefore remember that once you Gentiles in the flesh. He recalls these things so that they may not be ungrateful for the benefits of the giver, having been led from such great disgrace to the highest dignity of the kingdom.

You who were called the uncircumcision by what is called the circumcision. The Gentiles were called “the uncircumcision,” and the Jews “the circumcision.”

Made in the flesh by hands. By human hand: in flesh, not in the Spirit of God or in the heart.

You were at that time without Christ. Not knowing Christ, you worshiped insensible idols.

Alienated from the commonwealth of Israel. Israel was then the people of God.

And strangers to the covenants. Even if you had believed, you were regarded as proselytes—that is, as newcomers.

Having no hope of the promise. The promise that God made to Abraham; they alone seemed to have hope in it.

[Col. 0828B] And without God in this world. By following many false gods, they had lost the one true God.

But now in Christ Jesus, you who once were far away have been brought near. So that you might follow the Jews, who were with God.

In the blood of Christ. By believing that you had been freed through his blood and passion.

For he himself is our peace, who made both one. He is the reconciliation of both peoples with one another and with God.

And the middle wall of the dividing fence. The middle wall, hedge, and barrier were the burdens of the law, dividing the two peoples; and therefore that wall is called the wall of hostility.

Abolishing the hostility in his flesh. The circumcision and the other practices that had been demanded not so much by God’s will as by the circumstances of the time or the hardness of the people.

[Col. 0828C] Making void the law of commandments by decrees. Justifying by faith alone, and prescribing only moral requirements.

So that he might create the two in himself. Joining Jew and Gentile equally in his own body.

Making peace in one new man. Making one Christian people out of the two.

So that he might reconcile both in one body to God. Because both had been enemies through sin.

Killing the hostility in himself through the cross. Through the sole faith of the cross, which deters no one; for it is neither burdensome nor difficult, since even the crucified robber could possess it.

And coming, he proclaimed peace to you who were far away, and peace to those who were near. He came for this purpose: to call the divided [Col. 0828D] human race back to the grace of reconciliation, both in himself and with God.

For through him we both have access in one Spirit to the Father. “No one comes to the Father except through me.” In one Spirit there is one body, one spirit, and the sign of peace.

Therefore you are no longer strangers and newcomers, but fellow citizens with the saints and members of God’s household. No longer outsiders and proselytes; for God did not separate us from his people, as Isaiah said. Rather, we are citizens who share the same origin, household, and dwelling.

Built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, with Christ Jesus himself as the chief cornerstone, in whom the whole structure is constructed. The prophets [Col. 0829A] of the New Testament—among whom was Agabus—also have Christ as their foundation. He is likewise called the cornerstone, joining and holding together the two walls. He is therefore both foundation and summit, because the Church is founded and brought to completion in him.

It grows into a holy temple in the Lord. Only holy stones can be placed in a holy temple. He said that Christ’s body—that is, the Church—was constructed in comparison with the temple of Jerusalem; and reality possesses far greater purity and holiness than the image.

In him you also are built together into a dwelling place of God in the Holy Spirit. So that, together with the apostles and prophets, you may be God’s spiritual dwelling, not made by hand.

## CHAPTER III

[Col. 0829B] For this reason. The matter mentioned above: that the Son of God saved both Gentiles and Jews and made the two one.

I, Paul, a prisoner of Christ Jesus. Whether bound by chains or bound by love for Christ, I cannot do anything but the Lord’s will. Indeed, the way he calls himself a prisoner confirms the gospel of Christ. He shows how great is the hope for which he gladly embraces such sufferings, although among the Jews, as a teacher of the law, he could have possessed great wealth and enjoyed the highest honor.

For you Gentiles. According to the gospel, an enemy on your account, because we say that you are to be made like the Jews.

If indeed you have heard of the administration of God’s grace that was given to me for you. If indeed you firmly retain that I received among you the administration of the teaching. For who is the faithful and prudent servant [Col. 0829C] whom the Lord appointed over his household, to give them food at the proper time?

For according to revelation. Not according to human teaching.

The mystery was made known to me, as I wrote above. Namely, that Jews and Gentiles are one in Christ.

In brief, as you can understand my insight when you read. Not as much as I was able to write, but as much as you were able to grasp.

In the ministry of Christ. Not in worldly eloquence.

Which was not made known to the sons of men in other generations, as it has now been revealed to his holy apostles and prophets. The prophets certainly knew that the Gentiles would first be called; but they did not know that there would be no distinction between them and the Jews.

[Col. 0829D] That the Gentiles are fellow heirs in the Spirit. Through the Spirit revealed to me; or, that they have been joined in the Spirit, not by circumcision of the flesh.

And members of the same body, and fellow participants in the promise in Christ Jesus. That is, of one body—not merely fellow heirs, since people of different kinds could be fellow heirs; nor merely members of the same body, since sons of the same kind may nevertheless not share the same inheritance.

Through the gospel, of which I became a minister. Through my preaching it will become known to all, because this was specially revealed to me.

According to the gift of God’s grace that was given to me. Not according to my merit.

According to the working of his power. His power [Col. 0830A] strengthened me; or, his mighty works confirm my gospel.

For this grace was given to me, the least of all the saints. “Least” in time, not in labor. It should be noted that by humbling himself among the saints he made himself pleasing.

To proclaim among the Gentiles the unsearchable riches of Christ. To announce the future inheritances and the promised riches, which human understanding cannot grasp except through revelation.

And to enlighten everyone concerning the administration of the mystery. To disclose to Jews and Gentiles the meaning of this mystery.

Hidden from the ages in God. That is, in the earliest times it had been confirmed to God alone.

Who created all things. Both Jews and Gentiles; or every creature, so that the meaning may prevail against Marcion and all heretics.

[Col. 0830B] So that the manifold wisdom of God might be made known to the principalities and powers in the heavenly places through the Church. So that through me the manifold wisdom might be made known to those who exercise authority over heavenly matters throughout the whole Church.

According to the predetermination of the ages that he made in Christ Jesus our Lord. This is what they predetermine even in the present time, when people can no longer be saved in any other way except by being saved through faith in Christ.

In whom we have boldness and access with confidence through faith in him. Not through our righteousness, but through him whose faith forgave sins.

For this reason I ask that you not lose heart in my tribulations for you, which are your glory. Do not suppose, when you hear that I am suffering [Col. 0830C] injury with impunity, that I do not belong to God. Rather, you ought to glory in this, understanding that I could not endure such things without a firm confidence in hope.

For this reason I bend my knees before the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, from whom every family in heaven and on earth receives its name. From him every fatherhood has received its name; or, from him every entity is called “father.”

That he may grant you, according to the riches of his glory, to be strengthened with power through his Spirit. That through illumination of knowledge he may confirm you in the fruit of his riches.

That Christ may dwell through faith in your hearts, in the inner person. Wherever the inner person is strengthened through faith, there Christ dwells—not where the outer person is pampered.

Rooted and founded in love. So that they may stand [Col. 0830D] firmly in his love. He recalls his benefits so that, once they know his benefits, they may love him.

So that you may comprehend. So that you may be able to attain the magnitude of knowledge from every side.

With all the saints. “Seek wisdom among the wicked, and you will not find it.” And elsewhere: “But in the heart of the good wisdom rests.”

What is the breadth and length and height and depth. Some say that “breadth” means the spacious way; “length,” eternal life; “height,” heaven; and “depth,” hell—so that, possessing knowledge of all these things, they may know what to love and what to reject.

[Col. 0831A] And to know the love of Christ that surpasses knowledge. Its fruit surpasses knowledge.

So that you may be filled with all the fullness of God. So that you may become full of every virtue.

Now to him who is able to do exceedingly abundantly beyond all that we ask or understand, according to the power that works in us. He frequently grants greater things, not only than we ask, but even than we understand how to ask, according to what works in us.

To him be glory in the Church and in Christ Jesus. Because, when Christ came, he gathered the Church for the glory of God.

Throughout all generations of the age of ages. Amen. Immense benefits are to be celebrated with immense praises—not only those he bestowed in the times of Christ, but also those he bestowed before and will bestow hereafter. Amen.

## CHAPTER IV

[Col. 0831B]

Therefore I, a prisoner in the Lord, urge you to walk worthily of the calling with which you were called. I, who am imprisoned for your sake, ask you, recognizing the Son of God, to conduct yourselves worthily of so great an honor; for there is one dignity by which those who recognize it are acknowledged as belonging to its proper institutions.

With all humility and gentleness, with patience. Of both mind and body. True humility claims nothing for itself; the gentle harm no one; the patient return injury to no one.

Bearing with one another in love. Philosophers too have endured, but not in love. We, however, must bear with those whom we support not in order to be praised, but because we love them and want the one whom we endure [Col. 0831C] to make progress.

Taking care to preserve the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace. Through the bond of peace the unity of the Spirit is maintained among you. For the multitude of believers had one heart and one soul.

One body and one Spirit, just as you were called in one hope of your calling. One Lord, one faith, one baptism. The joining of all the members in one body, called to one hope of salvation, ought to have one harmony. Therefore those who, bound by worldly occupations, think that they may sin while others may not, should read this passage more carefully, since all were baptized into one body, received the same Spirit, and were called by God in one hope. Or understand it this way: if you have one Spirit and were born from one [Col. 0831D] Father, God, do not arrogate to yourselves anything on the basis of earthly nobility, lest you lose your glory.

One God and Father of all. Including those from the Gentiles who have believed.

Who is over all, and through all, and in us all. He is over all virtues as the powerful one; through all his works; and immeasurable among all Christians, according to whom he deigns to dwell.

But grace was given to each one of us. There are not many bodies because of the variety of graces, but different members.

According to the measure. Not so much according to our capacity as according to that of the giver.

[Col. 0832A] Of Christ’s gift. Whoever adapts himself to this grace attains it. For example, the diligent student of the law receives much wisdom; to the one who prays and fasts, the power of the Spirit is granted.

Therefore he says: “Ascending on high, he led captivity captive; he gave gifts to human beings.” Those whom the devil held captive for death, Christ took captive for life, so that he might place our head in the heavenly places.

But what does “he ascended” mean except that he also descended? He explains why he is said to have ascended, although there is no doubt that he is nowhere absent. This is according to the form of a servant, to which he had descended—not locally, but in his dignity.

First into the lower parts of the earth. No one now doubts that hell is beneath the earth.

[Col. 0832B] He who descended is also the one who ascended above all the heavens. He who descended with his soul into hell ascended with soul and body into heaven.

So that he might fill all things. With glory those who triumph; or, he fulfilled what had been written, when humanity had already become one with divinity.

And he himself gave some as apostles, some as prophets. This is against the Arians, so that the operation of the Son and the Father may be one. For in the Letter to the Corinthians he says that God the Father appointed these offices in the Church; here, however, he recalls that Christ appointed them.

And others as evangelists. Every apostle is an evangelist, but not every evangelist is an apostle, as in the case of Philip, who was one of the seven.

[Col. 0832C] And others as pastors and teachers. All pastors are those capable of instructing others. Thus every pastor is a teacher, but not everyone who is a teacher is a pastor.

For the perfecting of the saints, for the work of ministry, for the building up of the body of Christ. So that the saints may be perfected, or their number completed. All have been appointed for building up the Church, which is Christ’s body, so that they may lead all to perfection of faith.

Until we all come into the unity of faith. This wish is also present in false teachers: that is, “I want everyone to be like me.”

And of the knowledge of the Son of God. The one who does not sin has recognized the grace of the Son of God; for everyone who sins neither sees him nor has known him.

[Col. 0832D] To a perfect man, to the measure of the stature of the fullness of Christ. Whoever says that he remains in Christ ought to walk as Christ walked, and imitate not the number of his years but his fullness.

So that we may no longer be children, tossed about and carried around by every wind of doctrine. So that we may not be ignorant, doubtful, and wavering, setting the sails of our faith, like an inexperienced helmsman, toward every doctrinal wind, lest we be easily shipwrecked or never reach the harbor of perfection.

By the wickedness of human beings, by craftiness. The wickedness of human beings turns the unwary away from the straight course of faith through crafty arguments.

For the circumvention of error. Either because many think that the [Col. 0833A] remedy for their error lies in dragging many others into error with them, or because, promising those who err a remedy without effort, they make them remain in error.

But practicing the truth in love. Doing everything in the truth for the sake of Christ’s love, and doing nothing in hypocrisy.

Let us grow in him in all things. Let us grow in every respect into his perfection.

Christ, who is the head: from him the whole body, joined and connected through every supporting joint according to its working, grows. The body joined to its head grows through every connection of its operation, while the members build one another up by loving one another, so that each member may increase according to its measure. That is, the one who is an eye through wisdom may grow into the number of those who are to perform the office of an eye [Col. 0833B], and each of the members may make progress.

According to the measure of the growth of each individual member, the body makes its increase for its own building up in love. As the individual members grow, the body becomes greater.

Therefore I say this and testify in the Lord. Those whom he had earlier entreated, he now binds by an appeal made in the Lord.

That you no longer walk as the Gentiles walk. “I do not want you,” he says, “to be Christians in name only, confessing God with your mouth while denying him by your deeds. Rather, just as there is a difference between the devil and God, so great a difference ought to distinguish the children of God from the children of the devil in their works. Do not honor God with your lips while standing far away through fear in your heart, so that it may be said of you: ‘They worship me [Col. 0833C] in vain’—that is, they will receive no fruit from my worship.”

In the vanity of their understanding. For all human beings in whom there is no wisdom of God are vain.

Having their understanding darkened by darkness. That is, darkened by ignorance and by the gloom and darkness of anxieties concerning worldly things.

Alienated from the life of God. They were alienated from the life of God because they were ignorant; but you, because you have known God, ought to follow him.

Through the ignorance that is in them. It should be noted that contempt generated ignorance.

Because of the blindness of their hearts. They say, “There is no God.”

Who, having despaired, handed themselves over to shamelessness. [Col. 0833D] Despairing of the punishment of the wicked and the reward of the righteous, they must cling to present pleasures, since they despair of the future: “Come, and let us enjoy the good things that exist,” and so forth.

In the practice of every impurity, toward greed. He encompasses all crimes under the names of impurity and greed.

But you did not learn Christ in this way, if indeed you heard him and were taught in him. And do not live according to the Gentile manner. For the one who truly heard Christ and learned from him is one who is found to resemble the Gentiles in no vice.

As the truth is in Jesus. Just as he truly died and rose, so that we might truly walk in newness of life.

[Col. 0834A] Put off the old person according to your former way of life. He explained what the old person is and how it is put off: namely, that one should cast away the former errors of this world and be changed not in the members of the body but in mind and conduct.

Who is being corrupted according to the desires of error. Doing the will of carnal thoughts.

But be renewed in the spirit of your mind. As Jeremiah says: “Make for yourselves a new heart and a new spirit.”

And put on the new person. Understand “new” in contrast with “old.”

Who was created according to God in righteousness and holiness of truth. He explained what it means for a person to be created in the image of God: namely, to be righteous, holy, and [Col. 0834B] truthful like God; to be endowed with the holiness of truth, not of vanity—that is, not one that seeks the empty glory of human beings, since it is written: “You shall pursue what is just, and only what is just.”

Therefore, having put away falsehood. The very forms of chastity by which the new person is recognized are described here.

Speak the truth, each one with his neighbor, because we are members of one another. Let no one deceive his brother, because we are one body and the members cannot deceive one another. For neither does the hand mock the eye, nor do the teeth tear the members—unless perhaps an unclean spirit dwells there.

Be angry, and do not sin. Let anger not intoxicate the mind, but let truth govern it; and do not take notice of your own injury, but [Col. 0834C] of your brother’s sin.

Let not the sun go down upon your anger. Do not let the light of knowledge fail during your indignation.

Do not give place to the devil. By anger or by any other offense. For sin is the devil’s door, just as a righteous person is the door of the Holy Spirit.

Let the one who stole steal no longer; rather, let him labor. Let him compensate by his own labor for what he once seized from others, and by working let him give to those in need—he who by stealing made many needy.

Working with his hands what is good, so that he may have something to give to one suffering need. Not what is evil. For there are many dishonest or evil occupations, such as magic and everything that serves not the necessities of nature but the pleasure of desires.

[Col. 0834D] Let no evil word proceed from your mouth. Not one or two, but every evil word: in this Christians ought to be crucified.

But if there is anything good for the building up of faith. He did not impose silence, but showed the proper quality of speech, so that every word might build up Christian faith and our mouth might seek only the word of God. It should also be noted that this is commanded to the whole Church.

So that it may give grace to those who hear. This is what he says elsewhere: “Let your speech always be gracious, seasoned with salt”; and let those who hear receive grace through our speech.

And do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God. Speaking to human beings, he introduces a human comparison, so that from ourselves we may understand how great an injury [Col. 0835A] we inflict on the Holy Spirit when we pollute his gift with some stain of sin. And because he grieves for us over his lodging, he departs sorrowfully, grieving for himself. Otherwise, grief, anger, and other such things are passions in us, because we are capable of suffering; in God, however, they are acts of providential administration. We suffer these things unwillingly, whereas he assumes them willingly for our correction. This is the diversity and nature of these states, which concerns God and human beings.

In whom you were sealed for the day of redemption. You received the seal of the Holy Spirit on the day of baptism; you began to possess a new seal.

All bitterness. By which the Holy Spirit is grieved. He rightly placed bitterness, because it is itself the provocation.

And anger. He removes every kind of anger.

[Col. 0835B] And indignation. Indignation arises from pride, when we judge someone unworthy; therefore we do not wish to tolerate him.

And shouting. This descends from rage, which Christians should not possess. Isaiah, however, is rightly commanded to shout. Jesus himself also shouted in the temple: “Let the one who thirsts come, and let him drink.”

And let blasphemy be removed from you, together with every kind of malice. Malice that can repay even an enemy in kind.

But be kind to one another. He preserves the order of the law, so that not only malice may be removed, but kindness may also be implanted.

Compassionate. That is, sharing one another’s suffering.

Forgiving one another, just as God in Christ forgave you. Forgiving sins, lest it be said to you: “Wicked servant [Col. 0835C], I forgave you all your debt; ought you not also to have forgiven your fellow servant?”

## CHAPTER V

Therefore be imitators of God, as beloved children. We are sons of God by imitation, not by nature, as the Savior says: “So that you may be sons of my Father who is in heaven,” and so forth.

And walk in love, just as Christ also loved us. Hence the apostle John says: “By this we have known love: that he laid down his life for us.” Therefore we too ought to lay down our lives for our brothers.

And he handed himself over. He handed himself over voluntarily; he was not unwillingly handed over by another.

[Col. 0835D] For us. For sinners, so that they might become righteous.

As an offering and sacrifice to God for a fragrant aroma. Love is the sweetest fragrance to God.

But fornication, and every impurity, or greed. He briefly encompasses all crimes by indicating the roots of two crimes.

Let them not even be named among you, as is fitting for saints. It should be considered impermissible to do what it is impermissible even to name.

Or obscenity, or foolish talk. This too is censured among human beings of good character.

Or buffoonery, which does not pertain to the matter. Causing laughter in a way that does not suit Christian seriousness, because it does not pertain to heavenly or divine matters.

[Col. 0836A] But rather thanksgiving. You ought always to concern yourselves more with how to please God both in action and in thought.

For know this and understand: every fornicator or greedy person, who is an idolater, has no inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and God. He argues against those who say that faith alone is sufficient, because such acts are offered not to God but to the demon. The inheritance of the kingdom of heaven is prepared for God’s children, not the devil’s.

Let no one deceive you, saying that this alone is necessary: that there be faith and that a person receive Christ’s baptism; even if he sins, he cannot perish.

With empty words. Words that cannot set a person free.

[Col. 0836B] For because of these things the wrath of God comes. Learn the future from the past: if he did not spare the Sodomites and those who perished in the flood, will he spare you?

Upon the children of distrust. Those who did not believe that the threatened wrath would come upon them.

Therefore do not become their partners. If you become partners in the judgment of those who despair through sins, you will share their punishment.

For you were once darkness, but now you are light in the Lord. Walk as children of light. This was when you did not know the Lord’s will; now you know everything. As great as the difference is between light and darkness, so great should be the difference between your former conduct and your present conduct.

For the fruit of light consists in all goodness, righteousness, and truth. Knowledge bears such fruit.

[Col. 0836C] Testing what is pleasing to God. Test from the law what is pleasing to God, not what human beings assert.

And do not participate in the unfruitful works of darkness. Whatever is done without knowledge of the truth is of no benefit, because light cannot participate with darkness.

Rather, reprove them. Do not merely refuse to participate, but also reprove them.

For the things they do in secret. In the hidden places of houses or of the temple.

It is shameful even to speak of them. It is shameful for us to speak of the things that they do without shame even in darkness.

But everything that is reproved is made manifest by the light. As he says to the Corinthians: “The secrets of his heart are also made manifest.” And then, falling on his face, you will worship God, declaring that God truly is among us.

[Col. 0836D] For everything that is made manifest is light. It begins to be light when someone believes and is joined to you.

Therefore he says: “Rise, you who sleep.” With the voice of some wise person who desires to strike the conscience of an unbeliever, he awakens him from the sleep of ignorance.

And rise from the dead. From sins or idols.

And Christ will shine upon you. When you believe in him, you too will become light.

Therefore, brothers, see carefully how you walk—not as unwise people, but as wise. As children of wisdom and light, so that you do not give offense to anyone and begin to become a cause of that person’s destruction.

Redeeming the time. By your wisdom or caution.

Because the days are evil. The days are not evil in themselves [Col. 0837A], but because of human beings, just as a place is called evil in which something evil is committed.

Therefore do not become foolish, but understand what the will of God is. Search the law, in which his will is recognized.

And do not become drunk with wine, in which there is debauchery; rather, be filled with the Holy Spirit. He explains the usefulness of self-restraint. Those who have been crucified ought not to seek the material for debauchery, but to be filled with the Holy Spirit.

Speaking to one another in psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs. Not in the deeds of the world, as the prophet says: “So that my mouth may not speak of the works of human beings.”

Singing and making melody in your hearts. So that we do not merely cause the words of God to resound with our mouths.

Always giving thanks to the Lord for everything in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Whether for good things or bad things, as Job says: “Blessed be the name of the Lord.”

[Col. 0837B] To God and the Father. Be subject to one another in the fear of Christ. Not through human fear or the pursuit of greed, as some are accustomed to flatter their patrons.

Let wives be subject to their husbands. He did not feed them with milk, as he fed the Corinthians, but nourished them with the solid food of self-restraint. For he fears that, when the marital duty of the flesh has ceased in many, either submission in wives or affection in husbands might also cease, and that he might be thought to have taught divorce. Otherwise, his meaning is that, as a preacher of the new life, he would teach what they naturally possessed even though no cause existed.

As to the Lord. Just as Sarah was subject to Abraham, calling him “lord.”

[Col. 0837C] Because the husband is the head of the wife, just as Christ is the head of the Church, he himself being the Savior of his body. But just as the Church is subject to Christ, so also wives are subject to their husbands in everything. He gives a just reason for submission: the husband is first, and he ought to be the savior of both bodies.

Husbands, love your wives, just as Christ also loved the Church. With such holy and venerable love.

And he handed himself over for her. So you too should not refuse, if necessary, even to die for the holiness of your wives.

So that he might sanctify her, cleansing her by the washing of water in the word of life. Water washed the body, and teaching cleansed the soul, as he says to the Hebrews: “Having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience and our body washed with clean water.” So you too should cleanse the bodies of your wives and their souls, which are their consciences, with teachings.

[Col. 0837D] So that he might present the Church to himself in glory, not having spot or wrinkle or anything of this kind. Christ cleansed the Church for himself in such a way that he washed away its ancient crimes, and by word and example showed how we incur new stains and how we should cleanse them.

But so that she might be holy and without blemish. If she is without blemish in every respect, those who are blemished are considered alienated from her unless they are cleansed again through repentance.

In the same way, husbands ought to love their wives as their own bodies. Whatever kind of wives they want to find, they should show themselves to their wives to be of that kind.

He who loves his wife loves himself. Because the two are one flesh.

[Col. 0838A] For no one has ever hated his own flesh, but nourishes and cherishes it. Not so as to inflict labor and pain upon it, but to make it secure and tranquil. He does not condemn marriage, but exhorts them to self-restraint.

Just as Christ also does the Church, because we are members of his body. His members ought to imitate him in everything.

Of his flesh and of his bones. “For this reason a man will leave his father and mother.” Out of love, if it is not a good love.

And he will cling to his wife, and the two will be one flesh. This is an objection from the standpoint of carnal people who want to love carnally, as some think.

This mystery is great. But I speak with reference to Christ and the Church. “I say,” he says, “that this is to be understood of Christ and the Church.” Therefore you ought to love your holy and spiritual wives with greater [Col. 0838B] affection, since previously you loved sinful women and women in a Gentile, carnal manner.

Nevertheless, let each one of you love his wife as himself, and let the wife fear her husband. Let her be subject to him as the weaker one, so that she may be ruled.

## CHAPTER VI

Children, obey your parents in the Lord. He prepares them for the discipline by which he commanded them to be instructed by their parents according to God.

For this is just. So that you may show one another mutual love.

Honor your father and your mother. He commands honor toward parents, but toward good ones. As for those who live against God [Col. 0838C], Moses himself also forbade them to be acknowledged.

Which is the first commandment. The first on the second tablet, which contained six commandments concerning duties toward human beings. The first tablet properly demanded duties toward God.

In the promise: “that it may be well with you, and that you may be long-lived upon the earth.” Not upon this earth, on which the impious—and sometimes even criminals against their parents—grow old, but upon that earth which the Lord promises to the meek, in which the righteous will dwell and whose blessings they believe they will see.

And you, fathers, do not provoke your children to anger, but bring them up in the discipline and correction of the Lord. Or, in moderation. And do not beat them irrationally; or, by provoking them toward worldly studies, make them learn anger. Rather, instruct them in the disciplines of divine law. To such parents, therefore, he commands obedience.

Slaves, obey your earthly masters. For Christ did not come to change social conditions. Servitude was not given by nature, but was produced by captivity; nor did it arise from the curse of Ham, as some think, since we read that kings were descended from him. That curse was fulfilled in the sons of Ham who were subjected to Israel. Here the Apostle takes care lest the teaching of God be blasphemed in any respect, if believers become useless to their masters. And if someone who was perhaps about to permit other slaves to become Christians should see those already enslaved, he may begin to regret it. But if he sees them progressing toward what is better and becoming believers from unbelievers, he will not only wish his other household slaves to believe, but perhaps he himself will also be saved.

“With fear and trembling, in the simplicity of your hearts.” With complete obedience and the haste of humility, having laid aside former pride and hypocrisy.

“As to Christ.” Whatever is offered to human beings in contemplation of Christ is done as to Christ.

“Not by way of eye-service, as people-pleasers.” Not fearing their masters alone, as though they did not wish to please God as well.

“But as servants of Christ, doing the will of God from the heart.” In matters that are not contrary to God’s will. For in many respects the minds of masters agree with the natural law, since they desire to have slaves who are faithful, sober, chaste, and humble.

[Col. 0839B] “Serving with good will, as to the Lord and not to human beings.” Not with murmuring, lest you be deprived of favor with human beings and of your reward with God.

“Knowing that whatever good each person does, this he will receive from the Lord, whether slave or free.” Whatever you do for the Lord, you will receive a reward from him; nor should the condition of servitude make you despair.

And you, masters, do the same things to them. Otherwise, if they flee, you may begin to attribute it to your own wickedness rather than to the law. Even a pagan would have done this, if the commandment were treated otherwise; and do you refuse to hear from him what is just?

“Renouncing threats, knowing that both their Lord and yours is in heaven, and that there is no partiality with God.” Threaten for the sake of discipline, but renounce threats for the sake of mercy, and so that your own Lord may renounce them for you, before whom you are certainly equals, so that the inheritance which has been promised may be one inheritance among you.

As for the rest, brothers: he concludes the Epistle with a general exhortation.

“Be strengthened in the Lord and in the power of his might.” By the Lord’s example and power.

“Put on the armor of God, so that you may be able to stand against the schemes of the devil.” Against spiritual enemies, spiritual weapons must be taken up, so that, by the strength of these arms, one may be protected from the dissimilar nature of the devil.

“For our struggle is not against flesh and blood.” “Flesh and blood” means a human being.

“But against rulers and authorities.” Those who have usurped rule over the people of this world and who lead ignorant souls astray through sins.

“Against the rulers of the darkness of this world.” Against the power of demons, who, seizing power over the people of this world for themselves, presume to rule through errors of ignorance. They are compared with darkness, as he himself says: “For once you were darkness, but now you are light in the Lord.”

“Against spiritual wickedness in the heavenly places.” There are also spiritual goodnesses in the heavenly places, in the air, where the birds of heaven are said to be.

Therefore take up the armor of God, because you have such enemies.

“So that you may be able to resist on the evil day.” The day is not evil for itself, but for us, when we are attacked by evil.

[Col. 0840A] “And to stand perfect in all things.” He does not want a person to be perfect in only some respects; but this too should be noted: he exhorts everyone toward perfection.

“Stand, therefore, with your loins girded.” Stand perfectly, with the loins of your mind girded—that is, prepared for every battle and released from all worldly cares.

“In truth.” Without hypocrisy; for no one is crowned unless he has competed lawfully.

“And having put on the breastplate of righteousness.” Just as a breastplate is woven from many rings or links, so righteousness is joined together from various kinds of virtues. He warns not only against the consciousness of sin, but also against indulgence of the belly; it likewise reaches as far as the thighs, to restrain lust.

“And having shod your feet in the preparation of the gospel of peace.” [Col. 0840B] Walk forward confidently and preach without fear.

“In all things taking up the shield of faith, with which you may be able to extinguish all the flaming darts of the evil one.” Let us be fortified by faith in every contest. For just as a shield is the defense of the other weapons as well, and without it every armed person is unarmed, so these virtues cannot save without faith. For just as a shield repels and beats back everything hurled against it, so faith extinguishes all the devil’s persuasions, even though they may seem to possess something like the light of reason.

“And take the helmet of salvation.” Let it protect and conceal all the senses of the head from evil actions.

“And the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God.” No soldier dares to go to war without a sword: he may defend himself somehow, but he cannot kill the enemy. Sometimes he is even slain by a bold enemy and stripped of all his weapons. So, without the word of God, all righteousness is unprotected.

“Through every prayer and supplication.” Ask for this sword continually.

“Praying at all times in the Spirit.” Do not allow yourself to be prevented from praying always and from making supplication for spiritual matters.

“And keeping watch in it with all perseverance and supplication.” It is useless to hide bodily as though asleep and to be weighed down in spirit, while in this vanity one is unable to obtain anything even from a human being.

“For all the saints.” Be holy, so that you may be able to pray for the saints.

“And for me, that speech may be given to me in the opening of my mouth, so that with boldness I may make known the mystery of the gospel.” [Col. 0840D] So that I may explain abundantly and without fear the persecutions or hatred of the Jews, fortified by the cause of Christ’s people.

“For which I am an ambassador in this chain, so that in it I may dare to speak as I ought.” Every ambassador of a message must endure such things; but the word of God cannot be bound. Then there will be greater confidence if it is spoken reasonably and expressed abundantly through argument.

But so that you too may know what concerns me and what I am doing, Tychicus, the most beloved brother and faithful minister in the Lord, will make everything known to you. I have sent him to you for this very purpose: so that you may know what concerns us and that he may comfort your hearts. He acts diligently not only so that they may make progress, [Col. 0841A] but also so that they may not fail amid tribulations or be saddened in any respect.

Peace to the brothers and love with faith from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. Peace, love, and faith make the Christian perfect. Yet without faith love is fruitless, just as faith is without love—or peace. Love is greater than peace. For someone may not be hated, and yet not be loved.

Grace be with all who love our Lord Jesus Christ in incorruptibility. Amen. In whose heart, in the manner of adultery, love of Christ is not violated through worldly things.

# IN THE EPISTLE TO THE PHILIPPIANS

[Col. 0841]

## CHAPTER ONE

[Col. 0841A]

“Paul and Timothy, servants of Jesus Christ.” Both are servants, not both apostles. For every apostle is a servant, but not every servant is an apostle.

“To all the saints in Christ Jesus who are at Philippi.” [Col. 0841B] For no one is holy without Christ; and he addresses the saints, not all the Philippians—that is, not the pagans as well.

“With the bishops and deacons. Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.” Here we understand “bishops” to mean presbyters. For there could not have been several bishops in one city; this is also found in the Acts of the Apostles.

“I give thanks to my God at every remembrance of you.” He celebrates the memory of good people with thanksgiving.

“Always in all my prayers.” He shows his love for them, since he always prays for them.

“For all of you.” Because you are all of this character.

“Making supplication with joy.” Not in sadness or grief over some sin.

“Because of your fellowship in the gospel of Christ.” [Col. 0841C] Because you have shared with me in preaching the gospel.

“From the first day until now.” From the beginning of your faith, I pray that you may persevere; or, because from the beginning you have shared in preaching.

“Confident of this very thing.” I am confident that I shall obtain this.

“That he who began a good work in you.” He began by granting teaching or the grace of knowledge.

“Will bring it to completion.” By bringing to completion what they have been taught, so that they may teach it.

“Until the day of Christ Jesus.” Until the day on which they depart from the body. From then on each person is preserved for the Lord’s coming.

“As it is right for me to think this about all of you.” For love hopes all things.

“Because I have you in my heart and in my chains.” I love you so greatly that neither this tribulation nor the anxiety of my defense can take away the memory of you.

“And in the defense and confirmation of the gospel.” The confirmation of the gospel is the constant endurance of the preacher.

“You are all partners in my joy.” This is what I think and believe about you: just as you are partners in my tribulation, so you will also be partners in eternal joy. Or thus: I know that you have believed the gospel in such a way that, even in my tribulations for its defense, you rejoice together with me.

“For God is my witness, how I long for you all in the inward parts of Jesus Christ.” Either that you may be in his inward parts, or: I long for you as though you were the inward parts of Christ.

[Col. 0842A] “And this I pray, that your love may abound more and more.” So that you may abound still more in what you possess.

“In knowledge and all discernment, so that you may approve what is excellent.” It should be noted that, although they already possess knowledge, he still prays for knowledge for them, [Col. 0842B] so that they may be able to be sincere in everything. For no sick person recognizes whether he can be healed.

“So that you may be sincere and without offense for the day of Christ.” A sincere substance preserves its own nature, untainted by any external corruption. Such wine always progresses toward what is better, not what is worse.

“Filled with the fruit of righteousness through Jesus Christ.” May you not only be sincere, free from every corruption, but also abound in the fruit of righteousness, following Christ’s example: he not only lacks wickedness, but also overflows with goodness.

“To the glory and praise of God.” So that God may be glorified in your deeds.

“Now I want you to know, brothers, what has happened to me.” Here he comforts them concerning his tribulation, since they had heard that he was being held in chains in the city of Rome.

“They have turned out rather for the advancement of the gospel, so that my chains have become manifest in Christ throughout the whole praetorium and to all the rest.” They not only do no harm but have even proved beneficial, since it is made clear that I endure everything not for some crime but for Christ.

“So that most of the brothers, confident in the Lord.” More have been made steadfast by my tribulation than by teaching.

“Dare much more boldly, without fear, to speak the word of God because of my chains.” They were stirred up by the example of my chains, when they saw me endure most willingly for Christ.

“Some indeed preach Christ because of envy and rivalry.” Thinking that they are taking glory away from me among believers, [Col. 0842D] lest I alone appear to claim the knowledge of preaching.

“But others because of good will preach Christ.” Others, wishing also to save others, faithfully proclaim Christ.

“Some out of love.” Others, out of love for me, help me by defending the gospel.

“Knowing that I am appointed for the defense of the gospel.” Not out of the affection of human love, but because they know that I have been appointed by the Lord to defend the gospel.

“But others proclaim Christ out of rivalry, not sincerely, supposing that they are stirring up affliction for my chains.” Others preach out of hostility, to burden me, [Col. 0843A] as though I were making many disciples and trying to fill the whole world with my teaching, so that by this at least a greater injury or affliction might be heaped upon me.

“What then? Only that in every way, whether as a pretext”—of hatred or envy—

“or in truth”—of simple or pure preaching—

“Christ is proclaimed; and in this I rejoice, and I will also rejoice.” It does not matter to me with what intention they preach, provided that—as I desire—the name of Christ becomes known to everyone and is believed by many. Therefore I rejoice both now and in the future.

“For I know that this will turn out for my salvation, through your prayer.” What they think will harm me will result in salvation, because the Church of Christ is increased not only through my word and suffering, [Col. 0843B] but also through their hatred.

“And through the assistance of the Spirit of Jesus Christ.” Because I am guided by him in every respect toward salvation.

“According to my expectation and hope.” Because from all these things I expect and hope for a reward.

“For I will be put to shame in nothing.” Neither in life nor in death, neither in insults nor in reproaches—in short, the Apostle was ashamed in nothing. We are ashamed in everything, and when we are blamed, we do no more, even though we may have begun according to God. Thus we show that we serve neither for praise nor for Christ. The Apostle was not ashamed of chains; we are ashamed of reproaches.

“But with all boldness, as always.” Nothing can deter me.

“And now Christ will be magnified in my body.” He taunts his enemies because they cannot harm Christ. If they kill him, he will be crowned through martyrdom; if they preserve him for proclaiming Christ, he will produce abundant fruit.

“Whether by life or by death.” Both our life and our death contribute to Christ’s greatness.

“For to me, living is Christ.” I wished to live for no other reason than Christ, so that I might build up his body.

“And dying is gain.” A crown.

“But if living in the flesh means fruit for my work.” If they wish me to live in the flesh, I shall have time for working.

“And what I should choose, I do not know; I am pressed between the two.” Both are so suitable to me that I cannot know which I should choose.

“I have the desire to depart and be with Christ, which is much better; but to remain in the flesh is more necessary for your sake.” The former is better for me; the latter is necessary for you. He shows by his own example that they should not fear death but love it; and, so that they may not be saddened, he promises prophetically that he will remain in the flesh.

“And, trusting in this, I know that I shall remain.” I do not merely believe it, but know it with complete certainty.

“And I shall remain with all of you.” Not for myself—that is, not on my own account—

“For your progress and the joy of faith.” So that you may have progress from the fruit of your faith and joy; or, so that you may rejoice, because your faith and prayer have preserved me.

“So that your rejoicing in Christ Jesus on my account may abound through my coming again to you.” So that, after I have visited you, you may rejoice again even more abundantly.

“Only conduct yourselves worthily of the gospel of Christ.” Observing all its commandments; or, you must preserve yourselves worthily of the preachers of the gospel.

“So that whether I come and see you or, being absent, hear about you, you are standing firm in one spirit.” As we read: “They had one heart and one soul”; no one said that anything was his own, but everything was common to them.

“United in soul, striving together for the faith of the gospel.” Every battle undertaken in unity produces victory.

[Col. 0844B] “And in nothing be frightened by your adversaries, which is for them a cause of destruction but for you of salvation.” Do not be disturbed either by their deceptive arguments or by sufferings and reproaches. These can benefit you all the more as a reward, just as the apostles went away rejoicing because they had been considered worthy to suffer dishonor for the Lord’s name.

“And this is from God, because it has been granted to you for Christ.” He wishes you to be crowned after being tested, just as Job was permitted to be tested. He could not be conquered, and his glory had to be increased when the adversary was overcome and confounded.

“Not only to believe in him, but also to suffer for him.” The opportunity for faith was granted by God: if Christ had not come and taught, we certainly would not believe. Yet we also read of voluntary faith in the deeds of the Law. Therefore he wishes you to have not only the merit of faith but also the reward of martyrdom, while God permits you to be tested so that you may conquer.

“Having the same struggle as you saw in me and now hear about me.” You are suffering nothing new, but what you saw in me when I was present and now hear about me in my absence. Therefore do not regard as unworthy for you what you saw us glorying in.

## CHAPTER TWO

“If there is therefore any consolation in Christ.” If in every tribulation you are consoled by him alone, let your consolation not be earthly property.

“If any comfort from love.” The love of Christ, not that of friends.

[Col. 0844D] “If any fellowship of the Spirit.” Of spiritual people, not carnal ones.

“If any compassion.” Have compassion for yourselves rather than for your parents.

“Complete my joy.” Which I already possess in part; for a teacher rejoices in such people. Alternatively: If you offer me any consolation in Christ, and any comfort from love; if any fellowship of the Spirit binds you together; and if there is among you any compassion and piety, grant me this which I ask: complete our joy of unity and election.

“Being of the same mind, having the same love, united in soul and thinking the same thing.” Do not divide love by thinking differently.

[Col. 0845A] “Doing nothing through rivalry or empty glory.” Do nothing—not out of zeal for God, but so that each person may appear superior to another.

“But in all humility, regarding one another as superior to yourselves.” If we regarded all from whom we suffer injury as superior, we would easily preserve patience. For no one is distressed at having received an injury from a father or from the Lord.

“Not each considering his own interests, but those of others.” Not what benefits us alone, but what benefits others.

“For have this mind among yourselves which was also in Christ Jesus.” He wishes to show that Christ suffered not for himself but for others; or, let there be in you as humble a mind as there was in Christ. Moreover, many understand this passage to mean [Col. 0845B] that Christ humbled himself according to his divinity, specifically according to the form in which he did not seize equality with God as a prize, although he naturally possessed it. “He emptied himself” does not mean that he emptied his substance, but that he set aside his honor, taking the form of a servant—that is, assuming human nature—and becoming altogether human, with the humility of his obedience, not refusing even death on a cross. This is “in Christ Jesus”: according to the fact that he was anointed, he is Christ; he received the name Jesus—that is, according to his humanity.

“Who, though he was in the form of God.” In which he existed; or, because he was without sin—namely, in the image of God.

“Did not regard equality with God as a prize, but emptied himself.” He concealed what he was through humility, [Col. 0845C] giving us an example, so that we may not glory in things which perhaps we do not possess.

“Taking the form of a servant.” So that he even washed the feet of the disciples.

“Being made in the likeness of human beings.” At times “likeness” includes reality. For Adam begot a son according to his image and likeness and called his name Seth. He served in human likeness and humility, although he was Lord of all.

“And being found in appearance as a human being.” For this to be true, it must be understood in the same way as the phrase “as though [he were] the only-begotten from the Father” [reading uncertain].

“He humbled himself, becoming obedient unto death.” So that he might show us an example of perfect obedience.

“And the death of the cross.” Than which no death can be [Col. 0845D] worse.

“Therefore God also exalted him and bestowed on him the name.” Because the assumed human being deigned to humble himself, the divinity, which cannot be humbled, exalted him who had been humbled. But a name was also bestowed on him because previously he did not have it. Thus this passage is more correctly understood according to human nature than divine nature. If, therefore, we look down from above, let us serve our brothers according to Christ’s example. For if he, the Lord and teacher, ministered to servants and disciples, how much more ought we to serve equals and superiors, and obey God and his saints even unto death! Otherwise proud disciples may fail to follow their humble teacher, and ungrateful servants may despise their gentle Lord.

“Which is above every name.” For to which of the angels did he say, “You are my Son”?

“So that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of those in heaven and on earth.” So that all may together worship the human being assumed by the Word.

“And under the earth.” Here he introduces the guardians of the underworld.

“And every tongue confess.” Namely, of all nations.

“That the Lord Jesus Christ is in the glory of God the Father.” That is, in the nature and glory of divinity, since he has the same glory as the Father.

Therefore, my most beloved, just as you have always obeyed—following the example of the one who obeyed unto death—

[Col. 0846B] “Not only in my presence.” As servants who serve merely for appearance—

“But much more now in my absence.” Because if you acted more freely while I was present, I could correct you.

“Work out your salvation with fear and trembling.” Not negligently, but as Job says: “I feared all my works because of God, knowing that you would not spare the sinner.” The Holy Spirit rests upon the humble, quiet, and trembling person and upon the words of God.

“For God is the one working in you both to will and to accomplish.” He works the will by persuasion and by promising rewards: “The one who perseveres to the end will be saved.” But neither accomplishing nor willing anything is ours at all, since both are governed by the definition of the same passage.

[Col. 0846C] “According to his good will.” If you remain in it.

“But do everything without murmuring.” The servant is ungrateful who complains that his master’s commands are burdensome. For whoever murmurs about the commands doubts the rewards. Even if he acts, he does not act without complaint. Hence he says elsewhere: “Nor murmur,” and so forth.

“And hesitations.” Concerning the future reward.

“So that you may be without complaint, sincere children of God without reproach.” As God made you. Consider whose children you are: since he is holy and pure in all things, he cannot have degenerate children.

“Among a crooked and perverse generation.” A generation that perverts and destroys the whole order of rational nature.

“Among whom you shine like lights in the world.” So may God’s race shine among the human race, as the sun and [Col. 0846D] moon illuminate the world.

“Holding fast the word of life.” So that others may be illuminated by you and strengthened by your example.

“For my glory.” The glory of a father is his children’s glory, as Solomon says.

“On the day of Christ.” On the day of judgment.

“Because I did not run in vain or labor in vain.” For I acquired such a people for God.

“But even if I am poured out upon the sacrifice and service of your faith, I rejoice and rejoice with you all.” Even if he kills me, because he has offered the sacrifice and service of your faith to God: the progress of your faith overcomes the sadness of punishment or death. Or: I no longer fear dying [Col. 0847A] once the sacrifice of your faith has been completed; or, because I have ministered to your faith.

“In the same way, you also rejoice and rejoice with me.” Because it is a great reward for me to be killed for your sake; or, because it is beneficial for me to depart.

“But I hope in the Lord Jesus to send Timothy to you shortly.” He gives an example of not fearing what must be decided, but of promising everything in hope of the Lord.

“So that I too may be encouraged when I learn what concerns you.” So that you may know that my sufferings have not frightened you at all.

“For I have no one so united with me who will sincerely be concerned for you.” No one who is concerned with me in this way for the salvation of all of you.

“For all seek their own interests.” Their advantage [Col. 0847B] or comfort, unwilling to suffer for a soul.

“Not those of Jesus Christ.” They do not care about the body or the example of Christ, who did not at all refuse to die for the salvation of everyone.

“But you know his proven character.” So that you may know what he is like.

“Because as a son with his father, he served with me in the gospel.” According to his humanity, he became obedient unto death for the sake of human beings.

“Him, therefore, I hope to send to you as soon as I see what concerns me.” For now I am uncertain.

“But I trust in the Lord that I myself will also come to you shortly.” I am not sending only him, the one comfort I have.

“But I considered it necessary to send Epaphroditus, my brother, [Col. 0847C] and fellow worker.” Necessary for you and a fellow worker in the work of the gospel.

“And my fellow soldier, but your apostle.” A fellow soldier because of the honor involved, since he too had received among them the office of apostleship.

“And minister of my need.” I am sending him to you because he came to minister to my need on your behalf.

“For he was longing for you all.” He commends his anxious love for them, so that he may be loved by them all the more.

“And he was troubled because you had heard that he was ill.” He was saddened because your sorrow was the cause of his grief, since you had been excessively distressed by the report of his illness.

“For indeed he was ill almost to death, but God had mercy on him.” So that, by teaching, he might gather a greater harvest.

“And not only on him, but also on me, so that I would not have sorrow upon sorrow.” So that the sorrow of desolation would not increase the sorrow of imprisonment.

“Therefore I have sent him more quickly, so that when you see him you may rejoice again.” For I know that you are saddened by his absence.

“And so that I may be without sorrow.” The sorrow that your sorrow causes me.

“Therefore receive him with all joy in the Lord.” Removing whatever hesitation his mind may perhaps have conceived concerning his delay.

“And hold such people in honor.” Honor not only this man, [Col. 0848A] who is your teacher, but all who possess such grace.

“Because for the work of Christ he came close to death.” He was not afraid to minister to me in prison.

“Giving up his life.” Into the hands of enemies; that is, he was ready for death.

“To complete what was lacking in your service toward me.” So that he alone might complete what remained of your service toward me.

## CHAPTER THREE

Finally, my brothers, rejoice in the Lord.

Do not rejoice in human affairs or in anything except the Lord.

“For me to write the same things to you is not burdensome.” To repeat what I had said when present.

[Col. 0848B] “But for you it is necessary.” As a garden needs to be watered more frequently.

“Beware of dogs.” Here he speaks against the false apostles who tear apart the gospel of Christ.

“Beware of evil workers.” Those who try to destroy what we have built well.

“Beware of the mutilation.” They should be called “mutilation” rather than “circumcision.”

“For we are the circumcision, who serve God in the Spirit.” We are the Jewish men who do not cut away the skin of one member only, but the vices of the whole flesh—circumcised spiritually, that is.

“And glory in Christ Jesus and put no confidence in the flesh.” In the faith of Christ alone, not in bodily circumcision.

[Col. 0848C] “Although I myself have confidence in the flesh.” So that no one may think I say this because I have no reason for boasting and therefore do not boast.

“If anyone else thinks he has confidence in the flesh, I have more: circumcised on the eighth day, of the people of Israel.” Perhaps some of them were proselytes; I belong to the race itself, not one who became so after many years, like certain foreigners.

“Of the tribe of Benjamin.” Which always remained joined to Judah.

“A Hebrew of Hebrews.” Not a proselyte from the nations.

“According to the law, a Pharisee.” A teacher of the law, or one separated from the crowd, who could not fail to do what I approved.

“According to zeal, persecuting the Church of God.” I had such zeal that, even in ignorance, I persecuted the Church.

[Col. 0848D] “According to the righteousness that is in the law.” I was first in all the matters in which they falsely boast. But because I recognized that those things are no longer valid at this time, I consider them of no importance and cast them away as obstacles by which I had thought I could acquire life.

“Living without reproach.” I fulfilled all the justifications and ritual purifications and commandments; but I considered these things nothing when I believed in Christ, whom the Law itself had promised.

“But whatever things were gain to me, these I considered loss because of Christ.” In comparison with discovered gold, bronze is despised, although both were produced by the same creator and were once necessary according to the needs of the time.

[Col. 0849A] “Indeed, I consider everything to be loss because of the surpassing knowledge of Jesus Christ my Lord, for whose sake I have suffered the loss of all things and consider them refuse.” Refuse consists of the remnants of food and, formerly, of the waste of useful things.

“So that I may gain Christ and be found in him.” So that I may have Christ as my head and be found as one of his members.

“Not having my own righteousness, which is from the law.” That is, righteousness acquired by my own labor.

“But that which is through faith in Christ Jesus, the righteousness from God in faith.” Rather, the righteousness which is properly bestowed by God alone through faith upon Christians.

“To know him.” So that I may know his benefit perfectly.

“And the power of his resurrection.” For he rose for this reason: so that we too might rise in the same way. Whoever truly knows this acts sufficiently if he does not sin at all.

“And the fellowship of his sufferings, being conformed to his death.” For if we suffer with him, we shall also live with him.

“If somehow I may attain the resurrection from the dead.” That resurrection which properly belongs to the perfect, not the one which even the unwilling must necessarily possess.

“Not that I have already received it.” For the end of the world has not yet come; what we believe exists in hope, not in reality.

“Or am already perfect.” He still says that he is uncertain concerning this perfection and such a resurrection.

“But I pursue it, if somehow I may lay hold of that for which I was laid hold of by Christ Jesus.” If I may attain the merit of apostleship, in which apostleship I was seized by Christ.

[Col. 0849C] “Brothers, I do not consider myself to have laid hold of it.” By humbling himself, he removes glory from all and urges everyone toward perfection.

“But one thing I do: forgetting what lies behind and stretching forward to what lies ahead.” I know only this: that I make progress each day. Counting past labor as nothing, I hasten toward what lies ahead. Or: forgetting the Law, I hold fast to the perfect commandments of the gospel.

“I pursue the appointed goal, the prize of God’s heavenly calling in Christ Jesus.” That which God promised to the perfect in Christ in heaven, which only those who conquer will receive.

“Therefore, let as many of us as are perfect think this way.” How can he deny that he is perfect if others are, unless this is understood as spoken out of humility? Whoever is perfect should think this way: forgetting the old and pursuing the new. For Christ’s disciples ought to be perfect, although above he was speaking of the perfection of the reward, whereas here he is speaking of knowledge.

“And if you think anything differently, God will reveal this to you also.” If God has revealed something differently to others. He says “differently,” not “otherwise”—that is, by another assertion, not another faith.

“Nevertheless, let us proceed according to what we have attained.” To the perfection of the New Testament.

[Col. 0850A] “Let us think the same thing.” Let it be the same; that is, let one person not assert something different from another.

“And let us remain in the same rule.” For it is not enough to know without acting.

“Be imitators of me, brothers.” Follow me, not the false apostles.

“And observe those who walk in this way, as you have us for a pattern.” “Observe” has two meanings: either to imitate, as here; or to beware, as he says to the Romans: “Observe those who create dissensions and causes for stumbling.”

“For many walk—of whom I often told you.” He speaks of those who, taking away hope in the passion of Christ through which sins were forgiven, placed it in the ceremonies of the Law. It may also be understood of the practices of Jovinian, [Col. 0850B] who turned the austerities of fasting and every bodily torment into luxury and banquets.

“But now I tell you even weeping: they are enemies of the cross of Christ.” It should be noted that he desired the salvation of all with genuine affection, since he even wept for the enemies of Christ’s cross who were rushing willingly toward destruction.

“Whose end is destruction.” Because they sow in corruption of the flesh.

“Whose god is their belly.” They think they serve God in this way, if they eat, not listening to the Prophet who says: “If you eat and drink, are you not eating and drinking?”

“And their glory is in their shame, who set their minds on earthly things.” In circumcision, the shameful member.

“But our citizenship is in heaven.” One enslaved to earthly vices cannot say this.

“From where we also await a Savior, the Lord Jesus Christ.” Who is our head.

“Who will transform the body of our humiliation, conforming it to the body of his glory.” As he showed on the mountain, when he conformed one of the living and one of the dead to the body of his glory, displaying an example of resurrection both in the dead and in the living.

“According to the working of his power, by which he is also able to subject all things to himself.” For he not only conformed us, but also made all things subject to his body; or, according to the judgment by which he subjected everything to himself, this too is possible for him.

## CHAPTER FOUR

[Col. 0850D]

Therefore, my most beloved and most longed-for brothers. Because you are more perfect.

“My joy and crown.” Through you I rejoice in the present and will be crowned in the future.

“Stand firm in the Lord in this way, my beloved.” Place your hope in the faith of Christ alone, as I explained above, and in a heavenly way of life.

I urge Euodia, and I entreat Syntyche to be of the same mind in the Lord. That is, as he says: These women were learned in the Law together with me; for he recalls and exhorts them to think alike in the same way.

[Note: [Col. 0849D] Therefore those who insist that Syntyche was a man do not hold the correct view; among them is also Martianaeus. Most aptly, in the ancient inscription of our household shrine: “To the ship Salvia and to the Mother of the Gods, Claudia Syntyche gave and dedicated [this].” [Col. 0850D]]

I also ask you, Germanus, my true companion. He is called “Germanus” by name, and was a companion in office.

Help those women who labored with me in the Gospel. Not men, but women who were teaching—not in the Church, but in the house.

Together with Clement and my other fellow-workers. Clement was a man of great learning, formerly a philosopher, who became bishop of Rome.

Their names are in the book of life. So that they would not be troubled that their names had been included in this Epistle, he says that they are written in heaven. Moses and David also mention this book, as does the Lord in the Gospel.

Rejoice in the Lord always. You who do not possess the world’s joy.

Again I say, rejoice. He repeats this so that their joy may be strengthened more and more.

Let your moderation be known to all people. To all Jews and Gentiles who afflict and persecute you.

For the Lord is near. He knows what is necessary before you ask him; whether you are anxious about thoughts that are fitting, you know very well how near the Lord is to us, according to the saying: “The Lord is near to those who are troubled in heart.”

Be anxious about nothing. Do not think about what you will eat or what you will wear. The Gentiles seek all these things.

But in every prayer and supplication, with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known before God. Not with murmuring or sadness; then your prayer can be worthy of the Savior’s ears, if you give thanks for everything that you suffer, as the apostles did.

And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your thoughts in Christ Jesus. It sustains the wicked and the ungrateful. The peace of Christ, by which he prayed for his persecutors, surpasses and inclines every mind, if we reflect upon it. Therefore may this peace guard your hearts and your thoughts by Christ’s example.

Finally, brothers. At the end, to gather everything briefly.

Whatever is true. Things to be maintained.

Whatever is chaste, whatever is just, whatever is holy, whatever is lovely, whatever is of good repute. For every human nature knows diligently how to love what is good.

If there is any virtue, if there is any praise of discipline, think about these things, which you both learned and received, heard and saw in me: the virtue of endurance, or the praise of conduct, and the other good things that you learned in word, received by example, heard with your ears, and saw with your eyes. Think only about these things.

Do these things. Thought alone is not sufficient without action. These final words explain the preceding ones.

And the God of peace will be with you. If you not only think about these things, but also do them.

I rejoiced greatly in the Lord, because at last you have flourished again in your concern for me, just as you had been concerned. You were occupied, however. You have again received the flower of good work; having forgotten me, you had withered and become so through occupation, not through unwillingness.

I do not say this as though because of want. I do not say that I rejoiced on account of my own poverty, but on account of your fruit.

For I have learned to be sufficient in whatever condition I am. I have been taught by Christ to endure everything with equanimity.

I know how to be humbled, and I also know how to abound. Everywhere and in all things I have been instructed: both to be filled and to hunger, both to abound and to suffer want, so that I may neither be exalted by abundance nor broken by poverty.

I can do all things in him who strengthens me. He gives understanding, or confirms me by his teaching.

Nevertheless, you did well by sharing in my tribulation. My poverty ought not to have prevented your reward.

You yourselves know, Philippians, that at the beginning of the Gospel, when I departed from Macedonia, no church shared with me. You know when I departed, because we chose you alone, from whom we received support, judging you more faithful than all the others.

In the account of giving and receiving, except you alone. You gave material things and received spiritual things.

For even when I was in Thessalonica, you sent something for my needs once and twice—not because I seek the gift, but I seek the abundant fruit credited to your account. The abundant fruit of prayer is present when provision is made even for the saints who are absent.

But I have everything and abound. I am filled, having received from Epaphroditus the things you sent. He provokes them to generosity by praising them and giving thanks.

[Col. 0852C] As an aroma of sweetness. The aroma of sweetness consists not in the thing offered, but in the devotion of the mind; just as God is described as having smelled Noah’s sacrifice, although he himself says that he does not delight in the flesh or blood of animals.

An acceptable sacrifice, pleasing to God. It should be noted that almsgiving is called a sacrifice: just as it is acceptable when offered by the holy, so it is rejected when offered by those who have persisted in sins.

But my God will fulfill every desire of yours according to his riches in glory in Christ Jesus. To God, however, and our Father be glory for ages of ages. Amen. For, as the perfected could desire nothing else, their desires were for what accords with God’s riches, not those of the world, and for what pertains to Christ’s glory.

[Col. 0852D] Greet every holy person in Christ Jesus. The brothers who are with me greet you. For all those whom he orders to be greeted were holy, and he commands that all be greeted, as he does in all his Epistles; and without doubt he should be believed to have spoken truly. If they were truly holy, they were certainly not sinners; and because they were not sinners but holy, they could be what they were just as they could not be what they were not.
