Therefore it is possible, for this reason, for human beings to be holy.

All the holy ones greet you, especially those who are of Caesar’s household. Those who have recently been converted from Caesar’s household.

The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.

## ON THE EPISTLE TO THE COLOSSIANS

[Col. 0853]

## CHAPTER ONE

[Col. 0853A]

Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ through the will of God, and Timothy, a brother, to those who are in Colossae, holy and faithful brothers in Christ Jesus: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

We give thanks to God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, always praying for you, hearing of your faith in Christ Jesus and of the love that you have for all the holy ones. Without respect of persons or distinction of acquaintance, you love holiness alone in everyone.

Because of the hope laid up for us in heaven, which you heard about in the word of truth, the Gospel, which has reached you. Not for human praise, but for eternal life, which is in Christ.

As it is also in the whole world, and bears fruit. One bears thirtyfold, another sixtyfold, another a hundredfold, according to the parable of the sower.

And grows. In number or in virtue.

As it has also done among you from the day when you heard and came to know the grace of God in truth. You do not empty its benefits through evil deeds.

As you learned from Epaphras, our most beloved fellow-servant, who is a faithful minister of Christ Jesus for you. Faithfully laboring for you in prayer, he performs Christ’s ministry willingly.

He also made known to us your love in the Spirit. The spiritual love that you possess.

Therefore, from the day we heard, we have not ceased praying and asking for you, that you may be filled with the knowledge of his will in all wisdom and spiritual understanding. [Col. 0853C] For you cannot do it otherwise; understanding this, the Prophet said to God: “Teach me to do your will, because you are my God.”

So that you may walk worthily of God, pleasing him in all things, bearing fruit in every good work, and growing in the knowledge of God. He walks well with God who pleases him in all things; that is, who bears fruit in good work together with the knowledge of God. He has explained at the same time what he often expressed obscurely: namely, how God gives the will, or helps and strengthens it—by teaching wisdom and granting understanding and graces, not by taking away free choice. Thus also in the present passage he prays that they may be filled with the knowledge of his will in all wisdom and spiritual understanding, so that they may walk worthily of God in all things.

[Col. 0853D] Strengthened with every power. It is a great virtue to overcome long-established vices, or to overcome weakness amid the sufferings of the flesh.

According to the power of his glory. So that you, like him, may endure everything patiently.

With all patience and long-suffering, with joy. True long-suffering and patience exist where someone rejoices even to endure what he suffers.

Giving thanks to God the Father, who made us worthy to share in the lot of the holy ones in light. May the calling bring more joy than the sadness of sufferings brings affliction. He calls the lot of the holy ones the lot of inheritance, just as Scripture also says, because Jesus divided the land by lot.

Who rescued us from the authority of darkness. From ignorance or error.

And transferred us into the kingdom of the Son of his love. From the kingdom of error and death, so that we might also become beloved and sons.

In whom we have redemption and the forgiveness of sins. Having redeemed us by faith, he forgave sins through baptism.

Who is the image of the invisible God. According to the Epistle to the Hebrews.

The firstborn of every creature. Firstborn according to the form of the assumed human being, not in time but in honor, in accordance with the saying: “My son, the firstborn, Israel.”

For in him all things were created in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible, whether thrones, dominions, principalities, or powers. He says this against the Manichaeans.

All things were created through him and in him. They were created in his power.

And he is before all things, and all things hold together in him. Since they subsist through him.

And he is the head of the body, the Church. Because all believers are his members.

Who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead. The beginning of incorruptible glory.

So that he himself might hold first place in all things. Both among visible and invisible creatures.

Because in him it was pleasing that all the fullness of divinity should dwell. In others—that is, in apostles, patriarchs, or prophets—grace was present only in part. In Christ, however, the whole divinity dwelt bodily, as though one might say, in its fullness.

And through him to reconcile all things to himself, making peace through the blood of his cross. Through him human beings have been cleansed.

Whether the things in heaven or the things on earth. Earthly things were separated from heavenly things by the opposition of their way of life. Hence we are taught to pray that, just as God’s will is carried out in heaven, so it may also be done on earth.

And you, when you were once alienated and enemies in mind through evil works, he has now reconciled in the body of his flesh through death. What the enmity consisted in, he has made entirely clear.

To present you holy. So that, by making his benefit ineffectual, you would not again become enemies.

And spotless and blameless before him. See whether he knew that he had commanded impossible things.

If indeed you remain founded and steadfast and immovable in the faith. Then you will be able to be spotless, if the examples of human beings do not deceive you at all, but you firmly believe the things to come.

From the hope of the Gospel that you heard. Those who live against the Gospel cannot hope for the hope of the Gospel.

Which has been preached in all creation under heaven. That is, in rational creation. It should certainly be noted how he called human beings alone “all creation.”

Of which I, Paul, became a minister, who now rejoice in sufferings for you. He suffers for others because Christ first suffered for him.

And I complete in my flesh what is lacking in the sufferings of Christ, for the sake of his body, which is the Church, of which I became a minister. To such an extent am I not terrified by present persecutions that what I suffer seems small to me until the suffering is fulfilled in me, as he says to the Hebrews: “So that you may not grow weary, fainting in your minds; for you have not yet resisted to the point of blood.”

According to the stewardship of God that was given to me for you, so that I might fulfill the word of God, the mystery that had been hidden from ages and generations. The teaching of the Gospel, which I was commanded to dispense to you Gentiles.

But now it has been revealed to his holy ones, to whom God willed it. At the time when he willed to call the Gentiles, he opened the mystery to the holy ones whom he willed.

To make known the riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles. Because the same Lord is Lord of all, rich toward all who call upon him.

Which is Christ in you, the hope of glory, whom we proclaim, correcting every person and teaching in all wisdom. Jew and Greek, slave and free. Observe also that he teaches everyone wisdom.

So that we may present every person perfect in Christ Jesus. For this I also labor, striving according to his operation, which works in me with power. It should be noted that he endeavors to present everyone perfect.

## CHAPTER TWO

For I want you to know what concern I have for you, for those who are in Laodicea, and for all who have not seen my face in the flesh, so that their hearts may be comforted, instructed in love, and enriched with all the riches of fullness of understanding in the knowledge of the mystery of God the Father and of Christ Jesus. If they had seen me, and my love toward them, and had known more fully the riches of the mystery, they would have shown greater affection and would have been taught an abundance of understanding from me, which I learned from Christ himself; through these things they would have obtained consolation.

In whom are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge. They were hidden in the letters of the Law, as Isaiah says: “Our salvation has come in the treasures.”

Hidden. They were concealed from Moses by a veil.

I say this so that no one may deceive you with loftiness of speech. For that reason it would have been better if I had instructed you while present; nevertheless, I have briefly gathered together in him all wisdom, so that you may not only fear the thought or speech of philosophy that is opposed to him, but also count it as foolishness.

For although I am absent in body, I am with you in spirit, rejoicing and seeing your order and the firmness of your faith, which is in Christ. The apostles possessed this grace, so that, while situated elsewhere, they knew what was being done elsewhere, just as the spirit of Elisha was with Gehazi on the road. He supplies what is lacking for the usefulness of your faith, or fulfills what I cannot fulfill by my presence.

Therefore, just as you received Jesus Christ our Lord, walk in him. Christ’s example in you is sufficient for life, even if meanwhile you possess somewhat less knowledge.

Rooted and built up in him. According to the strength of the foundation, a sound building grows above it.

And established in the faith, just as you were taught, abounding in it with thanksgiving. Always growing in him and giving thanks for all his benefits.

See to it that no one deceives you through philosophy and empty deceit, according to human tradition, according to the elements of the world, and not according to Christ. He speaks against the philosophers, whose entire discussion is almost about the elements and visible creatures, and who judge God’s power from natural things, saying that nothing can be made from nothing; that the soul either has no beginning or is mortal; that a virgin absolutely cannot give birth; and that it is foolish for God to be born from a human being, to die, and to rise again.

Because in him all the fullness of divine nature dwells bodily. The entire fullness of the divine nature dwells in his body.

And you have been filled in him, who is the head of every principality and power. If you are taught by his knowledge, who revealed the beginning of the invisible creation, what can those contribute to you who understand nothing beyond what they see?

In him you were also circumcised with a circumcision not made by hand, in the stripping away of the body of flesh. Here he already censures the false apostles, so that some may not be led astray by them.

But in the circumcision of Jesus Christ, having been buried with him in baptism. Through which you stripped off the whole human being.

In him you were also raised through faith in the working of God, who raised him from the dead. You rose to a new life, believing that he also rose for this reason.

And you, when you were dead in transgressions and in the uncircumcision of your flesh. For not only sinners, but also those who are uncircumcised under the Law, will likewise be condemned. Since, therefore, you were unworthy in two ways, you have been made sharers in sonship.

He made you alive together with him, forgiving you all transgressions. By removing the causes of death, that is, sins.

Blotting out the bond written against us in decrees, which was contrary to us. He also removed it from the midst, fastening it to the cross. The bond is the curse of the Law. Hence he says elsewhere: “Christ redeemed us from the curse of the Law,” because it contains the words: “Cursed is everyone who does not remain in the book of the Law, to do these things.” Some say, however, that the bond is like a certain written record of sins kept with God. Hence he himself says in the songs: “Are these things not gathered with me and sealed in my treasuries?” And Jeremiah says: “The sin of Judah is written with an adamantine claw.” This too was erased on the cross, since, when sins were forgiven, even the memory of transgressions was forgotten.

And stripping principalities and powers. So that through death he might destroy him who held the dominion of death, offering himself for them.

He led them forth confidently and openly, triumphing over them in himself. Crucified openly, disregarding shame, he conquered and triumphed—not by killing, but by dying, so that, with all pride broken, he might show us an example.

Therefore let no one judge you concerning food or drink, or concerning a festival, a new moon, or Sabbaths. There is therefore no judgment in these matters, which are a shadow and have ceased when the body came; for there is no need of an image when the reality is present.

These are a shadow of things to come, but the body is Christ’s. For then the things that are now present were still future.

Let no one deceive you, delighting in humility and the religion of angels, walking in things he has not seen in vain, puffed up by the understanding of his flesh. Let no one, proud under a pretended humility and falsely claiming to see angels, vaunt himself vainly over others by speaking visions from his own heart; or let no one appear so humble and religious in his own eyes that he falsely claims to see the angels who behold God.

And not holding the head. Not believing in Christ, who is the head of all the holy ones.

[Col. 0857C] From whom the whole body, supplied and joined together through its ligaments and connections, grows. For members are joined to members throughout the whole body. Therefore whoever is outside this body, however much he may vaunt himself, does not have the head, which is Christ, who is life.

For the increase of God. The increase of that body which has been united to God.

If you have died with Christ to the elements of this world. These may also be understood as avarice, lust, and other things of this kind.

Why, as though living in the world, do you still make decrees? He did not even wish us to have any resemblance to those living in the world—that is, to those who do not believe in the future.

“Do not touch, do not taste, do not handle.” [Col. 0857D] With that touching, tasting, and handling by which those who abuse their desires and love earthly things instead of eternal things act.

Things that all perish in their very use. From the parts of the world we perceive its condition: since its members are composed and dissolved, the whole must at some time have been composed and at some time be dissolved. Therefore mortal things ought not to be loved in place of immortal and eternal things.

According to the precepts and teachings of human beings, which indeed have an appearance of wisdom in superstition and humility, but are not for sparing the body and have no honor in satisfying the flesh. According to what many people, taught by nature, handed down: that the world would at some time be dissolved; and therefore they venerated God, whom alone they understood to be eternal, although superstitiously yet humbly; and they did not consider the body worthy of being spared, nor the flesh worthy of honor in satiety, since it was destined to die. Alternatively: Do not let philosophy deceive you with a human teaching that is disguised under the appearance of wisdom and abstinence. In it the affliction of the body is so vain, and the purpose of the exercise so foolish; its supposed good is displayed as a kind of snare for capturing and weakening minds, while the devil hunts, so that he may more easily lead someone who follows his evil toward it.

## CHAPTER THREE

Therefore, if you have risen with Christ, seek the things that are above, where Christ is seated at the right hand of God. Consequently, he first says that we died together with him, and then that we rose together with him; and he urges us not only to die to earth but also to live for heaven: “Desire nothing earthly,” he says; “seek nothing mortal.”

Think about the things that are above, not the things on earth. For you have died. Pursue heavenly wisdom. But we devote ourselves more laboriously to human wisdom and occupy our minds with the most worthless arts.

And your life is hidden with Christ in God. When Christ, your life, appears, then you also will appear with him in glory. For although we are children of God, it has not yet appeared what we shall be. We know that when he appears, we shall be like him. Therefore we ought not seek our glory here, in the present, lest it also be said of us: “They have received their reward.”

Therefore put to death. Fulfill what you have professed.

Your members that are upon the earth. The members of your vices; or he calls the evil of your members your members.

Fornication, uncleanness, lust. He named every kind of immodesty, uncleanness, and lust.

Evil desire. For there is also good desire. Hence Daniel is called “a man of desires.” And David says: “My soul desires and languishes for the courts of the Lord.”

And greed, which is the service of idols. It profits nothing to serve God in name and idols in deeds.

[Col. 0858D] On account of these things the wrath of God comes upon the sons of unbelief. Upon Sodom and those who perished in the flood. From past examples, therefore, future things are to be feared.

In these things you also once walked, when you lived in them. But now you too must put away all these things. Therefore do not walk in them now, lest you appear to have believed in vain.

Anger, indignation, malice, blasphemy. This is what intoxicates the mind: through malice, inflicting on another what you would not wish to suffer.

Shameful speech from your mouth. Since this is not fitting in the education by which the children of human beings are raised, how much less is shameful speech fitting for God’s children, for whom speech is no less shameful than action!

Do not lie to one another. It is not fitting for children of truth to lie to one another, since no lie comes from the truth.

Stripping off the old person with his actions. With the actions of pleasures.

And putting on the new, the one who is renewed in knowledge of God. When he has learned whose image he is, he strives to imitate it, as far as he ought and is able.

According to the image of him who created him. He explained that the image consists in action.

Where there is neither male nor female, Gentile nor Jew, circumcision nor uncircumcision, barbarian nor Scythian, slave nor free. Before God, sex, race, or condition does not prejudge anyone; only conduct does.

But Christ is all and in all. All of us who have been baptized have put on Christ.

[Col. 0859B] Therefore put on, as God’s chosen ones, holy and beloved. Having put those things away, put these on, for you were made for this purpose.

Compassion, kindness, humility, modesty, patience. Since he had called the former things members, he has called these things inward parts.

Bearing with one another. Following the example of Christ, who bore our weaknesses.

And forgiving one another. Pardoning one another, just as Christ forgave everyone, even praying for his persecutors, so that our debts may also be forgiven by the heavenly Father; lest this saying be fulfilled in you: “A human being stores up anger against a human being and seeks healing from the Lord,” and so forth.

If anyone has a complaint against another. Let no one remember the malice of his neighbor, lest, while demanding payment from fellow servants, we also be compelled to repay our own forgiveness.

As the Lord also forgave you, so you also. If he forgave who had the power to punish, then vengeance is either nonexistent or very small.

But above all these things have love. Love is above all these things, because we endure everyone whom we love, but we do not love everyone whom we endure.

Which is the bond of perfection. For love gathers many members into one body.

And the peace of Christ. Not the peace of the world, which he left us—the one who died for all and loved us when we were enemies.

Let it rejoice in your hearts, in which you were also called in one body. Not with a deceitfully smiling face or deceptive speech.

And be grateful. Grateful, namely, for Christ’s benefits. In some copies it reads, “Be grace”: that is, do not resemble the Law, which repays in kind, but Grace, which forgives even enemies and prays to the Lord on their behalf.

Let the word of Christ dwell in you abundantly. Here it is shown that the word of Christ ought to be possessed not merely sufficiently but abundantly, even by laypeople, so that they may teach or admonish one another.

Teaching and admonishing yourselves in all wisdom. So that it may be expressed wisely and rationally.

In psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs, in grace. Psalms, such as David’s; hymns, such as those of the three youths; songs, such as those of Moses and the others—things that are spiritual, not carnal or shameful little songs.

Singing in your hearts to the Lord. Nowhere do we read that anyone sang without a voice. Therefore “in the heart” must here be understood as “from the heart”: namely, let us sing not only with the mouth but also with the heart. “I will confess to you,” he says, “with my whole heart.”

Whatever you do in word or deed, do everything in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, giving thanks to God the Father through him. Whether you teach or act, do nothing for your own glory, but everything for the Lord’s glory; giving thanks to God, who was pleased to send his Son to teach these things; or, let thanks be given to God through your actions.

Wives, be subject to your husbands, as is fitting in the Lord. A second law, in those matters that accord with the Lord.

Husbands, love your wives and do not be harsh toward them. Children, obey your parents in all things, for this is pleasing in the Lord. He would never encourage a natural duty unless they had begun to be continent, as is more fully noted in the Epistle to the Ephesians.

Fathers, do not provoke your children to indignation, so that they may not become fainthearted. Do not make them exasperated and irritable, when by your example they ought to have learned patience.

Slaves, obey your fleshly masters in all things. Those who exercise domination over the flesh alone.

[Col. 0860C] Not serving merely for the eye, as those who please human beings. Not working only so that you may appear to human beings to labor in the flesh.

But with sincerity of heart, fearing the Lord. He who everywhere and always sees and guards everything that has been done.

Whatever you do, work from the heart, as for the Lord and not for human beings. Do it willingly, not from the necessity of your condition but out of religious devotion, so that through your works thanks may be given to the Lord, when people see such things proceeding from the time of their belief.

Knowing that you will receive the reward of an inheritance from the Lord. Do not think that your service is fruitless; when it is offered for God’s sake, it will be weighed out by a heavenly recompense.

[Col. 0860D] Serve the Lord Christ. For the one who serves a human being for his sake serves God.

For whoever does wrong will receive what he has done unjustly. And there is no partiality with God. Whether it is a slave who has despised his master, or a master who has treated his slave unjustly. He says this so that they may have consolation, knowing that their wrong will not remain unavenged before God.

## CHAPTER FOUR

Masters, provide your slaves with what is just and fair. You ought to think of yourselves more as fathers than as masters. Hence they are also called heads of households.

Knowing that you too have a Lord in heaven. [Col. 0861A] As you want the Lord to be toward you, so also be toward your slaves.

Be devoted to prayer, keeping watch in it. For the prayer of one who is negligent and asleep cannot prevail even in obtaining anything from a human being.

With thanksgiving. For everything that has been granted to you.

Praying at the same time for us, that God may open for us a door of speech, to speak the mystery of Christ, on account of which I am also imprisoned. If we are freed from tribulation through your prayers, it will benefit you in teaching.

So that I may make it manifest, as I ought to speak. So that he himself may determine what should be done, when, and to whom he ought to preach, as Isaiah says: “So that I may know when it is fitting for me to speak.”

Walk in wisdom toward those who are outside. Do not provoke them any further to anger.

Redeeming the time. Through your prudence, making good time out of bad time.

Let your speech always be in grace. In the New Testament, that is; or certainly, let your speech be gracious.

Seasoned with salt. With wisdom and reason, so that our religion may not be judged foolish by philosophers and Gentiles.

So that you may know how you ought to answer each person. Differently to pagans, differently to Jews, and differently to heretics who contradict the truth. Hence Peter also says: “Always ready to give an answer,” and so forth.

Tychicus, the most beloved brother, faithful minister, and fellow-servant in the Lord, will make known to you everything concerning me; I have sent him to you for this very purpose, so that he may learn what concerns you and comfort your hearts, together with Onesimus, the beloved and faithful brother, who is one of you; they will make known to you everything that is being done here. [Col. 0862A] He wants them to be secure concerning his safety, so that they would not be occupied by this sadness.

Aristarchus, my fellow-prisoner, greets you. He was imprisoned together with him, or shared his suffering through the effect of love.

And Mark, Barnabas’s cousin, concerning whom you received instructions: if he comes to you, receive him. And Jesus, who is called Justus, who are of the circumcision. These alone are my fellow-workers for the kingdom of God, and they have been a comfort to me. In the New Testament, through which one enters the kingdom, just as Satan is called death because he is the cause of death.

Epaphras, who is one of you, a servant of Christ Jesus, greets you. He is always concerned for you in his prayers, so that you may stand perfect and complete in every will of God. They were so perfect that they are urged to persevere. Therefore he aided their labor through his prayers.

[Col. 0862B] For I bear him witness that he has much labor for you, for those who are in Laodicea, and for those in Hierapolis. Such were the disciples of the apostles in the earliest period: they imitated their teachers and were concerned for the salvation of all.

Luke, the most beloved physician, and Demas greet you. Greet the brothers who are in Laodicea, Nympha, and the church that is in her house. When this Epistle has been read among you, see that it is also read in the church of the Laodiceans, and that you likewise read the one from Laodicea. The evangelist was formerly a physician, just as Matthew, although already an apostle, is still called a tax collector.

And say to Archippus: “See to the ministry that you received in the Lord, so that you may fulfill it.” He is said to have been a deacon.

[Col. 0862C] The greeting in my own hand, Paul’s. Remember my bonds. Either pray that I may be restored to you, or remember that I suffer these things because of you, and imitate the endurance of my sufferings.

The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. Amen.

## ON THE FIRST EPISTLE TO THE THESSALONIANS

[Col. 0861]

## CHAPTER ONE

[Col. 0861C]

Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy, to the church of the Thessalonians. Through them the word had been announced to the children, as also to the Corinthians; he mentions this concerning the same people in the second Epistle.

In God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. Through faith in the Son they were in the Father as well as in the Son. For whoever confesses the Son also has the Father.

Grace to you and peace. From God the Father, that is, and our Lord Jesus Christ.

We always give thanks to God for all of you. For the memory of all of you is pleasing to us.

Making mention of you in our prayers without ceasing. In unending prayer, the extent of his memory and the love that their merits deserved are shown.

Remembering your work of faith and labor. Not without reason do they remember that faith, which is proved by the labor of righteousness, the affection of love, and endurance of sufferings.

And your love and steadfastness in the hope of our Lord Jesus Christ before our God and Father. Toward God our Father. Whoever possesses perfect love patiently endures everything because of future hope.

[Col. 0862D] Knowing, brothers beloved by God, your election. Remembering the time of your election, how we preached and you believed.

For our Gospel did not come to you in word alone. It should be noted that teaching can be effective when it is commended by an example of righteousness.

But in power. In power, whether of signs or of endurance in sufferings.

And in the Holy Spirit. Whom you received devotedly; or whose power we demonstrated through signs.

And in great fullness. Of perfection, righteousness, conduct, and life.

As you know what kind of people we were among you for your sake. For your progress, abstaining even from what was unlawful, as is contained below.

And you became imitators of us and of the Lord. Receiving the word amid sufferings, just as we taught and the Lord preached.

Receiving the word in much tribulation, with joy of the Holy Spirit. That is, rejoice truly in the Holy Spirit, as we read that the apostles did.

So that you became an example to all believers in Macedonia and Achaia. The examples of the perfected are presented as a pattern to all believers. Thus, through your example, the provinces too made progress.

For the word of the Lord has been proclaimed by you, not only in Macedonia and Achaia, but everywhere. Such is the nature of fame: whether one announces something good or something bad, it spreads everywhere with complete speed.

Your faith, which is directed toward God, has gone forth. It has turned from you toward God.

So that we do not need to say anything. This means that, when we begin to speak of your example, they themselves say that they know it very well.

For they themselves report concerning us what kind of reception we had among you, and how you turned to God. The character both of our steadfastness and of your conduct is known to everyone.

From idols, to serve the living and true God. “Idol” derives from *simulando*, “imitating.” Fittingly, they are said to have turned from false lords to the true and living God.

And to await his Son from heaven, whom he raised from the dead—Jesus. You are of such a character that you await the Lord’s coming confidently and with joy.

Who delivered us from the coming wrath. By forgiving sins, and by his teaching and example, he delivered us from wrath. Thus, we already possess freedom in hope.

## CHAPTER II

For you yourselves know, brothers, our reception among you. He reminds them of this so that they may recognize the truth of what they say and may make still greater progress through their example.

For it was not empty, but after first suffering much and being subjected to insults. A word that is fulfilled through steadfast endurance of suffering is not empty.

As you know, at Philippi. Since some of you seem to think that we suffered at Philippi, yet neither feared the persecutions nor ceased preaching.

[Col. 0863D] We had confidence in our God. He can deliver us in the present or in the future and repay everyone for our labor.

To speak the gospel of God to you amid much anxiety. Not carelessly or superficially, but with no small concern—indeed, with great concern.

For our exhortation was not from error. Therefore we do not err; for whoever thinks or teaches that many can reign with Christ in the manner stated elsewhere is in error: “Do not be deceived, for God is not mocked.”

Nor from impurity. Such was the teaching of Jovinian.

Nor in deceit. We were not teaching or persuading against our own steadfastness.

[Col. 0864A] But just as we have been approved by God to be entrusted with the gospel, so we speak—not as pleasing human beings, who can be deceived,

but God, who tests our hearts. We are upright, as having been tested by God and appointed by him to this office; he searches out the hidden things of the heart.

For we were never found in a word of flattery, as you know. Such are those who please human beings, granting the sick everything they desire while neglecting their death.

Nor under a pretext of greed—God is witness—nor seeking glory from human beings, either from you or from others. Everyone who flatters does so either for greed or for empty glory. But the one who is shown to teach for God’s sake is the one who seeks none of these things.

[Col. 0864B] Although we could have been a burden to you, as apostles of Christ. Either in this respect, or in what God ordained—that is, that we should live from the gospel.

But we became little children among you. Humbling ourselves and not even demanding the honor that was due.

As if a nurse were cherishing her own children. Humbling herself in everything and making herself like a little child, so that by her example she might lead them to greater things. For sometimes she even babbles with her tongue, pretends to eat, and grows accustomed to walking slowly with them.

So, desiring you with eager affection, we were willing to impart to you not only the gospel of God, but also our own souls. Just as a nurse wishes to pour into a little child not only words but also the whole sense of her perfection, so that the child may quickly become her equal, so we did everything [Col. 0864C] by which you could make progress.

Because you had become very dear to us. On account of your faith and conduct, which we mentioned above.

For you remember, brothers, our labor and toil, working night and day. The labor of our hands by night, and the toil of the word by day; otherwise, he was always at work when he was teaching.

So that we would not burden any of you. He labored among these people, as among the Corinthians and Ephesians, wishing to remove from them any pretext either for teaching or for suspecting something about him.

We preached the gospel of God among you. You are witnesses, and God is witness, just as Samuel calls the people to witness.

How holy, just, and blameless our conduct was among you who believed. We did this so that we would not seem to give you any cause for offense.

As you know how we exhorted each one of you, as a father does his own children. A nurse cherishes little ones; but once they are making progress, a father instructs them.

And, consoling you, we bore witness. In your tribulations we consoled you with the promises of Christ.

So that you might walk worthily of God. He walks worthily of God who does nothing unworthy of God.

Who called you into his own kingdom and glory. This will be possessed only by those like him, namely, through the example of righteousness and holiness.

Therefore we too give thanks to God without ceasing: because, when you received from us the word of the hearing of God. [Col. 0865A] That which you first heard from God—or as though you had heard God himself.

You received it not as the word of human beings, but, as it truly is, the word of God. One receives the word of human beings by despising it; but you believed in such a way that you thought you were hearing from God himself.

Who works in you who have believed. Through the word or through signs; that is, he exercises powers. For, says Mark, these signs will follow those who believe.

For you, brothers, became imitators of the churches of God that are in Judea in Christ Jesus. Of them it is said: “For you even showed sympathy to those in bonds and accepted with joy the seizure of your possessions.”

Because you too suffered the same things from your fellow-countrymen as they did from the Jews. I marvel at you all the more, since you had examples neither from the Law [Col. 0865B] nor from the Prophets.

Who killed both the Lord Jesus and the prophets, and persecuted us; and they do not please God. What wonder if evil people persecute us, when they did not spare the Lord himself?

And they are hostile to all human beings, forbidding us to speak to the Gentiles so that they may be saved, thus always filling up their sins. They hinder not only the Jews, but also begrudge the Gentiles, adding to the accumulation of their sins.

For the wrath of God has come upon them to the end. Either because I proclaim the punishment by which they have been taken captive, or because understanding has been removed from those who do not believe.

But we, brothers, having been separated from you for a time, in presence but not in heart. As he says elsewhere: “Absent in body, but present in spirit.”

[Col. 0865C] We hastened all the more eagerly to see your face, with much longing. For we wished to come to you—I, Paul, indeed, both once and again—but Satan hindered us: through the tribulations of our persecutors.

For what is our hope, or joy, or crown of glory? Is it not you, before our Lord Jesus Christ at his coming? We rightly long for you, through whom we hope for the joy of gladness and the crown of glory.

For you are our glory and joy. Good teachers generally place all their hope, joy, and glory in the progress of their disciples.

## CHAPTER III

Therefore, unable to endure any longer. That none of us should come to you.

[Col. 0865D] We decided to remain alone in Athens. We preferred to remain alone rather than not know what was happening with you.

And we sent Timothy, our brother. The question arises how Timothy was sent; but this was stated earlier.

And a minister of God in the gospel of Christ. Helpers are commonly called assistants to disciples.

To strengthen and exhort you concerning your faith. For this reason alone: because you had believed perfectly.

So that no one might be shaken by these tribulations. I do not say, “so that all might not be shaken,” but “so that not even one might be shaken.”

For you yourselves know that we have been appointed to this. Therefore you ought not to be surprised, since you know that we cannot pass through any other way, as the Lord says: “Behold, I am sending you as sheep into the midst of wolves.” And again: “Behold, I told you that you would have peace in me; but in this world, distress.”

For even when we were with you, we foretold that we would suffer tribulations; and so it happened, as you know. This was so that the novelty of the event would not frighten you, but rather our prophecy would strengthen you, just as the Lord foretold beforehand that he himself would suffer.

Therefore, since I could endure no longer, I sent to learn about your faith, lest the tempter had perhaps tested you. He says: “Consider what sort of things those suffer in whom you think God dwells”; and perhaps this might shake your faith.

He who tests. Just as Job was tested by the Lord.

But now, when Timothy came to us from you and announced to us your faith and love, and that you have a good remembrance of us, always longing [Col. 0866B] to see us, just as we also long to see you. Because, believing firmly in Christ, you hold fast to the faith, and you love us with your customary affection.

Therefore we were comforted, brothers, concerning you in all our need and tribulation, through your faith. We feel no need or tribulation because of the greatness of our joy at your condition.

For now we live, if you stand firm in the Lord. Even if we are killed, we live, because our life consists in your steadfastness.

For what thanksgiving can we render to God for you, in all the joy with which we rejoice because of you before our God and Lord? Your conduct provides us with a threefold cause for joy: you are making progress, the Lord is glorified through you, [Col. 0866C] and you offer an example to others.

Night and day praying most earnestly that we may see your face. He shows how greatly the brothers are to be desired, since he himself desires them so greatly. For who, after gaining a reputation, would not wish to see the one who has gained it?

And complete what is lacking in your faith. If your faith lacks anything in teaching.

Now may God himself, our Father, and our Lord Jesus Christ direct our way to you. Removing the stumbling-blocks of the devil, by which our arrival among you is hindered.

May the Lord multiply you and make your love abound. For it is already full and has been proved by its works.

Toward one another and toward all. So that you may love not only Christians but also people of every group—not because of error, but by the grace of nature—and may not deny them the mercy that God presently shows them in whatever they need.

Just as we do toward you, to strengthen your hearts. He made it abound so that you too might strengthen the hearts of others.

Blameless in holiness before our God and Father at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ with all his saints. Amen. Not before human beings, as is said of Zechariah and Elizabeth, and through Isaiah: “You shall be just for me, says the Lord.”

## CHAPTER IV

Finally, then, brothers. After praise and consolation, he begins the exhortation.

[Col. 0867A] We ask and exhort you in the Lord Jesus: just as you received from us how you ought to walk and please God, so walk in this way that you may abound more and more. Since Christ is the way for you, walk with steps worthy of him; for as faith and conduct ought to increase with age, so, with the age of the body, food and diligence increase.

For you know what commandments I gave you through the Lord Jesus. For this is the will of God, your sanctification: that you abstain from fornication. Sanctification withdraws the Christian from every form of self-indulgence; one who lacks self-control ought not to touch the holy body of Christ. This is especially so since Moses, wishing to sanctify the Jews, commanded the whole people to abstain from women so that they might deserve to attain God’s presence.

[Col. 0867B] That each of you should know how to possess his own vessel in sanctification and honor. Let each person sanctify and honor his own body by keeping it chaste. It must also be considered that he writes to them as perfect people, not as to the weak Corinthians.

Not in the passion of desire, like the Gentiles who do not know God. Do not become like the Gentiles, serving excessive and immoderate lust, who do not know that God loves chastity.

And that no one should overstep or defraud his brother in business. After a devoted commitment to continence, let no one attempt by force to impose some deception upon his brother; or, in any business matter, let no one defraud another.

For the Lord is an avenger in all these matters, as we told you beforehand and solemnly testified. Not only in fornication and public disgrace, but also in transgressing one’s commitment. For whoever has vowed continence to God has made unlawful for himself what was otherwise permitted.

For God did not call us to impurity. Impurity does not permit one to receive the body of Christ boldly.

But to sanctification. So that you may live according to Christ’s example. Whoever has this hope in him sanctifies himself, just as he is holy.

Therefore whoever rejects these things rejects not a human being but God, who also gave his Holy Spirit in us. Not me, but Christ, who speaks in me; everyone who does not live holily does injury to his Spirit.

But concerning brotherly love, we have no need to write to you. [Col. 0867D] See how perfect they were: they did not need to be admonished about such an important and necessary commandment.

For you yourselves have been taught by God to love one another. Indeed, you do this toward all the brothers throughout Macedonia. By Christ, who said: “I give you a new commandment.” This is new: that we should die for one another, because this did not belong to his own former Testament.

But we ask you, brothers, to abound still more and to make it your aim. That is, to love those who are still unknown.

To live quietly, to attend to your own affairs, and to work with your hands, as we commanded you. Some were restlessly going around various houses, [Col. 0868A] even asking unbelievers for things to the reproach of religion. Although he deals with this more fully in the second letter, he therefore prefers that they be occupied either with caring for their own affairs or with the labor of their hands, rather than incur the harm of idleness and the sin of restlessness.

So that you may walk honorably before those who are outside, and desire nothing belonging to anyone. Do not let those who seem able to provide for you themselves mark you with reproach.

But we do not want you to be ignorant, brothers, concerning those who sleep. One who is certain to rise again sleeps, as was said in the Gospel concerning Lazarus.

So that you may not grieve like the others who have no hope. One manner is appropriate for someone going abroad, another for someone who is dying.

For if we believe that Jesus died and rose again, [Col. 0868B] if we believe things we do not see, and through his resurrection are certain that we have not failed to attain salvation, why should we not similarly believe that which the Gentiles, who do not believe in the seeing God, do not believe?

So also God will bring with Jesus those who have fallen asleep. He who raised up the head promises that he will also raise up the remaining members.

For we say this to you by the word of the Lord. From the pronouncement of the Gospel.

For we who live, who remain until the coming of the Lord. The Apostle always made the day of the Lord a matter of concern, as though it might find them in the body.

Will not precede those who have fallen asleep. Their resurrection will be as swift as our being taken up.

For the Lord himself will descend from heaven with a command, with the voice of an archangel, [Col. 0868C] and with the trumpet of God. He shows the terror of that day, when every heavenly power and the elements will be moved, so that we may know with what conscience we ought to await the day of the Lord.

And the dead who are in Christ will rise first. Then we who live, who are left, will be caught up together with them in the clouds to meet Christ in the air. Those who have died in Christ will rise first; and those who are found alive and holy will be caught up together with them. They will not be judged, but rather will judge.

And so we shall always be with the Lord. In the same glory [Col. 0868D] of eternity.

Therefore comfort one another with these words. It should be noted that he gives this command to those who are joyful, so that they may instruct one another with teachings.

## CHAPTER V

But concerning the times and the moments, brothers, you have no need for us to write to you. For you yourselves know carefully. You have been taught by the clearest reading of the Gospel.

For the day of the Lord will come like a thief in the night. When everyone thinks that they are sleeping securely.

When they say, “Peace and security,” then sudden destruction will come upon them. Then punishment is especially to be feared, because they do not now expect it.

[Col. 0869A] Like labor upon a woman with child, and they will not escape. Just as a woman does not escape the pains when childbirth comes.

But you, brothers, are not in darkness, so that that day may seize you like a thief. You are not so ignorant that you do not know that you must always be prepared.

For you are all children of light and children of day. Of the knowledge of truth.

We are not of night or of darkness. For just as darkness gives confidence to commit wrongdoing, so does ignorance.

Therefore let us not sleep, as the others do. Those who have slept in this way have even forgotten themselves.

But let us watch and be sober. Pay attention to yourselves, lest your hearts become burdened with feasting, drunkenness, and the cares of this life; for cares too intoxicate the mind.

[Col. 0869B] For those who sleep, sleep at night; and those who are drunk, are drunk at night. Therefore they are idle and drunk, because they are in darkness.

But let us who belong to the day be sober. We who have Christ as our day ought to be neither idle nor drunk.

Having put on the breastplate of faith and love, and the helmet of the hope of salvation. Everything stands through faith, love, and righteousness, which elsewhere he compares to a breastplate.

For God did not appoint us for wrath, but for the obtaining of salvation through our Lord Jesus Christ. They have been appointed for wrath because they have already been judged.

Who died for us. So that we would not die.

So that whether we watch or sleep, we may live together with him. Whether we are found in the body or outside the body, we may always live with him.

Therefore comfort one another and build one another up, just as you are doing. It should be noted that he gives this command to the laity, whom he also urges to devote themselves to works of love.

But we ask you, brothers, to recognize those who labor among you. That is, to understand their labor.

And preside over you in the Lord and admonish you. By the example of righteousness, not by earthly power, as Peter says.

And to esteem them very highly in love because of their work, and be at peace among yourselves. Presbyters who labor in the word are to be honored doubly: namely, with the service of love and the dignity of their office.

But we ask you, brothers: rebuke the restless, [Col. 0869D] console the fainthearted. According to the variety of diseases, different medicines must be applied. The former must be rebuked so that they may not perish; the latter must be consoled so that they may not fail.

Support the weak. Sustain those who have only recently come to faith and have not yet been strengthened.

Be patient with everyone. Even with those who are rebuked, because an impatient person is not corrected but provoked.

See that no one repays evil for evil to anyone. With all diligence, take care that you do not return evil to someone weaker—as an ignorant person might; for I do not think anyone does this deliberately. Everyone who inflicts injury does evil; and whoever returns an injury inflicts injury and does evil, because, as was said above, everyone who inflicts injury does evil.

But always pursue what is good toward one another and toward all. Not only toward you Christians, but also toward human beings.

Rejoice always. In purity of conscience.

Pray without ceasing. If you cannot do so constantly with the tongue, at least do so in the heart, as it is said to Moses while he was silent: “Why do you cry out to me?” Or let your every action be such that it may always pray to God for you.

Give thanks in all things. In everything that happens, [Col. 0870B] as Job did; or let thanks be rendered to the Lord throughout your entire conduct.

For this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning all of you. Just as it was fulfilled in every respect in Christ, so may it be fulfilled in all of you.

Do not extinguish the Spirit. Do not extinguish the Spirit of exhortation through questions. Or he used “spirit” for the grace of tongues, as he says: “If I pray in a tongue, my spirit prays.” Thus also he says to the Corinthians: “Do not forbid speaking in tongues.” So here too he bears witness that the Spirit must not be extinguished.

Do not despise prophecies. But test everything; hold fast to what is good; abstain from every kind of evil. Whether they are proclaiming future events or discussing past events, test only whether what is said is contrary to the Law; if anything of that kind is found, reject it.

Now may the God of peace. Who endures everything, even those who blaspheme.

Sanctify you in every respect. Whether through grace or through teaching.

So that your spirit, soul, and body may be complete. Although the grace of the spirit is always complete in itself, it is not complete in us unless it is possessed by those who are complete.

May it be kept blameless at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ. Until the day of judgment, because it is not only beginnings that should be praised, but the end.

Faithful is he who called you. He who said: “Come to me, all who labor and are burdened, and I will give you rest.”

[Col. 0870D] He will also do it. Brothers, pray for us. Greet all the brothers with a holy kiss. This is what he promised.

I adjure you by the Lord that this letter be read to all the holy brothers. One may adjure, but not swear an oath.

The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. Amen. May grace remain with everyone.

# INTO THE SECOND LETTER TO THE THESSALONIANS

[Col. 0869]

## CHAPTER I

[Col. 0869D] Paul, and Silvanus, and Timothy, to the church of the Thessalonians in God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. Grace to you and peace from God the Father and the Lord [Col. 0870D] Jesus Christ. We ought always to give thanks to God for you, brothers, as is fitting. He has acquired for himself such a church.

Because your faith is growing greatly. Therefore praise increases.

And the love of each one of you for one another abounds, so that we ourselves boast of you among the churches of God. You are making such progress that not only do all those beneath you praise you, but we ourselves also set you before everyone as examples to imitate.

For your patience and faith in all your persecutions and tribulations. Unless you believed in future things, you would be utterly unwilling to endure these things.

Which you endure as an example of the righteous judgment of God. So that you may provide an example of awaiting God’s just judgment, [Col. 0871B] which you believe will come in this way.

So that you may be considered worthy of the kingdom of God, for which you also suffer. Those are worthy of the kingdom of God who have given glory to him, knowing that no suffering is equal to its worth.

If indeed it is just with God to repay tribulation to those who trouble you. Here “if indeed” is an expression of affirmation, not doubt, as though he were saying: “If justice is able to judge externally what is just.” For just as he unquestionably promised rest to those who suffer for the Lord’s name, so without hesitation he promised tribulation to those who trouble them.

And to you who are troubled, rest with us. Because you suffer together with us.

At the revelation of the Lord Jesus from heaven with the angels [Col. 0871C] of his power,

in flaming fire, giving vengeance. If, by God’s command, the flame was able not to touch the three boys at all, why should it not be believed that the same power could be harsher toward some and gentler toward others? He says this against those who imagined that punishment consisted in conscience, because this seemed impossible to them.

To those who do not know God and do not obey the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ. Not only to those who do not know, but also to those who do not obey the disciplines of the gospel.

They will suffer eternal punishment in destruction. Punishment cannot be said to exist in the one who suffers.

Away from the face of the Lord and from the glory of his power. From the sight of the Just One, they will receive the sentence of condemnation.

[Col. 0871D] When he comes to be glorified in his saints. He himself is to be glorified in his members, his children, who will shine with the splendor of the sun.

And to become wonderful in all who have believed. The wicked and those who mocked humility will marvel at the jubilation of the saints’ unexpected salvation.

Because our testimony concerning you was believed on that day. Because many of you believed our testimony on that day.

For this reason we also always pray for you, that our God may deem you worthy of his calling. That you may be found worthy of that to which you were called, because those invited earlier were not worthy.

And may he fulfill every good intention of his goodness and the work of faith in power. Through the help of grace and the consolation of the knowledge of the virtues that belong to the work of faith.

So that the name of our Lord Jesus Christ may be glorified in you, and you in him. May the name of Christ be renowned in your deeds, and may you be glorious in his signs and virtues.

According to the grace of our God and the Lord Jesus Christ. He asks from us what we can do; what we cannot do, may he bestow.

## CHAPTER II

But we ask you, brothers, concerning the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ. I am certain that nothing is dearer to you than this.

And concerning our gathering to him. When the elect will be gathered from the four [Col. 0872B] winds of heaven, so that where the body is, there the eagles may gather.

That you not be quickly shaken from your understanding or terrified. One is very easily shaken who departs from the Gospel’s teaching concerning the Lord’s coming.

Neither by a spirit nor by a word. Do not let signs terrify you as though they had been performed through a spirit, since the Savior also warned of this beforehand; nor let a dialectical argument mislead you.

Nor by a letter supposedly sent by us. The devil could devise this too by his cunning, as is evident in many apocryphal writings, which are given the names of the apostles in order to create belief in falsehood.

As though the day of the Lord were already present. Let no one deceive you in any way, saying: “Here is the Christ,” or, “There he is.”

[Col. 0872C] For unless the apostasy comes first. Unless the Antichrist comes, Christ will not come. What he calls “apostasy” here, elsewhere he called “refuge.” In the Latin copies, both are to be understood in this way: unless the deserter from the truth comes, whether the deserter from his own principate, or the departure of the Gentiles from the Roman Empire, as he says in Daniel through the image of the beast.

And the man of sin is revealed. That is, the devil.

The son of perdition. He will possess him as though he had been born for him, in servitude; according to Isaiah, he is said to trouble the nations.

Who opposes and exalts himself above everything called God or worshiped, so that he takes his seat in the temple of God, displaying himself as though he were God. He will boast himself above every power and eternity, claiming that he will correct or enlarge the mysteries of worship, and he will attempt to rebuild the temple of Jerusalem and restore all the ceremonies of the Law—only so that he may dissolve the truth of Christ’s gospel. This will persuade the Jews to accept him as Christ, since he will come in his own name, not in God’s.

Do you not remember that when I was still with you, I used to tell you these things? And now you know what is restraining him. That is, what delay prevents him from coming.

So that he may be revealed in his own time. That time has not yet arrived.

For the mystery of iniquity is already at work. In those who prepare the way before him through his false teachings, whom blessed John says have gone out into the world.

Only that he who now restrains may continue to restrain, until he is removed from the midst. [Col. 0873A] And then the lawless one will be revealed. Until the kingdom that now holds power is removed from the midst, before the Antichrist is revealed.

Whom the Lord Jesus will kill with the breath of his mouth. By heavenly command, or by that alone.

And destroy by the brightness of his coming. For, like lightning, he will flash everywhere throughout the world, when the elements have been loosed and shaken by fire.

The one whose coming is according to the working of Satan, with every power and signs and lying wonders, and with every deception of wickedness for those who are perishing. As he foretold earlier, they will perform signs in order to deceive, if possible, even the elect, through the appearance and imitation of powers, just as Jannes and Mambres did before Pharaoh.

[Col. 0873B] Because they did not receive the love of the truth so that they might be saved. Therefore God will send them a working of error, so that they may believe the lie. He permits it to come; for if God sends it, it is not the working of Satan.

So that all who did not believe the truth but consented to iniquity may be judged. Let them not excuse themselves, claiming that they did not believe the divine powers because of the obscurity of Christ’s incarnation, when they believed a human being deceived by diabolical art.

But we ought always to give thanks to God for you, brothers beloved by God. Because we have received the love of the truth, and for this reason he loves us.

Because God chose us as firstfruits for salvation, in sanctification of the Spirit and faith in the truth. Seeing that you were ready to believe, just as elsewhere it was revealed to the man reclining at table by the Macedonian.

Through this he also called you by our gospel to the obtaining of the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ. We have been called for this: to obtain Christ’s glory. For we know that when he appears, we shall be like him.

Therefore, brothers, stand firm. Immovable in the faith of the truth.

And hold fast to the traditions that you learned, whether through a word or through our letter. When he wants his own traditions to be held, he does not want foreign ones added. The apostolic tradition is what is preached throughout the whole world, such as the mysteries of baptism.

Now may our Lord Jesus Christ himself, and God our Father, who loved us. Even though we were not worthy.

[Col. 0873D] And gave eternal consolation and good hope through grace. A promise, or the consoling Spirit, who in Greek is called *παράκλητος* (*paraklētos*). There can also be a bad hope through grace.

May he exhort your hearts and strengthen them. Through virtues and revelation.

In every good work and word. First in work, and afterward in word.

## CHAPTER III

Finally, brothers, pray for us. He gives an example of humility and an occasion for love, so that we may more boldly pray for one another. At the same time, it should be noted in what matters the Apostle asks for prayer.

That the word of God may run and be glorified, as it is among you. [Col. 0874A] May it run through abundance and be magnified through the progress of its hearers.

And that we may be delivered from unreasonable and evil people. For not everyone has faith. Not everyone believes; therefore they contradict.

But God is faithful. For he does not abandon anyone except those who abandon him.

Who will strengthen you and guard you from evil. In faith, through teaching and grace.

But we have confidence in you, brothers, in the Lord: that whatever we command, you both do and will do. May the Lord direct your hearts into the love of God and the patience of Christ, revealing how great are the things he has promised for the sake of his love to those who suffer insults.

But we command you, brothers, in the name of our Lord [Col. 0874B] Jesus Christ, to withdraw from every brother who walks disorderly and not according to the tradition that they received from us. Because in the first letter we admonished them more gently, and they did not wish to correct themselves. Or let them be ashamed in this way: that the saints separate themselves from them. By the authority of this passage, one ought plainly to withdraw from every Christian who does not walk according to the Apostle’s commands.

For you yourselves know how you ought to imitate us, because we were not restless among you, nor did we eat bread from anyone without paying, but worked in labor and toil night and day, so that we would not burden any of you. We are an example to believers.

Not as though we had no authority. For “the laborer is worthy of his wages.”

[Col. 0874C] But so that we might offer ourselves as an example for you to imitate us. We did not want to provide anyone with an occasion for greed, which is the source of restlessness.

For even when we were with you, we commanded these things. Because we foresaw that some would be of this sort.

For if anyone does not wish to work. Let them either remain quietly seated, or, if they are true apostles, let them follow us, if they claim to walk not for greed but for God’s sake.

Neither should he eat. Let this be not only the punishment of restlessness, but also its correction.

For we hear that some among you walk restlessly, doing no work. He gives the reasons for the preceding statement, indicating to whom it should properly apply: namely, to those who walk restlessly, not to those who sit quietly.

But acting inquisitively. Investigating what is happening in each city, province, and household.

To such people we command and exhort in the Lord Jesus Christ. He does not cease admonishing them even after a second correction.

That, working quietly, they should eat their own bread. Not someone else’s through restlessness.

But you, brothers, do not grow weary in doing good. I forbid giving to such people, not to everyone, so that you will not think I am cutting off the practice of good works.

If anyone does not obey our word through this letter, mark that person and do not associate with him. If anyone refuses to be corrected a third time,

so that he may be put to shame. Not so that he may be cut off completely.

And do not regard him as an enemy, but correct him as a brother. Correct him so that he may amend his ways, and do not cut him off so that he may despair. The sick person must be healed, not killed, lest restlessness turn into apostasy.

God himself of peace grant you everlasting peace in every place. The Lord be with you all. The greeting in my own hand—Paul’s—which is the sign in every [Col. 0876A] Epistle, I write thus: “The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.” With these words he subscribed all his Epistles, except that to the Galatians, which he wrote out entirely in his own hand, so that afterward neither he nor an angel might be believed.

# ON THE FIRST EPISTLE TO TIMOTHY

[Col. 0875]

## CHAPTER ONE

[Col. 0875A]

**Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ.** The authority both of his name and of his office is stated beforehand, because of those to whom he was going to respond.

**According to the command of God our Savior, and of Christ Jesus our hope.** Not according to my own presumption: at the same time, the one command of the Father and the Son is demonstrated.

**To Timothy, a beloved son in the faith.** A son in faith, not in the flesh.

**Grace and mercy and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.** Having freely obtained mercy, we have been reconciled to God.

**Just as I urged you to remain at Ephesus when I was going to Macedonia, so that you might charge certain persons not to teach differently.** [Col. 0875B] He had foretold that wolves would enter among them, who would not spare the flock.

**Nor to devote themselves to fables.** Which they call *Deuteroseis*. Hence, in the Gospel, those who teach human doctrines are condemned.

**And endless genealogies.** The genealogies of the ancients, in which they claim supreme knowledge if they enumerate all the generations from the beginning.

**Which produce questions rather than God’s edification, which is in faith.** Both ancient controversies and the needless anxieties concerning genealogies are superfluous.

**But the end of the commandment is love from a pure heart.** The love of God and neighbor, on which the whole Law and the Prophets depend: if this comes from a pure heart, we shall scarcely be able to sin.

[Col. 0875C] **And a good conscience.** So that your conscience may bear witness to the truth.

**And sincere faith.** For faith is insincere when it is promised only with the mouth and denied in action.

**From these some, having strayed, have turned aside to empty talk, wishing to be teachers of the Law, although they understand neither what they say nor the matters about which they make assertions.** It is the height of folly to wish to establish what is not understood by means of matters understood even less.

**But we know that the Law is good.** As promulgated by God, in keeping with the character of the time; just as elsewhere it is called holy law.

**If someone uses it lawfully.** If someone knows for whom, why, and for how long it was given to be observed.

**Knowing this, that the Law is not laid down for the righteous.** Therefore [Col. 0875D] Christians do not need it, since they have been justified through Christ and have also learned to avoid occasions of sin. For why is it said, “You shall not kill,” to those who are not permitted even to become angry?

[Col. 0876A] **But for the unjust and disobedient, the ungodly and sinners, the wicked and defiled, murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers, killers, fornicators, men who have intercourse with males, kidnappers, liars and perjurers.** It was given for all those whom it strives to recall after they have cast aside their crimes.

**And if there is anything else opposed to sound doctrine, which is according to the Gospel.** There are therefore doctrines that are not sound; against these the Law was also given, since they are contrary to heavenly ordinances. What, then, are they seeking there that they do not have here? At the same time he shows that the Law agrees with the Gospels.

**Of the glory of the blessed God.** Through which God is glorified.

**Which was entrusted to me.** Lest his opponents say, “Who was he to whom the Gospel should be entrusted?” he says:

**I give thanks to him who strengthened me, Christ Jesus [Col. 0876B] our Lord.** When I was useless and weak.

**Because he considered me faithful, appointing me to the ministry.** Although I was formerly a blasphemer, a persecutor, and an insolent man. A righteous person first accuses himself, so that as soon as he begins, the adversary may be confounded.

**But I obtained the mercy of God, because I acted ignorantly.** It is shown that the sin of ignorance is lighter.

**In unbelief.** Because, not believing, I was unable to understand.

**But the grace of our Lord abounded exceedingly, with the faith and love that are in Christ Jesus.** Where iniquity had abounded, as soon as I believed I began to love Christ more greatly, since he had forgiven me my great sins.

**The saying is trustworthy and worthy of all acceptance.** Let all believe it, and let the conscience of all recognize it as true.

[Col. 0876C] **That Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners.** Therefore he also saved me among the other sinners. He would rightly have prejudged me if he had come to call only the righteous.

**Of whom I am chief.** Here “I am” is used for “I was,” just as Matthew is called a tax collector although he was already an apostle of Christ.

**But for this reason I obtained mercy.** As David says: “I will teach transgressors your ways, and the ungodly shall turn back to you.” If they see that my sins have been forgiven, then I shall teach that no one ought to despair.

**So that Christ Jesus might first display in me all patience.** He not only forgives persecutors when they are converted but also bestows on them the honor of apostleship.

[Col. 0876D] **For an example to those who are going to believe in him for eternal life.** As an example, so that they may not despair.

[Col. 0877A] **Now to the King of the ages, immortal, invisible, the only God, be honor and glory forever and ever. Amen.** He who granted me forgiveness though I was undeserving. For a king who rules for a short time, is mortal and visible, and can have a partner, may possess temporal honor and glory, but not everlasting honor.

**This command I entrust to you, son Timothy.** Up to this point he has spoken about his own status and how to respond to opponents; from here he gives authority to appoint and teach, and commends the commands that must be observed.

**According to the prophecies previously made about you.** According to the fact that even before this office you had the gift of prophecy.

**So that in them you may wage the good warfare.** The good warfare is that in which one fights against the devil and vices.

[Col. 0877B] **Having faith.** Faith in Christ perfected, as armor.

**And a good conscience.** By fulfilling what you teach.

**Which some, rejecting, have suffered shipwreck concerning the faith.** By living badly they lost the faith itself, which they appeared to possess; or else, by then defending their vices.

**Among whom are Hymenaeus and Alexander.** Through love of their vices they passed over to heresy.

**Whom I handed over to Satan, so that they may learn not to blaspheme.** For the destruction of the flesh, so that through their present correction they may learn not to deny the future judgment. They were handed over for correction, not for destruction.

## CHAPTER TWO

**I urge, therefore, first of all that supplications be made.** [Col. 0877C] Supplication is prayer offered with greater earnestness.

**Prayers, petitions, and thanksgivings.** For the fact that he made us worthy, even for those who persecute and afflict you.

**For all people, for kings, and for all who are in positions of authority.** So that they may come to know God, or so that they may keep the nations subject. For our tranquility depends upon their peace; but even if we Christians suffer the disturbance of persecution, all unrest will cease.

**So that we may lead a quiet and peaceful life in all piety and purity.** He wants us to be quiet for this purpose: so that our tranquility may advance through piety and purity, not through dissension and luxury.

**For this is good and acceptable before our Savior [Col. 0877D] God.** So that, being quiet, we may serve him in holy works.

**Who desires all people to be saved.** Here [Note: [Col. 0877D] See the notes of Baluzius on Agobard, p. 37 and following.] it is proved that no one ought to be compelled to believe or deprived of freedom of choice. This passage also resolves the objection concerning Pharaoh’s hardening and other questions of the same kind.

**And to come to a knowledge of the truth.** Provided that they themselves are willing to consent to God, who calls them.

**For there is one God.** There is one God, the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit; that is, there is one nature of the Godhead in three persons.

**And one mediator between God and human beings, the man Christ [Col. 0878A] Jesus.** Just as there is one God, so there is one mediator between God and all human beings: that is, no one else of this kind—not Moses, nor any prophet—because he was both human and God. But since he was going to speak about the tradition, he named him only as man.

**Who gave himself as a redemption for all.** He gave himself for all, if all were willing to be redeemed.

**Whose testimony was confirmed at its proper times.** He gave the human race an example of holy life as a testimony, because the prophets also bore witness in their own times. Finally he sent his Son to the tenants.

**For which I was appointed a preacher and an apostle.** In the testimony of Christ, or in Christ.

**I speak the truth; I do not lie, a teacher of the nations in faith [Col. 0878B] and truth.** Therefore I want men to pray in every place. The teacher of the nations gives the law of prayer: by the Savior’s authority, no one should choose a place for prayer either on the mountain or in Jerusalem, but in the spirit, which is understood to be with us everywhere. Indeed, concerning this passage and this matter a question was raised by the Jews, who wished to pray only in the Temple at Jerusalem.

**Lifting up pure hands without anger and disputation.** From slaughter, blood, and every evil deed. The raising of the hands is a testimony of innocence. But one must keep not only one’s hands free from evil action, but also one’s mind clean from anger and thoughts of disputation—the mind that asks to be forgiven. No one can obtain anything while thinking otherwise.

**Likewise also women.** Everything I have said concerning men.

[Col. 0878C] **In an adorned manner.** Honorably and suitably to nature.

**Adorning themselves with modesty and self-control.** These are the adornments of a Christian woman.

**And not with braided hair.** They ought not to provide an occasion for lust.

**Or with gold or pearls.** These are parts of the earth, over which the human being was appointed master.

**Or expensive clothing.** Clothing which, because of its excessive thinness, does not even keep out the cold, and whose price could have clothed many people of the same nature.

**But with what is fitting for women who profess piety through good works.** Such things, therefore, belong not to women who profess chastity but to women who deny it.

**Let a woman learn in silence, with complete submission.** Let her indeed learn, but with all humility and love.

[Col. 0878D] **But I do not permit a woman to teach.** He does not permit her to teach publicly; for she ought to teach a son or brother privately.

**Nor to exercise authority over a man, but to be in silence.** She should not become proud by usurping the office of teacher, but should remain silent in the Church.

**For Adam was formed first, then Eve. And Adam was not deceived, but the woman was deceived.** He gives the reason why he wants them to be subject: namely, because they are later in creation and first in guilt.

**She was in transgression. But she will be saved through the bearing of children.** She was in transgression of the commandment. But a woman should not therefore despair, because through baptism—which is the generation of children—she will be saved: not Eve, but a believing woman. Eve was introduced as an example of creation; the discussion did not properly concern her salvation. Otherwise, just as “the righteousness of the righteous will be upon himself,” and just as Noah, Job, and Daniel will deliver their sons, so Eve will be saved through her children.

**If they remain.** Just as above he passed from the plural number of women to the singular when he said, “Let a woman learn in silence,” so here he returns to the plural.

**In faith and love.** In the faith of Christ and love of neighbor.

**And sanctification with self-control.** It should be noted that faith alone is not sufficient for the salvation of one who lives on after baptism unless she possesses holiness of mind and body, which is difficult to preserve without self-control.

## CHAPTER THREE

[Col. 0879B]

**The saying is trustworthy: If anyone desires the office of bishop.** First he instructs the laity, from whom the best are chosen for the priesthood; then he explains what sort of men should be ordained.

**He desires a good work.** He urges him toward the desire for good work, not toward honor.

**For a bishop must be irreproachable.** Otherwise he will not be the ruler of the Church, which the Apostle elsewhere defined as without blemish.

**The husband of one wife.** Men are not even permitted to walk about veiled; much less are they permitted what is forbidden even to a layman.

**Temperate.** In mind and body.

**Well ordered, prudent, chaste.** With all these spiritual adornments.

**Hospitable.** The whole people should be encouraged to works of humanity by the example of their leader.
