**A teacher.** Both by word and by example. If he wished—or ought—to know everyone’s concerns and how all might respond, how much more should a priest inquire into the Law, since he is the angel of almighty God!

**Not given to wine.** So that he may be able to rebuke drunkards confidently.

**Not violent.** Either so that he is not aggressive in striking, or so that he does not wound the consciences of the weak by his bad example.

**But moderate.** One who does everything with measure.

**Not quarrelsome, not greedy, but managing his own household well, having children subject to him with all purity.** A servant of God ought not to quarrel. Quarrels and disputes arise chiefly from greed.

**But if someone does not know how to manage his own household well, how will he take care of the Church of God?** In what follows he explained this: whether he has raised his children in purity and humility. By this his diligence is proved. If he did not know how to educate his own children, how will he govern so many children of God, whose characters differ according to their number? Or with what confidence will one who has undisciplined children dare to demand discipline?

**Not a recent convert, lest, being puffed up, he fall into the judgment of the devil.** He must not be so recently reborn that he can quickly be exalted through ignorance and think that he has obtained not a ministry of humility but the administration of secular power, thereby deserving condemnation for pride—like the devil, who was judged and cast down because of his arrogance.

[Col. 0880A] **Moreover, he must also have a good testimony from those who are outside.** So that he may preside over the Church of God without offense to Jews, unbelievers, or Greeks. For everyone naturally knows how to condemn vices and praise virtues.

**So that he may not fall into reproach and the devil’s snare.** So that our ministry may not be blamed and the devil, through him, may hold in his snare many who could have become Christians.

**Deacons likewise.** They must be irreproachable, so that they may be chosen as bishops. It is asked why he made no mention of presbyters but included them under the name of bishops. The reason is that it is the second, indeed almost the same, rank, just as he writes to the Philippians about bishops and deacons, since one city cannot have several bishops; and in the Acts of the Apostles, when he was about to go to Jerusalem, he gathered the presbyters of the Church and said: “Among other things, watch over the flock in which the Holy Spirit appointed you bishops.”

[Col. 0880B] **Chaste.** That is, continent.

**Not double-tongued.** A whisperer and a double-tongued person disturb many who are at peace.

**Not devoted to much wine.** He allowed a little to necessity but denied more to pleasure.

**Nor pursuing dishonest gain.** Dishonest gain is to pursue earthly things from heavenly mysteries.

**Holding the mystery of the faith with a pure conscience.** The mystery is that Christ’s Passion is the redemption of human salvation. If he understands this purely, he is not ashamed of Christ’s humility. Or, if he preaches the mystery of faith only for the reason for which it ought to be preached, he must not regard the mystery as a means of profit beyond what is due, [Col. 0880C] nor consider piety a source of gain.

**And let these also first be tested, and then let them serve, being without accusation.** Not only bishops but these men also must be tested before ordination.

**Women likewise must be chaste.** He commands that they too be chosen like deacons. Hence it is understood that he is speaking of those whom, even today, in the East they call deaconesses.

**Not slanderers.** This is the vice that especially dominates them.

**Temperate, faithful in all things.** Doubting in nothing.

**Let deacons be husbands of one wife, managing their children and their own households well.** Not so that they should marry if they have no wife, but so that they should not have two. If a wife makes someone more worthy, why are men with two or three wives not ordained all the more?

**For those who have served well.** He shows that not merely ministry but the quality of ministry earns a reward.

**Acquire for themselves a good rank.** Here “good” means a higher rank; for they are the lesser ministers.

**And great confidence in the faith that is in Christ Jesus.** Confidence to ask before the Lord and to teach, or even rebuke, before human beings.

**I write these things to you, son Timothy, hoping to come to you soon. But if I delay, so that you may know how one ought to conduct oneself in the household of God, which is the Church of the living God.** So that, confirmed by the judgment of this Epistle, you may have authority from me to arrange everything.

[Col. 0881A] **The pillar and foundation of the truth.** In it alone the truth now stands firmly established; formerly it was placed in the Law or in nature, which alone supports the structure.

**And manifestly great is the mystery of piety.** I want you to know the mystery of Christ’s incarnation, through which piety was bestowed upon the human race.

**Which was manifested in the flesh.** Which has now been revealed in his flesh.

**And justified in the spirit.** It was demonstrated.

**Appeared to angels.** When they said, “Glory to God in the highest,” and when they ministered to him in the wilderness.

**Preached among the nations.** By “the nations” he includes every kind of human being.

**Believed on in the world, taken up in glory.** In the sight of the Apostles he ascended into heaven.

## CHAPTER FOUR

**But the Spirit expressly says that in the latter [Col. 0881B] times some will depart from the faith.** He introduces the prophetic manner of speaking, as the ancients used to say: “Thus says the Holy Spirit.”

**Giving heed to deceitful spirits and doctrines of demons.** Every heretical doctrine has been composed by the art of demons.

**Through the hypocrisy of liars, whose consciences are seared.** They speak hypocritically: although they are not continent, they wish to appear so chaste that they even condemn marriage; so abstinent that they judge God’s creatures, using them sparingly, while they themselves indulge in banquets. Here, however, he preaches chastity and abstinence in such a way that he condemns neither nature nor God’s creatures. He urges the stronger toward that ideal and grants this concession to the weak. The others did this out of love of chastity and abstinence, but in order to obscure [Col. 0881C] its justice: they wanted to appear holier than the one who, out of love of chastity, even allowed marriage, namely, so that they might not incur the crime of fornication. For everyone who condemns marriage is not a lover but an enemy of chastity, since he both removes praise from the continent and, by taking away the remedy of marriage, exposes the incontinent to the danger of committing fornication.

**Forbidding marriage and requiring abstinence from foods that God created to be received with thanksgiving by the faithful and by those who know the truth. For every creature of God is good, and nothing is to be rejected if it is received with thanksgiving. For it is sanctified through the word of God and prayer.** If you attend to the exact wording, some monstrous doctrine is being preached—one that forbids both marriage and abstinence—from those who say all the things that follow.

**By setting these things before the brothers, you will be a good minister of Christ Jesus.** Keeping a balance in all things and dispensing everything rationally and moderately.

**Nourished by the words of faith and of the good doctrine that you have attained.** For he had been instructed from childhood in the sacred writings of the Law. The words of faith proper to him are the handing down of the Creed; good doctrine, however, is that by which Christian life is ordered.

**But avoid silly and old-womanish fables.** Things unsuitable to faith or religion.

**But train yourself for piety.** Piety consists also in assisting others even amid one’s own tribulation, as the widow of Zarephath did.

**For bodily training is useful for a little.** [Col. 0882A] This refers to holy baths, hunting, and similar activities, which benefit bodily health for a short time.

**But piety is useful for everything, holding a promise of the life that now is and of the life to come.** Both for the present time and for the future. For that widow herself is chaste in the present, and her reward remains with her.

**The saying is trustworthy and worthy of all acceptance.** A true saying in the judgment of everyone’s conscience, one to which no one can object.

**For this is why we labor and are reviled: because we hope in the living God.** Since it is certain that we have done nothing deserving hatred among human beings, what else follows but that we are blasphemed because our life is unlike theirs?

**Who is the Savior of all people, especially of the faithful.** “Of all” in the present; “of the faithful” in the future. Or because he delivers everyone from dangers, and especially the faithful.

[Col. 0882B] **Command and teach these things.** Command that they be done; teach how they should be done, or with what reward they are to be repaid.

**Let no one despise your youth.** Act so that you may be admired before you are despised. For he commands him to do what lay within his power.

**But be an example to the faithful.** It is a small thing to be an example to unbelievers, among whom whoever has no serious crimes is considered great. This is much more: to present himself as one through whom even the saints may advance.

**In speech, in conduct.** Say nothing more than the word of the Lord. It should be noted that he also wants him to provide the faithful with an example in speech.

**In love.** So that he may show them an example of love.

**In faith.** Catholic or perfect faith.

[Col. 0882C] **In chastity.** Of mind and body; its marks are also displayed in the gravity of one’s bearing.

**Until I come, attend to reading, exhortation, and teaching.** Do: read; exhort them to do what is read; teach how obscure things are to be understood, so that what is read may be put into practice.

**Do not neglect the gift that is in you.** He neglects the gift who does not exercise the talent he has received.

**Which was given to you through prophecy, with the laying on of the hands of the presbytery.** He had the gift of prophecy when he was ordained to the episcopate.

**Meditate on these things.** For every advance proceeds from meditation.

**Be devoted to them.** For not everyone who is occupied with these matters meditates upon them.

**So that your progress may be evident to all.** It will be evident if you are always engaged in meditation; and when it has become evident, others will be able to advance toward better things by your example.

[Col. 0882D] **Pay attention to yourself and devote yourself to them in teaching.** By doing this you will save both yourself and those who hear you. First attend to yourself, then to doctrine, so that everywhere you may save them both by action and by doctrine, equally by example.

## CHAPTER FIVE

**Do not rebuke an older man, but appeal to him as a father.** Lest, offended at being corrected by a younger man, he become embittered and make no progress; rather, appeal to him so that, like a father, he may instruct the younger by his own example.

**Younger men as brothers.** For they are more freely admonished in this way; and likewise younger women as sisters.

[Col. 0883A] **Older women as mothers.** With every form of reverence.

**Younger women as sisters, in all chastity.** Both of mind and of body.

**Honor widows.** By providing what they need or strengthening them with consolation.

**Those who are truly widows.** He defines as true widows those who have been relieved of every concern and left desolate by everyone.

**But if any widow has children or grandchildren, let her first learn to manage her own household and to repay her parents in kind. For this is acceptable before God.** She manages the household as long as she teaches her young children or grandchildren to return to their children what she received from her parents as an act of piety. Yet she must not use this as an excuse to pursue greed, but should reserve only what is sufficient for herself and should not herself give her children an opportunity to serve the world.

[Col. 0883B] **But the woman who is truly a widow and desolate should hope in God and continue in supplications and prayers night and day.** Such as Anna, daughter of Phanuel, was: he commands that women of this kind be honored.

**But she who lives in luxury is dead.** Whatever exceeds the measure of nature is counted as luxury. Here he especially touches the widows of our own time, who, although they do not clothe a person of their own nature with even an ordinary piece of cloth, adorn their walls with costly slabs of marble.

**And command these things, so that they may be irreproachable.** It should be noted that he says they both can and ought to be irreproachable.

**But if anyone does not care for his own, and especially for those of his household, he has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever.** [Col. 0883C] If anyone rejects widows or orphans, and especially parents and the poor, he is worse than an unbeliever, because even unbelievers naturally show piety toward their own. Or, if a widow neglects her orphaned children, she incurs the guilt of this sentence. At the same time, it should be noted that there are some who are called faithful but are worse in conduct than unbelievers.

**Let a widow be chosen who is not less than sixty years old and has been the wife of one man.** He wanted such women to be chosen as deaconesses, so that they might be examples of living to everyone.

**In good works.** If she has observed all these things from the time of her widowhood.

**Having a testimony.** As Tabitha did.

**If she has brought up children.** “For God” is understood.

**If she has shown hospitality, if she has washed the feet of the saints.** If she possesses not merely the marks of humility—for it is not enough for her to receive guests, but she must also wash the feet of her guests with her own hands.

[Col. 0883D] **If she has assisted those suffering tribulation.** That is, those in prison or the sick.

**If she has followed every good work.** He briefly summed up everything.

**But avoid younger widows.** Avoid appointing them to the ministry of the diaconate, lest a bad example be given in place of a good one.

**For when they have become wanton, they desire to marry in Christ.** When, during that period, they have possessed an abundance of religious observance, which often tends to produce wantonness.

**Having condemnation because they have nullified their first faith.** They had promised to remain widows. [Col. 0884A] This rule is to be understood not only of widows but also of continent virgins who have nullified their first faith.

**At the same time they also learn to go around from house to house, being idle.** They are restrained neither by fear of God nor subject to a husband’s authority, and they are bound by no concern for domestic occupation.

**Not only idle, but also talkative and inquisitive, saying things they ought not.** While they wish to offer an example of their own willfulness.

**Therefore I want younger women to marry and bear children.** “I want,” because it is necessary that such women do this before they make that promise; afterward, if they transgress, they incur condemnation.

**To manage households.** Women may be called household managers even if they have only two or three servants. He says this so that greed may not be defended by the name.

**Giving the adversary no occasion for reproach.** If they are incontinent, or lest religion be blasphemed because of them.

**For some have already turned back after Satan.** He gives the reasons why he said they would want to marry, lest we think that he desired this: some, failing to fulfill the promise they had made to God, had committed fornication.

**If any believing man has widows, let him assist them, so that the Church may not be burdened.** In his own household, as he would assist his parents.

**So that it may be sufficient for those who are truly widows.** Those who are desolate and dependent upon the help of everyone.

**Let the presbyters who preside well be considered worthy of double honor.** Both for their office and for their teaching.

[Col. 0884C] **Especially those who labor in speech and teaching.** He did not say “all who possess the word,” but “those who labor in the word.” Otherwise, he commands that all who possess it be appointed.

**For Scripture says: “You shall not muzzle the ox while it is threshing,” and, “The laborer is worthy of his wages.”** He wants him to provide bodily necessities to the one from whom others receive spiritual things, because those occupied with teaching cannot provide what they need for themselves.

**Do not accept an accusation against a presbyter unless there are two or three witnesses.** It is unjust even to accept an accusation against a layman, since secular authorities do not do this; how much more unjust is it against a priest of the Lord!

[Col. 0884D] **Rebuke those who sin in the presence of all.** If the accusation has been established against them.

**So that the rest may have fear.** When they see that you have spared no one.

**I charge you before God and Christ Jesus and his elect angels to observe these things without prejudice.** He adjures him by divine and heavenly testimony, so that nothing may prejudice him in observing these commands—not even the elect angels who attend the sacred altars.

**Doing nothing by inclining to either side.** Neither to the right nor to the left.

**Lay hands hastily on no one.** Unless you have found someone to be as I have described.

[Col. 0885A] **Nor share in the sins of others.** He says that one shares in sins when someone is ordained without having been tested.

**Keep yourself chaste.** He does not command him to guard others, so that he may be able to rebuke sinners boldly.

**No longer drink only water, but use a little wine, for the sake of your stomach and your frequent illnesses.** He did not want Timothy to think that, because of abstinence, he should provide an example even to the weak, especially since he had heard his teacher say that it is good for everyone not to drink wine. He therefore gives him the advice to care more for the cause of teaching than for abstinence; at the same time he shows what illnesses medicine from created things can heal.

**The sins of some people are manifest, going before them to judgment.** Those who are exposed are excommunicated, or are condemned by present punishments.

[Col. 0885B] **But the sins of others also follow after them.** At the future judgment—or they cannot remain hidden here for long. They therefore should not be ordained easily.

**Likewise, good works are manifest, and those that are otherwise cannot be hidden.** A city set on a mountain cannot be hidden; and even things that remain concealed for a time cannot be kept hidden for long.

## CHAPTER SIX

**Let all who are under the yoke of slavery consider their masters worthy of all honor.** Not only those who are good, but also unbelievers.

**So that the name of the Lord and the doctrine may not be blasphemed.** So that they may not appear to have become worse through their religion.

[Col. 0885C] **But those who have believing masters must not despise them because they are brothers.** They must not despise someone equal to themselves.

**Rather, let them serve all the more, because they are faithful and beloved, since they are participants in the benefit.** If they served unbelievers out of hateful fear, how much more ought they to serve the faithful, whose love they deserve to share!

**Teach and exhort these things.** Teach that they ought to be done; exhort them by showing that God is the reward.

**If anyone teaches otherwise and does not assent to the sound words of our Lord Jesus Christ and to the doctrine that is according to piety.** That is, the doctrine of the New Testament; the doctrine of the Old Testament is severe.

**He is conceited, knowing nothing.** He exalts himself over others, although the wisdom he preaches has come from above.

[Col. 0885D] **But he is sick concerning questions.** For by refusing he does not wholly die to the faith, nor does he recover through knowledge of the opposition; rather, he languishes through various pretexts.

**And disputes about words.** Having abandoned the meaning of truth, they scrutinize ambiguities of words, as the Manichaeans derive the diversity of the Testaments from a word.

**From these arise envy, strife, blasphemies.** These produce quarrels and blasphemies as they fight against God through arguments.

**Evil suspicions.** Either they suspect heresy in another, or, when they hear something, they think they can establish the truth.

**Conflicts among people of corrupt minds, and deprived of the truth.** Deprived of the integrity of the Gospel or of nature.

[Col. 0886A] **Who suppose that piety is a means of gain.** They think that the New Testament came for the sake of their profit.

**But piety with contentment is great gain.** The one who has piety seeks much; contentment belongs not to luxury but to nature. Or, just as piety is the worship of God, so impiety is contempt.

**For we brought nothing into this world; without doubt, neither can we take anything away.** We were born naked, and naked we shall die. Whatever is found here will be left here; what is not always ours is not truly ours. Therefore, as pilgrims, let us be content with sufficient use. Let us acquire those riches that we can carry with us to our heavenly homeland.

**But having food and clothing, let us be content with these.** Above he spoke of contentment; whatever exceeds these things is counted as riches.

[Col. 0886B] **For those who want to become rich.** He defined the will to possess riches; this desire exists both in those who already have them and in those who seek them.

**Fall into temptation and the devil’s snare.** The desire to possess riches is an occasion of temptation and the devil’s snare.

**And into many foolish and harmful desires.** The desires for riches are therefore never satisfied.

**Which plunge people into destruction and ruin.** While swollen with ambition for possessions and lifted up to the heavens, they are plunged down as far as the underworld; or, desiring the wealth of others, like Ahab, they go so far as to plot murder.

**For the love of money is the root of all evils.** It is both the source and the increase of every crime. A root, when cut off, always produces branches more densely; the root must therefore be torn out, lest the branches be cut off in vain.

[Col. 0886C] **By desiring it, some have wandered away from the faith.** That is, they withdrew from faith in God’s promises while delighting in present things.

**And have pierced themselves with many pains.** The more they possess, the more they endure the tortures of anxieties. Hence the Lord also declared, in the other words concerning desire, that the anxieties of riches choke the rest.

**But you, man of God.** Not a man of riches but of God; not a servant of Mammon but of Christ, to whom all visible things belong.

**Flee these things.** As causes of faithlessness or of pain.

[Col. 0886D] **But pursue righteousness, piety, faith.** I want you to be rich in these riches.

**Love.** Of God and neighbor.

**Endurance and gentleness.** Endurance in bearing with others, gentleness in doing no harm.

**Fight the good fight of faith.** The good fight is not to struggle for worldly things but, even unto death, to contend for the truth of the faith, as it is written: “Strive for your soul in righteousness,” and, “Fight for righteousness even unto death.” Or, just as those devoted to riches strive to conquer everything, so you should do so in faith.

**Take hold.** As I myself was taken hold of.

**Of eternal life, to which you were called.** Just as they desire to possess temporal life.

[Col. 0887A] **And you confessed the good confession.** In baptism, by renouncing the world and its pomp.

**In the presence of many witnesses.** Priests, ministers, and the heavenly powers.

**I charge you before God.** He commands with the authority of a teacher.

**Who gives life to all things.** All things that live, even if they wither, live again through his power.

And to Christ Jesus, who bore witness under Pontius Pilate to the good confession: saying to Pilate, “For this I came into this world, to bear witness to the truth”—that is, to die for it as well.

That you may keep the commandment. Just as he did, even unto death.

Without stain, blameless. The one who sins in some manner stains the commandments and causes them to be reproached.

[Col. 0887B] Until the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ. “The one who perseveres to the end will be saved.”

Whom the blessed and only Sovereign, the King of kings and Lord of lords, will display at his proper times. Whenever he wills—God, who alone has this power.

Who alone possesses immortality. He alone possesses it properly, since he gave angels and human beings the ability to possess it. We, however, possess it neither alone nor from ourselves, as he does. This is directed against the Manichaeans, who suppose that the nature of evil is immortal and everlasting.

And dwells in inaccessible light. Inaccessible to every creature. “For no one knows the Father except the Son, nor the Son except the Father and the Holy Spirit”; the Spirit also searches the depths of God.

Whom no human being has seen, nor indeed can see: [Col. 0887C] to whom belong honor and everlasting dominion. Amen. No one knows him, but each person understands him according to his merit. For individuals see the sun all the more clearly the purer the sharpness of their eyes is.

Command those who are rich in this present age. There are also rich people of the other age: those who buy for themselves refined gold from God; those who possess gold in heaven; and those who bring forth things new and old.

Do not be high-minded. First of all, he touched upon their chief disease. You will hardly find a rich person who is not proud, who acknowledges the poor—or even his own relatives—and who does not take it badly when honor is not paid to him by someone inferior.

Nor place their hope. By not being hoped in, riches become cheap; and when they are despised, they are spent.

Upon uncertain riches. For it is uncertain whether they will be taken from you more quickly, or you from them; many have had them taken away together with their lives. Some have seen them taken away before their own eyes; others, unwillingly, have left them to strangers.

But in the living God. To whom all things belong.

Who provides us abundantly with all things. He provides abundantly for this reason: so that we may live while also giving generously to others—not so that, destroying ourselves through great toil, we may build larger barns.

[Col. 0888B] For enjoyment. Not for concealing or trading.

To do good: to become rich in good works. Not in gold and silver.

To give readily, to share. The one who gives readily will soon cease to be rich. To give is to donate; to share, however, is to give generously.

Storing up for themselves a good foundation for the future. “Go: sell everything you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me”—which is the foundation of perfection.

So that they may take hold of the true life. For this is not the true life, which does not remain in its own condition. “Vanity under the sun,” says Ecclesiastes.

O Timothy, guard the deposit. Guard the deposit of faith entrusted to us and to be preserved by you.

Avoiding profane novelties of words. What you have not heard from me, do not readily accept even if it is said by an angel.

And oppositions of falsely named knowledge, which some professing have fallen away from the faith. These are the devices of dialectical art, by which heretics promise themselves boundless knowledge of things; and for this reason they fall away from the truth of the faith.

Grace be with you. Amen. May it remain forever.

## THE SECOND EPISTLE TO TIMOTHY

[Col. 0887]

### CHAPTER ONE

[Col. 0887D]

Paul, apostle of Jesus Christ through the will of God. Not through my own merits; or, sent by Christ, but not without the will of God.

According to the promise of life that is in Christ Jesus. Offering a service worthy of the promise.

To Timothy, my dearest son. “Dearest,” that is, dearer than the others.

Grace and mercy and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord. Such is Paul’s greeting, that in it all the benefits of the Father and of Christ are remembered.

I give thanks to my God. To the God who taught us such love for one another.

Whom I serve, as did my forefathers, with a pure conscience. All my ancestry worshiped the one Christ; I ravaged the Church not through ill will but through zeal for the Law.

[Col. 0888D] That without ceasing I have remembrance of you in my prayers, night and day desiring to see you. He both displays his love and provides a continual example of prayer.

Remembering your tears, so that I may be filled with joy. Tears which you poured out abundantly for me, so that you might also provoke me to sorrow; tears which I long to see revealed by your presence.

Receiving the remembrance of the faith that is in you, an unhypocritical faith, which first dwelt in your grandmother Lois. A faith that truly proves by your works that you are what you profess, as James defined it; and which descended to you from the instruction of your ancestral succession, as though by hereditary right.

And in your mother Eunice. Because she believed first.

But I am confident that it is also in you. For this reason I remind you. Because I have approved your faith, you need to be reminded, not instructed.

[Col. 0889A] That you may rekindle the grace of God. As though it had been put to sleep by tribulations.

Which is in you through the laying on of my hands. Namely, for the episcopate.

For God did not give us a spirit of fear, but of power. Power to despise punishments. Those who sin rightly seem to fear human penalties, as he says elsewhere: “But if you do evil, be afraid.”

And of love and self-control. Whether toward the Lord or toward one another. Let us also gladly die, so that we may do everything with a disciplined mind.

Therefore do not be ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, nor of me, his prisoner. For Christ did nothing deserving shame; nor did I, whom you know, suffer all these things for any crime, but because of God.

[Col. 0889B] But suffer hardship with the Gospel. By your conduct or by your teaching.

According to the power of God. Which, for its own sake, assists those who labor.

Who saved us and called us with his holy calling. That is, from sins.

Not according to our works, but according to his purpose and the grace that was given to us in Christ Jesus. By which he purposed to save us freely through Christ.

Before the eternal ages. In relation to God’s foreknowledge, he had already given it before the ages. For human beings customarily prepare estates for their children before they are born.

But it has now been manifested. What previously lay hidden.

Through the illumination of our Savior Jesus Christ. [Col. 0889C] Namely, through his words and examples.

Who indeed destroyed death, but brought life and incorruption to light. By his teaching and conduct he destroyed sins, which generated human death; and he showed how life and incorruption are to be sought.

Through the Gospel. He taught those who were willing; he did not compel the unwilling.

For which I was appointed a preacher, apostle, and teacher of the Gentiles. In comparison with others they may be called teachers; in comparison with no one is anyone a true teacher.

For this reason I also suffer these things. Not because of any crime, as Peter urges us to suffer when he says: “Let none of you suffer as a murderer”; but, suffering as a Christian, let him not be ashamed.

[Col. 0889D] But I am not ashamed. Here he is not ashamed of his chains, whereas we are ashamed at mere insults.

For I know whom I have believed, and I am certain that he is able. I know that he is faithful and powerful.

To preserve my deposit for that day. With me, he himself will preserve what he entrusted; or, what I commend to him, he will restore in the future.

Hold to the pattern of sound words that you heard from me, in faith and love in Christ Jesus. According to my pattern, see and teach what you received briefly from me: how we ought to believe wholly and love one another.

Guard the good deposit through the Holy Spirit who dwells in us. Guard, with his help, the deposit that I entrusted to you through the Holy Spirit.

[Col. 0890A] For you know this: that all who are in Asia have turned away from me, among whom are Phygelus and Hermogenes. For this reason I remind you, because those whom I did not expect have abandoned me.

May the Lord grant mercy to the household of Onesiphorus, because he often refreshed me and was not ashamed of my chain. He censures those who deserted and praises those who remained, in order to deter from bad imitation and summon to good example.

But when he came to Rome, he diligently sought me and found me. May the Lord grant him to find mercy from the Lord on that day. And how much he ministered to me at Ephesus, you know better. He found me because he diligently sought me; from this it is also shown why not everyone who seeks finds: they inquire negligently.

[Col. 0890B] ### CHAPTER TWO

You therefore, my son, be strengthened in the grace that is in Christ Jesus, and in what you heard from me through many witnesses. Either: in the presence of many people I gave you commands concerning how you ought to teach; or: what I said I confirmed by many examples and testimonies of the prophets.

Entrust these things to faithful people. To those who can faithfully administer the grace of God—that is, preach for the sake of God alone.

Who will also be capable of teaching others. Not merely doing these things themselves, but also instructing others.

Labor as a good soldier of Christ Jesus. We are called soldiers because we have enemies against whom we must fight laboriously.

[Col. 0890C] No one serving as a soldier for God entangles himself in worldly affairs, so that he may please the one who enlisted him. He uses the comparison of soldiers to show that we ought much more to be free from worldly affairs in order to please Christ, since even soldiers of this age abstain from other activities so that they may please their commander perfectly.

For even the one who competes in the contest is not crowned unless he has competed lawfully. By another comparison he says the same thing. Many compete, but only the one who has conquered with complete strength is crowned.

The laboring farmer ought first to receive a share of the fruits. Lest he say, “From what, then, shall I live if I devote myself entirely to teaching?” he shows that the farmer ought to receive the firstfruits from the people, besides the reward that he will receive from the Lord in the future.

[Col. 0890D] Understand what I say. For the Lord will give you understanding in all things. Understanding of those matters which, on account of those seeking an occasion, had been obscured beneath the veil of comparison.

Remember that Jesus Christ, risen from the dead, is of the seed of David. This is directed against those who deny the resurrection of the flesh and consequently also denied Christ; and against those who deny that Christ came in the flesh, whom John calls antichrists.

According to my Gospel. According to that which you know I preach.

For which I suffer hardship even to chains as though I were a criminal. Yet I am not one.

[Col. 0891A] But the word of God is not bound. For I continue to teach those who are present with confidence, and do not cease to strengthen those who are absent by letters.

Therefore I endure everything for the sake of the elect. For this reason I sought the tribune’s assistance and afterward appealed to Caesar, so that they might be strengthened through me, although I could have ended these sufferings by dying.

So that they too may obtain the salvation that is in Christ Jesus, with heavenly glory. The salvation that is in Christ is not naked but clothed with glory; nor is it earthly glory, but heavenly.

The saying is faithful: for if we have died with him, we shall also live with him. It rests upon the reasoning of truth. For if we have died with Christ to vices and pleasures, we shall live with him. Otherwise, how could we hope for this?

[Col. 0891B] If we endure, we shall also reign with him. If we endure, when necessary, what he endured, then at last we shall be able to reign together with him.

If we deny him, he also will deny us; if we do not believe, he remains faithful—he cannot deny himself. Whether we believe or do not believe, he cannot offer each person anything other than what he promised. For truth will not act against itself, lest it appear to deny itself.

Remind them of these things, testifying before God. Bind them under God’s testimony.

Do not quarrel about words; for it is useful for nothing except the subversion of those who hear. Without the testimonies of Scripture, such disputation does not build up but destroys the hearers; for they think that everything rests on sharpness and subtlety. Or: do not overcome by words, but by [Col. 0891C] deeds.

But diligently take care to present yourself as approved to God. Above all, labor for this: to present yourself before God in such a way that the people may rightly obey you.

An unashamed worker. Live in such a way that your words do not blush when your deeds fail to support them.

Rightly handling the word of truth. He handles it rightly who confirms his words by examples. Doctrine is the adornment of life; action is the foundation of the word.

But avoid profane and empty talk. For it advances greatly toward ungodliness. These are the irreligious stories of heretics who deny the resurrection; through them, once fear of the Judge has been removed, one proceeds to every form of ungodliness and every crime.

Their word spreads like cancer. Cancer is the name for a wound that arises in women’s breasts; unless it is quickly treated, when the poison has spread to the heart, there is no remedy. So the conversations of heretics must be avoided, lest through the ears they irreparably wound the mind.

Among them are Hymenaeus and Philetus, who have fallen away from the truth. He names them so that one may know whom to avoid.

Saying that the resurrection has already taken place, and they have overthrown the faith of some. In the children—or in the bones of Israel brought to life in Ezekiel—they interpreted the resurrection as referring to those gathered from captivity, as though they had already risen.

But God’s firm foundation stands, bearing this seal. Those in whose hearts the faith of Christ was founded were not deceived or shaken; and this was because, as God’s own, they possessed the judgment described in the time of Moses, when Dathan and Abiram were overthrown. They did not perish together with the ungodly, since God knew them to be excellent, as it is written in the book of Numbers.

The Lord knows those who are his; and everyone who invokes the name of the Lord must depart from iniquity. Lest Zion perish together with the wicked.

But in a great house. By the great house he does not mean the Church, as some think—the Church that has neither stain nor wrinkle—but the world. Hence Jeremiah says: “O Israel, how great is the house of the Lord!” and so forth. In it tares are mixed with wheat; for those who deny the resurrection cannot be in the Church.

[Col. 0892B] There are not only vessels of gold and silver. Precious and strong vessels.

But also wooden and earthen ones. Weak vessels.

Some indeed for honor, others for dishonor. Therefore, if anyone cleanses himself from these things, he will be a vessel for honor, sanctified and useful to the Lord, prepared for every good work. If anyone cleanses himself from heretical teachers and believes in the future resurrection, he strives to fulfill the judgment of God through every good work.

But flee youthful desires. For those who act in ways that do not accord with Christian gravity cannot be among the elders; and they are overcome by the young if they retain such frivolity.

But pursue righteousness, faith, hope, and love. Here he means integrity by “faith.”

And peace. The peace that is owed to religion.

With those who call upon the Lord from a pure heart. “Blessed are the pure in heart”; concerning such people it is said: “Why do you call me God, and do not do what I say?”

But avoid foolish and undisciplined questions, knowing that they produce quarrels. All questions concerning the Law are foolish and undisciplined.

The servant of the Lord must not quarrel. He is Christ’s servant, who did not cry out or contend, and no one heard his voice, according to what the prophet Doeg foretold.

But be gentle toward everyone. Not only toward friends.

Able to teach, patient, correcting with modesty [Col. 0892D] those who resist the truth. Always teach everyone patiently, not in anger but with modesty.

Lest at some time God grant them repentance for knowledge of the truth, and they recover from the snares of the devil, by whom they are held captive for his will. He does not doubt God’s goodness, but the perversity of those receiving it. May God grant them continual, gentle, and gracious correction, so that, having accepted reason, they may recover their senses. This is also directed against the Novatians, who denied repentance and maintained that converted heretics could not obtain pardon.

### CHAPTER THREE

But know this: in the last days difficult times will come. Do not be surprised that worse things come each day.

[Col. 0893A] For people will be lovers of themselves. Seeking not the glory of God but their own interests.

Greedy, boastful. Avaricious and glorying in their avarice.

Proud, blasphemous. Since they do not wish to learn, they usurp teaching.

Disobedient to parents, ungrateful, wicked, without affection. Namely, toward the ancient teachers who begot them through the Gospel.

Without peace, accusers of the saints’ peace.

Without self-control, ruthless, without kindness. In every vice.

Defiant, swollen with pride, and lovers of pleasures more than lovers of God. Concern is an indication of greater love: whoever listens or speaks more willingly of the pleasures of the world than of the Lord’s commands is such a person.

[Col. 0893B] Having the appearance of piety. In dress or in doctrine.

But denying its power. Denying the reality itself by their works.

Avoid these people. So that corrupt conversations do not corrupt good morals.

For among them are those who enter houses and take captive little women burdened with sins. They seize those burdened with sins, promising them impunity and pardon; or, these are weak minds, compared with women.

Who are led by various desires. Always wanting to learn something new.

Always learning and never arriving at knowledge of the truth. Because they hold nothing definite, and each person wants to maintain different, unapproved traditions. What one person says is destroyed by another.

[Col. 0893C] Just as Jannes and Jambres resisted Moses, so these also resist the truth. Just as those men did so through the deceptions of magical art, so these do through the fallacy of arguments. At the same time he shows that Moses was a teacher of the truth, against the detractors of the Old Testament.

People corrupted in mind, disqualified concerning the faith. As corrupt in their conduct as they are disqualified concerning the faith.

But they will not advance further. He speaks of all heretics, but especially of those whom he knew at that time, in the Spirit, were soon to be destroyed. Otherwise, below he foretells that some would advance toward worse things.

For their folly will be manifest to all, just as [Col. 0893D] theirs also was. They confessed that they had been overcome by the finger of God.

But you have followed my teaching, conduct, purpose, faith, patience, love, and endurance. Believe me about myself more than them; or, for this reason I have no fear concerning you, because I know that you have thoroughly understood my teaching and virtue.

Persecutions, sufferings—such as happened to me at Antioch, Iconium, and Lystra; what persecutions I endured. From these you could understand that I do nothing for the sake of human beings, since I have suffered so much.

And the Lord delivered me from them all. So he will also deliver you from everything, if you follow.

And all who wish to live devoutly in Christ Jesus will suffer persecution. Not I alone, but all who do not kill souls by flattery. Therefore we must fear that we are not living devoutly, since we suffer nothing for God.

But evil people and impostors will advance toward worse things, deceiving and being deceived. He says this about flatterers, who, while they are loved by foolish people, become more deceived and deceive others; or it should be understood of heretics.

But you remain in what you have learned. I do not want these things to frighten or seduce you.

And which have been entrusted to you. By God through us.

Knowing from whom you learned them. And because from infancy you have known the sacred writings. Either from the true apostle, or through the Law from God.

[Col. 0894B] Which are able to instruct you for salvation through faith in Christ Jesus. For without the faith of Christ they are no longer sufficient for salvation.

For every Scripture inspired by God is also useful for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for instruction in righteousness, so that the person of God may be more perfectly equipped for every good work. The instruction of the Law was therefore given so that, doing everything according to its guidance, we may do what is just justly.

### CHAPTER FOUR

I testify before God and Christ Jesus, who is about to judge the living and the dead, and by his appearing and his kingdom. He charges him by everything that the Christian religion believes, so that he may proclaim the word of God urgently. He will judge the living and the dead because he will find the living and raise the dead.

Preach the word; persist in season and out of season. It is “in season” when people willingly listen; it is “out of season” when one preaches to an unwilling hearer.

Reprove, exhort, rebuke with all patience and teaching. Reprove sinners and testify that they should not sin. Rebuke those who resist; but do all these things with patience and according to teaching.

For there will be a time when they will not endure sound teaching. True and perfect teaching, just as Israel refused to hear the prophets.

But according to their own desires they will heap up teachers for themselves. They will seek such teachers as say what they themselves desire to hear, so that they may sin securely.

[Col. 0894D] Having itching ears. They desire to be pleased, not pierced by remorse.

And they will indeed turn their hearing away from the truth, but will turn to fables. From the truth of the Law, which condemns vices, to human arguments that contrive the idea that God, being gracious, will not avenge wrongdoing.

But you, be watchful; labor in all things. In those matters that concern the benefit of the hearers.

Do the work of an evangelist. Let your word conform to your works.

Fulfill your ministry; be sober-minded. Namely, the episcopate. For I will not always be in the body, so as to be able to remind you.

For I am already being poured out, and the time of my departure [Col. 0895A] is near. He called his death a sacrifice destined for God, in order to encourage him to martyrdom.

I have fought the good fight; I have completed the course. Now he says this confidently, standing at the final boundary of life. He uses a comparison drawn from those competing in a contest.

I have kept the faith. I have preserved the faith of the office I undertook all the way to the end.

For the rest, the crown of righteousness is laid up for me, which the Lord, the just judge, will give me on that day. He knows that I fought for righteousness unto death.

And not only for me. For merit is owed not to persons but to labor.

But also for those who love his appearing. Those who rejoice that Christ has come and taught righteousness. Or: those who live in such a way that they gladly await the Lord’s appearing.

Hurry to come to me quickly. For Demas has abandoned me, loving this present world, and has gone to Thessalonica. It was necessary that one who loved the world should leave one who did not love the world. For every animal is joined to one like itself.

Crescens has gone to Galatia; Titus to Dalmatia; Luke alone is with me. These men were sent; they did not abandon me.

Take Mark and bring him with you; for he is useful to me in the ministry. But I sent Tychicus to Ephesus. For the word of God or for whatever need there was.

The cloak that I left at Troas with Carpus, bring when you come, and the books—especially the parchments. He did not say “my cloak,” for perhaps someone who had converted and come to his feet had placed it among other things to be sold.

[Col. 0896A] Alexander the coppersmith showed me much evil; the Lord will repay him according to his works. For he resisted the words of God, though they were reasonable.

You too avoid him. He warns them to beware of one who barks.

For he strongly resisted our words. If he resisted ours, how much more will he resist yours!

At my first defense no one stood by me, but everyone abandoned me; may it not be counted against them. When I first began to defend the Gospel.

But the Lord stood by me and strengthened me. By saying that the Lord had been with him in all things, he encourages Timothy not to fear.

So that through me the proclamation might be fulfilled and all the nations might hear. Not because I was afraid to die.

And I was delivered from the lion’s mouth. From the persecutor.

[Col. 0896B] The Lord delivered me from every evil work. From the wickedness of those lying in wait.

And he will save me into his heavenly kingdom. Just as he delivers here, so he leads into the kingdom.

To him be glory forever and ever. Amen. Greet Prisca and Aquila and the household of Onesiphorus. Erastus remained at Corinth. On account of all these things.

But I left Trophimus sick at Miletus. Hurry to come before winter. Eubulus, Pudens, Linus, Claudia, and all the brothers greet you. From this it is proved that the apostles did not care only for bodily health, but also in order to display signs; for here he did not heal his own disciple.

The Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. For though he died in the flesh, you live spiritually.

[Col. 0896C] Grace be with you all. Amen.

## THE EPISTLE TO TITUS

[Col. 0895]

### CHAPTER ONE

[Col. 0895C]

Paul, servant of God. Not of sin.

But apostle of Jesus Christ. Not every servant is an apostle; he is called Christ’s because he had been sent by him to preach.

According to the faith of God’s elect and the knowledge of the truth that accords with godliness, in hope of eternal life. According to that faith by which believers are chosen when they come to know the truth; this knowledge does not arise from merit but from the Lord’s truth.

[Col. 0895D] Which God, who does not lie, promised. If he does not lie, he does not provide something other than what he promised to the righteous and the unrighteous, although this may seem harsh to human beings.

Before the eternal ages. Before all ages he purposed within himself, through the Son, to save those who believe.

But he manifested his word at his proper times. Then he manifested his plan, when he had foreknown that the whole world would be made different from righteousness.

In the preaching entrusted to me according to the command of our Savior God. He commanded Paul and Barnabas to be set apart so that they might preach to the Gentiles.

To Titus, his beloved son according to the common faith: [Col. 0896C] Grace and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Savior. A son according to faith, not by nature.

For this reason I left you in Crete, so that you might correct what remains deficient and appoint presbyters in every city, as I also directed you. Correct what is deficient according to the right rule; only then will you be able to ordain presbyters, when everyone in the Church has been set right.

If anyone is blameless, the husband of one wife. It should be noted that in a priest even things permitted to others are forbidden.

Having faithful children, not accused of debauchery [Col. 0896D] or disobedient. Otherwise he would not be able confidently to rebuke offenders; or, so that the quality of his teaching might be known from the discipline of his household.

For a bishop must be blameless. He calls the one whom he previously named a presbyter a bishop.

As God’s steward. If, then, presbyters are sought as administrators of human laws, what sort of people must those be who administer divine laws—and how just!

Not arrogant, not quick-tempered, not addicted to wine, not violent, not greedy for shameful gain. Christ’s disciple must not strike, since Christ was struck and did not strike back. He must not pursue shameful gain through flattery—earthly gain, while promising heavenly and divine things.

But hospitable. First he condemned vices so that he might implant virtues, according to the custom of Scripture.

[Col. 0897A] Kind. So that he may receive guests not with sadness but with goodwill.

Sober-minded, just, holy, self-controlled. The Apostle never speaks of lack of self-control or self-control except in relation to sexual immorality; “just” refers to judgment, and “self-controlled” to holiness—so that, because he had mentioned one wife, no one might suppose that he had allowed an opportunity for lack of self-control.

Holding fast to the faithful word that accords with the teaching. Loving the teaching and always speaking from it, not worldly and empty fables.

So that he may be able to exhort with sound teaching and refute those who contradict it. Such a person must be chosen who can exhort and refute those who contradict sound teaching—teaching that heals its hearers, or teaching corrupted by no falsehood.

[Col. 0897B] For there are many who are also disobedient, empty talkers, and deceivers. They do not obey apostolic teaching and speak to no useful purpose.

Especially those of the circumcision. Those who observe human traditions rather than divine commandments.

They must be rebuked, since they overthrow entire households, teaching what they ought not to teach for the sake of shameful gain. Things that had already become superfluous in the time of Christ; he says that they teach Jewish ceremonies.

One of them, their own prophet, said this. Namely, Callimachus. See what sort of people they are, since they even earned such testimony from one of their own.

Cretans are always liars. They love lying, are harmful speakers, and are equally idle.

Evil beasts, lazy bellies. For this reason they readily accept holidays and idleness.

This testimony is true. For this reason rebuke them sharply, so that they may be sound in the faith, not paying attention to Jewish fables and human commandments. These are human traditions about which the Lord speaks to the Jews in the Gospel: according to Isaiah, they honor the Lord not in their heart but with their lips.

Turning away from the truth. Namely, from the New Testament.

All things are pure to the pure. For at that time they still called things unclean according to the Law.

But to the defiled and unbelieving. Defiled and unbelieving are those who do not believe that the Lord removed the yoke of the Law from the necks of believers—that is, all the things that had been instituted for a temporal purpose.

But both their mind and conscience are defiled. [Col. 0897D] Even in this very matter.

They profess to know God, but they deny him by their deeds. They say that they know Christ better, as one promised in the Law; but by their deeds they deny his coming, when they suppose that they cannot be justified without the assistance of the Law.

Being detestable, unbelieving, and disqualified for every good work. In the mere confession of the Law they claim to be more religious, although they do not do what is required.

### CHAPTER TWO

But you speak what accords with sound teaching. Things that pertain to the life of Christ.

Older men are to be sober-minded, dignified, prudent, sound in faith, love, and endurance. Here “older men” may be understood both by age and by rank, especially the elders of the Church, to all of whom it is necessary to provide a pattern.

Older women likewise. Those who were chosen as an example to other women.

In holy conduct, not slanderers. For conduct is not holy when, as he says elsewhere, there are “braided hairstyles,” and so forth.

Not enslaved to much wine. But using a little.

Teaching what is good, so that they may teach prudence. He permitted them to teach, but women; and this not in the Church, but privately.

Young women are to love their husbands and love their children, to be prudent, chaste, and sober-minded. Not other men; or, he says this so that other women who were continent might not fail to love their husbands and the word of God might be blamed as though it preached discord.

[Col. 0898B] Caring for their households. So that they might not distress their husbands in anything.

Kind, submissive to their own husbands, so that the word of God may not be blasphemed. So that they themselves may not blaspheme if they are Gentiles, or so that others, seeing them become worse than they were before the faith, may not blaspheme.

Likewise exhort the young men to be sober-minded. Removing from them the occasion of debauchery.

In all things. In the things joined together, or not only in body but also in mind.

Show yourself as an example of good works. So that you do not destroy the word by your example, and so that you may rebuke offenders confidently.

In teaching, integrity, and seriousness. Only by these can one teach; integrity is neither corrupted by gifts nor influenced by partiality.

Sound, blameless speech. Not weakened by the heat of any flattery.

So that the one who is opposed may be ashamed, having nothing evil to say about you. How can anyone who can oppose you say anything if he has found nothing of this sort in you?

Slaves are to be subject to their own masters, pleasing them in all things. In whatever they command that is just.

Not contradicting. So that, by murmuring, you do not both lose your wages and prove yourselves ungrateful people.

Not defrauding, but showing good faith in all things. Whether in the matters granted to them, or so that they may show by their work that what they believe is good.

So that they may adorn the teaching of God our Savior in all things. [Col. 0898D] While they are praised for their works.

For the grace of God and of our Savior has appeared to all people. It excludes no condition.

Training us to deny ungodliness and worldly desires. Every carnal desire and every temporary dwelling is worldly.

Soberly. Perfectly, as the Lord says: “Take heed lest your hearts be weighed down with debauchery, drunkenness, and the cares of this life.”

And to live justly and devoutly in this age. Justice is not properly ordered unless piety is joined to it.

Awaiting the blessed hope. Those who have kept his commandments.

And the appearing of the glory of our great God and Savior [Col. 0899A] Jesus Christ. He calls the Spirit the great God, because we await his appearing.

Who gave himself for us, so that he might redeem us from all iniquity and purify for himself an acceptable people, zealous for good works. Since he gave himself, let us beware lest we make his benefit empty and ineffective.

Speak these things and exhort. Let all your speech consist in this exhortation.

And rebuke with all authority. Rebuke sharply those who do not live in this way.

Let no one despise you. Present yourself in such a way that you cannot be despised. For life gives authority to speech.

### CHAPTER THREE

Remind them to be subject to rulers and authorities, to obey the command, and to be ready for every good work, [Col. 0899B] not for anything evil.

To speak evil of no one. Not even of those who deserve it.

Not to be quarrelsome, but moderate. So that, returning insult for insult, they do not provoke a quarrel.

Showing all gentleness toward all people. Not only toward the good or toward friends.

For we too were once foolish, unbelieving, deceived, serving various desires and pleasures, living in malice and envy, hateful and hating one another. Lest they despair because of their rebuke, he sets himself forward as an example, saying that we too were once such people; therefore we ought patiently to tolerate their foolishness.

But when the kindness and humanity of our Savior [Col. 0899C] God appeared—not because of works of righteousness that we had done, but according to his mercy—he saved us. Either this means the generosity of God’s mercy, or Christ according to his humanity.

Through the washing of regeneration and renewal by the Holy Spirit. For the Holy Spirit renewed us through baptism.

He poured out upon us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Savior. More abundantly than in the Old Testament.

[Col. 0900A] So that, having been justified by his grace, we might become heirs according to the hope of eternal life. Not according to a carnal inheritance of temporal life.

This saying is trustworthy. So that no one may doubt.

And concerning these things I want you to affirm them strongly. To strengthen those who know, not to instruct the ignorant.

So that those who believe in God may take the lead in good works. They should take the lead in teaching good works.

These things are good and useful for humanity. These things, not those that follow.

But avoid foolish questions, genealogies, and disputes. He does not want us entangled in superfluous controversies that arise in the Law concerning genealogies; rather, we should always speak about those things from which the hearers will make progress.

And avoid quarrels about the Law, for they are useless and futile. [Col. 0900B] As though they were contradictory objections pursued by heretics.

Avoid a heretical person after one and a second admonition, knowing that anyone of this kind is perverted and is sinning, being condemned by his own judgment. He does not permit us to occupy ourselves with such people if, after being admonished a second time, they do not correct themselves, lest we waste time in an empty dispute; and an attempt made according to one’s own judgment will accomplish nothing, because freedom of choice remains with each person, and everyone is bound by the cords of his sins.

When I send Artemas or Tychicus to you, hasten to come to me at Nicopolis, for I have decided to winter there. Diligently send ahead Zenas the lawyer and Apollos, so that they may lack nothing. So that, by delaying, they may lose nothing of the fruit of their teaching.

[Col. 0900C] And let your people also learn to take the lead in good works for necessary uses, so that they may not be unfruitful. He repeats the same thing he had said above: Let those who believe take the lead in good works.

All those who are with me greet you. Greet those who love us in the faith. The grace of God be with all of you. Amen. Those who love us faithfully, or those who love us because of the faith. It should be noted that he excludes the apostles whom he greets.

## ON THE EPISTLE TO PHILEMON

[Col. 0899]

### CHAPTER ONE

[Col. 0899D]

Paul, a prisoner of Jesus Christ, and Timothy, the brother. In prison, or in chains.

To Philemon, our beloved and fellow-worker, and to Apphia, our most beloved sister. A helper in the Gospel. Apphia, however, is believed to have been either a sister or a wife.

And to Archippus, our fellow soldier. He was a deacon, concerning whom he says to the Colossians: “Say to Archippus: See to the ministry that you received, and fulfill it.”

And to the Church that is in your house: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. He entreats with every expression of thanksgiving and with joy.

I give thanks to my God, always making mention of you in my prayers, hearing of your love and faith. This becomes known to us through good works.

[Col. 0900D] Which you have in the Lord Jesus and toward all the saints. Whoever loves the head must necessarily love all the members.

So that the sharing of your faith may become evident in the recognition of every good work in Christ Jesus. You love all the saints, to such an extent that all our good people may plainly recognize that you are faithful.

For I have had great joy and consolation in your love, because the hearts of the saints have found rest through you, brother. By receiving them as guests, you refreshed them.

Therefore, having great confidence in Christ Jesus to command you. Although the matter itself gave us confidence to command, we preferred to entreat you to act out of love rather than to order you.

[Col. 0901A] What pertains to the matter. What pertains to the Christian cause.

For love’s sake I rather entreat you, since you are such a person as Paul, an old man; and now also a prisoner of Jesus Christ. In character such as the one who, even in old age, does not refuse bonds for Christ.

I entreat you for my son, whom I begot in chains, Onesimus, who was once useless to you, but now useful both to me and to you; whom I have sent back to you. When he was a gentile, or carnal.

But receive him as my own heart. As our most beloved son.

Whom I had wished to keep with me, so that he might minister to me on your behalf in the bonds of the Gospel. From this recognize what kind of person he is: he pleased me so much that he might minister on your behalf.

[Col. 0901B] But without your counsel I wished to do nothing. He speaks in such a way as to send him back to Philemon himself, or rather to commend his usefulness more strongly.

So that your good deed might not be as though forced, but voluntary. It should be noted that he did not want anyone to do anything good under compulsion, lest he lose his reward.

For perhaps he departed from you for an hour for this reason: so that you might receive him [Col. 0902A] forever. Perhaps divine providence arranged this.

No longer as a slave, but in place of a slave, as a most beloved brother. For he is no longer a slave as though under compulsion, but a voluntary brother.

Especially to me; but how much more to you, both in the flesh and in the Lord! To whom he owes service both according to the flesh and according to the faith.

But if he has wronged you in anything or owes you anything, charge it to me. I, Paul, have written this with my own hand: I will repay it—not to mention that you owe me even your own self. Yes, brother, may I enjoy you in the Lord; refresh my heart in Christ. Trusting in your obedience, I have written to you, knowing that you will do even more than I say. At the same time, prepare lodging for me also. For I hope that through your prayers I shall be granted to you. [Col. 0902B] Here it is shown that he was released from the city on the first occasion.

Epaphras, my fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus, greets you, as do Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, and Luke, my fellow-workers. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen. Not because of any crime, but through fellowship in the faith.

[Col. 0901]

[Note: [Col. 0901] This distribution is entirely that of Vallarsi; but since the Italian author, in completing his recension, included several works foreign to St. Jerome, and since we, in preparing a more general work elsewhere, have decided to assign each work to its proper author, let the reader know that the items marked with obeli in this survey have deliberately been omitted and will be restored in their proper place. EDIT.]

ARRANGED IN TEN VOLUMES AND COMPARED WITH THE DISTRIBUTION OF THE OLDER AND BENEDICTINE EDITIONS.

[Col. 0911]

## GENERAL INDEX TO ALL THE WORKS OF ST. JEROME

Much fuller than those appended to the individual volumes. [Note: [Col. 0911] This index refers to volumes 22 through 30 of Patrologia Latina. In this index, Arabic numerals refer to the column numbers printed in bold type in the text.]

This eighth volume has no place here, since its special index is constructed according to the order of the years, or the Abrahamic numbers; nor do the following two volumes, which contain the Latin translation of Sacred Scripture. Roman numerals indicate the volume, while Arabic numerals, corresponding to the bold characters inserted in the authentic text, designate the column.

## A

[Col. 0911]

The letter A is often pronounced as He by the Hebrews, III, 331.

Aaron’s garments breathe forth heavenly mysteries, I, 276. His sacrilege was corrected by fraternal prayers, 460. What Aaron and his sons and the Levites were in the temple, bishops, presbyters, and deacons should claim for themselves in the Church, 1083. Aaron the high priest died at Beroth, III, 171.

Habakkuk is interpreted as “a strong and unyielding wrestler,” I, 278. He contemplates Christ on the cross, ibid. The account of his being sent to Daniel is approved, 95. The Song of Habakkuk is inscribed with this title, II, 738. He spoke boldly to the Lord, rebuked himself, and wrote a song of repentance, 739. What he begs for, 772. The account of Habakkuk’s being sent to Daniel is not found in Hebrew, 349. Habakkuk’s tomb was shown at the village of Keilah, III, 186, 207, and at Gabatha, 223. The account of Habakkuk’s being sent to Daniel is uncertain among some writers, VI, 591.

Mount Abarim, I, 494. Mount Abarim, where Moses died, III, 142.

“Abba” is said in the Hebrew and Syriac languages, VII, 451. Jerome does not know by what license this name is bestowed in monasteries, ibid.

Obadiah is interpreted as “servant of God,” I, 278. The subjects of his prophecy, ibid. Obadiah’s remains lie at Samaria, 209. He was buried there, 703. Who was Obadiah? VI, 362. The Jews think that his prophecy is directed against Rome, 366. A large part of Obadiah is contained in Jeremiah, 365. At Sebaste is the tomb of Obadiah, Elisha, and John the Baptist, 363. What does Obadiah signify? VII, 688.

[Col. 0912] “Let us depart from these dwellings,” words of angels heard in the Jerusalem temple, I, 53, 202, 831, and V, 112.

Why Abel is called righteous, VII, 190. He was killed by Cain in the field of Damascus, according to Hebrew tradition, V, 316.

Abel-Shittim, I, 497.

Abela, “fertile in wine,” III, 158.

Abgar, king of Osrhoene, VII, 57.

Abimelech, a name of kings among the Philistines, V, 341.

The aid of God and the angels is said to depart from us whenever human weakness is abandoned to its own frailty, VI, 806.

The interpretation of Abishag, I, 257. The mystery of Abishag sleeping with David is explained, ibid., 255.

The renunciation of Satan, with his pomp and wickedness, in baptism, I, 31.

The time of weaning was set at the fifth year, or at the twelfth year, according to the opinion of the Hebrews, III, 335.

What is self-denial? VII, 713.

The abomination of desolation, I, 859, and VII, 195.

Those who procure abortions, I, 97. What an abortion signifies mystically, 860.

Abraham is tested and found more faithful, I, 173. In the midst of great wealth he was a friend of God, 498. By leaving Chaldea, Abraham seeks what he does not know, lest he lose the one whom he had found, 432. He did not think that he could possess both his homeland and the Lord at once, ibid. Since he was not content with present virtue, he reached forward into the future, ibid. He received a mystical name, ibid. What path did he open for us? ibid. In what was Abraham rich? 401. How large was his household? ibid. After frequent acts of hospitality, he deserved to receive God, ibid. He did not entrust the care of guests to servants and maidservants, but together with Sarah alone devoted himself to hospitality, ibid. He did not allow the good work he practiced to be diminished through others, ibid. He stood like a servant while the strangers dined, ibid. Abraham joyfully kills his only son, 184. He slaughtered him by will, 797. He did not despair that the one whom he had heard would become heir of the world would live even after death, ibid. In Gomorrah he received God with the angels, 890. Abraham and Isaac dig wells; the foreigners resist them, 419. The town in which four men were buried—Abraham, Isaac, and the others—700. Abraham: virtue and faith, II, 713. Abraham, conscious of his weakness, fell prone upon the ground, 796. Thinking that he could hide from God, he did not dare to laugh openly, ibid. He does not believe what God promised, and explains the reasons for his disbelief, ibid. God reproves him by a hidden answer, ibid. Abraham is asserted to have had three wives, 268. He adjures his servant in Christ, 252. Abraham and Sarah are reproved for laughter, 731. By the fact that afterward they believed, they received the palm of righteousness, ibid. Abraham and the others were not rich for themselves, ibid. According to Hebrew traditions, Abraham was delivered from fire because he refused to worship the idols of the Chaldeans, III, 323 and 324. His mausoleum, and the oak of Mamre, which was worshiped superstitiously, 130 and 195. He was Syrian by nationality, 356. Why Israel was called so, 357. Abraham was preserved from the fire of the Chaldeans through the integrity of his faith, IV, 779. He did not possess good things because he was rich, but because he used his riches well, 645. He offered Isaac on Mount Moriah, 1026. No one before Abraham was called an old man, 47 and 48. Abraham sinned; Moses and Aaron sinned, 523. Abraham’s faith is commended, V, 403. He was called Hebrew, that is, “one who crosses over,” 65. Abraham’s works: what were they? VI, 296. Who are the sons of Abraham? 876. Trade is conducted in Abraham’s tent, 885. What does Abraham signify? VII, 472. His faith is commended, 425.

Abraxas, I, 453. See Mithra.

Abrech, III, 367.

Abredotas was killed, II, 311.

No one dares give southernwood to a sick person unless he has learned how, II, 472.

The disgrace of amputation, VII, 492.

What it means to hide God’s commandments within oneself, IV, 12.

Absence loses little when it is joined to a person by continual letters, I, 937.

Food of wormwood in proportion to the greatness of evils, IV, 907.

Excessive abstinence from food is not approved—why? I, 988. Before the years of mature strength, abstinence is dangerous for the young, 685. It is much better to take a little every day than enough only rarely, 289. The reputation of abstinence is sought amid luxuries, 266. The good of abstinence and the evil of fullness, II, 346, 347. The blessedness of paradise could not be inaugurated without abstinence from food, 346. The good of abstinence, VII, 700. See Fasting, Continence, Food.

The consul Abundantius was exiled at Pityus, I, 344.

To abuse. A person who abuses creatures beyond measure does not possess true joy or a good heart, III, 462.

There are abysses of various kinds, VI, 410.

The abyss is understood indifferently in either direction, ibid.

Acacius was bishop of Caesarea after Eusebius Pamphilus, VII, 191. His works and his exposition of a certain passage of blessed Paul, ibid.

The gymnasia of the Academy, I, 270.

The New Academics, whom Cicero follows, I, 1026. What they think about the eradication of passions, ibid. The Academics, II, 558. The same Academics, VII, 737.

Variation of accents in Hebrew names produces a different meaning, III, 309.

Achad, a city of Babylonia, III, 127. It is now called Nisibis, ibid.

What Achates signifies, III, 363.

We receive more than we give, I, 398. Never asking, let us rarely accept when asked, 269. What is the difference between accepting and receiving? VII, 450.

Acco is now called Ptolemais, I, 696.

A true accusation against a brother is displeasing, II, 467. No one dares accuse his superior, III, 454.

The penitent Ahab is heard, I, 460.

Ahab and Jezebel are rebuked by Elijah’s reproach, 891. Ahab’s repentance and Jezebel’s obstinacy, ibid. One merits pardon; the other is condemned, ibid.

The Churches of Achaia, afflicted by many heresies, II, 893.

Whether Ahaz begot a son in the eleventh year, I, 445 and following. His evil life, ibid.

“Acheldama” is a Syriac name, not a Hebrew one, III, 89.

Ahikam, son of Shaphan, freed Jeremiah, II, 1031.

Achillas the lector, II, 193.

Alexander visited the tomb of Achilles, II, 13.

The valley of Achor, I, 702.

The Actaean shore, II, 659.

Actoria, wife of Marcus Cato the Censor, II, 316. Her vices, ibid.

[Col. 0914] The Acts of the Apostles seem to present bare history and to weave the infancy of the Church, I, 280. All the words of this book are medicine for a languishing soul, ibid. The Acts and Epistles of the Apostles are absorbed with the whole will of the heart, 688.

Hadad was the fourth to reign in the land of Edom, III, 218.

Adadremmon, a city near Jezreel, now called Maximianopolis, VI, 904.

Adam was created in perfect maturity, according to the Jews, I, 719. After being expelled from paradise, he had one wife, 507. Adam obeyed his belly, 95. Adam and Eve are figures of Christ and the Church, 968. They were monogamous, ibid. Where he lived and died, 193. Adam was overthrown by the hope of divinity, II, 43. Adam and Eve, virgins in paradise, enjoyed the companionship of the Lord, 241, 265. He was monogamous, 264. Nearly all Scripture is full of this idiom, by which it calls the entire human race Adam’s children, III, 466. Adam is said to have been buried in the city of Arba, or at the place of Calvary, 130. Why was Adam expelled from Paradise? IV, 778. Original sin in Adam, VI, 417. Adam, the first prophet, VII, 660. Where he was buried, 233. That everything said about Adam and Eve can be interpreted of Christ and the Church is difficult, 660.

Adamah and Zeboiim, two cities of the Pentapolis, VI, 129. Adamah and Zeboiim are used of Israel; Sodom and Gomorrah are used of the people of Judah, ibid.

The nature of adamant, IV, 957. Adamant, the strongest stone, VI, 328 and 836.

Why Origen was called Adamantius, I, 153. His diligence, VII, 735. His and Pierius’s copies, 199. What is absent from the copies of Adamantius, 418. See Origen.

A non-canonical addition, II, 759.

The tower of Eder, I, 700.

Who was the queen of Adiabene? I, 697.

How greatly Admetus was loved, II, 311.

The rich young man who said that he had done everything cannot overcome riches in the first contest, I, 794.

Youth endures many battles of the body, I, 256. The demons’ first weapons against youth, 93. The path of youth is slippery, 19. Youth is commonly struck by arrows of thought, 506. They are driven back by frequent prayers, ibid. The company of young women must be avoided, I, 912. The lustful flesh of young women is broken by frequent and repeated fasts, 713. Young men, by accusing distinguished men, sought fame for their own name, I, 633. The folly of youth is joined to it, III, 484.
